title: Madea's Witness Protection
tagline: Believe it or not, they know too much.
overview: For years, mild-mannered Wall Street banker George Needleman has meandered through life oblivious to his family's dysfunction and his company's malfeasance, but he's forced to wake up when he learns that he's been framed in a mob-backed Ponzi scheme. Placed under federal protection, George and his family are shipped down South to Madea's house, where the no-nonsense matriarch whips them all into shape using her special brand of tough love.
plot:
Madea's Witness Protection is a comedy film that explores the complexities of family dynamics and the challenges of adapting to new identities. The movie delves into the theme of identity, as the main character, Earl, played by Tyler Perry, navigates his new life under witness protection. He must leave behind his old self and adopt a new persona, which leads to comedic misunderstandings and cultural clashes.

The film also touches on the idea of family and the importance of embracing one's roots. Despite the challenges of adapting to a new identity, Earl ultimately finds solace in his newfound family, who accept him for who he is. This theme is exemplified through the character of Madea, played by Tyler Perry, who serves as a catalyst for change and growth.

Furthermore, the movie pokes fun at the bureaucratic red tape involved in witness protection programs, highlighting the absurdities and frustrations that can arise from such systems. The film's lighthearted tone and comedic approach to these themes make it an entertaining watch, while also offering commentary on the human experience.

Overall, Madea's Witness Protection is a heartwarming and humorous exploration of identity, family, and the complexities of adapting to new circumstances.

title: The Hunt
tagline: The lie is spreading.
overview: A teacher lives a lonely life, all the while struggling over his son’s custody. His life slowly gets better as he finds love and receives good news from his son, but his new luck is about to be brutally shattered by an innocent little lie.
plot:
The Hunt (Danish: Jagten) is a 2012 Danish psychological drama film co-written, produced and directed by Thomas Vinterberg. Set in a small Danish village around Christmas, it stars Mads Mikkelsen as Lucas, a divorced kindergarten teacher whose life is destroyed by mass hysteria after he is falsely accused of abusing a child, with Thomas Bo Larsen as his best friend Theo, Annika Wedderkopp as Theo's daughter Klara.

Lucas is well liked in his close-knit community. His fortunes seem to improve when his teenage son, Marcus, says he would like to live with him and he begins dating Nadja, a colleague. Klara often wanders off when her parents argue, and Lucas looks out for her. When she develops a crush on him and kisses him on the mouth, he gently rebuffs her. Upset, and drawing on a pornographic image her older brother's friend showed her, she makes remarks that lead the kindergarten's director, Grethe, to believe Lucas exposed himself to her. After Klara nods along to leading questions in an interview, Grethe alerts the authorities and the other parents. Klara later retracts her story, but the adults take this as denial. Lucas loses his job and Theo's friendship and is shunned by the village, without even knowing the exact accusations, which grow to involve several children. Believing Nadja doubts him, he ends their relationship.

Marcus comes to stay with his father and is turned away at the supermarket, sees Lucas arrested, and is taken in by Lucas's friend Bruun after confronting Klara. Bruun notes that many of the children's invented accounts describe a basement in Lucas's house, which has none, and Lucas is released. Someone kills his dog and throws a stone through his window. On Christmas Eve he is beaten by supermarket staff, and at the church service he confronts Theo, daring him to look in his eyes and find a lie. That night Klara tells her father that Lucas did nothing, and Theo brings Lucas food. A year later the community appears reconciled, but during a hunt an unseen shooter fires a bullet that narrowly misses Lucas.

The film premiered in competition at the 2012 Cannes Film Festival, where Mikkelsen won Best Actor. Made for 20 million Danish kroner, it earned over $16 million worldwide. It won the Nordic Council Film Prize and was Denmark's submission for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film, and critics praised Mikkelsen's performance, with 92% approval on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: The Lords of Salem
tagline: We've been waiting... we've always been waiting
overview: Heidi, a radio DJ, is sent a box containing a record - a "gift from the Lords". The sounds within the grooves trigger flashbacks of her town's violent past. Is Heidi going mad, or are the Lords back to take revenge on Salem, Massachusetts?
plot:
The Lords of Salem is a 2012 supernatural horror film written, produced and directed by Rob Zombie. It stars Sheri Moon Zombie as Heidi, a troubled disc jockey in Salem, Massachusetts, alongside Bruce Davison, Jeff Daniel Phillips, Ken Foree, Patricia Quinn, Dee Wallace, María Conchita Alonso, Judy Geeson and Meg Foster. A novelization by Zombie and B. K. Evenson was published a month before the film's release.

Heidi, a recovering drug addict, hosts a hard rock radio show with her colleagues Whitey and Munster. She receives a wooden box containing a record by a band called the Lords, whose eerie music gives her a vision of Satan-worshipping women ritually giving birth to a baby. When the station plays the record, Salem's women fall into a trance. Heidi's landlady, Lacy, and Lacy's sisters, Sonny and Megan, take an unusual interest in her, and in the supposedly vacant apartment 5 she experiences visions of a demon and a witch who commands her to "bleed us a king." Her nightmares worsen, and she relapses into drug use.

Meanwhile Francis Matthias, an author who interviewed Heidi about his book on the Salem witch trials, discovers that the Lords' music matches a centuries-old score. He learns that in the late 17th century Reverend Jonathan Hawthorne had a coven of witches executed for using the music to control Salem's women, and that their leader, Margaret Morgan, cursed the town's women and Hawthorne's descendants, whose bloodline would bear the devil's child. Matthias realizes Heidi is a descendant of Hawthorne, but before he can warn her, Lacy and her sisters, themselves witches, murder him while Heidi listens and does nothing. At the Lords' concert, the sisters and the ghosts of Margaret's coven perform a satanic rite. The music drives the women in the audience to strip, and amid surreal visions Heidi gives birth to a monstrous creature. The next day, the radio reports the mass suicide of 32 female descendants of Salem's original settlers at the concert and Heidi's disappearance.

Shot from October 2011, the film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 10, 2012, and was given a limited US release by Anchor Bay Films on April 19, 2013, grossing about $1.5 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed, praising its atmosphere but finding it short on scares; Rotten Tomatoes reported 45% approval and Metacritic a score of 57. Several critics have read it as a metaphor for drug addiction.

title: Mac & Devin Go to High School
original_title: Mac & Devin Go to High School

overview: A comedy that follows two high school students -- one overachiever struggling to write his valedictorian speech, the other a senior now going on his 15th year of school.
plot:
Mac & Devin Go to High School is a 2012 American stoner comedy film directed by Charles Stone III and written by John Whitesell. The movie stars Snoop Dogg and Wiz Khalifa as the titular characters, Mac Davis and Devin Williams.

The plot follows two high school friends, Mac (Snoop Dogg) and Devin (Wiz Khalifa), who are struggling to find their place in the world after graduation. Mac is a laid-back, smooth-talking rapper from Los Angeles, while Devin is a more aggressive and competitive rapper from Philadelphia. Despite their differences, they remain close friends.

The movie begins with Mac and Devin returning to their high school alma mater for a homecoming game. However, things take a turn when they discover that the school's principal has been replaced by a new, strict administrator who is determined to rid the school of its "bad influence." The two friends decide to take matters into their own hands and concoct a plan to expose the new principal's true intentions.

As Mac and Devin navigate the complexities of high school life once again, they must also contend with their own personal demons. Mac is struggling to find his place in the music industry, while Devin is trying to balance his rap career with his desire to attend college.

Throughout the movie, Mac and Devin's antics cause chaos and hilarity throughout the school, as they engage in pranks, parties, and other misadventures. Along the way, they also encounter a range of colorful characters, including a seductive cheerleader (Ashley Benson) and a group of eccentric teachers.

As the story unfolds, Mac and Devin's plan to expose the new principal comes to fruition, but not without some unexpected twists and turns. In the end, the two friends successfully defeat the villainous principal and restore order to their alma mater.

One of the standout aspects of Mac & Devin Go to High School is its lighthearted, comedic tone. The movie is full of humorous moments, from Snoop Dogg's signature smooth-talking style to Wiz Khalifa's goofy antics. The chemistry between the two leads is undeniable, and their banter provides much of the movie's humor.

Overall, Mac & Devin Go to High School is a fun, entertaining film that is sure to appeal to fans of stoner comedies and hip-hop culture. While it may not be a particularly original or groundbreaking movie, its lighthearted tone and comedic performances make it a worthwhile watch.

title: Battlestar Galactica: The Plan
tagline: They have a plan!
overview: When the initial Cylon attack against the Twelve Colonies fails to achieve complete extermination of human life as planned, twin Number Ones (Cavils) embedded on Galactica and Caprica must improvise to destroy the human survivors.
plot:
Battlestar Galactica: The Plan is a 2008 television miniseries that serves as a prequel to the re-imagined series. It explores the events leading up to the Cylon attack on the Twelve Colonies, and delves into the complexities of human nature, politics, and the consequences of war.

At its core, the story revolves around the themes of fate, free will, and the cyclical nature of violence. The characters are faced with an existential crisis as they grapple with the inevitability of their own demise, and the question of whether their actions can change the course of events or if it's already set in motion.

The miniseries also delves into the consequences of playing god, as the characters struggle to understand the nature of the Cylons and their motivations. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, raising questions about the ethics of scientific discovery and the responsibility that comes with it.

Furthermore, The Plan explores the human condition, revealing the flaws and vulnerabilities of its characters. The story highlights the tension between individual desire for power and the greater good, as well as the blurred lines between heroism and villainy.

Ultimately, Battlestar Galactica: The Plan is a thought-provoking exploration of the human experience, one that challenges viewers to confront the darker aspects of their own nature and the consequences of their actions.

title: The Good Dinosaur
tagline: Little Arms With Big Attitude
overview: An epic journey into the world of dinosaurs where an Apatosaurus named Arlo makes an unlikely human friend.
plot:
The Good Dinosaur is a computer-animated adventure film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and released by Walt Disney Pictures in 2015.

In an alternate timeline, on November 12, 1859, a massive asteroid hurtles towards Earth. However, due to the intervention of a friendly dinosaur named Archimedes, who deflects the asteroid with his tail, the course of history is altered. In this new reality, dinosaurs and humans coexist in the same world.

The story follows Arlo, a young Apatosaurus (also known as Longneck) who lives on a ranch in New Mexico with his family. Arlo's life is marked by fear and anxiety, particularly after an incident where he was attacked by a Tyrannosaurus Rex when he was just a hatchling. His father, Buck, tries to protect him from the dangers of the world but also wants Arlo to grow up and take responsibility.

One day, while out exploring, Arlo is swept away by a flood and separated from his family. He finds himself lost in an unfamiliar forest, where he meets a wild and fierce Tyrannosaurus Rex named Spot. Initially, Spot appears to be a threat, but as the story progresses, it becomes clear that she is also a scared and lonely creature who has been ostracized by her own kind.

As Arlo and Spot embark on a journey together, they form an unlikely bond. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, ferocious predators, and even a group of hostile humans. Through their shared experiences, Arlo learns to confront his fears and develop courage, while Spot finds acceptance and belonging.

Throughout their adventure, Arlo and Spot's relationship evolves from one of predator and prey to a deep and abiding friendship. Along the way, they meet a cast of colorful characters, including a wise old triceratops named Big Red, who serves as a mentor to both Arlo and Spot.

As the story unfolds, Arlo comes to realize that his family's past is not just about survival but also about love, loss, and letting go. He learns to appreciate the beauty of the world around him and finds a new sense of purpose in life.

In the end, Arlo and Spot successfully navigate their challenges and find their way back home. Along the way, Arlo confronts his fears and develops the courage to face the unknown. The film concludes with Arlo returning to his family's ranch, where he is welcomed back with open arms. However, it also leaves room for speculation about what might have happened if Archimedes had not deflected the asteroid.

The Good Dinosaur is a heartwarming and visually stunning film that explores themes of friendship, courage, and the power of imagination. The movie features stunning animation, lovable characters, and a story that will leave audiences of all ages smiling.

title: Beverly Hills Chihuahua 3: Viva la Fiesta!
original_title: Beverly Hills Chihuahua 3: Viva la Fiesta!
tagline: Family Always Matters
overview: When Papi, Chloe, the pups, Uncle Pedro, and their owners move to a hotel, the smallest pup Rosa feels like she doesn't fit in, and Papi wants to make her feel better by showing her how special she is.
plot:
Beverly Hills Chihuahua 3: Viva la Fiesta! is an American family comedy of 2012 directed by Lev L. Spiro, the third and last entry in Disney's Beverly Hills Chihuahua series, released straight to home video. George Lopez and Odette Annable voice the chihuahua couple Papi and Chloe, with Kay Panabaker as their daughter Rosa, Logan Grove as Papi Jr., Ernie Hudson as Pedro, Jake Busey as Oscar, Lacey Chabert as Charlotte, Tom Kenny as Sebastian and Miguel Ferrer as Delgado. Marcus Coloma and Erin Cahill play the dogs' owners Sam and Rachel, with Cedric Yarbrough as hotel manager Mr. Hollis.

Two years after their wedding, Sam and Rachel take jobs at the luxurious Langham Hotel as landscaper and sous-chef, moving in with Papi, Chloe, their puppies and Pedro. Mr. Hollis, worried about competition from the rival Montague hotel, wants Chloe to make appearances for the Langham, and the puppies are enrolled in the hotel's Doggy Day School, run by Jenny and her dog Oscar, which leaves Papi disappointed that he will no longer teach them himself. Rachel suffers under the arrogant Chef Didier, who has her washing dishes, while Sam is saddled with the lazy assistant Lester. Rosa, the runt of the litter, is teased by a big dog for wearing swimming aids, and her siblings take revenge on her behalf.

In an overgrown garden, Papi befriends Arnie, a mute stray, and begins to suspect that Jenny and Oscar are hiding something, though Arnie's attempt to warn him with a carving at first confuses him. Feeling small and wanting to grow up, Rosa asks for a quinceañera, the Mexican coming-of-age celebration Papi once took part in, and he promises to throw her one, helped by his old friend Sebastian. As Papi juggles the party preparations with his growing suspicions, Rosa saves Charlotte, a VIP guest's dog who cannot swim, after she falls into the pool. Papi, Pedro and Arnie enlist the police dog Delgado to help expose Jenny, who ends up stuck in a puddle of peanut butter, while Delgado appears with the rival hotelier Montague. Chloe apologises to Papi for doubting him, and Rosa's quinceañera goes ahead with her siblings in matching outfits. Jenny and Oscar are arrested, Papi becomes the new teacher at the day school, and Hollis adopts Arnie.

Disney released the film on Blu-ray and DVD in September 2012. Zachary Gordon and Chantily Spalan did not return as Papi Jr. and Rosa, and it was Kay Panabaker's final film before she retired from acting to study zoology.

title: Erased
tagline: Far from home. Far from safe. Far from over.
overview: A former agent of the CIA and his estranged daughter go on the run after his employers target them for assassination.
plot:
Erased, released outside the United States as The Expatriate, is an action thriller of 2012 directed by Philipp Stölzl and written by Arash Amel. Aaron Eckhart stars as Ben Logan, a former CIA operative living quietly in Belgium, with Liana Liberato as his teenage daughter Amy, Olga Kurylenko as the CIA officer Anna Brandt, and Garrick Hagon as the executive James Halgate III.

He works for the Kohler Company, part of the multinational technology firm the Halgate Group, testing ways to defeat security systems such as locks and iris scanners. After a colleague notices that the company holds no patent for one of its products, Ben reports it to his boss, Kohler. Soon afterwards he arrives to find the office deserted, with no trace of the company or of his employment. While he tries to prove his job through bank records, his co-worker Floyd seizes him and Amy at gunpoint and forces them into Ben's car. Ben deliberately crashes it and kills Floyd before his shocked daughter, and the two flee the police. Hiding in an empty house, Amy demands the truth, and he hints only that he used to get people out of difficult situations.

Learning that all his colleagues have been murdered, Ben goes underground with help from Algerian illegal immigrants Amy has befriended. He uncovers evidence of a vast conspiracy in which Halgate is smuggling arms to African insurgents in order to win lithium mining rights once they seize power; the shell company had been using Ben's skills to steal the incriminating documents from a CIA cache. He finally admits to Amy that he was once a CIA operative. Hunted by the Belgian police, a Halgate assassin and a CIA team led by Anna, Ben's former lover, who is secretly on Halgate's payroll and had recommended him for the job. When the two finally meet, Ben persuades her that she has lost her moral bearings, and she switches sides, but she is killed trying to save Amy after the assassin captures the girl. Ben offers himself and the documents in exchange for his daughter, hiding a homemade bomb in the briefcase. After saying goodbye to Amy, who leaves with her Algerian friend Nabil, he hands over the case; when Halgate orders Amy and her grandfather killed within a week, the bomb kills him, his assistant and the assassin. Ben and Amy are reunited at an airport.

Acquired by RADiUS-TWC, the film was released in American cinemas in May 2013. Critics found it derivative, giving it 28% on Rotten Tomatoes and 34 on Metacritic.

title: The Wolf of Wall Street
tagline: EARN. SPEND. PARTY.
overview: A New York stockbroker refuses to cooperate in a large securities fraud case involving corruption on Wall Street, corporate banking world and mob infiltration. Based on Jordan Belfort's autobiography.
plot:
The Wolf of Wall Street is a biographical comedy-drama film directed by Martin Scorsese, based on the memoir of the same name by Jordan Belfort. The movie stars Leonardo DiCaprio as Belfort, a stockbroker who becomes embroiled in a world of corruption and excess.

The film begins with Belfort (DiCaprio) graduating from college and landing a job at L.F. Rothschild, Unterberg, Towbin, a prestigious investment firm on Wall Street. However, he soon becomes disillusioned with the company's conservative culture and decides to strike out on his own.

Belfort teams up with Donnie Azoff (Jonah Hill), a young and ambitious stockbroker who shares his desire for wealth and success. Together, they start their own brokerage firm, Stratton Oakmont, which quickly gains a reputation for its aggressive and unscrupulous tactics.

As Belfort's wealth and influence grow, so does his ego and sense of entitlement. He becomes embroiled in a world of corruption and crime, using his firm to scam investors out of millions of dollars. He also becomes involved with a series of high-profile prostitutes, including Naomi (Margot Robbie), who becomes his mistress.

Despite the risks, Belfort's success continues to grow, and he becomes one of the most successful stockbrokers in the country. However, his excesses eventually catch up with him, and he is forced to confront the consequences of his actions.

Throughout the film, Scorsese uses a non-linear narrative structure, jumping back and forth between different periods of Belfort's life. The film also features a number of memorable supporting performances, including Matthew McConaughey as Mark Hanna, a mentor who teaches Belfort how to become a successful stockbroker.

The Wolf of Wall Street is a scathing critique of the excesses of 1980s capitalism and the corrupting influence of wealth and power. The film's depiction of Belfort's rise and fall is both fascinating and repellent, and DiCaprio's performance is both captivating and disturbing.

Overall, The Wolf of Wall Street is a wild and unapologetic ride that explores the darker side of human nature. With its sharp wit, clever dialogue, and outstanding performances, it is a must-see for fans of Scorsese and DiCaprio.

title: Machete Kills
tagline: Trained to kill. Left for dead. Back for more.
overview: Ex-Federale agent Machete is recruited by the President of the United States for a mission which would be impossible for any mortal man – he must take down a madman revolutionary and an eccentric billionaire arms dealer who has hatched a plan to spread war and anarchy across the planet.
plot:
Machete Kills is an action-packed film that delves into various themes, primarily revolving around the consequences of violence and the blurred lines between good and evil.

The movie follows Machete, a Mexican federale, as he navigates a complex web of corruption, politics, and power struggles. As Machete fights his way through the story, he encounters a range of characters, from politicians to revolutionaries, each with their own motivations and agendas.

One of the primary themes of Machete Kills is the exploration of the cyclical nature of violence. The film stars Tom Hanks as Captain Richard Phillips, a merchant mariner who becomes the target of Somali pirates.

The film begins with an introduction to Captain Phillips (Tom Hanks), a seasoned sailor who has spent his entire life at sea. He is married to Andrea (Catherine Keener) and has two children. The story then shifts to April 2009, when Phillips' ship, the MV Maersk Alabama, sets sail from the port of Aden in Yemen.

As the ship navigates through the Indian Ocean, it becomes a target for Somali pirates. On April 8, 2009, the ship is hijacked by three pirates, led by Abduwali Abdukhadir Muse (Barkhad Abdi). The pirates take Phillips and four crew members hostage, demanding a ransom in exchange for their safe release.

The film then follows the events that unfold as Phillips tries to negotiate with the pirates. He attempts to reason with them, but they are unwilling to listen. As tensions rise, Phillips realizes that he must find a way to escape or be killed by the pirates.

Meanwhile, the US Navy is alerted to the hijacking and begins to track the ship's location. The Navy sends a team of SEALs, led by Lieutenant Michael Murphy (Taylor Kitsch), to rescue the hostages. However, the operation is complicated by the fact that the pirates are hiding in a remote area with limited communication.

As the standoff between Phillips and the pirates continues, it becomes clear that Muse has no intention of releasing his captives alive. In a tense and dramatic confrontation, Phillips manages to outsmart the pirates and escape from the ship. However, he is left stranded in a lifeboat, adrift in the ocean with limited supplies.

The film's climax features an intense and suspenseful rescue operation, as the SEALs finally reach the location of the Maersk Alabama. In a daring move, Murphy sacrifices himself to distract the pirates and allow the other SEALs to board the ship and rescue Phillips.

In the aftermath of the rescue, Phillips is hailed as a hero for his bravery and cunning in outsmarting the pirates. The film ends with Phillips reflecting on the experience, realizing that he has been forever changed by the ordeal.

Overall, Captain Phillips is a gripping and intense thriller that showcases Tom Hanks' remarkable acting abilities. The film's tense and suspenseful plot, combined with its well-developed characters and themes of bravery and sacrifice, make it a compelling watch.

title: Evil Dead

plot:
Evil Dead is a 2013 American supernatural horror film directed by Fede Álvarez in his feature debut, from a screenplay he co-wrote with Rodo Sayagues. A soft reboot and the fourth installment of the Evil Dead series, it stars Jane Levy as Mia, Shiloh Fernandez as her brother David, Lou Taylor Pucci as Eric, Jessica Lucas as Olivia and Elizabeth Blackmore as Natalie.

In a prologue, a possessed young woman held in a remote cabin's cellar is burned and shot by her father. Later, David and his girlfriend Natalie come to the cabin, his family's holiday home, with his estranged younger half-sister Mia and their friends Eric, a teacher, and Olivia, a nurse. They plan to help Mia quit heroin; her last attempt ended in a relapse in which she briefly died. In the cellar they find animal corpses and a book, the Naturom Demonto, and Eric reads an incantation that awakens a demonic force. Mia sees a demonic double of herself, flees in Eric's car, crashes and is possessed after vines attack her. When she scalds herself, flooded roads stop David from taking her to a hospital.

The possessed Mia shoots David, vomits into Olivia's mouth and is locked in the cellar. Olivia, now possessed, mutilates herself and attacks Eric before he kills her. Mia bites Natalie, who is possessed through the wound and dies after attacking with a nail gun. The book says the Taker of Souls needs five souls to raise the Abomination, and that Mia can be purified only by live burial, dismemberment or burning. Eric is fatally stabbed protecting David, who buries Mia alive and then revives her with a makeshift defibrillator, freeing her of the demon. The entity possesses Eric's corpse, and David sacrifices himself by igniting a gasoline can. His death is the fifth soul. Blood rains from the sky, and the Abomination rises. Mia, losing a hand under David's overturned Jeep, splits it in two with a chainsaw. In a post-credits scene, Bruce Campbell appears as Ash Williams.

The project was announced in 2011 with Ghost House Pictures producing and Diablo Cody revising the script. Jane Levy replaced Lily Collins as Mia. The film was shot near Auckland, New Zealand, in 2012 and premiered at South by Southwest on March 8, 2013, before TriStar Pictures released it on April 5. It opened at number one and grossed $97.5 million on a $17 million budget. Reviews were mixed. Rotten Tomatoes reported 64% approval, noting that it trades the original's absurd humor for brutal, gory terror. Evil Dead Rise followed.

title: Hit & Run
tagline: A Comedy That Never Takes Its Foot Off The Gas
overview: When former getaway driver, Charlie Bronson jeopardises his Witness Protection Plan identity in order to help his girlfriend get to Los Angeles, the feds and Charlie's former gang chase them on the road.
plot:
Hit and Run, stylised as Hit & Run, is a 2012 American action comedy written by Dax Shepard, who co-directed it with David Palmer as their second collaboration after Brother's Justice in 2010. Shepard stars alongside his real-life partner Kristen Bell, with Kristin Chenoweth, Tom Arnold, Michael Rosenbaum and Bradley Cooper in supporting roles. Much of the film's appeal rests on its car chases, which feature vehicles from Shepard's own collection, including a restored Lincoln Continental. It was released in August 2012.

Shepard plays Charlie Bronson, a former getaway driver living in Witness Protection in the small town of Milton, California, under the clumsy supervision of U.S. Marshal Randy Anderson, played by Arnold. Charlie's girlfriend Annie Bean, played by Bell, is a college lecturer with a doctorate in non-violent conflict resolution. When she is offered a job interview at UCLA in Los Angeles, a city Charlie has sworn never to return to, he decides to risk everything and drive her there himself in his souped-up Continental.

Annie's jealous ex-boyfriend Gil, played by Rosenbaum, suspects that Charlie is a dangerous criminal and digs into his past with the help of his brother, a police officer. He learns that Charlie's real name is Yul Perrkins and that he once testified against his former bank-robbing crew. Gil tracks down one of them, Alex Dimitri, played by Cooper, on social media and tips him off. Soon Charlie and Annie are pursued across California by Alex and his associates, by Gil, by local police and by the hapless Randy, setting off a series of chases, confrontations and arguments. Along the way Annie learns uncomfortable truths about Charlie's history, and the couple must decide whether their relationship can survive the revelations.

The film combines stunt-driving action with romantic comedy, and its humour comes from bickering, eccentric side characters and the gap between Charlie's violent past and Annie's pacifist ideals. It was made on a modest budget, with Shepard performing much of the driving himself.

Hit and Run received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 49 percent; the critical consensus acknowledges some off-kilter filmmaking but finds that the action adds little and the writing is uneven. The film earned a modest box-office return.

The film takes place in a post-apocalyptic world where the last remnants of humanity are confined to a massive train that travels around the frozen globe.

As Curtis navigates the cramped and claustrophobic tail section, he discovers that it has been designed as a prison for the poor and marginalized, while the wealthy and powerful reside in luxurious comfort at the front of the train. As Curtis and his companions begin to organize a revolution, they realize that the train is not just a physical barrier but also a metaphorical one. The ruling class has created a system of oppression and control, where the privileged few are allowed to live in luxury while the many struggle to survive.

The plot thickens as Curtis and his allies launch a series of attacks against the front section of the train, seeking to overthrow Wilford and bring about change. Along the way, they uncover dark secrets about the train's past and the true nature of its purpose.

As the rebellion gains momentum, Curtis faces off against Wilford in a final confrontation. The two engage in a philosophical debate about the morality of their actions and the nature of humanity, with Curtis arguing that the ends justify the means and Wilford claiming that the system is necessary to preserve human civilization.

In the end, Curtis emerges victorious, but not without scars. He and his companions succeed in toppling Wilford's regime, but the train is left in a state of chaos and uncertainty. The film concludes with Curtis standing at the front of the train, looking out at the frozen landscape, symbolizing a new beginning for humanity.

Throughout the film, Bong Joon-ho explores themes of class struggle, social inequality, and the human condition. Snowpiercer is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that challenges viewers to consider the consequences of our actions and the morality of our choices.

This newfound power allows her to protect herself and those around her from harm. However, it also puts her in danger of being discovered by humans who fear and hunt werewolves.

As tensions rise, Yūko must confront the reality of her children's condition and find a way to keep them safe while also teaching them how to control their powers. Along the way, she learns valuable lessons about motherhood, love, and acceptance.

The film's climax features an intense confrontation between Hana and a group of hunters who seek to capture and kill werewolves. With her newfound powers, Hana is able to defend herself and those she cares about, ultimately emerging victorious.

In the end, Yūko comes to terms with her children's condition and finds a way to live with it. The film concludes on a hopeful note, with Hana embracing her identity as a werewolf and finding a sense of belonging among others who accept her for what she is.

title: The Body
tagline: Death is not always the end
overview: A woman’s body disappears mysteriously from the morgue without a trace. Police inspector Jaime Peña investigates the strange occurrence with the help of Álex Ulloa, the widower of the missing woman.
plot:
The Body (Spanish: El cuerpo) is a 2012 Spanish psychological thriller directed by Oriol Paulo, from a screenplay he co-wrote with Lara Sendim. José Coronado stars as a police inspector, Hugo Silva as a widower under suspicion, Belén Rueda as his wealthy wife and Aura Garrido as his young mistress. It was released in Spain in December 2012.

One night, the night watchman at a forensic institute flees in panic and is struck by a car, leaving him in a coma. Inspector Jaime Peña, called to investigate, learns that a body has vanished from the morgue: that of Mayka Villaverde, a powerful pharmaceutical executive who died of an apparent heart attack hours earlier. Her much younger husband, Álex Ulloa, is summoned from a rendezvous with his lover, Carla, whom he has assured that Mayka is dead. Peña, who still speaks of his own wife, killed years earlier in a car accident, in the present tense, notices that Álex refers to Mayka in the past tense far too easily and suspects that someone stole the body to prevent an autopsy.

Álex is in fact guilty: he poisoned Mayka's wine with TH-16, an experimental toxin from her company that induces a heart attack after several hours and leaves no trace. As the night wears on, strange incidents at the morgue convince Álex that Mayka faked her death and is alive and seeking revenge, having discovered his affair and his plans. Under pressure he confesses to Peña, but evidence against him accumulates, the watchman wakes to describe a masked gunman, and Peña tells him that there is no record of a woman named Carla at the address he provided.

While Álex is being transported, Mayka's body is found in the woods. Álex flees and collapses, and Peña finally reveals the truth. Years earlier, Mayka and Álex caused the crash that killed Peña's wife and fled without calling for help, leaving her to die in front of Peña and his young daughter. Carla is that daughter, who seduced Álex as part of a plan devised with her father to expose him, and the disappearance of the body was staged by them. As Álex struggles to breathe, he learns that Carla dosed him with TH-16 hours earlier, so that his death will look like a stress-induced heart attack.

The film was well received for its twisting plot, one reviewer calling it lean, moody and superior. Its success led to numerous remakes, including a Tamil-Kannada version, the South Korean film The Vanished (2018), the Hindi film The Body (2019), and Italian and Indonesian versions.

title: Daniel & Ana
overview: Being kidnapped shatters a brother and sister's harmony, forcing them to confront their desires.
plot:
Daniel & Ana is a 2009 Mexican thriller drama directed by Michel Franco in his feature debut, starring Darío Yazbek Bernal and Marimar Vega as a brother and sister whose lives are torn apart by a violent crime. It premiered on May 18, 2009, at the Cannes Film Festival. The story was inspired by a real case, and the film deals with the abduction of two siblings who are forced to perform sexual acts together on camera, and with the trauma that follows.

Daniel and Ana are siblings from a wealthy family in Mexico City. Daniel, the younger of the two, is dating a girl named Mariana, while Ana is engaged to Rafa, who is considering a job offer in Spain. One day while they are out running errands, the pair are kidnapped at gunpoint. Under threat of death they are filmed being forced into intercourse, and their captors confirm to an unseen client that they have the footage before releasing them. Although they are physically unharmed when they return home, the experience shatters both of their lives. Unable to speak about what happened to each other or anyone else, they search in vain for the video online.

Over time Ana proves more resilient. She sees a psychiatrist and repairs her relationship with Rafa, and she urges Daniel to join her in therapy, but he refuses. Daniel's emotional state deteriorates as he struggles with confused feelings about his sister and with guilt and anger he cannot express. His behavior grows increasingly disturbing and violent, culminating in an assault on Ana and an attempt to force himself on Mariana. Ana decides to leave and move to Spain with Rafa, and Daniel's attempts to make her stay come to nothing. On Ana's wedding day, he arrives with a dagger intending to harm Rafa but cannot bring himself to do it. The newlyweds say goodbye, and the siblings part after an awkward embrace.

The film closes with title cards warning of a rise in pornography made with coerced amateurs and stating that the real siblings never learned what became of the video. Vega later said she was initially nervous about the film's nudity but was reassured after the director explained how he would approach the scenes.

Critical reception was mixed. The film has a 50% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 43. The New York Times suggested that its stylistic restraint deflected accusations of exploitation but that its muted emotions impeded the audience's connection with the victims, while The Village Voice felt it was effective until its final act.

plot:
Berserk: The Golden Age Arc I – The Egg of the King is a 2012 Japanese animated dark fantasy film, the first in a trilogy adapting the Golden Age arc of Kentaro Miura's manga Berserk. Produced by Studio 4°C under chief director Toshiyuki Kubooka, with a screenplay by Ichirō Ōkōchi, it covers roughly the middle of the manga's fourth volume to the middle of its sixth. The Japanese cast features Hiroaki Iwanaga as Guts, Takahiro Sakurai as Griffith and Toa Yukinari as Casca, while the English dub reunites Marc Diraison, Kevin T. Collins and Carrie Keranen from the original television anime.

Guts is an immensely strong sword-for-hire with no direction in life beyond the next battle. When he kills an enemy champion during a siege, he draws the attention of the Band of the Hawk, a mercenary company led by the beautiful and charismatic Griffith, who defeats him in single combat and forces him to join. The relationship between the two men grows into a bond that wavers between rivalry and friendship, while Casca, the band's only woman and a tough swordswoman, struggles to accept the newcomer and his influence. Employed by the Kingdom of Midland in its Hundred Year War against the Tudor Empire, the Hawks win battle after battle, and Griffith rises steadily through the kingdom's ranks in pursuit of a mysterious, prophesied ambition. During another siege, Guts and Griffith encounter the monstrous demon Nosferatu Zodd, who notices the pendant around Griffith's neck and warns Guts that Griffith will be his doom. Griffith's rapid ascent angers Midland's noblemen, and after the king's brother, Julius, tries to have him assassinated, Griffith charges Guts with murdering Julius. Guts carries out the killing but also kills the noble's young son, an act that leaves him deeply shaken. Afterwards, he overhears Griffith say that the Hawks are his comrades, but that a true friend is someone who pursues a dream of their own rather than someone else's. The words haunt him.

The film was released in Japan by Warner Bros. Pictures Japan on 4 February 2012, with a score by Shirō Sagisu and a theme by Susumu Hirasawa, and Viz Media released it on home video in North America that November. Anime News Network called it an exciting, faithful adaptation but criticized its heavy use of 3D CG animation, a complaint shared by other reviewers.

The movie highlights the tension between Effie's desire for autonomy and her societal obligations, which ultimately lead to a crisis of identity.

The film also touches on the theme of art as a means of expression and empowerment, as Effie becomes increasingly involved in Millais' work and finds solace in his creative process. Through Effie's character, the movie showcases the ways in which art can be both a source of comfort and a means of rebellion against societal norms.

Furthermore, the film explores the complexities of relationships and the blurred lines between love, friendship, and mentorship. The bond between Effie and Millais is multifaceted, oscillating between romantic tension and platonic affection, leaving the audience to ponder the nature of their connection.

Ultimately, Effie Gray is a poignant portrayal of a woman's journey towards self-discovery and artistic expression, set against the backdrop of a bygone era. Cockneys vs Zombies is a 2012 British comedy horror film that satirizes zombie apocalypse movies while maintaining a strong sense of British culture and humor. The movie's main theme revolves around the clash between traditional British values and the chaos brought about by an unexpected threat.

At its core, Cockneys vs Zombies explores the idea of community and resilience in the face of adversity. The film's protagonist, Danny Jones (played by Ralph Ineson), is a lovable but slightly dim-witted cockney who finds himself at the forefront of the zombie outbreak. As he navigates this new world, he must rely on his wits, resourcefulness, and the support of his community to survive.

The movie also delves into themes of class and social hierarchy, poking fun at the traditional British class system while highlighting the importance of unity in the face of danger. The film's characters are often stereotypical, but they're also relatable and well-developed, making it easy for audiences to root for them as they work together to overcome their undead foes.

Furthermore, Cockneys vs Zombies is a commentary on the absurdity of modern life and our tendency to take ourselves too seriously. The movie's over-the-top humor and ridiculous situations serve as a reminder that even in the darkest of times, there's always room for laughter and levity.

Overall, Cockneys vs Zombies is a lighthearted, entertaining film that uses humor and satire to explore themes of community, resilience, and the importance of not taking oneself too seriously.

Let It Shine is a 2012 American musical television film directed by Paul Hoen and written by Eric Daniel and Don D. Scott, a hip hop retelling of Edmond Rostand's 1897 play Cyrano de Bergerac made for Disney Channel. It stars Tyler James Williams as Cyrus DeBarge, a shy teenage musician who secretly writes rap lyrics, Coco Jones as the pop star Roxie Andrews, Trevor Jackson as Cyrus's best friend, Kris McDuffy, and Brandon Mychal Smith as the rapper Lord of Da Bling, with Dawnn Lewis as Cyrus's mother, Gail.

In Atlanta, fifteen-year-old Cyrus is a gifted church choir director who writes rap verses under the alias "Truth", both because his father, Pastor Jacob, disapproves of hip hop and because he is far more reserved than the outgoing Kris. Without his father's knowledge, Cyrus works as a busboy at a club called Off the Street, where the record label of Roxie, a childhood friend who has become a teen singing star, holds a songwriting contest. Roxie picks Truth's song "Don't Run Away" as the winner, but because Cyrus's submitted photo showed both boys, she assumes Kris is Truth. Kris, who has feelings for Roxie, persuades Cyrus to let him keep the credit, and as Kris uses Cyrus's words to win Roxie and enjoy his new fame, Cyrus grows resentful.

Roxie finds she can talk more easily with Cyrus than with Kris, and Cyrus invites her to sing with his church choir, but Jacob publicly humiliates her by condemning "hip-hop-crisy". Persuaded by Gail to apologize at the club, Jacob discovers his son working there and writing rap. Furious at first, he grounds Cyrus, but after realizing that the lyrics carry positive messages, he lifts the punishment. Cyrus and Kris come to blows, and the club owner, Levi, urges them to save their friendship. During a duet with Roxie, Cyrus takes Kris's place onstage to perform "Me and You", revealing himself as Truth, and Roxie walks off feeling deceived. At a rap battle, Cyrus defeats the arrogant Lord of Da Bling by exposing him as a fraud who works as a taxi driver. Kris tells Roxie that Cyrus only hid his identity for his friend's sake and is the one she should be with, and Roxie finds Cyrus at the church, where they embrace and sing "Let It Shine".

Shot in Atlanta and Marietta, Georgia, with thirteen original songs, the film premiered on Disney Channel on June 15, 2012, drawing 5.7 million viewers, the top cable audience of the day. It was the most watched Disney Channel Original Movie of 2012 up to that point.

Ash and his friends, Iris and Cilan, arrive in Elesa's city, where they meet Elesa, a powerful Electric-type Pokémon trainer from Unova. Elesa has been searching for Reshiram, the mythical Pokémon said to have the power to control time. Ash and his friends soon discover that Reshiram is being held captive by Team Plasma, a group of rogue trainers who seek to free all Pokémon from their trainers.

As Ash and his friends try to rescue Reshiram, they learn about the history of Reshiram and its connection to the mythical Pokémon Victini. According to legend, Reshiram and Victini were once connected, but they were separated by a powerful artifact known as the "Reshiram Crystal." The crystal was said to have been created by the ancient Pokémon, Dialga.

Ash and his friends soon discover that Team Plasma is planning to use the Reshiram Crystal to free all Pokémon from their trainers. They also learn that Elesa's city is in danger of being destroyed if the crystal is used.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Ash and his friends are forced to make a difficult choice: to save Elesa's city or to rescue Reshiram. In the end, they decide to work together with Team Plasma to stop the destruction of the city.

In the climactic final battle, Ash and his friends face off against Team Plasma leader, Ghetsis. With the help of Elesa and her Pokémon, Ash is able to defeat Ghetsis and shatter the Reshiram Crystal, freeing Reshiram from its prison.

With Reshiram freed, it is revealed that the crystal was actually a powerful artifact created by Dialga, which had been keeping Reshiram captive for centuries. The movie ends with Ash and his friends reflecting on their adventure and the lessons they learned about friendship and teamwork.

Overall, Pokémon the Movie: Black - Victini and Reshiram is an action-packed adventure that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and the importance of understanding and respecting the natural world.

title: Blue Lagoon: The Awakening
overview: Two high school students become stranded on a tropical island and must rely on each other for survival. They learn more about themselves and each other while falling in love.
plot:
Blue Lagoon: The Awakening is a 2012 American romantic drama television film that premiered on Lifetime on 16 June 2012. It stars Indiana Evans and Brenton Thwaites, with Denise Richards, Patrick St. Esprit and Frank John Hughes. Based loosely on Henry De Vere Stacpoole's 1908 novel The Blue Lagoon and its earlier film adaptations, it departs from them in several ways: the story is contemporary rather than Victorian, the leads are teenagers raised in ordinary society rather than children who grow up on the island, the setting is the Caribbean instead of the South Pacific, and roughly equal time is given to life on the island and the world back home.

Emma and Dean are high school students on a class trip to Trinidad to help build a school for underprivileged children. Emma is a popular, high-achieving student with her future carefully planned, while Dean is a withdrawn loner who often gets into trouble and has kept to himself since his mother died. Emma attracts the attention of Steven, the school's quarterback, but she is curious about Dean. During a boat party on their second night, Emma sees Steven kissing another girl and, in the confusion of a police raid, falls overboard. Dean jumps in after her and pulls her into a dinghy, then cuts it loose to avoid trouble, only to discover that it has no motor.

The pair drift to a deserted island, where the tide soon carries off their dinghy. With no way of knowing whether they will be rescued, they must rely on each other to survive, learning to build a fire, catch fish, find fresh water and make shelter. At first they clash, but as weeks pass their differences give way to friendship and then romance. Meanwhile, their families, classmates and teacher back home struggle with uncertainty about their fate and continue to search for them. When they are eventually rescued and return to their old lives, Emma and Dean must face the question of whether the bond they formed on the island can survive the pressures of the world they left.

Reviews were mixed, though often more favorable than those of the critically reviled 1980 film. On Metacritic it holds a score of 51 out of 100 based on five critics. Linda Stasi of the New York Post compared it with the original, noting its tamer approach to the story's romance.

title: Paranoia
tagline: In a war between kings even a pawn can change the game.
overview: An entry-level employee at a powerful corporation finds himself occupying a corner office, but at a dangerous price—he must spy on his boss's old mentor to secure for him a multi-billion dollar advantage.
plot:
Paranoia is a 2013 American techno-thriller directed by Robert Luketic. Barry L. Levy and Jason Hall wrote the screenplay, loosely based on Joseph Finder's 2004 novel of the same name. Liam Hemsworth stars as Adam Cassidy, with Gary Oldman as Nicholas Wyatt, Amber Heard as Emma Jennings and Harrison Ford as Jock Goddard. Lucas Till, Julian McMahon and Richard Dreyfuss co-star.

Adam is a low-level inventor at Wyatt's company. After he is fired for insubordination, he uses a company credit card to treat his friends at an expensive nightclub. Wyatt and his enforcer, Miles Meachum, then blackmail him: unless he becomes Wyatt's corporate spy, he will be prosecuted for fraud. Coached by Dr. Judith Bolton, Adam is placed inside the company of Goddard, Wyatt's former mentor and bitter rival, who stole some of Wyatt's ideas. He wins Goddard's favor and begins a relationship with Emma, Goddard's marketing director, whom he had met at the club, partly to get access to confidential files. FBI Agent Gamble warns him that three other Wyatt employees who moved to Goddard's company have turned up dead, but Adam ignores him.

The pressure grows when Wyatt threatens Adam's father, Frank, and orders him to steal Occura, Goddard's revolutionary prototype phone. Adam finds cameras in his apartment and destroys them, and Meachum retaliates by running down his friend Kevin with a car. Given 48 hours, Adam uses Emma's fingerprint, lifted from a spoon, to break into the vault, only to be caught by Goddard. Goddard reveals that he knows Adam is Wyatt's spy and plans to use him to take over Wyatt's company, and Emma realizes she has been used. With Kevin's help, Adam turns the tables. At a meeting between the two tycoons, where it emerges that Bolton has been working for Goddard, Adam secretly records both men discussing their crimes and sends the recording to the FBI. Wyatt, Goddard, Bolton and Meachum are arrested. Adam starts a small company in Brooklyn with his friends and reconciles with Emma.

Filming took place in Philadelphia in 2012, and Junkie XL wrote the score. Relativity Media released the film on August 16, 2013. It opened 13th with $3.5 million and grossed just $17.1 million worldwide against a $35 million budget, and Variety listed it among the year's biggest flops. Reviews were very negative: Rotten Tomatoes' consensus called it a clichéd, unoriginal techno-thriller with indifferent performances and few thrills.

Jobs is a biographical drama film that delves into the life of Steve Jobs, co-founder of Apple Inc. The movie explores his tumultuous relationship with his family, particularly his daughter Lisa Brennan-Jobs, and his struggles with identity, creativity, and innovation.

At its core, Jobs is a story about the tension between perfectionism and humanity. Steve Jobs' relentless pursuit of innovation and design is contrasted with his complicated personal life, marked by strained relationships with those closest to him. The film highlights the sacrifices he made for his craft and the toll it took on his family.

The movie also touches on the theme of legacy and the weight of expectation. As a visionary entrepreneur, Jobs' impact on technology and design is undeniable, but this comes at a cost. His personal relationships suffer as a result, leaving him to grapple with the consequences of his actions.

Furthermore, Jobs explores the idea of identity and how it shapes our experiences. Steve Jobs' journey is marked by moments of self-discovery, where he confronts his own demons and seeks to redefine himself. This introspection is reflected in his design philosophy, which emphasizes simplicity, elegance, and innovation.

Ultimately, Jobs is a nuanced portrayal of a complex individual, one who embodies both the creative genius and the personal struggles that often accompany it. The film invites viewers to reflect on the human side of innovation and the sacrifices we make for our passions.

title: Paddington
tagline: The adventure begins.
overview: A young Peruvian bear travels to London in search of a new home. Finding himself lost and alone at Paddington Station, he meets the kindly Brown family.
plot:
Paddington is a 2014 comedy that combines live action and animation, written and directed by Paul King from a story he developed with Hamish McColl, based on Michael Bond's beloved children's character. Produced by David Heyman, it features Ben Whishaw as the voice of the bear, with Hugh Bonneville and Sally Hawkins as Henry and Mary Brown, Julie Walters as the housekeeper Mrs Bird, Jim Broadbent as the antiques dealer Mr Gruber, Peter Capaldi as the neighbor Mr Curry and Nicole Kidman as the villainous Millicent Clyde. Michael Gambon and Imelda Staunton voice the bear's uncle and aunt.

In the jungles of Peru, a British explorer encounters a pair of rare, intelligent bears who can speak and adore marmalade. He names them Lucy and Pastuzo, leaves them his hat, and tells them they will always be welcome in London. Some forty years later, after Pastuzo is killed in an earthquake and Lucy retires to the Home for Retired Bears, their orphaned nephew stows away on a cargo ship to London. Alone at Paddington station, he is taken in by the Browns, who name him after the station. Henry is wary of the newcomer, but Mary, their children Judy and Jonathan, and Mrs Bird soon warm to him.

Hoping to find the explorer, whose name he does not know, the bear learns from Mr Gruber that the hat comes from the Geographers' Guild. Sneaking into its archive with Henry's help, he discovers that the explorer was Montgomery Clyde and that the Guild had erased the record of his expedition. Meanwhile Millicent, a taxidermist at the Natural History Museum, learns of the rare bear and, with help from Mr Curry, tries to capture him in the Browns' home. When a fire breaks out and the Browns do not believe his account, Paddington sets off alone to find Clyde, only to meet Millicent, the explorer's daughter, who resents her father for refusing to bring a bear home. She lures him to the museum and sedates him, but Mr Curry alerts the Browns, who rescue him. Millicent is sentenced to community service, and Paddington becomes a permanent member of the family.

Released in the United Kingdom on 28 November 2014, the film topped the box office there and grossed $326 million worldwide against a budget of €38.5 million. It received critical acclaim, with a 96% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, and BAFTA nominations for Best British Film and Best Adapted Screenplay. It was followed by Paddington 2 and Paddington in Peru.

title: Epic
tagline: Discover a world beyond your imagination
overview: A teenager finds herself transported to a deep forest setting where a battle between the forces of good and the forces of evil is taking place. She bands together with a rag-tag group characters in order to save their world—and ours.
plot:
Epic is a 2013 American computer-animated adventure comedy film produced by 20th Century Fox Animation. The movie follows the story of Mary, a young girl who discovers that she has the ability to communicate with nature and must use her powers to save the forest from an evil polluter.

The movie begins in a small town called Bloomville, where Mary (voiced by Amanda Seyfried) lives with her father, John (voiced by Josh Hutcherson), a park ranger. Mary's mother is deceased, and she has been raised by her father to appreciate nature and respect the environment. One day, while on a hike in the forest, Mary meets a talking tree named Mub (voiced by Colin Farrell) who tells her that she has the ability to communicate with nature.

As Mary explores her newfound powers, she discovers that an evil polluter named Ronin (voiced by Christoph Waltz) is threatening the forest and its inhabitants. Ronin is a ruthless industrialist who seeks to destroy the forest to build a new factory, which would allow him to exploit the natural resources of the area.

Mary soon learns that she has the ability to communicate with animals and plants, and that she can use her powers to defend the forest against Ronin's evil plans. With the help of Mub and other creatures in the forest, including a wise old owl named Thistle (voiced by Aziz Ansari) and a mischievous rabbit named Leila (voiced by Rachel Dratch), Mary sets out on a quest to stop Ronin and save the forest.

As the story unfolds, Mary faces numerous challenges and obstacles as she navigates the complexities of her newfound powers. She must also confront her own doubts and fears about her abilities, as well as the consequences of using them to defend the forest.

In the end, Mary uses her powers to rally the creatures of the forest and launch a final attack against Ronin's factory. With the help of her friends and allies, Mary is able to defeat Ronin and save the forest from destruction.

Throughout the movie, the animation is stunning, with beautifully rendered landscapes and characters that bring the world of nature to life. The voice cast delivers strong performances, with Colin Farrell bringing a sense of gravitas and authority to Mub's character. Amanda Seyfried shines as Mary, capturing her vulnerability and determination as she navigates her newfound powers.

Overall, Epic is a heartwarming and visually stunning film that celebrates the beauty and wonder of nature. With its engaging storyline, lovable characters, and impressive animation, it is a must-see for families and nature lovers alike.

title: The Secret Life of Walter Mitty
original_title: The Secret Life of Walter Mitty
tagline: Stop Dreaming, Start Living
overview: A timid magazine photo manager who lives life vicariously through daydreams embarks on a true-life adventure when a negative goes missing.
plot:
The Secret Life of Walter Mitty is an American adventure comedy-drama of 2013 directed and co-produced by Ben Stiller, who also plays the title role, from a screenplay by Steve Conrad. Adapted from James Thurber's 1939 short story, and closer to a remake of the 1947 film version, it co-stars Kristen Wiig as Cheryl Melhoff, Sean Penn as the photojournalist Sean O'Connell, Shirley MacLaine as Walter's mother Edna, Adam Scott as Ted Hendricks, Kathryn Hahn as his sister Odessa and Patton Oswalt as Todd Maher.

Walter manages photo negatives at Life magazine in New York and escapes his uneventful life through vivid daydreams. He is too shy to approach his co-worker Cheryl, and his online dating profile is blank where it asks about places visited and things done. When the magazine prepares its final print issue before going online, the legendary Sean O'Connell, who still shoots on film, sends Walter a roll of negatives and a wallet as a gift, saying that frame 25 captures the "quintessence" of life and should be the last cover. But negative 25 is missing, and Walter stalls the smug transition manager Hendricks. Using the other frames as clues, he sets off for Greenland, jumps from a helicopter flown by a drunken pilot into frigid, shark-infested waters to reach a ship, and follows Sean's trail to Iceland, racing across the countryside by bike and skateboard only to miss him as Eyjafjallajökull erupts.

Back home, Walter is fired and throws away Sean's wallet. Recognising his mother's piano in one of the negatives, he learns that she had met Sean and baked the clementine cake whose wrapper bore his notes, which lead Walter to the Himalayas in Afghanistan, where he finds Sean photographing a rare snow leopard. Sean reveals that he had tucked the negative inside the wallet. Detained at Los Angeles airport on his return, Walter is vouched for by Todd, the dating-site representative who has followed his adventures. His mother has rescued the wallet; Walter delivers the negative without looking at it and tells Hendricks off for his treatment of the staff. Reconciled with Cheryl, he finds the final issue on a newsstand: its cover shows Walter himself at work outside the Life building, a tribute to the magazine's staff.

After two decades of development, it premiered as the Centerpiece Gala of the New York Film Festival in October 2013 and opened in December. Reviews were mixed, with 52% on Rotten Tomatoes, critics finding it ambitious but short on substance.

title: The Wailer
tagline: The Legend of La Llorona
overview: On their way to Mexico, six students are stranded in a small town where years before a tragedy took place.
plot:
The Wailer (Spanish: La Llorona) is a 2006 American supernatural horror film directed by Andrés Navia from a screenplay by Rafy Rivera, based on a story by Rivera and Al Bravo, and produced by Skyline Films and Laguna Productions. Released direct to video, it draws on the Mexican folk legend of La Llorona, the weeping woman who murdered her own children and whose ghost is said to cry out for them.

A prologue set years earlier shows a woman drowning her two children in a small river. Her horrified husband confronts her, calling her mad, and in the ensuing struggle she weeps over what she has done and kills herself with his knife; he carries her body away and hides it, and no one knows where it was left. In the present, six American students on a road trip to Mexico become stranded in a small town where that tragedy once took place. With nowhere else to stay, they accept the only lodging available, a small cabin, where inexplicable things begin to happen at night: the sound of a woman sobbing echoes through the house, and their growing fear keeps them trapped inside.

Soon they begin to glimpse a woman with a bloodied face who picks off whoever lets their guard down. Julie and Andrew find a rosary that seems to have belonged to the dead woman and search the house, only to hear the ghost crying out for her children as they piece together the truth behind the legend. In the end La Llorona kills all of the friends except Julie, who is possessed by the spirit and murders the man who looks after the cabin before disappearing.

The cast is led by Vanessa Rice as Julie and John Patrick Jordan as Andrew, with Brenda Mejia as Ashley, Eltony Williams as Jay, Nicole Danielle as Michelle and Hugo Medina as Mike. The film was followed by a sequel, The Wailer 2 (2007), in which a professor searches Mexico for his missing daughter Julie, and by a prequel, The Wailer 3 (2012), set before the events of the first two films. Critical response from the horror blogs that reviewed it was largely negative, faulting its clichés, slow pacing, weak acting and reliance on cheap jump scares, though a few reviewers singled out the design of the ghost and some effective moments; the Fringes of Horror blog gave it its lowest rating.

title: White House Down

overview: Capitol Policeman John Cale has just been denied his dream job with the Secret Service of protecting President James Sawyer. plot:
White House Down is a 2013 American action thriller film directed by Roland Emmerich and written by James Vanderbilt. The movie stars Channing Tatum as Capitol Police Officer John Cale, a young officer who has been training to join the Secret Service, and Jamie Foxx as President James Sawyer, the newly elected President of the United States.

The movie begins with John Cale (Channing Tatum) trying to get into the White House for his daughter's birthday party. However, he is denied entry due to a security breach. Despite this, Cale manages to sneak in and meets President Sawyer (Jamie Foxx), who is struggling to connect with his 12-year-old daughter Emily.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Cale has a personal connection to the White House - his father was a Secret Service agent who died on duty when he was a child. Cale's desire to join the Secret Service is motivated by a sense of duty and loyalty to his father's memory.

Meanwhile, a group of heavily armed terrorists, led by Emil Stenz (Richard Jenkins), take over the White House and hold its occupants hostage. The terrorists are seeking revenge against President Sawyer for his role in the death of their leader, who was killed during a previous operation.

As the situation escalates, Cale finds himself trapped inside the White House with Emily, who is being held captive by the terrorists. Despite the danger, Cale uses his knowledge of the building and his training to try and rescue Emily and take down the terrorists.

President Sawyer, meanwhile, is trying to negotiate with Stenz and his team, but they are unwilling to listen. As the standoff continues, it becomes clear that Stenz has a personal vendetta against the President and will stop at nothing to carry out his plan.

In the end, Cale comes up with a plan to take down the terrorists from within the White House. He uses his knowledge of the building's ventilation system to sneak into the control room where Stenz is holding the hostages. In a tense showdown, Cale manages to defeat Stenz and his team, saving Emily and President Sawyer.

The movie ends with Cale being offered a job as a Secret Service agent, and he accepts, finally fulfilling his dream of joining the agency. The film concludes on a hopeful note, with Cale and his daughter starting a new life together, free from the trauma of their past.

Overall, White House Down is an action-packed thriller that explores themes of loyalty, duty, and redemption. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has its fans, who appreciate its over-the-top action sequences and Channing Tatum's performance as the lead character.

title: Olympus Has Fallen
tagline: When our flag falls our nation will rise.
overview: When the White House (Secret Service Code: "Olympus") is captured by a terrorist mastermind and the President is kidnapped, disgraced former Presidential guard Mike Banning finds himself trapped within the building. As the national security team scrambles to respond, they are forced to rely on Banning's inside knowledge to help retake the White House, save the President and avert an even bigger disaster.
plot:
Olympus Has Fallen is a 2013 American political action thriller directed and co-produced by Antoine Fuqua from a screenplay by Creighton Rothenberger and Katrin Benedikt, the first installment of the Has Fallen series. Gerard Butler, who also co-produced, stars as a disgraced Secret Service agent, with Aaron Eckhart as the President and Morgan Freeman as the Speaker of the House, alongside Angela Bassett, Ashley Judd, Melissa Leo, Dylan McDermott and Rick Yune.

Mike Banning, a former Army Ranger on the presidential detail, has grown close to President Benjamin Asher, First Lady Margaret and their young son, Connor. When the presidential limousine skids off an icy bridge during a winter drive, Banning pulls the President to safety but cannot save Margaret. Eighteen months later, he has been moved off the detail to a desk job at the Treasury Department.

During a visit by the South Korean prime minister, a commando unit led by the North Korean terrorist Kang Yeonsak launches a coordinated air and ground assault on Washington and seizes the White House, aided by Dave Forbes, a former Secret Service agent working in private security. Asher and members of his cabinet are taken hostage in the underground bunker, and the prime minister is executed on camera. Banning fights his way into the building and makes contact with Speaker Allan Trumbull, now acting president, and Secret Service director Lynne Jacobs at the Pentagon. Kang demands the withdrawal of American forces from the Korean peninsula, but his real goal is Cerberus, a system for destroying nuclear missiles in flight, which he plans to use to detonate America's arsenal in its silos. It can be activated only with codes held by Asher and two senior officials.

Operating alone inside the White House, Banning rescues Connor, kills Forbes and many of the attackers, and destroys the anti-aircraft weapons that annihilated a military helicopter assault. Kang executes hostages in reprisal, then fakes his own and Asher's deaths in a helicopter explosion to cover an escape. Banning sees through the ruse, kills Kang in the bunker, and with Trumbull's guidance shuts down Cerberus with seconds to spare before escorting Asher out.

Released by FilmDistrict on March 22, 2013, it grossed about $170 million worldwide against a $70 million budget. Reviews were mixed, praising the action and Butler but faulting the violence and script. It was followed by London Has Fallen (2016) and Angel Has Fallen (2019).

title: Diana
tagline: The legend is never the whole story
overview: During the last two years of her life, Princess Diana campaigns against the use of land mines and has a secret love affair with a Pakistani heart surgeon.
plot:
Diana is a 2013 British biographical drama film directed by Oliver Hirschbiegel and written by Stephen Jeffreys, adapted from Kate Snell's 2001 book Diana: Her Last Love. Naomi Watts plays Diana, Princess of Wales, with Naveen Andrews as the heart surgeon Hasnat Khan, alongside Douglas Hodge, Charles Edwards and Geraldine James. The film covers the last two years of Diana's life and centres on her secret romance with Khan. It had its world premiere in London on 5 September 2013 and opened in British cinemas later that month.

The story begins after the collapse of Diana's marriage to Charles, Prince of Wales, as she adjusts to life as a divorced royal under constant press scrutiny. Visiting a hospital, she meets Hasnat Khan, a Pakistani cardiac surgeon working in London, and the two fall in love. Their relationship is conducted largely in secret, with Diana going to considerable lengths to avoid photographers, wearing disguises and arranging discreet meetings, while the couple try to imagine a shared future away from the public eye.

Alongside the romance, the film follows Diana's humanitarian work, notably her campaign against landmines that took her to Angola, and her travels to places including Australia, Pakistan, New York, Bosnia, Italy and finally Paris, with many of her real outfits carefully recreated. Khan, a deeply private man devoted to his work, becomes increasingly uncomfortable with her fame and with the impossibility of an ordinary life alongside her, and their relationship eventually breaks down.

After the break-up, the film presents Diana's relationship with the Egyptian businessman Dodi Fayed as a calculated attempt to provoke Khan's jealousy rather than a serious love affair. The narrative builds towards the end of August 1997, when Diana, Fayed and their driver were killed in a car crash in the Pont de l'Alma tunnel in Paris, although the crash itself is not staged on screen.

Diana was poorly received by critics, who faulted its direction and screenplay and found Watts's committed performance undermined by the material. On Rotten Tomatoes only 7% of over one hundred reviews were positive, and the film was a commercial disappointment.

Guardians of the Galaxy is a 2014 American superhero film directed by James Gunn and produced by Marvel Studios. The movie follows the story of Peter Quill, a human who was abducted by aliens as a child and became a space pirate.

The aliens take Peter to their spaceship, where he grows up surrounded by their culture. However, when Peter discovers that his mother's music is playing on one of the ship's speakers, he becomes obsessed with finding her.

Years later, Peter is now a grown man who has become a space pirate, using the alias Star-Lord. He steals valuable artifacts and sells them to the highest bidder. During one of his missions, Peter encounters Gamora (Zoe Saldana), a deadly assassin working for the villainous Ronan the Accuser (Lee Pace). The two engage in a fierce battle, but eventually form an uneasy alliance.

The group also meets Drax the Destroyer (Dave Bautista), a powerful warrior who seeks revenge against Ronan for killing his family. There's also Rocket Raccoon (voiced by Bradley Cooper), a genetically engineered raccoon with enhanced abilities and a sarcastic attitude. Finally, there's Groot (voiced by Vin Diesel), a tree-like humanoid who can only say three words: "I am Groot."

The group soon discovers that Ronan is searching for the Orb, a powerful artifact that could destroy entire planets. They also learn that Gamora was once a member of Ronan's crew but has since defected.

As they journey through space, the Guardians face numerous challenges and obstacles, including battles with Ronan's minions and navigating treacherous asteroid fields. Along the way, Peter begins to form close bonds with his new allies, particularly Gamora and Drax.

The movie reaches its climax when the Guardians confront Ronan on the planet Morag. In a final showdown, Peter and his friends manage to defeat Ronan, but not before he destroys the Orb, which shatters into pieces.

In the aftermath, the Guardians come together to celebrate their victory and form an unbreakable bond. The movie ends with Peter returning home to Earth, where he is reunited with his long-lost father, Ego (Kurt Russell), who reveals that he is actually Peter's celestial being father.

The film concludes on a hopeful note, as the Guardians set out on new adventures together, ready to face whatever challenges come their way. The movie's success can be attributed to its unique blend of humor, action, and heart, which has made it a beloved classic among fans of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

However, in the present day, peace ended when a group of ninja called the Akatsuki attack Konoha under the guidance of Tobi, the mysterious masked man behind Fox's rampage years ago who intends on executing his plan to rule the world by shrouding it in illusions.
plot:
Road to Ninja: Naruto the Movie is a Japanese animated action-adventure film directed by Tensai Okamura, based on the popular manga and anime series Naruto. The movie was released in 2012 by Bandai Visual.

The story begins with Naruto Uzumaki, a young ninja from the Hidden Leaf Village, who is struggling to find his place in the world. He is constantly overshadowed by his teammates, Sakura Haruno and Sasuke Uchiha, and feels like he doesn't measure up to their expectations. One day, while on a mission with his friends, Naruto discovers that he has the ability to travel through time using the "Road to Ninja" technique.

Naruto soon finds himself transported back in time to the era of the Fourth Great Ninja War, where he meets a young version of himself who is struggling to survive. The younger Naruto is being hunted by Akatsuki members, and our protagonist must help him escape and find his way back to his own time.

As they journey through the past, Naruto and his younger self encounter various obstacles and challenges, including fierce battles with powerful enemies and encounters with other characters from the Naruto series. Along the way, Naruto learns valuable lessons about perseverance, friendship, and believing in himself.

Meanwhile, a mysterious figure known as the "White Ninja" is revealed to be manipulating events from behind the scenes. The White Ninja is a powerful ninja who seeks to destroy the village of Konoha and rule over the entire ninja world.

As the story unfolds, Naruto and his younger self face off against the White Ninja in an epic battle. With the help of his friends and allies, Naruto is able to defeat the White Ninja and restore balance to the timeline.

In the end, Naruto returns to his own time, where he is welcomed back as a hero by his friends and teammates. The movie concludes with Naruto reflecting on the lessons he learned from his journey through time and realizing that he has grown stronger and more confident as a result of his experiences.

Overall, Road to Ninja: Naruto the Movie is an action-packed adventure that explores themes of identity, friendship, and self-discovery. With its engaging storyline and memorable characters, it is a must-see for fans of the Naruto series.
