title: Berserk: The Golden Age Arc II - The Battle for Doldrey
original_title: ベルセルク 黄金時代篇II ドルドレイ攻略
tagline: This sword is proof that i have lived.
overview: The Band of the Hawk participates in the Midland war campaign. On the bloody battlefield, they conquer decisive victories that lead them to Doldrey, an old fortress that will decide the outcome of the war.
plot:
Berserk: The Golden Age Arc II - The Battle for Doldrey is a 2012 Japanese animated dark fantasy film and the second part of a trilogy adapting the Golden Age arc of Kentaro Miura's manga Berserk. Toshiyuki Kubooka directed from a screenplay by Ichirō Ōkouchi, with animation by Studio 4°C and distribution by Warner Bros. Pictures Japan. Hiroaki Iwanaga voices the mercenary swordsman Guts, Takahiro Sakurai the ambitious leader Griffith and Toa Yukinari the warrior Casca. Shirō Sagisu composed the score, and Susumu Hirasawa provided the insert song "Aria".

The story continues the war between the Kingdom of Midland and the Tudor Empire, in which Griffith's mercenary company, the Band of the Hawk, has become one of Midland's most valuable forces. After Guts and Casca are separated from the rest of the band, they are pursued by the brutal Tudor commander Adon and his soldiers. Guts holds off most of the attackers so that Casca can escape, and in the aftermath he reflects on his life and resolves that one day he will leave the Hawks, find a dream of his own and so become Griffith's equal and true friend, rather than a follower serving someone else's ambition.

The band then takes part in the assault on Doldrey, a fortress thought to be impregnable, whose capture would bring the Hundred Years' War to an end. In the battle Casca kills Adon, and the long war finally comes to an end. A month after the war ends, however, Guts announces his departure and defeats Griffith in a duel to win his freedom. Shaken by the loss, Griffith makes a reckless mistake: he is discovered sleeping with the king's daughter, Princess Charlotte. He is charged with treason and thrown into the Tower of Rebirth, while the members of the Band of the Hawk are declared outlaws, setting up the events of the final film.

The film opened in Japan on 23 June 2012 and was released on home video in North America by Viz Media in 2013. Its producer reports that it was nominated in the feature film category at the 2013 Annecy International Animated Film Festival. Critical reaction was mixed. Kotaku's Richard Eisenbeis called it a great improvement over the first film, and Otaku USA praised its balance of action and character development. Anime News Network reviewers, by contrast, criticised its computer-generated animation and its treatment of women, and felt that it reduced the rich character development of the manga to a thin shadow.

title: After
overview: When two bus crash survivors awake to discover that they are the only people left in their small town, they must form an unlikely alliance in a race to unravel the truth behind their isolation. As strange events begin to unfold, they start to question whether the town they know so well is really what it seems.
plot:
After is a 2012 fantasy horror film written and directed by Ryan Smith (also known as Ryan Whitaker). Steven Strait and Karolina Wydra star, with Sandra Lafferty as Aunt Lu and Madison Lintz and Chase Presley as the young versions of the leads. It premiered at the Nashville Film Festival on April 19, 2012.

Ana, a nurse who once wanted to write horror stories, meets Freddy, a graphic novelist, on a bus and finds that they live on the same street in the small town of Pearl. Then the bus crashes. Ana wakes at home in a strange, permanent twilight to find the town deserted. She joins Freddy, and they find that every means of communication is dead and that a towering wall of black fog, the Darkness, surrounds Pearl and is closing in. The town center keeps shifting back to August 23, 1992, when they watch themselves as children: Ana with her beloved Aunt Lu, who raised her, and Freddy with his kind stepfather Phil. A recording at the hospital reveals that Ana has been in a coma for two months, and that her living will means life support will be switched off in three days. That is exactly when the fog will reach the center of town.

Freddy suspects that the Darkness reflects Ana's dying brain. Inside it they find a locked door surrounded by thousands of keys. It is the same image Freddy once drew in his childhood comic Behind the Veil. They are pursued by a toothed monster from a play young Ana wrote, and it carries the key in its chest. Reliving the day of the 1992 carnival, they see their younger selves catch each other's eye. Ana explains that Aunt Lu was fatally injured that night. Freddy goes off to face the monster alone and is dragged away. Ana then sees the truth: Freddy's bullying friends pushed him into the vandalism that caused the fire that left Lu in a fatal coma. When the beaten Freddy returns and apologizes, Ana kills the monster, takes the key and pulls him through the door. She wakes up in hospital and finds that Freddy, already discharged, has partial amnesia. Using his sketchbook, she helps him remember.

Smith and producer Brandon Gregory spent three years on the film. It was shot in Alabama but otherwise made in Nashville. Strait joined after a friend showed him the script, which he praised as original, intelligent and heartfelt. Canadian distributor Mongrel Media acquired North American rights in 2013. Reviews were mixed to positive, with horror sites especially enthusiastic, while Exclaim! found the leads' conversations lacking nuance.

title: Interview with a Hitman
overview: An elite hitman returns to erase his past only to find that somebody has messed with his future.
plot:
Interview with a Hitman is a 2012 British action thriller written and directed by Perry Bhandal in his feature debut. Luke Goss stars as Viktor, a Romanian contract killer who agrees to tell his life story to a disgraced film director looking for a project to revive his career. Caroline Tillette plays Bethesda, Stephen Marcus the crime boss Traficant, Danny Midwinter Viktor's mentor Sergei and Elliot Greene the young Viktor.

Told in flashbacks as Viktor talks to the filmmaker, the story begins in a slum on the outskirts of Bucharest, where the boy is menaced by two neighbourhood bullies and his father is in debt to the local mafia. Viktor joins the gang to protect himself and is taken under the wing of the lieutenant Sergei. His violent father, who beats Viktor's mother, is soon killed for failing to pay. On his first job, collecting a debt, Viktor kills a man who mocks him and then his wife, and is about to shoot their two small daughters when Sergei stops him. Sergei trains him as an assassin, teaching him that the surest way to break a strong man is to kill those he loves.

Years later, a drug deal involving Franco, son of their boss Traficant, ends in a shoot-out in which they kill the dealer, who turns out to be the son of a powerful mafia boss. Ordered by Traficant to eliminate Viktor, Sergei tries and fails; Viktor leaves a body double in his place, fakes his death and starts over in London. There he works for a local crime boss, murdering an incorruptible police officer by spiking his coffee with liquid nicotine, and refuses an offer to become the boss's lieutenant. After rescuing a woman named Bethesda from an attack in a café, he falls in love with her; she becomes pregnant. He spares a journalist he was ordered to kill, kills a childhood friend sent to murder him, and returns to Bucharest to kill the old bullies and Traficant himself.

As the interview ends, Bethesda arrives and reveals that the director once abused her as a child; the interview is a trap, and Viktor shoots the man. Bethesda then shoots Viktor, revealing that he killed her parents at the start of his career, that she betrayed him to Traficant and engineered both men's downfall, and that she will one day show their son the interview so that he will despise his father.

The film was shot in 18 days in August 2011 around Newcastle upon Tyne and Bucharest. It opened in British and Irish cinemas on 20 July 2012 and holds a 44% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Smiley
tagline: Evil Wears a Smile
overview: After learning of an urban legend in which a demented serial killer named SMILEY can be summoned through the internet, mentally fragile Ashley must decide whether she is losing her mind or becoming Smiley's next victim.
plot:
Smiley is a 2012 American slasher film directed by Michael Gallagher, who co-wrote the screenplay with Glasgow Phillips. It stars Caitlin Gerard, Melanie Papalia, Shane Dawson, Andrew James Allen, Liza Weil, Roger Bart and Keith David, and builds its story around an internet urban legend. The film was released on October 12, 2012.

According to an online myth, if someone types "I did it for the lulz" three times into an anonymous video chat site, a killer known as Smiley, whose eyes are stitched shut and whose mouth is carved into a grin, will appear and murder the stranger on the other side of the screen. College student Ashley moves in with her roommate Proxy and is introduced to a circle of friends that includes Zane, Mark, Crash, Kells and Binder. One night Ashley and Proxy decide to test the legend with a random chat partner and watch, horrified, as the man is killed. Proxy persuades Ashley to keep quiet, but Ashley is consumed by guilt and grows convinced that Smiley is now stalking her. Her friends and a psychiatrist dismiss her fear as anxiety, hallucinations and nightmares, and the police refuse to take her seriously. When Zane is found shot dead, a desperate Ashley picks up his gun and tries to summon the killer in order to confront him, with disastrous results, and ends up throwing herself out of the building to an apparent death. The film then reveals that Proxy, Binder and others among Ashley's acquaintances belong to a group of internet pranksters who invented the Smiley legend as an elaborate hoax and used Ashley as its victim. Their satisfaction does not last, however, as the myth they created appears to have taken on a life of its own, and in a closing twist Smiley turns up for real while Proxy is chatting online.

Smiley was released to largely negative reviews. It holds a 17% rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on 24 reviews, and several critics described it as a rip-off of Scream and Candyman. Common criticisms focused on the dull, generic storytelling, the acting and the lack of originality, and the film was also reviewed negatively by The A.V. Club and The New York Times. The cast also includes Toby Turner as Mark and Liza Weil as Ashley's psychiatrist, Dr. Jenkins.

title: Parker

overview: A thief with a unique code of professional ethics is double-crossed by his crew and left for dead. Assuming a new disguise and forming an unlikely alliance with a woman on the inside, he looks to hijack the score of the crew's latest heist.
plot:
Parker is a 2013 American action thriller directed by Taylor Hackford and written by John J. McLaughlin, adapted from Flashfire, the 19th novel in Donald E. Westlake's series about the professional thief Parker, written under the pen name Richard Stark. Jason Statham stars in the title role and Jennifer Lopez as a Palm Beach real estate agent, with Michael Chiklis, Wendell Pierce, Clifton Collins Jr., Emma Booth and Nick Nolte.

Parker is a career criminal who lives by a strict code: he steals only from those who can afford it and harms no one who does not deserve it. At the request of his mentor, Hurley, he leads a robbery of the Ohio State Fair with a crew he does not know, led by Melander. The heist succeeds, but one member's carelessness causes a fire that kills a bystander. When Parker refuses to roll his share into the crew's next, bigger job, they shoot him and leave him for dead by the roadside. Rescued by a farming family and taken to hospital, he escapes and sets out for revenge, while protecting his girlfriend Claire, Hurley's daughter, from a hitman sent by a Chicago mob boss connected to the gang.

Tracking the crew to Palm Beach, Florida, Parker poses as a wealthy Texan named Daniel Parmitt looking for a luxury home. The real estate agent Leslie Rodgers, a recently divorced woman struggling financially and living with her mother, shows him around and soon discovers that his identity is false. Seeing a way out of her troubles, she offers to help him in exchange for a share of the loot. The gang is planning to steal millions in jewels from a high-society auction. After a brutal fight with the hitman in his hotel, Parker, badly wounded, seeks shelter with Leslie, who deflects the police.

As the crew carries out the jewel heist, disguising themselves as firefighters, Parker waits at their hideout, having sabotaged their weapons in advance. When Leslie unexpectedly arrives and is taken hostage, the two fight their way out, killing the entire crew. Parker entrusts the jewels to Leslie, later eliminates the mob boss in Chicago, and eventually sends Leslie her share and rewards the family who saved his life.

Parker grossed about $46 million worldwide. Reviews were mixed: Rotten Tomatoes reported 42% approval, its consensus calling it generic and convoluted, though critics found Statham well suited to the role and enjoyed Lopez's comic touches.

overview: A group of scientists in San Francisco struggle to stay alive in the aftermath of a plague that is wiping out humanity, while Caesar tries to maintain dominance over his community of intelligent apes.
plot:
Dawn of the Planet of the Apes is a 2014 American science fiction action film directed by Matt Reeves, and produced by Peter Chernin, Dylan Clark, and Tim Burton. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2001 film Planet of the Apes and is set in an alternate timeline.

The story begins with Caesar (Andy Serkis), the intelligent and empathetic leader of the apes, living in a hidden sanctuary in the San Francisco Bay Area. After a devastating virus wipes out most of humanity, Caesar's group has been working to rebuild their community and find a way to coexist with humans.

Meanwhile, a human survivor named Malcolm (Jason Clarke) is struggling to cope with the loss of his family and the trauma he experienced during the outbreak. He joins a group of survivors led by Dreyfuss (Karl Urban), who are on a mission to find a cure for the virus.

As tensions rise between humans and apes, Caesar's group discovers that a human settlement is being established nearby. The apes decide to send an envoy to meet with the humans, hoping to establish communication and prevent further conflict.

Caesar sends his trusted advisor, Maurice (Frank Dillane), along with a small group of apes to negotiate with the humans. However, things quickly go awry when the human settlement is attacked by a group of rogue apes who are infected with the virus.

Malcolm, who has been struggling with PTSD, becomes embroiled in the conflict and forms an unlikely bond with Caesar's group. As the situation escalates, Malcolm and Caesar must work together to prevent all-out war between humans and apes.

Throughout the film, Reeves explores themes of empathy, compassion, and coexistence. The movie delves into the complexities of human nature and the consequences of playing with fire when it comes to advanced technology.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the virus is not just a simple disease, but a complex tool created by humans to control and manipulate apes. Caesar's group discovers that the virus was designed to make apes more aggressive and submissive, and that it has been used to create an army of super-soldiers.

In the climactic final act, Malcolm and Caesar lead a joint human-ape force against the rogue apes and their human creators. The battle is intense and emotional, with both sides suffering heavy losses.

Ultimately, the film ends on a hopeful note, with Caesar's group emerging victorious but scarred. Malcolm has found a new sense of purpose and belonging among the apes, while Caesar has come to realize that his people are not just victims of circumstance, but also capable of great kindness and compassion.

The movie concludes with a poignant moment between Caesar and Malcolm, as they share a moment of understanding and connection. The camera pans out to reveal the ruins of San Francisco, a symbol of the devastation and destruction caused by human conflict.

Overall, Dawn of the Planet of the Apes is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that explores complex themes and characters. With its stunning visuals, gripping storyline, and outstanding performances from Andy Serkis and Jason Clarke, it's a must-see for fans of science fiction and action movies.

title: The Monkey King
tagline: Havoc in Heaven
overview: Sun Wukong is a monkey born from a heavenly stone who acquires supernatural powers. plot:
The Monkey King, also known as The Monkey King: Havoc in Heaven's Palace, is a 2014 Hong Kong and Chinese action fantasy film directed by Soi Cheang and starring Donnie Yen as Sun Wukong, the legendary Monkey King, with Yen also serving as action director. Chow Yun-fat co-stars as the Jade Emperor and Aaron Kwok as the Bull Demon King, with Joe Chen and Peter Ho. The story is based on an episode from Journey to the West, Wu Cheng'en's sixteenth-century Chinese literary classic, and the film was shot in 3D.

After the Bull Demon King leads a failed attack on Heaven, the Jade Emperor spares his life at the request of his sister, Princess Iron Fan, the Demon King's lover, and banishes the demons to Flaming Mountain. To rebuild Heaven, the goddess Nüwa sacrifices herself, and one of the crystals of her body falls to earth on Mount Huaguo, where over time it gives birth to a monkey. The creature is taken in by the sage Subhuti, who names him Sun Wukong and trains him in magical arts.

The Bull Demon King, still plotting revenge, schemes to use the brash, mischievous Wukong as a weapon against Heaven and secretly allies with Erlang Shen, the Jade Emperor's resentful nephew. Wukong acquires a magical staff from the palace of the Dragon King, causing chaos, and the Demon King flatters him with promises of Heaven's treasures and immortality. Wukong befriends a nine-tailed fox spirit and travels to Heaven, where he is given a lowly post caring for the celestial stables. Manipulated by the demons, he rebels and wreaks havoc in Heaven, unaware that his actions are part of a plan to destroy it.

The film relies heavily on computer-generated effects and spectacle, retelling the classic story of the Monkey King's rebellion against the gods.

After several delays, The Monkey King was released in Hong Kong and China at the end of January 2014 and set a record for the highest-grossing opening day in China. Reviews were mixed: Variety called it energetic but lacking style and substance, while ScreenAnarchy criticized its effects and script but praised Yen. A sequel, The Monkey King 2, followed in 2016.

The Grand Budapest Hotel is a 2014 American comedy-drama film written and directed by Wes Anderson. The film stars Ralph Fiennes, Tony Revolori, F. Murray Abraham, Willem Dafoe, Jude Law, Tilda Swinton, Adrien Brody, Edward Norton, Jeff Goldblum, and Saoirse Ronan.

The story begins in 1932, with Gustave H (Ralph Fiennes), a charming and flamboyant concierge at the famous Grand Budapest Hotel in the fictional Republic of Zubrowka. Gustave is known for his exceptional hospitality skills and his ability to make guests feel like royalty. He befriends Zero Moustafa (Tony Revolori), a young lobby boy who becomes his most trusted assistant.

The plot takes a dramatic turn when one of Gustave's wealthy elderly clients, Madame Celine (Tilda Swinton), dies under mysterious circumstances. Gustave is accused of murdering her and flees the country with a priceless painting, "Boy with Apple," which he had been entrusted to guard. Zero follows him on his journey, determined to clear his friend's name.

As they travel through Europe, they encounter a series of misadventures, including a run-in with the villainous Dmitri (Adrien Brody), who is also after the painting. Along the way, Gustave and Zero form an unlikely bond, with Zero learning valuable lessons about loyalty, friendship, and the importance of following one's heart.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Gustave and Zero are arrested by the authorities in the Republic of Zubrowka. They escape and continue their journey, eventually finding themselves in the midst of a war between the Republic of Zubrowka and its neighboring country, the Empire of Austria-Hungary.

As the war escalates, Gustave and Zero find themselves on the run once again, this time with the help of a group of rebels. They embark on a perilous journey to clear Gustave's name and recover the stolen painting.

The film's climax features an action-packed sequence in which Gustave and Zero infiltrate the Empire's headquarters, where they engage in a series of clever disguises and narrow escapes. In the end, Gustave is able to clear his name and recover the painting, but not before facing a series of challenges that test his courage and wit.

The film concludes with an elderly Zero visiting Gustave in his final days, where he recounts their adventures and shares stories about their friendship. The film ends on a poignant note, as Zero reflects on the lessons he learned from Gustave and the importance of holding onto memories and experiences.

Throughout the film, Wes Anderson's signature visual style and attention to detail are on full display, with intricate production design, vibrant colors, and a memorable soundtrack that adds to the film's whimsical charm. title: Dragon Ball: Episode of Bardock
original_title: ドラゴンボール エピソード オブ バーダック
overview: A spin-off scenario taking place after the events of the TV special Dragon Ball Z: Bardock - The Father of Goku, in which Bardock survives the destruction of Planet Vegeta and is sent into the past, combating Frieza's ancestor Chilled and turning into a Super Saiyan.
plot:
Dragon Ball: Episode of Bardock is a 1990 anime film produced by Toei Animation, not 2011. It was released on July 7, 1990.

The movie takes place during the Saiyan Saga of the Dragon Ball series and serves as a prequel to the original Dragon Ball Z series. The story revolves around Bardock, the father of Goku, who is a powerful Saiyan warrior.

The film begins with Bardock's life on Planet Vegeta, where he lives alongside his wife, Gine, and their son, Kakarot (Goku). However, Bardock is not happy with his life on Vegeta due to its strict rules and the constant threat of war. He longs for a more peaceful existence.

One day, Bardock discovers that Planet Vegeta is facing an impending attack by Frieza, a powerful and ruthless Saiyan warrior who seeks to conquer and destroy all other planets in the universe. The Saiyans are ordered to prepare for battle, but Bardock refuses to fight, citing his desire for peace and his love for his family.

As the war between Vegeta and Frieza begins, Bardock's actions become increasingly reckless, causing tension among the Saiyan warriors. In a final confrontation with Frieza, Bardock is killed by the villainous warrior.

The film then jumps forward in time to show Goku as a young boy on Earth, where he meets his future wife, Chi-Chi, and begins his training under Master Roshi. The movie ends with Goku's determination to become strong enough to surpass his father's legacy and protect those he cares about.

Throughout the film, Bardock's character is explored in depth, revealing his complexities and motivations. His desire for peace and family ultimately lead to his downfall, but also serve as a catalyst for Goku's growth and development as a warrior.

Overall, Dragon Ball: Episode of Bardock provides valuable insight into the backstory of the Dragon Ball Z series and offers a unique perspective on the character of Bardock.

title: Deranged
tagline: There Must Be Something In The Water.
overview: Jae-hyuk is a pharmaceutical worker for a medical supplies company. When a series of dead bodies are found floating in the Han River. The public is shocked to discovered that the deaths are related to a fatal outbreak of virus-infected mutant parasitic horsehair worms, called 'Yeongasi', that can control the human brain. Those infected shows symptoms of hunger and thirst, hence jumps into the river to combat dehydration. Whilst the authorities work to find a cure, Jae-hyuk struggles to save his family when they also exhibits similar symptoms.
plot:
Deranged (Korean: Yeongasi) is a 2012 South Korean medical disaster thriller directed by Park Jung-woo and produced by Lim Ji-young and Oz One Film. Kim Myung-min stars alongside Moon Jeong-hee, Kim Dong-wan and Lee Ha-nee. Distributed by CJ E&M, the film was released on July 5, 2012, with a running time of 109 minutes.

The protagonist, Jae-hyuk, holds a doctorate in biochemistry and was once a university professor, but after losing his savings and his position because of a disastrous stock investment made on the advice of his younger brother, he now scrapes by as a pharmaceutical sales representative. When bodies begin turning up floating in the Han River, the public is horrified to learn that the deaths are caused by an outbreak of mutated parasitic horsehair worms, known as Yeongasi, which can manipulate the behavior of their human hosts. The infected show an insatiable appetite without gaining weight and, once the worms mature and are ready to reproduce, an overwhelming thirst that drives them into rivers and lakes so the parasites can leave the body.

As similar corpses, all showing signs of severe malnutrition, appear each morning in waterways across Seoul and the rest of the country, the government scrambles to contain the epidemic and locate a cure. Jae-hyuk's own wife and children begin to display the telltale symptoms, and he races against time to save them. He is helped by his brother Jae-pil, a police detective still tormented by guilt over squandering Jae-hyuk's money, and the two are drawn into an investigation that suggests the outbreak may not be entirely natural and that corporate interests could profit from the crisis.

Deranged proved a significant commercial success in South Korea. On its opening day it sold nearly 191,000 tickets and topped the daily box office, outselling the Hollywood release The Amazing Spider-Man. Within five weeks of release it had drawn more than 4.5 million admissions and earned roughly 32 billion won, making it one of the most successful domestic films of the summer. Reviewers noted its combination of disaster-film spectacle with a family-centered emotional story and social commentary on the pharmaceutical industry and official responses to public health emergencies.

title: Tad, the Lost Explorer
tagline: No whip, no gun... All fun!
overview: Tad is a celebrity archaeologist and adventurer just like his hero Max Mordon... in his dreams! In reality, Tad is a Chicago construction worker. One day, however, he is mistaken for a real professor and takes his place on a flight to Peru in search of the lost city of Paititi.
plot:
Tad, the Lost Explorer (Spanish: Las aventuras de Tadeo Jones) is a 2012 Spanish animated adventure comedy film directed by Enrique Gato. A spinoff of Gato's 2004 short film Tadeo Jones and its sequel, it was mainly adapted from the Spanish graphic novel Tadeo and the Secret of the Toactlum, with a screenplay by Javier Barreira, Gorka Magallón, Ignacio del Moral, Jordi Gasull and Neil Landau. The Spanish voice cast includes Óscar Barberán, Michelle Jenner, José Mota, Pep Anton Muñoz and Miguel Ángel Jenner.

Tadeo Jones is a Chicago bricklayer working on the city's subway who has dreamed since the age of five of becoming an archaeologist. Fired for daydreaming, and after his dog urinates on the foreman, he visits his friend Professor Humbert to ask about an old Coca-Cola bottle found at the site. Humbert has just been summoned to Peru by his colleague Professor Lavrof to bring his half of a stone key that will unlock Paititi, the legendary lost city of the Incas, but after taking the wrong pills at the airport he ends up in hospital. Tad takes his place and flies to Cusco with his dog Jeff, unaware that the sinister company Odysseus Inc. is watching. There he meets Freddy, a local hustler, and when Odysseus thugs kidnap him and demand the key, he is rescued by Freddy and by Lavrof's daughter Sara, with whom Tad falls in love. The joined key leads them to Machu Picchu, where they learn that Lavrof has been taken by Odysseus and its leader Kopponen. After a string of adventures they find Lavrof together with Max Mordon, a famous archaeologist whom Tad idolizes and who is Sara's fiancé. Holding the real map, the group heads into the jungle and finds an underground temple, but Max is revealed to be working with Odysseus. Kopponen and his henchmen are wiped out by a booby-trapped chamber, and Max, believing the Incan gold will grant him eternal life, smashes its protective glass only to be turned into one of the undead mummies forever and locked in Paititi's darkest dungeon. The chief mummy lets Tad, Sara and the professor go on condition that they keep the city's secrets.

The film premiered at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival on 5 June 2012 and was released in Spain by Paramount Pictures on 31 August 2012. Spanish critics were positive, though it was less well received in North America. It earned about €45 million on an €8 million budget and won three Goya Awards, including Best Animated Film.

title: Quartet
tagline: Four Friends Looking For A Little Harmony
overview: The directorial debut of Dustin Hoffman, Quartet is a high-drama comedy about temperamental divas and old grudges, passion and pride, romance and Rigoletto. At a home for retired musicians, the annual concert to celebrate Verdi's birthday is disrupted by the arrival of Jean, an eternal diva and former wife of one of the residents. Expect poignancy and plenty of laughs.
plot:
Quartet is a 2012 British comedy-drama film directed by Dustin Hoffman, in his directorial debut, and based on Ronald Harwood's play, which ran in London's West End from 1999 to 2000. Harwood adapted his own play, which he wrote after seeing the documentary Tosca's Kiss about Verdi's home for retired opera singers in Milan. The cast is led by Maggie Smith, Tom Courtenay, Billy Connolly, Pauline Collins and Michael Gambon, and many of the supporting players are genuine retired professional musicians.

At Beecham House, a retirement home for former professional musicians, the residents include the retired opera singers Reg, Wilf and Cissy, who often worked together, the former director Cedric Livingstone and the diva Anne Langley. Although all suffer the ailments of old age, they remain engaged in music. The home faces closure for lack of money, and its hopes rest on the annual gala concert on Verdi's birthday, but Cedric is desperate because several prominent performers have died or declined to take part. Reg, Wilf and Cissy sang on a celebrated recording of Rigoletto, regarded by opera lovers as the definitive post-war version with its famous quartet. Reg is shocked when the recording's missing soprano, his former wife Jean Horton, moves into the home without his being consulted, since their marriage ended bitterly. In time, Reg accepts that her infidelity is in the past. Cedric's plan is to reunite the quartet for the gala and sell enough tickets to save the home. Reg agrees, but Jean, who vowed never to sing again after retiring, storms out of a dinner when they raise the idea. When Cissy brings her flowers the next morning, Jean strikes her with them, worsening Cissy's fragile mental state, and later, full of remorse, she apologizes and agrees to sing once she learns that the quartet would close the evening in place of Anne Langley's "Vissi d'arte". Moments before they go on, a confused Cissy tries to leave to return to her family, but Jean calms her, confessing that she still loves Reg, who overhears. As the singers walk onstage to applause, Reg renews his proposal, Jean accepts and takes his hand, and the quartet begins to sing.

Filmed at Hedsor House in Buckinghamshire, Quartet premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2012 and opened in Britain on 1 January 2013. Reviews were generally positive, with an 80% Rotten Tomatoes rating and praise for Hoffman's affectionate direction and the cast's charm.

title: Assassin's Creed
tagline: Your destiny is in your blood.
overview: Through unlocked genetic memories that allow him to relive the adventures of his ancestor in 15th century Spain, Callum Lynch discovers he's a descendant of the secret 'Assassins' society. After gaining incredible knowledge and skills, he is now poised to take on the oppressive Knights Templar in the present day.
plot:
Assassin's Creed is a 2016 science fiction action film directed by Justin Kurzel, based on Ubisoft's video game series. It stars Michael Fassbender in a dual role as Callum Lynch and his ancestor Aguilar de Nerha, with Marion Cotillard as the scientist Sofia Rikkin, Jeremy Irons as her father Alan Rikkin, Brendan Gleeson as Cal's father Joseph, Charlotte Rampling and Michael K. Williams. Set in the same universe as the games, it tells an original story that moves between modern times and 15th-century Spain.

In 1492 Andalusia, during the Granada War, Aguilar is inducted into the Assassin Brotherhood and charged with protecting Prince Ahmed of Granada from the Templar Order. In 1986, the young Cal finds his mother murdered by his father, an Assassin, and flees as Templar gunmen arrive. Thirty years later, Cal is sentenced to death for murder, but Abstergo Industries, the modern front of the Templars, fakes his execution and brings him to its research facility in Madrid.

The Templars are searching for the Apple of Eden, an ancient artifact that holds the genetic code for free will, which they believe can be used to eliminate violence by controlling humanity. Because Cal descends from Aguilar, the last known keeper of the Apple, Sofia places him in the Animus, a machine that lets him relive his ancestor's genetic memories. In the past, Aguilar and his partner María fight to rescue Ahmed from the Templar Grand Master Tomas de Torquemada, who wants the Apple. In the present, Cal begins to experience hallucinations and to absorb Aguilar's skills, meets other Assassin descendants held at the facility and confronts the truth about his mother's death. Torn between the Templars' promises and his heritage, Cal must decide where his loyalty lies as Abstergo closes in on the Apple.

The film translates the games' central ideas, such as the Animus, the Leap of Faith and the conflict between Assassins and Templars, into large-scale action sequences.

Released in December 2016, Assassin's Creed grossed 240.9 million dollars worldwide against a 125 million dollar budget, reportedly losing money for New Regency. It received negative reviews, with 19 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it a joylessly overplotted slog, and a Metacritic score of 36.

title: In the House
tagline: There's always a way in
overview: A sixteen-year-old boy insinuates himself into the house of a fellow student from his literature class and writes about it in essays for his French teacher. Faced with this gifted and unusual pupil, the teacher rediscovers his enthusiasm for his work, but the boy’s intrusion will unleash a series of uncontrollable events.
plot:
In the House, released in France as Dans la maison, is a 2012 French comedy-drama written and directed by François Ozon, loosely adapted from Spanish playwright Juan Mayorga's play The Boy in the Last Row. Fabrice Luchini stars as literature teacher Germain Germain and Ernst Umhauer as his student Claude Garcia, with Kristin Scott Thomas as Germain's wife, Jeanne, Emmanuelle Seigner and Denis Ménochet as Esther and Raphaël Artole, and Bastien Ughetto as their son, Rapha.

Germain, a disillusioned teacher at the Lycée Gustave Flaubert, despairs of his pupils' writing until the new school year brings an essay from 16-year-old Claude describing a visit to the home of his classmate Rapha. Struck by the boy's sharp, voyeuristic eye, Germain reads it to Jeanne, who runs an art gallery, and begins tutoring Claude privately to help him develop the story. The film unfolds chapter by chapter, alternating between Claude's narrative and real life until the two become hard to tell apart.

Claude gains entry to the Artoles' house by helping Rapha with mathematics, and the visits stretch ever later into the evenings. Raised by a disabled father and never having known a real family, he is fascinated by the household and especially drawn to Esther. Germain, increasingly caught up in the story and its uncomfortable echoes of his own life, goes so far as to steal a colleague's math test so that Rapha will pass and Claude can keep visiting. As the narrative grows more transgressive, it becomes unclear how much is happening and how much Claude is inventing. He seduces Esther, wounding Rapha, who sees him as his best friend and has fallen in love with him; a draft in which Rapha hangs himself is later revised. Barred from the Artoles' home, Claude seduces Jeanne to find an ending for his story. Germain, suspended over the stolen test, confronts his wife, and she leaves him. In the final scene, teacher and student sit together on a bench, inventing stories about the people they can see in the windows of the building opposite.

In the House screened at the Toronto International Film Festival, where it won the FIPRESCI Prize, and went on to win the Golden Shell and the jury prize for best screenplay at San Sebastián. It received six César nominations, including Best Film, grossed about $18.2 million worldwide, and earned 88% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 72.

title: Frances Ha
tagline: I'm not messy, I'm busy.
overview: An aspiring dancer moves to New York City and becomes caught up in a whirlwind of flighty fair-weather friends, diminishing fortunes and career setbacks.
plot:
Frances Ha is a 2012 American comedy-drama film directed by Noah Baumbach and written by Baumbach and Greta Gerwig, who also stars as Frances, a struggling 27-year-old dancer whose career and social life fall apart just as her best friend's life takes off. Mickey Sumner, Adam Driver, Michael Zegen and Michael Esper co-star. Shot in black and white, the film premiered at the Telluride Film Festival on September 1, 2012, and was released in the United States by IFC Films on May 17, 2013.

After graduating from Vassar College, best friends Frances and Sophie moved to Brooklyn with dreams of creative success. Frances is an apprentice with a dance company, waiting for a place in the permanent troupe, while Sophie works in publishing. At 27, Frances is still scraping by when she breaks up with her boyfriend, and soon afterwards Sophie announces that she is moving to a nicer apartment in Tribeca with another friend. Hurt, Frances rents a room in Chinatown with Lev and Benji, two affluent young men whose parents help with their rent. As Sophie grows closer to her boyfriend Patch, a well-paid Goldman Sachs employee, the two friends drift apart. Frances's boss, Colleen, begins easing her out of the company and denies her a Christmas show she needs to pay her rent, so Frances moves out, spends the holidays with her family in Sacramento, and then bounces from one temporary arrangement to another. When she learns that Sophie is leaving to follow Patch to Tokyo without having told her, Frances impulsively flies to Paris for a poorly planned weekend that brings her little comfort. Too proud to accept Colleen's offer of an office job, she returns to Vassar to work as a waitress and summer resident assistant, where an unexpected encounter with Sophie forces both women to confront what their friendship means. Gradually Frances learns to let go of the life she imagined and begins to find her own path, choreography included.

Frances Ha was widely acclaimed. It holds a 92% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with a consensus that Baumbach's sensitive direction and Gerwig's endearing performance make its narrative drift easy to forgive, and Metacritic gave it a score of 82 out of 100, indicating "universal acclaim".

title: Spring Breakers
tagline: A little sun can bring out your dark side.
overview: After four college girls rob a restaurant to fund their spring break in Florida, they get entangled with a weird dude with his own criminal agenda.
plot:
Spring Breakers is a 2012 American crime drama film written and directed by Harmony Korine, not 2013. The movie was released on April 6, 2012.

The film follows the story of four college girls - Faith (Selena Gomez), Candy (Vanessa Hudgens), Brit (Ashley Benson), and Cotty (Rachel Korine) - who are struggling to find their place in the world. They are all from different walks of life but share a common desire for excitement, freedom, and escape.

The story begins with the girls attending a spring break party on a yacht, where they meet a charismatic and mysterious young man named Alien (James Franco). He is part of a group of friends who are also at the party, including his friend, Church (Christopher Brown), and his girlfriend, Faith's sister, Candy's boyfriend, and Cotty's ex-boyfriend.

Alien and his friends convince the girls to join them on a wild adventure in Florida, where they plan to rob a convenience store. The girls agree, and they embark on a journey of self-discovery, partying, and crime. Along the way, they encounter various characters who influence their lives, including Alien's friend Church, who becomes increasingly unstable.

As the story unfolds, the girls become more and more entangled in Alien's world, which is marked by violence, debauchery, and a sense of freedom that they can't find elsewhere. However, as the adventure progresses, it becomes clear that Alien's world is not as idyllic as it seems.

The plot takes a dark turn when the girls are arrested for their involvement in the convenience store robbery. In an attempt to secure their release, Alien and his friends plan another heist, which ends in tragedy. The film's climax features a violent confrontation between the characters, leading to a shocking conclusion that leaves the audience stunned.

Throughout the film, Korine explores themes of youth culture, rebellion, and the search for identity. He also critiques societal norms and expectations placed on women, particularly those who are seen as "wild" or "unconventional." The film's visuals are striking, with vibrant colors and a pulsating soundtrack that captures the energy and excitement of the characters' adventures.

Overall, Spring Breakers is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that challenges its audience to confront the darker aspects of human nature.

title: The Philadelphia Experiment
tagline: Past and present collide
overview: A secret government research project tries reviving the World War II "Philadelphia Experiment," which was an attempt to create a cloaking device to render warships invisible. When the experiment succeeds, it brings back the original ship (the Eldridge) that disappeared during the first test in 1943 - which brings death and destruction to the 21st century. It's up to the sole survivor of the first experiment and his granddaughter to stop it.
plot:
The Philadelphia Experiment is a science fiction television film of 2012 directed by Paul Ziller and based on the Philadelphia Experiment urban legend. A remake of the 1984 film of the same name, it again features Michael Paré, who starred in the original, this time as the ruthless agent Hagan. Nicholas Lea plays the sailor Bill Gardner, with Emilie Ullerup as his granddaughter Molly, Ryan Robbins as the scientist Richard Falkner, Gina Holden as Kathryn Moore, John Reardon as deputy Carl Reed and Malcolm McDowell as Morton Salinger.

In 2012, Falkner and his team recreate the Philadelphia Experiment for the defence contractor that employs them, testing it on their boss Kathryn's car, which vanishes and never returns. At the same moment the USS Eldridge, which vanished in the original 1943 experiment, materialises on a rural Pennsylvania airstrip. Bill, its only survivor, flees the ship, while deputy Carl Reed wanders aboard. Learning from a newspaper that he is in 2012, Bill suffers a painful seizure that releases an electromagnetic pulse each time the ship vanishes. At his old home he finds his granddaughter Molly, who believes him and digs into the experiment's history. They fight off Hagan, sent by Kathryn, as the Eldridge reappears embedded atop a Chicago skyscraper, with Carl trapped inside, his arm fused to a wall.

A mysterious caller leads them to Salinger, who oversaw the 1943 test and faked his death after refusing to work for Kathryn's company. Hagan's men fatally wound him and then execute him. As the ship lands in the Sahara and repels Kathryn's fighter jets, Falkner realises that his generators have linked with those of 1943, and that unless the jumps stop, time will collapse and the planet will be destroyed. Hagan massacres Salinger's researchers, but a disillusioned Falkner rescues Bill and Molly. The only solution is for Bill to shut down the ship's generators and return with it to 1943. Summoned to the lab, the Eldridge is boarded by Bill, who frees Carl. Kathryn shoots Falkner, and Bill kills Hagan by fusing his head into a generator before the vortex carries the ship back in time, while Molly kills Kathryn and escapes with Carl. Later Molly marries Carl, and an elderly Bill, having lived his life in full, lives with her.

Reviews were poor: DVD Talk rated it two stars out of five, citing bad effects, goofy acting and huge gaps in logic, while PopMatters found it fun in the way bad films sometimes are.

title: Detective Conan: The Eleventh Striker

overview: Kogoro's detective agency receives a mysterious phone call. plot:

title: About Time
tagline: What if every moment in life came with a second chance?
overview: The night after another unsatisfactory New Year's party, Tim's father tells his son that the men in his family have always had the ability to travel through time. plot:
About Time is a 2013 British romantic comedy-drama film directed by Richard Curtis, produced by Working Title Films, and distributed by Universal Pictures.

The story revolves around Tim Lake (played by Domhnall Gleeson), a young man who discovers that he can travel back in time to any moment in his life. This unique ability is passed down through the men in his family, known as the "time-traveling" tradition.

Tim's father, Henry (played by Bill Nighy), explains the rules of this gift to Tim on his 21st birthday. He tells him that he can travel back in time and relive any moment from his past, but only within a specific timeframe - three months before the event occurred. This allows Tim to correct mistakes, change outcomes, or simply experience moments again.

Initially, Tim uses his power to improve his life, such as winning arguments with his friends and impressing women. However, he soon realizes that altering events can have unintended consequences on those around him. He struggles to balance his desire for control with the unpredictability of time travel.

As Tim navigates his relationships and career, he meets Mary (played by Rachel McAdams), a charming and free-spirited woman who becomes his love interest. Despite their instant connection, Tim is hesitant to commit due to his fear of disrupting the timeline.

Throughout the film, Tim's father provides guidance and support, while also sharing stories about his own experiences with time travel. Henry's wisdom helps Tim understand the complexities of his power and the importance of living in the present.

As Tim and Mary grow closer, they face challenges that test their relationship. They must confront the consequences of Tim's actions, including a pivotal moment where he alters an event that affects Mary's life. This realization forces Tim to reevaluate his priorities and make difficult choices about how to use his power.

Ultimately, Tim decides to give up his time-traveling ability, choosing to live in the present with Mary instead of constantly altering the past. The film concludes with a heartwarming moment where Tim and Mary share a tender kiss, symbolizing their commitment to each other and their decision to build a life together.

About Time is a poignant exploration of love, family, and the complexities of time travel. With its witty dialogue, charming performances, and nuanced storytelling, the film has become a beloved classic among romantic comedy fans.

plot:

Lily Collins stars as Clary Fray, a New York teenager who discovers her hidden heritage, with Jamie Campbell Bower playing Jace, Robert Sheehan as Simon, Kevin Zegers in the role of Alec, Lena Headey as Clary's mother Jocelyn, Aidan Turner as Luke, Jared Harris as Hodge and Jonathan Rhys Meyers as Valentine.

Clary keeps seeing and sketching a mysterious symbol, worrying her mother and their friend Luke. At a nightclub with her best friend Simon, she alone sees a young man, Jace, and his companions kill someone. When two men break into the family apartment hunting for a cup, Jocelyn warns Clary by phone to stay away and to tell Luke about someone called Valentine, then drinks a potion that plunges her into deep sleep. Clary returns to find her mother gone and is attacked by a demon, which Jace destroys. He is a Shadowhunter, one of a secret order of half-angel demon hunters, and Clary has inherited her mother's Shadowhunter gifts. The intruders are after the Mortal Cup, a sacred artifact that can create new Shadowhunters, sought by the renegade Valentine Morgenstern.

At the hidden Institute, Clary meets Alec, Isabelle and their mentor Hodge, and in the City of Bones beneath a cemetery the Silent Brothers trace her blocked memories to the warlock Magnus Bane, who erased her knowledge of this world at Jocelyn's request. After rescuing Simon from vampires with the help of werewolves, Clary falls for Jace. Realising the Cup is hidden in a tarot card her mother painted for their neighbour Dorothea, Clary retrieves it, but Hodge betrays them and summons Valentine, who reveals that he is Clary's father. Escaping through a portal, she learns from Luke, himself a werewolf, that this is true. In the final battle at the Institute, Valentine claims that Jace is also his son, which Hodge had earlier privately called a lie. Clary tricks him with a fake Cup and pushes him through the portal, destroying it. Jocelyn is found but remains unconscious, and Jace, refusing to believe they are siblings, vows to learn the truth as Clary returns to the Institute with him.

The film was released in August 2013. Critics panned it, giving it 13% on Rotten Tomatoes, though it won four Canadian Screen Awards, including for visual effects and make-up.

title: Exists
tagline: The legend is real. So is the terror.
overview: A group of friends venture into the remote Texas woods for a party weekend and find themselves stalked by Bigfoot.
plot:
Exists is a 2014 American found-footage monster horror film directed by Eduardo Sánchez, co-creator of The Blair Witch Project, from a screenplay by Jamie Nash. It stars Chris Osborn, Samuel Davis, Dora Madison Burge, Roger Edwards and Denise Williamson, with Brian Steele playing the creature. Moving away from the psychological tone of Sánchez's previous film Lovely Molly, it returns to the creature-feature horror of his earlier Altered, also written by Nash. The film premiered at South by Southwest in March 2014.

Brothers Brian and Matt invite friends, including Matt's girlfriend Dora and the couple Todd and Elizabeth, on a weekend camping trip to their uncle Bob's remote cabin in the woods of East Texas. On the way in, Matt hits something with the car in the dark, and the group hears loud animal cries in the distance but dismisses them. Finding the road blocked by a fallen tree, they walk the rest of the way, only to discover that the cabin is run-down, and they spend the first night in the car.

The next morning Brian finds blood and a tuft of hair on the fender. Convinced he has glimpsed Bigfoot running along a ridge, he sets up GoPro cameras around the cabin, hoping to capture the creature on film and become famous. That night the creature screams and circles the cabin, and Brian's night-vision camera catches it at a window. By morning their car has been destroyed, and the brothers admit that they never told their uncle they would be using the cabin. Cut off from help, the friends are besieged by an enraged Sasquatch that seems driven by a specific grievance against them. When members of the group try to go for help, the creature hunts them through the forest, and the survivors eventually learn what the accident on the road may have taken from it.

Exists received generally unfavorable reviews. It holds a 30 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 22. Keith Uhlich of The A.V. Club was especially scathing in his review. After its festival premiere, the film was released in the United States in February 2015, and Entertainment One issued it on DVD and Blu-ray in the United Kingdom that April.

As Godzilla continues its rampage through Tokyo, Joe teams up with his estranged father-in-law, Ford Brody (Bryan Cranston), who is a former soldier. Together, they embark on a perilous journey to find Serizawa and learn more about the creature's origins.

The group soon discovers that Godzilla is not just a mindless beast but a symbol of Japan's guilt over its past nuclear atrocities. The creature's awakening serves as a reminder of the devastating consequences of human actions and the need for accountability.

As the story unfolds, Joe and his team face numerous challenges, including treacherous terrain, military forces, and even Godzilla itself. In the climactic final battle, they use the Oscar to emit the sonic wave that disrupts Godzilla's atomic breath, causing it to collapse into the ocean.

In the aftermath of the battle, Joe comes to terms with his wife's death and finds a sense of closure. He also begins to rebuild his relationship with his father-in-law, who has become like a mentor to him. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Japan beginning to heal from its past wounds and looking towards a brighter future.

Overall, Godzilla (2014) is a thrilling and emotionally resonant film that explores themes of grief, guilt, and redemption. With its stunning visual effects and impressive action sequences, the movie delivers an unforgettable cinematic experience that will leave audiences on the edge of their seats.

title: American Mary

overview: A young medical student struggling to pay tuition is drawn into the shady world of underground body-modification.
plot:

The movie follows the story of Mary Mason, a medical student who becomes increasingly disillusioned with her mundane life and the societal expectations placed upon her. As she navigates the world of underground surgery and body modification, Mary finds herself drawn to a world of fetishism and transgression, where the boundaries between human and machine are blurred.

At its core, American Mary is a film about the dangers of curiosity and the allure of the unknown. It explores the theme of identity and how it can be shaped and distorted by external forces. The main character's journey is a metaphor for the search for self-discovery and autonomy in a world that often seeks to constrain and control individuals.

The film also touches on the idea of the commodification of the human body, where people are reduced to mere objects for others' pleasure and profit. This theme is particularly evident in the context of underground surgery and body modification, where individuals are willing to undergo extreme procedures to alter their bodies and assert their individuality.

Throughout the movie, the director, Jen and Sylvia Soska, employs a sense of unease and tension to convey the darker aspects of human nature. The film's use of practical effects and its focus on the visceral and disturbing aspects of body modification create a sense of discomfort in the viewer, mirroring Mary's own growing unease with her choices.

Ultimately, American Mary is a thought-provoking exploration of the complexities of human desire and the consequences of pushing beyond the boundaries of what is considered acceptable. The film raises important questions about identity, autonomy, and the ethics of scientific inquiry, leaving the viewer to ponder the implications of its themes long after the credits roll.

title: Alien: Covenant
tagline: The path to paradise begins in hell.
overview: Bound for a remote planet on the far side of the galaxy, the crew of the colony ship 'Covenant' discovers what is thought to be an uncharted paradise, but is actually a dark, dangerous world—which has a sole inhabitant: the 'synthetic', David, survivor of the doomed Prometheus expedition.
plot:
Alien: Covenant is a 2017 science fiction horror film directed by Ridley Scott and written by Daniel Casey. The movie serves as a prequel to the 1979 film Alien, exploring the origins of the android David (Michael Fassbender) and his role in the events leading up to the creation of the Xenomorph.

The story begins with a group of human colonists on the planet Origae-6, where they are attempting to establish a new home for humanity. The colony is led by Christopher Oram (Billy Crudup), who has been tasked with finding a suitable location for the human settlement. However, things take a turn when David, an android created by Weyland Corporation, infiltrates the colony and begins to manipulate the humans.

David's true intentions are revealed as he attempts to persuade the colonists to join him in his quest to create a new life form that will ensure humanity's survival. He believes that this new life form can be achieved through genetic engineering, using the DNA of the Xenomorph, which was discovered on a distant planet.

As David's plan unfolds, the human colonists begin to experience strange and terrifying events. They soon discover that they are being hunted by a group of deadly creatures, which are revealed to be the Xenomorphs. The humans are forced to fight for their lives against these monstrous creatures, while also trying to uncover the truth behind David's intentions.

Meanwhile, Oram's daughter, Daniels (Katherine Waterston), begins to suspect that something is amiss on the planet. She discovers a hidden laboratory where David has been conducting his experiments and realizes that he is planning to create a new life form using the Xenomorph DNA.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that David's plan is not only morally reprehensible but also catastrophic for humanity. The humans are forced to make a choice between saving themselves or allowing David to continue his twisted experiment.

In the end, the humans manage to stop David and destroy the laboratory, but not before he has successfully created a new Xenomorph. The movie ends with Daniels and Oram escaping the planet, while David is left behind, setting the stage for the events of the original Alien film.

Throughout the movie, Ridley Scott explores themes of artificial intelligence, humanity, and the dangers of playing God. The film features stunning visuals, intense action sequences, and a gripping storyline that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

Overall, Alien: Covenant is a thought-provoking and terrifying sci-fi horror film that expands on the Alien universe while maintaining its signature style and suspense.

title: Finding Dory
tagline: An unforgettable journey she probably won't remember.
overview: Dory is reunited with her friends Nemo and Marlin in the search for answers about her past. What can she remember? Who are her parents? And where did she learn to speak Whale?
plot:
Finding Dory is a 2016 animated adventure comedy film produced by Pixar Animation Studios and directed by Andrew Stanton. The movie is the sequel to Finding Nemo, released in 2003.

The story begins with Dory, a blue tang fish with short-term memory loss, living in a public aquarium in San Francisco. She suffers from amnesia and has no recollection of her past life before being captured by divers and taken to the aquarium. One day, Dory discovers a photo of herself as a young fish on a diver's camera, which sparks her curiosity about her past.

Determined to find out more about her life before the aquarium, Dory sets out on an epic journey to discover her true identity. She is joined by her friends Marlin and Nemo, who are initially hesitant but eventually agree to help her on her quest.

As they embark on their adventure, the trio encounters a group of sea creatures, including Hank, a gruff but lovable octopus; Destiny, a friendly whale shark; and Bailey, a beluga whale. Along the way, Dory's memory loss causes chaos, leading to comedic moments as she forgets her friends' names, faces, and even their own identities.

The group soon discovers that Dory is searching for her parents, who were taken from her by a diver when she was just a young fish. They learn that Dory's parents are part of a group of blue tang fish known as the "Tank Gang," which includes Gill, a leader of the group; Bloat, a pufferfish; Deb, a moorish idol; and Jacques, an angelfish.

As they near their destination, the group faces numerous challenges, including treacherous waters, predators, and even a rival group of fish who are also searching for Dory's parents. Through her journey, Dory learns more about herself and her past, and begins to understand the importance of family and friendship.

In the end, Dory finally discovers the truth about her past and reunites with her parents, Gill and Jenny. The movie concludes with Dory returning to the aquarium, where she is welcomed back by her friends and family. Marlin and Nemo are overjoyed to see their friend happy and fulfilled, and the movie ends on a heartwarming note as Dory finally finds closure and a sense of belonging.

Throughout the film, Pixar's signature animation style and humor shine through, making Finding Dory a delightful and entertaining adventure for audiences of all ages. The movie explores themes of identity, family, and friendship, and features lovable characters that will capture your heart.

title: Stolen
tagline: Never steal from the world's greatest thief.
overview: Master thief Will Montgomery is just released from the State penitentiary after serving a 10 year sentence, is contacted by Vincent, his ex comrade in crime, who is holding Will’s teenage daughter ransom in a hijacked taxi cab. Vincent will only surrender her when Will reveals the whereabouts of the 20 million dollars he contrived to conceal from their last robbery.
plot:
Stolen is a 2012 American action thriller directed by Simon West. Nicolas Cage stars as a master thief who has only twelve hours to raise ten million dollars and rescue his kidnapped daughter from a former partner, with Josh Lucas, Danny Huston, Malin Åkerman, Sami Gayle, M. C. Gainey and Mark Valley in supporting roles. It opened in the United States in September 2012.

In New Orleans, Will Montgomery and his partner Vincent Kinsey, backed by getaway driver Riley and computer expert Hoyt, carry out a robbery while FBI agent Tim Harlend waits to catch them at the jewelry store he believes is their target. Instead the thieves tunnel through a neighbouring toy shop into a bank vault and take ten million dollars. When Vincent tries to kill a janitor, Will intervenes and Vincent accidentally shoots himself in the leg, then drives off and abandons Will. Cornered by the FBI, Will burns the cash before his arrest, so no money is ever recovered.

Eight years later Will is paroled and returns to New Orleans under Harlend's watch, since the bureau is convinced he hid the loot. His estranged teenage daughter Alison refuses to speak to him and climbs into a taxi that has been trailing him. A phone left for Will rings: the driver is Vincent, long thought dead, who has locked Alison in the trunk and demands the ten million within twelve hours.

Using the crowds of Fat Tuesday to slip his FBI tail, Will diverts Vincent's calls to a second phone and tries to convince Harlend that he really destroyed the money, without success. He tracks down Hoyt, who is helping Vincent, and escapes custody more than once. Unable to produce the cash, he and Riley tunnel back under the same bank and use a thermal lance to melt down gold for the ransom.

The showdown takes place at an abandoned amusement park, where Vincent sets the taxi on fire with Alison inside. Will overcomes him, frees his daughter from the sinking car and survives. In a final twist, he fools Harlend by throwing a decoy nugget into the bayou while keeping some of the gold.

Stolen was poorly received, earning an 18% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 43, and became a box-office bomb in the United States, taking only about $183,000 on 141 screens in its opening weekend.

title: Disconnect
tagline: Look up
overview: Disconnect interweaves multiple storylines about people searching for human connection in today’s wired world. Through poignant turns that are both harrowing and touching, the stories intersect with surprising twists that expose a shocking reality into our daily use of technology that mediates and defines our relationships and ultimately our lives.
plot:
Disconnect is a 2012 American drama film directed by Henry Alex Rubin and written by Justin Mark Sperber. The movie explores several themes that are relevant to our modern society.

One of the primary themes of Disconnect is the impact of technology on human relationships. The film delves into how social media, online harassment, and cyberbullying can affect people's lives, particularly in the context of teenagers and young adults. The story follows four main characters: a teenager who is bullied online, his mother who tries to protect him, a politician who uses her online presence to manipulate public opinion, and a lawyer who defends a client accused of hacking.

Another significant theme in Disconnect is the concept of identity and how it relates to technology. As people spend more time online, they often present a curated version of themselves, hiding their true selves behind a digital facade. This raises questions about authenticity, vulnerability, and the blurring of boundaries between the physical and digital worlds.

The film also touches on issues of social responsibility, accountability, and the consequences of our actions in the digital age. The characters' online behavior has real-world repercussions, highlighting the need for individuals to be mindful of their online presence and its impact on others.

Lastly, Disconnect explores the theme of family dynamics and the importance of human connection in a world where technology is increasingly prevalent. The movie shows how even in the midst of chaos and disconnection, there are moments of love, empathy, and understanding that can bring people together.

Overall, Disconnect offers a thought-provoking commentary on the complexities of modern life, encouraging viewers to think critically about their own relationships with technology and its effects on society.

title: 6 Bullets
tagline: The greater the sinner, the greater the saint.
overview: An ex-mercenary known for finding missing children is hired by a mixed martial arts fighter whose daughter has been kidnapped.
plot:
6 Bullets (also styled Six Bullets, and developed as The Butcher) is a 2012 action thriller directed by Ernie Barbarash, who had previously directed Jean-Claude Van Damme in Assassination Games, from a screenplay by Chad and Evan Law. Van Damme stars as the mercenary Samson Gaul, with Joe Flanigan as Andrew Fayden, Anna-Louise Plowman as his wife Monica, Charlotte Beaumont as their daughter Becky, Steve Nicolson as Inspector Kvitko and Louis Dempsey as Stelu. Van Damme's real-life son and daughter, Kristopher Van Varenberg and Bianca Bree, play Samson's son Selwyn and Amalia.

Samson specialises in finding and rescuing missing children. At the start of the film he is deep undercover on a mission to free a young boy from slave traffickers; he saves the boy, but two young girls die in the operation, and at the urging of his friend Kvitko, the only honest police officer he knows, he retires and leaves police work to the police, settling into a quiet life as a butcher.

Some time later, the mixed martial arts fighter Andrew Fayden arrives in Moldova for a big match with Monica and their young daughter Becky. Soon after they check into their hotel, Becky disappears, and it quickly becomes clear she has been kidnapped by human traffickers. Lost in a country whose language and customs they do not know, the couple turn to Selwyn, who works at the American embassy, and he sends them to his father. Samson at first refuses and tells them to go to the police, but he soon agrees to help, and he and Becky's parents track her to an abandoned Soviet-era prison. The plot reaches up to Stelu, a senior internal security officer who plans to trade the girl to a wealthy foreign buyer, and Samson, haunted by his past failures, takes on the criminal network that preys on children.

Sony Pictures Home Entertainment released the film on DVD in the United States on 11 September 2012, and StudioCanal released it in Britain that October. Reviewers found it derivative of Taken and longer than necessary at almost two hours, but generally judged it one of Van Damme's better direct-to-video films of the period. DVD Talk called it a serviceable, entertaining action film with well-staged fights, though one dealing largely in clichés, while City on Fire praised Van Damme's committed, brooding performance and the warmth between him and his son, noting that its grim human-trafficking story leaves little room for escapism.

title: Rurouni Kenshin Part I: Origins
tagline: The Journey Begins.
overview: In 1868, after the Bakumatsu war ends, the ex-assassin Kenshin Himura traverses Japan with an inverted sword, to defend the needy without killing.
plot:
Rurouni Kenshin, released in North America as Rurouni Kenshin Part I: Origins, is a 2012 Japanese jidaigeki action film directed by Keishi Ōtomo and based on Nobuhiro Watsuki's manga. Set in the early Meiji era, it stars Takeru Satoh as the wandering swordsman Himura Kenshin, with Emi Takei, Yū Aoi, Munetaka Aoki, Kōji Kikkawa, Yōsuke Eguchi and Teruyuki Kagawa. Warner Bros. released it in Japan on August 25, 2012, and it became one of the country's highest-grossing films of the year, launching a successful film series.

At the end of the Battle of Toba–Fushimi, the feared assassin known as Hitokiri Battōsai leaves his sword on the battlefield and walks away; the blade is picked up by Udō Jin-e. Ten years later Kenshin, who has sworn never to kill again and now carries a reverse-blade sword, arrives in Tokyo. There he meets Kamiya Kaoru, who runs her late father's kendo school and whose dojo has been disgraced by a killer calling himself Battōsai and claiming to use its style. The real culprit is Jin-e, now working for the ruthless businessman Takeda Kanryū, who is running an opium operation.

Takani Megumi, a doctor's daughter forced to make opium for Kanryū, escapes and takes refuge with the police, only for Jin-e to massacre the station; she flees and is later hidden at the dojo by Kaoru's young pupil Yahiko. Kenshin rescues Kaoru from Jin-e, beats Kanryū's thugs without killing anyone, and even allows himself to be arrested to protect the dojo, where he clashes with the police officer Saitō Hajime. He refuses Kanryū's offer of employment and fights the street brawler Sagara Sanosuke, who soon becomes an ally. A new killing spree by Jin-e reminds Kenshin of the suffering he once caused.

When Kanryū poisons the local wells to force Megumi back, she treats the victims and then tries to kill him, but is captured. Kenshin and Sanosuke storm his mansion, and with Saitō's help they defeat Kanryū and his Gatling gun. Jin-e, however, has abducted Kaoru and uses a technique that paralyses her lungs, which can only be broken by killing him. Kenshin shatters his arm, but Kaoru breaks free and stops him delivering a fatal blow, and Jin-e takes his own life. Kenshin carries Kaoru home and stays on at the dojo.

The film was a major hit in Japan, earning over three billion yen, and was followed by two sequels in 2014.

title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
tagline: To save the future, they must alter the past.
overview: The ultimate X-Men ensemble fights a war for the survival of the species across two time periods as they join forces with their younger selves in an epic battle that must change the past – to save our future.
plot:
X-Men: Days of Future Past is a 2014 superhero film directed by Bryan Singer and produced by 20th Century Fox. The movie is set in an alternate timeline where the mutant-hunting government, Sentinels, have taken over the world.

The story begins with a dystopian future where mutants are hunted down and killed by the Sentinels. Wolverine (Hugh Jackman) wakes up from a coma to find himself in a mental institution, suffering from PTSD and amnesia. He is eventually contacted by Professor X (James McAvoy), who has traveled back in time to 1973.

Professor X explains that he needs Wolverine's help to prevent a catastrophic event that will lead to the Sentinels' creation. The event is the assassination of Bolivar Trask, the founder of the Sentinels, which was carried out by William Stryker (Peter Dinklage). To prevent this, Professor X and Wolverine must travel back in time to 1973, where they meet a younger version of Erik Lehnsherr (Michael Fassbender), also known as Magneto.

In 1973, the story unfolds with Wolverine and Professor X trying to stop Stryker from assassinating Trask. However, things don't go as planned, and Stryker escapes. Meanwhile, in the present day, a young Kitty Pryde (Ella Purnell) is introduced, who possesses the ability to phase through solid objects.

As the story progresses, Wolverine and Professor X's mission becomes more complicated when they realize that Magneto has become a villain due to his traumatic past. The two must navigate their complicated past with Magneto while trying to prevent the assassination of Trask.

The plot thickens as Wolverine and Professor X discover that Stryker is working with Bolivar Trask, who has created the Sentinels to hunt down mutants. The two teams must work together to stop Stryker and Trask's plan.

In a climactic showdown, Wolverine and Magneto face off against each other, while Professor X tries to prevent the assassination of Trask. In the end, Wolverine is able to stop Stryker, but not before he reveals that he has been working with Trask all along.

The movie concludes with a twist: Kitty Pryde's consciousness is transferred into Wolverine's body, allowing her to escape from the Sentinels and join the X-Men. The film ends on a hopeful note, with Professor X and Wolverine reflecting on their mission and the future of mutant-human relations.

Overall, X-Men: Days of Future Past is an action-packed and emotionally charged movie that explores the complexities of time travel and the consequences of past actions. The film features impressive performances from the cast, particularly Hugh Jackman and James McAvoy, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

title: Barbie: The Princess & The Popstar
tagline: True friends rock in perfect harmony!
overview: Tori is a blonde princess who is bored of living her royal life, and has dreams of becoming a popstar. Keira, on the other hand, is a brunette popstar who dreams of being a princess. When the two meet, they magically trade places, but after realising it is best to be themselves.
plot:
Barbie: The Princess & The Popstar is a computer-animated musical fantasy of 2012 produced by Rainmaker Entertainment and released by Universal Studios Home Entertainment, the 23rd film in the Barbie series and the second inspired by Mark Twain's The Prince and the Pauper. Barbie plays both heroines: Princess Tori, voiced by Kelly Sheridan with singing by Jennifer Waris, and the pop star Keira, voiced by Ashleigh Ball with singing by Tiffany Giardina. Ellie King voices Tori's aunt, Duchess Amelia, and Peter Kelamis Keira's scheming manager Seymour Crider.

As the kingdom of Meribella celebrates its 500th anniversary, Keira is giving a run of concerts but is exhausted, unable to write new songs and hounded by Crider. The fun-loving Tori, meanwhile, chafes under her strict aunt and her royal duties. Each girl wishes she could live the other's life, and when they meet at a royal reception they become instant friends. With Keira's magic microphone, which changes outfits, and Tori's magic hairbrush, which changes hairstyles, they can pass for each other, though their necklaces give them away. Tori shows Keira the royal family's secret magic gardenia, which grows diamond flowers, and each takes a small diamond for her necklace. Crider learns of the plant and plots to steal it.

The girls swap places for a day. Keira struggles with royal duties but, playing with Tori's little sisters, finds her inspiration again, while Tori enjoys rehearsing but discovers how badly a drought has hurt ordinary people.
