They find themselves at the same rooftop on New Year's Eve, each with their own reasons for being there, but ultimately, they form an unlikely bond that transcends their individual struggles.

The film also touches on the theme of regret and the choices we make in life. Each character is haunted by past mistakes or missed opportunities, and as they navigate their relationships with one another, they are forced to confront these regrets head-on. Through their conversations and interactions, the movie shows how our choices can shape us, but also how we can learn from them and grow.

Furthermore, A Long Way Down explores the idea of human connection in a world that often seems to value superficiality over depth. The characters' relationships with one another are raw, honest, and sometimes painful, but ultimately, they offer a sense of belonging and understanding that is hard to find elsewhere.

Overall, the movie presents a nuanced and empathetic portrayal of complex characters navigating the challenges of modern life. Through its thoughtful exploration of themes such as isolation, regret, and human connection, A Long Way Down offers a powerful and moving cinematic experience.

tagline: You can't save the world alone
overview: Fuelled by his restored faith in humanity and inspired by Superman's selfless act, Bruce Wayne and Diana Prince assemble a team of metahumans consisting of Barry Allen, Arthur Curry and Victor Stone to face the catastrophic threat of Steppenwolf and the Parademons who are on the hunt for three Mother Boxes on Earth.
plot:
Justice League is a 2017 superhero film directed by Zack Snyder and Joss Whedon, based on the DC Comics team of the same name. The movie brings together some of DC's most iconic heroes to form a team that must band together to save the world from an ancient evil.

The film begins with Bruce Wayne (Ben Affleck), aka Batman, who has been training a young Diana Prince (Sally Hawkins) in the ways of combat and leadership. However, their mission is interrupted by Steppenwolf (Ciarán Hinds), an alien warlord who seeks to collect three powerful artifacts known as the Mother Boxes.

Meanwhile, Arthur Curry (Jason Momoa), aka Aquaman, is introduced as he struggles with his half-human, half-Atlantean heritage. He eventually teams up with Mera (Amber Heard) and together they embark on a quest to find the Trident of Atlan, which will help him claim his rightful place as king.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Superman (Henry Cavill), who has been missing since his battle with General Zod in Man of Steel, is revealed to be alive. However, he is being held captive by Steppenwolf and his minions.

As the heroes begin to assemble, they realize that they must work together if they hope to stop Steppenwolf's plans. Batman brings his strategic mind, Wonder Woman (Gal Gadot) brings her combat skills and compassion, Aquaman brings his aquatic abilities and determination, Cyborg (Ray Fisher) brings his technological expertise and emotional vulnerability, and The Flash (Ezra Miller) brings his speed and enthusiasm.

The team faces numerous challenges as they try to stop Steppenwolf's plans. Along the way, they also uncover a deeper conspiracy involving Darkseid (Jensen Ackles), who is revealed to be manipulating events from behind the scenes.

As the battle against Steppenwolf reaches its climax, the heroes must put aside their differences and work together if they hope to save the world. In the end, they succeed in defeating Steppenwolf and shattering the Mother Boxes, which prevents Darkseid from gaining control over the planet.

The film concludes with a sense of hope and unity among the heroes, as they realize that they have found a new family and a new purpose. The ending also sets up the possibility for future team-ups and adventures, as the heroes look to the future and prepare for whatever challenges may come their way.

Overall, Justice League is an action-packed superhero film that brings together some of DC's most iconic heroes in a thrilling adventure. While it received mixed reviews from critics, fans of the franchise will enjoy the excitement and spectacle of this epic battle between good and evil.

title: Time Travel Mater
overview: When a clock lands on Mater's engine, he travels back in time to 1909 where he meets Stanley, an ambitious young car on his way to California. With the help of Lightning McQueen, Mater alters history by convincing Stanley to stay and build Radiator Springs. Stanley meets Lizzie and they commemorate the opening of the new courthouse with their wedding.
plot:
Time Travel Mater is a 2012 American computer-animated short film produced by Pixar, the eleventh entry in the Cars Toons series of Mater's Tall Tales. Directed by Rob Gibbs and written by John Lasseter, Gibbs and Scott Morse, it runs about six minutes, with music by Mark Watters, and was the third production of the Pixar Canada studio. It first aired on Disney Channel on 5 June 2012 and had its official premiere on 15 June at the Blue Sky Cellar in Disney California Adventure, celebrating the opening of Cars Land, before airing on ABC the next day. It was later included on the Pixar Short Films Collection, Volume 2.

Outside the Radiator Springs courthouse, Lizzie greets Lightning McQueen and Mater curtly but speaks fondly to the statue of the town's founder, Stanley, prompting McQueen to ask how the two met. Mater explains that it all started the week before, when a new town sign with a clock fell on him, leaving the clock on his nose; when he sneezed, he vanished and found himself in the Tail Light Caverns in 1909, before the town existed. At a nearby spring he meets a young Stanley, a radiator cap salesman about to leave for California in search of customers. Realising that without Stanley there will be no Radiator Springs, Mater zips back to the present to fetch McQueen, removes his radiator cap so that Stanley has a customer, and suggests he build a town beside "this here radiator spring". Stanley loves the idea and names the town on the spot.

Jumping ahead to 1927, the pair find the young town thriving when a Model T named Lizzie breaks down there. Mater fears she is falling for McQueen, which would ruin history, but it turns out she only has eyes for Stanley. McQueen introduces them, and the friends later return in time to see the couple marry before honeymooning at Comfy Caverns. Back in the present, McQueen insists that time travel is impossible, until Lizzie thanks him for introducing her to Stanley.

Larry the Cable Guy voices Mater, Keith Ferguson Lightning McQueen, John Michael Higgins Stanley and Katherine Helmond Lizzie. Unusually for the series, McQueen appears in his World Grand Prix paint scheme from Cars 2, the twins Mia and Tia do not appear, and each era is given its own colour treatment reminiscent of photographs from the period. Several locations seen in the short, including the caverns, are drawn from the Cars Land attraction.

title: Batman: The Dark Knight Returns, Part 2

tagline: Justice Returns... Vengeance Returns... Redemption Comes to Gotham.
overview: Batman has stopped the reign of terror that The Mutants had cast upon his city.  Now an old foe wants a reunion and the government wants The Man of Steel to put a stop to Batman.
plot:
Batman: The Dark Knight Returns, Part 2 is a 2013 American animated superhero film directed by Jay Oliva and produced by Warner Bros. Animation and DC Entertainment, the second half of an adaptation of Frank Miller's landmark 1986 four-issue graphic novel The Dark Knight Returns. Peter Weller voices an aging Bruce Wayne, with Ariel Winter as his new Robin, Carrie Kelley, Mark Valley as Superman, Michael Emerson as the Joker, Maria Canals-Barrera as Ellen Yindel, Michael McKean as Dr. Bartholomew Wolper, Robin Atkin Downes as Oliver Queen, Jim Meskimen as the President and Conan O'Brien as the talk-show host David Endochrine.

Having crushed the Mutant gang's reign of terror, the returning Batman now faces two final confrontations. The Joker, feigning remorse, persuades his psychiatrist Dr. Wolper to bring him on a television talk show to tell his story, while a henchman supplies him with a mind-controlling lipstick. Meanwhile, Superman, who works as a government agent in exchange for permission to help people in secret, is asked by the President to put an end to Batman's vigilantism, against the backdrop of rising tension between the United States and the Soviet Union over the island of Corto Maltese. Gordon's successor, Commissioner Yindel, orders Batman's arrest. On the talk show, the Joker kills the entire studio audience with his laughing gas and escapes, then uses an aging Selina Kyle's escort service to take control of a congressman. Batman pursues him to a county fair, where the Joker kills dozens of people; in their brutal fight Batman breaks his neck without finishing him, and the Joker, stabbing the hero repeatedly, completes the job himself to frame Batman for murder. After Superman deflects a Soviet nuclear missile, the electromagnetic pulse plunges the country into darkness, and Batman rallies the Sons of Batman and Gotham's citizens to keep order. Ordered to stop him, Superman confronts Batman in Crime Alley, where the old hero, wearing a powered exoskeleton and helped by the one-armed Oliver Queen's kryptonite arrow, defeats him before apparently dying of a heart attack. At the funeral, Superman hears a faint heartbeat and winks at Carrie, and Bruce is later revealed to have faked his death to continue his mission in secret with Carrie, Queen and his followers.

The film was released on home video in January 2013, following Part 1 in 2012. Christopher Drake's music for both parts was released by WaterTower Music in October 2013.

overview: A year has passed since Guts parted ways with the Band of the Hawks. Meanwhile, his former mercenary group is plotting a rescue mission to save an imprisoned Griffith.
plot:
Berserk: The Golden Age Arc III - The Advent is a 2013 Japanese animated dark fantasy film and the final instalment of a trilogy adapting the Golden Age arc of Kentaro Miura's manga Berserk. Directed by Toshiyuki Kubooka from a screenplay by Ichirō Ōkouchi, it was animated by Studio 4°C and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures Japan. Hiroaki Iwanaga voices the swordsman Guts, Takahiro Sakurai the charismatic mercenary leader Griffith and Toa Yukinari the warrior Casca, with Akio Otsuka as the Skull Knight. The score is by Shirō Sagisu, with Susumu Hirasawa's song "Aria" as the theme.

A year has passed since Guts left the mercenary company known as the Band of the Hawk to pursue his own dream. In his absence, Griffith was caught in a liaison with the king's daughter, Princess Charlotte, imprisoned for treason in the Tower of Rebirth and tortured, while his followers were branded outlaws and hunted. Guts rejoins his old comrades to rescue him, but the man they free from the dungeon is a broken, mute and withered figure, barely alive after months of torture.

Overwhelmed by despair, Griffith tries to kill himself, and the strange pendant he has always worn reacts to his anguish. It opens a gateway to another realm under a solar eclipse, pulling Griffith and the entire Band of the Hawk inside. There they face the God Hand, a circle of archdemons, who tell Griffith that his whole life has been leading to this moment. He agrees to sacrifice his comrades in return for rebirth as Femto, a new member of the God Hand. The Hawks are massacred by monstrous Apostles, former humans like the demon Zodd, and Femto assaults Casca while Guts, fighting desperately to reach her, loses his left arm and his right eye. The mysterious Skull Knight carries Guts and the shattered Casca back to the human world and warns Guts that he now bears a brand that will draw evil spirits to him every night. Leaving Casca in the care of their former comrade Rickert, Guts sets out to hunt the Apostles and the God Hand.

The film was released in Japan on 1 February 2013 and later on home video in North America by Viz Media. It earned less at the Japanese box office than the first film. Reviews were divided: Kotaku's Richard Eisenbeis praised it as an emotionally harrowing and extremely graphic climax, while Anime News Network criticised its animation and its streamlining of the story.

title: Monsters: Dark Continent
tagline: Fear has evolved
overview: Seven years on from the events of Monsters, and the ‘Infected Zones’ have spread worldwide. Humans have been knocked off the top of the food chain, with disparate communities struggling for survival. American soldiers are being sent abroad to protect US interests from the Monsters, but the war is far from being won.
plot:
Monsters: Dark Continent, also known as Monsters 2, is a 2014 British science-fiction war film directed by Tom Green, in his feature debut, and written by Green and Jay Basu. A sequel to Gareth Edwards's Monsters (2010), it introduces an entirely new set of characters; Edwards, busy with Godzilla, served only as an executive producer. The cast includes Johnny Harris, Sam Keeley, Joe Dempsie, Kyle Soller and Nicholas Pinnock.

A decade after the alien creatures first appeared on the border between Mexico and the United States, they have spread to the Middle East. Four close friends from Detroit, Michael, Frankie, Inkelaar and Williams, a new father, serve together in the U.S. Army and are deployed there on their first tour, where troops must contend both with the creatures, now simply called monsters, and with a fresh insurgency. Under their squad leaders Forrest and Frater, they see a colossal monster brought down by gunfire on their first mission. Three months in, the squad is sent to find four missing soldiers in a dangerous area. Roadside bombs wreck their vehicles and kill Forrest, Williams and others, and insurgents pin the survivors down. Inkelaar is killed by a sniper, Frankie is wounded, and Frater surrenders the group. Captive, Michael and Frater are forced to watch Frankie bleed to death.

Using a passing creature as a distraction, Frater kills a guard and the two escape on motorbikes, resolved to complete the mission. When the fuel runs out they continue east on foot. Michael finds a badly hurt boy, and villagers take the soldiers in out of gratitude; at night Michael watches a creature scatter glowing spores across the desert. The boy dies, and an exasperated Frater insists that they get back to the mission. At the village they were heading for, they learn the men they came to rescue were already dead. Frater snaps and kills a villager, and Michael has to shoot him to save the rest of the family. As a gigantic creature rises from the sand at the extraction point, Frater collapses and dies, and a helicopter carries off a silent Michael.

Green and Basu were given free rein as long as the film featured monsters, and chose to make a war movie about socially relevant themes. It was shot in Jordan and Detroit from March 2013 and premiered at the BFI London Film Festival in October 2014. Reviews were mostly negative, with 17% on Rotten Tomatoes, though Kim Newman of Empire gave it four stars.

title: The Last Exorcism Part II
tagline: The second coming
overview: As Nell Sweetzer tries to build a new life after the events of the first movie, the evil force that once possessed her returns with an even more horrific plan.
plot:
The Last Exorcism Part II is a 2013 American supernatural horror film co-written, edited and directed by Ed Gass-Donnelly, a sequel to The Last Exorcism (2010). Ashley Bell returns as Nell Sweetzer, a young woman trying to rebuild her life after her possession, with Julia Garner, Spencer Treat Clark and Louis Herthum. Unlike its predecessor, it abandons the found-footage format.

A couple discover a feral, terrifying Nell crouching beside their refrigerator, and she is taken to a hospital, where she seems catatonic. Months later she has settled into a New Orleans group home for girls run by the kind therapist Frank and found work as a hotel chambermaid, and her nightmares have stopped. At a Mardi Gras parade with her new friends, however, she notices strange things, including masked men watching her, and signs grow that the demon Abalam has returned. After Stephanie, another girl at the home, dies of an unnatural seizure, Nell's former nurse, Cecile, tells her about the Order of the Right Hand, a secret society that has been monitoring her. Her friends find a YouTube video of the events of the first film, revealing that the lost footage has surfaced and turning Nell into an unwilling internet celebrity, and Chris, a hotel co-worker who likes her, slits his own throat after watching a clip in which she lies about how she became pregnant.

Cecile turns to the Order, whose members Calder and Jeffrey try to transfer the demon, which they say is in love with Nell, into a sacrificed chicken. The force proves too strong, and Calder injects Nell with a lethal dose of morphine. As her pulse stops, the demon appears to her in the shapes of Nell herself, her father and Chris, begging her to take its hand. Believing her dead, the Order members are caught off guard when she yields; the house burns, killing all three. Nell then kills Frank and sets the group home ablaze, leaving her friends to die, and drives away as buildings and cars burst into flames around her, fulfilling a prophecy of the end times.

The film premiered in Russia on February 28, 2013, and opened in the United States the next day after being cut from an R to a PG-13 rating. It was not screened for critics and was panned, earning 16% on Rotten Tomatoes and 35 on Metacritic, though The Hollywood Reporter praised Bell's performance. It grossed about $25 million worldwide on a $5 million budget, far below the original's $67.7 million.

title: RED 2
tagline: The best never rest.
overview: Retired C.I.A. agent Frank Moses reunites his unlikely team of elite operatives for a global quest to track down a missing portable nuclear device.
plot:
RED 2 is a 2013 action comedy film directed by Roy H. Wagner and starring Bruce Willis, Helen Mirren, John Malkovich, and Catherine Zeta-Jones.

The movie takes place six years after the events of the first film. Frank Moses (Bruce Willis), Marvin Boggs (John Malkovich), and Sarah Jordan (Mary-Louise Parker) are still on the run from the CIA and other government agencies that want to capture them for their alleged involvement in a conspiracy involving Russian spies.

The story begins with Frank, now living under an assumed identity as "Jack", working as a handyman. However, his life is disrupted when he receives a mysterious message from Marvin, who has been captured by the CIA. The agency plans to use Marvin's knowledge of Soviet espionage to gain access to highly classified information.

Frank and Sarah team up with Marvin's former partner, Teddy (Catherine Zeta-Jones), to rescue him from the CIA's clutches. Along the way, they encounter a new villain, Viktor Chagarin (Mekhi Phifer), who is revealed to be a Russian spy working for the CIA.

As Frank and his team navigate through various obstacles, including a high-speed car chase and a shootout with CIA agents, they uncover a conspiracy involving the CIA's plans to use Soviet-era spies to gain access to classified information. The team also discovers that Viktor Chagarin is actually a double agent working for the Russians.

The plot thickens as Frank and his team learn that the CIA has been using the Russian spies to gather intelligence on the United States, which could compromise national security. The team must use their skills and experience to stop the CIA's plans and bring down Viktor Chagarin.

In the end, Frank and his team successfully rescue Marvin and defeat Viktor Chagarin in a thrilling showdown. However, not before discovering that the CIA has been using the Russian spies to gather intelligence on the United States, which could have catastrophic consequences.

The movie ends with Frank, Sarah, and Marvin returning to their normal lives, but not before sharing a moment of camaraderie and acknowledging that they will always be there for each other. The film concludes with a sense of closure, but also leaves room for potential sequels or spin-offs.

Overall, RED 2 is an action-packed comedy that delivers on its promise of high-octane thrills and witty banter. The movie's cast delivers strong performances, and the chemistry between the leads is undeniable. While some may find the plot a bit predictable, the film's pacing and humor make it an enjoyable ride from start to finish.

Through its gripping narrative and well-developed characters, Closed Circuit raises important questions about the nature of terrorism, the role of government in times of crisis, and the importance of empathy and understanding in breaking down barriers between individuals.

title: Prisoners
tagline: Every moment matters.
overview: Keller Dover faces a parent's worst nightmare when his 6-year-old daughter, Anna, and her friend go missing. The only lead is an old motorhome that had been parked on their street. The head of the investigation, Detective Loki, arrests the driver, but a lack of evidence forces Loki to release his only suspect. plot:
Prisoners is a psychological thriller film directed by Denis Villeneuve, released in 2013 by Warner Bros. Pictures.

The movie begins with the disappearance of two young girls, Anna and Joy Mullins, who are taken from their homes on Thanksgiving Day. The story then shifts to Keller Dover (played by Hugh Jackman), a father whose daughter, Braden, has also gone missing. Desperate for answers, Keller sets out to find his daughter, but his search is hindered by the lack of evidence and the skepticism of the police.

As the investigation unfolds, Keller's obsession with finding his daughter leads him to take matters into his own hands, putting himself at odds with Detective Loki (played by Jake Gyllenhaal), who is initially hesitant to involve Keller in the case. Meanwhile, a mysterious figure known as "The Kidnapper" begins to leave clues and taunt the police.

As the story progresses, it becomes clear that The Kidnapper is not just any ordinary kidnapper, but someone with a twisted motive for taking the girls. The plot thickens when Keller discovers a cryptic message left by The Kidnapper, which leads him to believe that his daughter may still be alive.

The second half of the movie takes a dark and unexpected turn as Keller's search becomes more intense and violent. He eventually tracks down The Kidnapper, who is revealed to be Alex Jones (played by Paul Dano), a quiet and unassuming man with a sinister secret.

As the story reaches its climax, Keller's actions become increasingly erratic, putting himself and others at risk. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that The Kidnapper has been using the girls as bait to lure in other victims, including Braden. Keller's desperation leads him to make a horrific decision, which ultimately puts an end to the kidnappings.

The movie ends with Keller finally finding his daughter, but not before she has been severely traumatized by her experience. The film concludes on a somber note, leaving the audience to ponder the consequences of Keller's actions and the true cost of his desperation.

Throughout the movie, Villeneuve masterfully builds tension and suspense, keeping the viewer on the edge of their seat as they follow Keller's desperate search for his daughter. The performances by Jackman, Gyllenhaal, and Dano are outstanding, bringing depth and complexity to the characters.

Overall, Prisoners is a gripping and unsettling thriller that explores themes of desperation, obsession, and the true cost of parental love.

title: Runner Runner
tagline: The house always wins.
overview: When a poor college student who cracks an online poker game goes bust, he arranges a face-to-face with the man he thinks cheated him, a sly offshore entrepreneur.
plot:
Runner Runner is a 2013 American crime thriller film directed by Brad Furman and written by Brian Koppelman and David Levien, starring Justin Timberlake, Ben Affleck, Gemma Arterton and Anthony Mackie. Set in the world of online gambling, it follows a Princeton graduate student who is drawn into the operations of a powerful but corrupt gambling tycoon in Costa Rica. Principal photography took place in 2012 in Puerto Rico and at Princeton.

Richie Furst, a former Wall Street professional, is ineligible for financial aid at Princeton, so he pays for his master's degree by steering fellow students to online gambling sites in return for a cut. When the dean threatens to expel him, Richie tries to win his tuition at online poker, only to lose everything to a player he can prove statistically was cheating. He flies to Costa Rica to confront Ivan Block, the man who runs the world's largest empire of online gambling websites. Impressed when Richie's evidence exposes coders who rigged the software, Ivan fires them and offers Richie a lucrative job helping run the business. Richie is soon living a life of luxury and grows close to Rebecca Shafran, Ivan's former lover, but the job quickly turns dark: he is sent to blackmail a business affiliate and to bribe a local official, who has him beaten when the payment proves too small. Meanwhile, FBI agent Shavers, who has no legal authority in Costa Rica and uses ruthless methods, pressures Richie to help bring Ivan down, at one point having drugs planted in his luggage. Richie's friend Andrew Cronin, who works on the software, suspects that Ivan is running a Ponzi scheme with his players' money. When Ivan brings Richie's father, a heavy gambler, to Costa Rica by buying up his debts, and Cronin is found badly beaten, Richie realizes that he is being set up as the fall guy for Ivan's crimes and must find a way to outmaneuver both the tycoon and the FBI.

Runner Runner was released in the United States on October 4, 2013. It received generally negative reviews from critics and grossed about $62 million worldwide.

title: Delivery Man
tagline: You're never quite ready for what life delivers.
overview: An affable underachiever finds out he's fathered 533 children through anonymous donations to a fertility clinic 20 years ago. Now he must decide whether or not to come forward when 142 of them file a lawsuit to reveal his identity.
plot:
Delivery Man is a 2013 American comedy-drama written and directed by Ken Scott and produced by DreamWorks Pictures and Reliance Entertainment. A scene-for-scene remake of Scott's 2011 French-Canadian film Starbuck, it stars Vince Vaughn as David Wozniak, with Chris Pratt as his friend and lawyer, Brett, and Cobie Smulders as his girlfriend, Emma; Britt Robertson, Jack Reynor and the Polish actor Andrzej Blumenfeld, as David's father, also appear.

David is a deliveryman for his family's butcher shop in New York, hounded by thugs to whom he owes $80,000, and his girlfriend, Emma, a police officer, is pregnant with his child. One day a lawyer for a sperm bank tells him that the 693 donations he made as a student, which earned him $24,255, were used to father 533 children, and that 142 of them have filed a class-action lawsuit to learn the identity of the donor known only by the alias "Starbuck". Brett, a struggling lawyer and harried father, takes the case to keep the records sealed and gives David profiles of the plaintiffs. Curious, David seeks them out anonymously and performs random acts of kindness, covering a shift so a struggling actor can audition, and, posing as a pizza deliveryman, saving a daughter from an overdose.

Although tempted to reveal himself, David agrees to countersue the sperm bank for punitive damages after the thugs assault his father, and he wins $200,000 while keeping his identity secret. Regret soon sets in, but going public would cost him the settlement. When David confesses to his father that he is Starbuck, his father pays off his debts, and David announces his identity on Facebook. Hurrying to Emma's, he finds her in premature labor; at the hospital their baby is born, David proposes, and many of his children arrive to greet them. In the closing scenes, David keeps in touch with many of his offspring.

Starbuck served as the working title, and filming began in October 2012 in the Hudson Valley before moving to Brooklyn and Manhattan. Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures released the film through its Touchstone label on November 22, 2013. It grossed $53.1 million against a $26 million budget. Reviews were mixed: Rotten Tomatoes gave it 40%, its consensus finding it sweet but inferior to Starbuck, and Metacritic scored it 44, while audiences gave it a B+ CinemaScore. Variety called it a heartfelt celebration of parenthood and singled out Pratt's performance, but TheWrap found it neither funny nor moving.

title: Exodus: Gods and Kings
tagline: Once brothers, now enemies.
overview: The defiant leader Moses rises up against the Egyptian Pharaoh Ramses, setting 400,000 slaves on a monumental journey of escape from Egypt and its terrifying cycle of deadly plagues.
plot:
Exodus: Gods and Kings is a 2014 biblical epic directed and produced by Ridley Scott and written by Adam Cooper, Bill Collage, Jeffrey Caine and Steven Zaillian. Inspired by the story of Moses leading the Hebrews out of Egypt in the Book of Exodus, it stars Christian Bale as Moses and Joel Edgerton as Ramesses, with John Turturro, Aaron Paul, Ben Mendelsohn, Sigourney Weaver and Ben Kingsley. It was released by 20th Century Fox on December 12, 2014.

In 1300 BC, Moses, raised in the Egyptian royal household, serves as a general alongside his adoptive cousin Prince Ramesses. Before a battle against the Hittites at Kadesh, a priestess tells Pharaoh Seti that one of the two men will save the other and become a leader. When Moses saves Ramesses in combat, the prophecy unsettles both. Visiting the city of Pithom, Moses is appalled by the conditions of the Hebrew slaves, and the elder Nun reveals to him that he is himself a Hebrew, saved as an infant from the slaughter of Hebrew boys by his sister Miriam.

After Seti's death and Ramesses' accession, Hegep reveals the secret. When Ramesses threatens Miriam, Moses admits his origins and is exiled into the desert. He survives and reaches Midian, where he marries Zipporah, has a son, Gershom, and lives as a shepherd. Years later, injured in a rockslide, he sees a burning bush and meets Malak, a boy who acts as the messenger of God and orders him to free the Hebrews.

Returning to Egypt, Moses meets his brother Aaron and demands that Ramesses free the slaves. When the Pharaoh refuses, Moses trains the Hebrews in guerrilla warfare, but Malak tells him that God will act instead, and Egypt is struck by a series of plagues. Ramesses remains defiant, even turning on his own people, until the final plague kills the firstborn of Egypt, including his infant son, while the Hebrews, who have marked their doors with lamb's blood, are spared.

Ramesses lets the Hebrews go, but in his grief soon pursues them with his army. Reaching the Red Sea with no way to cross, Moses despairs, but by morning the waters have receded, opening a path. As the Hebrews cross, the sea returns and drowns most of the Egyptian army, leaving Ramesses alive but broken. Moses rejoins his family and receives the Ten Commandments, and decades later, as an old man travelling with the Ark of the Covenant, he sees Malak watching over his people.

The film received mixed reviews, and was banned in Egypt. It grossed 268 million dollars worldwide.

The movie follows Duncan, a shy and introverted teenager who embarks on a summer vacation with his family to a beach town. There, he meets Owen, a charismatic and confident water park employee who becomes a mentor and confidant to Duncan. Through their unlikely friendship, Duncan begins to confront the difficulties of his home life, including his distant father's emotional unavailability and his mother's overbearing presence.

As Duncan navigates this new relationship with Owen, he is forced to confront his own insecurities and vulnerabilities. The film masterfully captures the turmoil of adolescence, where self-doubt and uncertainty are omnipresent. However, it also suggests that these feelings can be a catalyst for growth and transformation.

One of the primary themes of The Way Way Back is the power of human connection in overcoming adversity. Duncan's friendship with Owen serves as a beacon of hope and acceptance, allowing him to feel seen and understood for the first time. This theme is beautifully intertwined with the idea that family is not just about blood ties but also about the relationships we cultivate and nurture.

The film also explores the tension between authenticity and conformity, highlighting the difficulties of navigating societal expectations while staying true to oneself. Duncan's journey is a powerful metaphor for the struggle to find one's authentic voice in a world that often values superficiality over sincerity.

Ultimately, The Way Way Back is a heartwarming and thought-provoking film that celebrates the resilience of the human spirit and the transformative power of meaningful relationships.

title: Monster Truck Mater

plot:
Monster Truck Mater is a 2010 American computer-animated short film produced by Pixar, the sixth entry in the Cars Toons series of Mater's Tall Tales. It was directed by John Lasseter with Rob Gibbs as co-director, and written by Lasseter, Gibbs, Matthew Luhn, Scott Morse, Kevin O'Brien and Derek Thompson. Running a little over four minutes, it premiered on television on 30 July 2010 and was included in the Cars Toons: Mater's Tall Tales DVD and Blu-ray compilation released on 2 November 2010.

At Flo's V8 Café, Lightning McQueen and Mater watch a monster truck roll by, and Mater scoffs that he used to wrestle trucks far bigger than that. He then launches into an outlandish account of his past, this time as a professional monster truck wrestler. In 1975 he starts out in a small-time ring, introduced by the announcer as "The Tormentor", to the boos of the crowd. His first opponent is the I-Screamer, a monstrous ice cream truck; Mater flees, then returns disguised as a kid in a propeller hat, orders a sundae and, while his rival's back is turned, hooks him and flips him onto his roof to win.

With a new look and a bigger set of wheels, The Tormentor works his way up the ranks, pinning Captain Collision, overturning the Rasta Carian by snatching away his bungee-cord dreadlocks, launching Dr. Feel Bad out of the ring and into hospital, and leaving Paddy O'Concrete covered in his own cement. At the world championship he expects an easy win over the reigning champion, Dr. Frankenwagon, until the doctor's enormous monster comes to life. When McQueen asks what happened next, Mater insists that the two of them fought as a tag team, and McQueen is pulled into the story in wrestling gear. After the monster turns on him, Mater hooks the creature, drives under the ring and pulls the whole thing over, defeating the doctor and his monster; the referee declares The Tormentor and "Frightening McMean" the new champions.

McQueen dismisses the tale as nonsense until The Tormentor's biggest fan arrives asking for Mater's autograph, and an eager McQueen's offer of his own leaves the fan uncomfortable. Larry the Cable Guy voices Mater and Keith Ferguson McQueen, with Jess Harnell as Captain Collision, Jan Rabson as the I-Screamer, Simon Petrie as the Rasta Carian, James Rankin as Dr. Feel Bad, Danny Mann as the referee, Lance Henriksen as Paddy O'Concrete and Frank Welker as the monster. Uploaded to Disney Junior's YouTube channel in 2024, it drew about five million views.

title: The Wind Rises
tagline: We must live.
overview: A lifelong love of flight inspires Japanese aviation engineer Jiro Horikoshi, whose storied career includes the creation of the A-6M World War II fighter plane.
plot:
The Wind Rises (Japanese: Kaze Tachinu) is a 2013 Japanese animated historical drama film written and directed by Hayao Miyazaki, based on his own 2009 manga. Produced by Studio Ghibli and distributed by Toho, it features the voices of Hideaki Anno, Miori Takimoto, Hidetoshi Nishijima, Masahiko Nishimura and Nomura Mansai, and offers a fictionalized account of the life of aeronautical engineer Jiro Horikoshi, the designer of Japanese fighter aircraft before and during the Second World War.

As a nearsighted boy in 1918, Jiro realizes he can never be a pilot, but in recurring dreams the Italian aircraft designer Giovanni Battista Caproni tells him that building airplanes is better than flying them. Years later, while studying aeronautical engineering in Tokyo, Jiro is on a train when the Great Kantō earthquake strikes, and he helps a young girl, Nahoko Satomi, and her injured maid reach safety before parting without learning each other's names. After graduating, he and his friend Honjo join Mitsubishi, where their first fighter design breaks apart during testing. The company sends them to Germany to study the work of Hugo Junkers, and the visit shows them how far Japan lags behind. Back home, Jiro's next design also fails, and he takes a holiday at a resort in Karuizawa, where he meets the now grown-up Nahoko again. They fall in love, but she is suffering from tuberculosis. A German guest at the resort, critical of the Nazi regime, warns Jiro about the war to come, and his remarks later bring Jiro to the attention of the secret police, forcing him into hiding at the home of his supervisor, Kurokawa. Determined to share whatever time she has, Nahoko leaves a mountain sanatorium to marry Jiro, and the couple live together while he pours himself into a new fighter design for the Imperial Navy, torn between his beautiful dream of flight and the knowledge of what his machines will be used for.

The Wind Rises was met with critical acclaim, although it also provoked some political controversy and criticism in Asia. It won the Japan Academy Prize for Animation of the Year and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature and the Golden Globe Award for Best Foreign Language Film. It was originally intended to be Miyazaki's final feature film, before he reversed that decision and went on to direct The Boy and the Heron.

tagline: Based on a true story
overview: A young family moves into a historic home in Georgia, only to learn they are not the house's only inhabitants. Soon they find themselves in the presence of a secret rising from underground and threatening to bring down anyone in its path.
plot:
The Haunting in Connecticut 2: Ghosts of Georgia is a 2013 American supernatural horror film directed by Tom Elkins and written by David Coggeshall. A spiritual successor to The Haunting in Connecticut (2009) rather than a direct sequel, it stars Abigail Spencer and Chad Michael Murray as Lisa and Andy Wyrick, Emily Alyn Lind as their daughter Heidi, Katee Sackhoff as Lisa's sister Joyce and Cicely Tyson as Mama Kay. The story is loosely inspired by alleged events at the Wyrick family's home in Ellerslie, Georgia, described in the book The Veil: Heidi Wyrick's Story. It was released on home video in February 2013, with limited theatrical screenings.

Andy and Lisa Wyrick and their young daughter Heidi move into an old house on a large rural property in Ellerslie, hoping for a fresh start. Soon after they settle in, strange events begin. Heidi starts talking to a mysterious old man she calls Mr. Gordy, who seems friendly at first but becomes increasingly unsettling. Lisa, who has spent years suppressing her own psychic visions with medication, finds them returning, and she realizes that Heidi shares the same gift. Lisa's free-spirited sister Joyce, who lives in a trailer on the property, encourages Lisa to stop running from her abilities.

As the haunting intensifies, Heidi encounters more spirits and Lisa is tormented by visions of suffering and death. Investigating the history of the land, the family learns that the property was once a stop on the Underground Railroad, where a stationmaster sheltered escaped slaves on their way north. Lisa, Joyce and Andy uncover dark secrets about what really happened to some of the people who passed through, and about the stationmaster's own fate, and they turn for guidance to Mama Kay, an elderly woman with knowledge of the area's past. As the spirits draw Heidi deeper into their world, the family must discover which ghosts want to help and which want to harm, and confront a malevolent presence linked to terrible crimes committed on their land, before they lose their daughter.

The film received generally negative reviews, holding a 19 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 25. Critics praised Tyson's brief appearance and some atmospheric moments but found the scares formulaic and the story's treatment of its historical subject matter superficial.

title: Inside Out
tagline: Meet the little voices inside your head.
overview: Growing up can be a bumpy road, and it's no exception for Riley, who is uprooted from her Midwest life when her father starts a new job in San Francisco. Riley's guiding emotions— Joy, Fear, Anger, Disgust and Sadness—live in Headquarters, the control centre inside Riley's mind, where they help advise her through everyday life and tries to keep things positive, but the emotions conflict on how best to navigate a new city, house and school.
plot:
In the mind of a young girl named Riley Andersen are five personified emotions that influence her actions: Joy, Sadness, Fear, Disgust, and Anger. They process her experiences into memories stored as colored orbs in "Headquarters", her conscious mind, and send them into long-term memory each night. The aspects of the most important "core memories" within her personality take the form of five floating islands. Joy acts as the leader and tries to limit Sadness's influence, perceiving her as an unnecessary burden for Riley.
At age 11, Riley moves from Minnesota to San Francisco for her father's new job. On Riley's first day at her new school, Sadness retroactively saddens joyous memories, making Riley cry in front of her class. This creates Riley's first sad core memory. Joy tries to dispose of it using a pneumatic tube but knocks loose the other core memories during a struggle with Sadness, disabling the personality islands. Joy, Sadness, and the core memories are sucked out of Headquarters. In their absence, Anger, Fear, and Disgust attempt to create new happy core memories but push Riley away from her parents, friends, and favorite activities. Goofball, Friendship, and Hockey Island thus collapse into the Memory Dump, where forgotten things gradually disappear forever.
In the vast long-term memory area, Joy and Sadness encounter Bing Bong, Riley's childhood imaginary friend, who suggests riding the "train of thought" back to Headquarters. They miss it after Bing Bong naively leads them into Abstract Thought. In Imagination Land, which is under heavy renovations, Bing Bong bemoans Riley outgrowing him and rejects Joy's attempts to cheer him up in favor of Sadness's empathy. The trio catches the train, but it stops when Riley goes to sleep. At Dream Productions, Bing Bong is imprisoned in Subconscious for crashing a dream being filmed; Joy and Sadness get themselves arrested and free him as well as Jangles the Clown, Riley's scariest memory, frightening her awake. Meanwhile, Anger inserts an idea bulb into the console to make Riley run away to Minnesota, believing this will form new happy memories.
Honesty Island collapses after Riley steals her mother's credit card, leaving only Family Island and derailing the train. Joy tries to ride a "recall tube" back to Headquarters, but the ground below collapses, plunging her and Bing Bong into the Memory Dump. Joy discovers a sad memory of Riley losing an ice hockey game that turns happy when Riley's parents and friends comfort her. She realizes Sadness's purpose is to alert others when Riley is emotionally overwhelmed. Joy and Bing Bong try to use his song-fueled rocket wagon to escape the Memory Dump, but cannot ascend due to their combined weight. On the third attempt, Bing Bong jumps out of the wagon mid-ascent, fading away as Joy escapes to freedom.
Anger's idea bulb shorts out the console, putting Riley into depression as she boards a bus to Minnesota.

title: Cinderella
tagline: Midnight is just the beginning.
overview: When her father unexpectedly passes away, young Ella finds herself at the mercy of her cruel stepmother and her daughters. Never one to give up hope, Ella's fortunes begin to change after meeting a dashing stranger in the woods.
plot:
Cinderella is a 2015 American musical fantasy film directed by Kenneth Branagh, produced by Walt Disney Pictures, and based on the classic fairy tale of the same name. The film stars Lily James as Cinderella, Richard Madden as Prince Charming, Cate Blanchett as Lady Tremaine, and Helena Bonham Carter as Fairy Godmother.

The story begins with Cinderella's father, a widower, who marries Lady Tremaine (Cate Blanchett) and her two daughters, Drizella and Anastasia. After Cinderella's father passes away, Lady Tremaine treats Cinderella poorly, forcing her to do all the household chores while making her stepdaughters spoiled and lazy.

One day, an invitation arrives from the palace announcing a royal ball, where Prince Charming (Richard Madden) will be attending. Lady Tremaine is determined for one of her daughters to attend the ball and marry the prince, but Cinderella is not allowed to go.

Fairy Godmother (Helena Bonham Carter), who has been watching over Cinderella from afar, appears and helps Cinderella get ready for the ball by transforming a pumpkin into a beautiful carriage, mice into horses, and a rat into a coachman. She also gives Cinderella a stunning gown and off she goes to the palace.

At the ball, Cinderella and Prince Charming dance and fall in love, but Cinderella must leave before midnight when the magic wears off. In her haste, she loses one of her glass slippers, which Prince Charming finds and vows to find the girl whose foot fits it.

The next day, Prince Charming visits all the eligible maidens in the kingdom, trying the glass slipper on each foot until he finds Cinderella's. When he arrives at Cinderella's house, Lady Tremaine tries to fit her own daughters into the slipper, but it doesn't fit either of them. When Cinderella finally gets a chance to try the slipper, it fits perfectly.

Prince Charming and Cinderella get married in a grand ceremony, with Fairy Godmother watching over them. The film ends with Cinderella and Prince Charming living happily ever after, surrounded by their friends and family.

Throughout the film, Kenneth Branagh's direction brings a new level of depth and emotion to the classic story, while Lily James shines as the kind and gentle Cinderella. The film's visuals are stunning, with beautiful costumes and sets that bring the fairy tale world to life.

Meanwhile, Skipper is struggling with his own identity crisis as he tries to balance his racing career with being a mentor to Dusty. The two eventually form a bond, and Skipper becomes a valuable ally in Dusty's journey.

The film features stunning animation, heartwarming humor, and exciting action sequences. The voice cast delivers memorable performances, bringing the characters to life in a way that is both authentic and endearing.

As the story unfolds, Dusty faces off against El Chupacabra, who is revealed to be the main antagonist of the film. In a thrilling finale, Dusty uses his quick thinking and resourcefulness to outsmart El Chupacabra and cross the finish line first.

In the end, Dusty learns that being different doesn't make him any less special or capable. He returns home as a hero, with a newfound sense of confidence and purpose. The film concludes on a heartwarming note, with Dusty's friends celebrating his victory and Skipper proudly calling him "the fastest plane in the world."

Overall, Planes is a delightful animated adventure that explores themes of self-discovery, friendship, and perseverance. With its lovable characters, exciting action sequences, and stunning animation, it's a film that will leave audiences of all ages smiling and inspired.

title: Phantom
tagline: You will never see it coming.
overview: The haunted Captain of a Soviet submarine holds the fate of the world in his hands. Forced to leave his family behind, he is charged with leading a covert mission cloaked in mystery.
plot:
Phantom is a 2013 American independent thriller written and directed by Todd Robinson, set aboard a Soviet submarine during the Cold War. Ed Harris stars as a veteran Soviet captain, with David Duchovny, William Fichtner, Lance Henriksen and Johnathon Schaech in supporting roles. The story is loosely inspired by the real-life sinking of the Soviet submarine K-129 in 1968.

Captain Dmitri "Demi" Zubov is nearing the end of a career that has never matched the reputation of his legendary father, and he is haunted by an accident years earlier in which members of his crew died in a collision and fire. He is unexpectedly given command of his old diesel submarine for one last top secret mission. As Demi and his promising executive officer Alex Kozlov put to sea, they are joined by a KGB contingent led by the enigmatic Bruni, and a series of ominous signs suggests that the mission is not what it seems; the officer who gave Demi his orders takes his own life as the submarine departs.

Bruni's team has brought aboard an experimental device called the Phantom, which can alter the submarine's acoustic signature to make it sound like a merchant ship or any other vessel. Bruni eventually reveals that he and his men are rogue operatives acting without government orders. Fearing that a secret American program will make the United States immune to Soviet nuclear weapons, they intend to disguise the submarine as a Chinese vessel and launch a nuclear missile at the American Pacific Fleet, provoking a war between the United States and China. When Demi refuses to cooperate, he and his loyal officers are locked up. Demi and Kozlov lead the remaining crew in retaking the boat while two crewmen work to disable the warhead, and a desperate struggle breaks out on board even as another Soviet submarine closes in. The film ends with a final, more spiritual reckoning for the captain and his crew.

The film received generally negative reviews. Rotten Tomatoes reports a 26% approval rating from more than 50 critics, with a consensus noting that its solid cast cannot overcome a clunky, tension-free script. Richard Roeper praised Harris's performance as nomination-worthy while criticizing the rest of the film, The New York Times called it a Cold War howler of unpardonable monotony, and USA Today described it as a leaden thriller.

title: The Immigrant
overview: 1921 New York. An immigrant woman is tricked into a life of burlesque and vaudeville until a dazzling magician tries to save her and reunite her with her sister who is being held in the confines of Ellis Island.
plot:
The Immigrant is a 2013 American period drama directed by James Gray, who co-wrote the screenplay with Richard Menello. Marion Cotillard stars as a young Polish woman who arrives in New York in 1921, with Joaquin Phoenix and Jeremy Renner as the two men who vie for her, and Angela Sarafyan and Dagmara Domińczyk in supporting roles.

Ewa Cybulska and her sister Magda, Polish Catholics fleeing the devastation of post-World War I Poland, arrive at Ellis Island in search of a better life. Magda is diagnosed with a lung disease and held in the island's infirmary, and Ewa, accused of loose morals during the voyage, faces deportation. She is rescued by Bruno Weiss, a smooth-talking man who claims to work for a travelers' aid society and bribes a guard to release her. Bruno takes Ewa to his Lower East Side apartment and gives her work as a seamstress and dancer at the burlesque theater he manages, but he soon reveals himself to be a pimp. Desperate to raise the money needed to free Magda, and rejected by her aunt and uncle, Ewa is drawn into prostitution under his control.

Ewa's prospects seem to change when she meets Orlando, a charming stage magician who is also Bruno's cousin and rival. Orlando falls for her and promises to take her away to California, provoking Bruno's jealousy. The rivalry between the cousins escalates, culminating in a violent confrontation in which Bruno kills Orlando. Ewa is suspected of the crime, and with the police hunting them, Bruno, consumed by guilt and his own love for Ewa, comes to recognize the damage he has done. In a final act of atonement, he arranges for Magda's release so that the sisters can leave together, and the film ends as Ewa and Magda depart by boat while Bruno walks away alone, a sequence framed in a single celebrated shot.

The film was shot in New York City in early 2012. Harvey Weinstein acquired US distribution rights and pressed Gray to change the ending; Gray refused. The director's cut premiered in competition for the Palme d'Or at the 2013 Cannes Film Festival, but The Weinstein Company gave it only a limited US release in May 2014 with little promotion, and it grossed about $5.9 million worldwide. Reviews were generally positive, with special praise for Darius Khondji's cinematography and Cotillard's performance, which won Best Actress awards from the National Society of Film Critics and the New York Film Critics Circle.

Meanwhile, Theodore is struggling with his feelings for his ex-wife, Catherine (played by Rooney Mara), who has moved on with her life.

One of the most interesting aspects of Her is its exploration of loneliness and human connection in a world where technology has made it easier to interact with others but also more isolating. The film raises questions about what it means to be lonely and whether technology can truly fill that void.

As the story reaches its climax, Theodore and Samantha's relationship becomes increasingly complicated. They face challenges like jealousy, possessiveness, and even a crisis of identity. In the end, Theodore is forced to confront the reality of his relationship with Samantha and decide what he wants from life.

The ending of Her is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the nature of love, relationships, and what it means to be human. The film's conclusion suggests that Theodore has found a new sense of purpose and connection with Samantha, but also acknowledges the complexity and uncertainty of their relationship.

Overall, Her is a thought-provoking and emotionally charged film that explores the complexities of human relationships in a world where technology is increasingly integrated into our lives.

title: Devil's Knot
tagline: They say the crimes were satanic. The truth may be scarier.
overview: The savage murders of three young children sparks a controversial trial of three teenagers accused of killing the kids as part of a satanic ritual.
plot:
Devil's Knot is a 2013 American biographical crime drama directed by Atom Egoyan, adapted by Paul Harris Boardman and Scott Derrickson from Mara Leveritt's 2002 book of the same name. Reese Witherspoon stars as Pam Hobbs, the mother of one of the murdered children, and Colin Firth as Ron Lax, a private investigator, with Dane DeHaan, Mireille Enos, Bruce Greenwood, Elias Koteas, Stephen Moyer and Alessandro Nivola. The film dramatizes the case of the West Memphis Three, three teenagers convicted of murdering three young boys amid the Satanic panic of the early 1990s.

In 1993, in the working-class, deeply religious community of West Memphis, Arkansas, three eight-year-old boys, Stevie Branch, Christopher Byers and Michael Moore, disappear. Their bound and beaten bodies are found the following day. Because of the brutal nature of the crime, the community and the police quickly become convinced that the killings were the work of a satanic cult.

A month later, three teenagers, Damien Echols, Jason Baldwin and Jessie Misskelley Jr., are arrested after Misskelley confesses following twelve hours of police interrogation. Ron Lax, a private investigator who comes to work with the defense, uncovers inconsistencies in the evidence, mishandled clues and alternative suspects, while Pam Hobbs, grieving for her son Stevie, begins to have doubts about the guilt of the accused. Despite the weakness of the case and the defendants' insistence on their innocence, Baldwin and Misskelley are sentenced to life in prison and Echols to death. The film ends by noting that the three men were released in 2011 after nearly two decades in prison by entering Alford pleas, under which they remain convicted felons, and that questions about the case remain unanswered.

The case had previously been the subject of the acclaimed Paradise Lost documentary series and the documentary West of Memphis, which the film's critics frequently cited.

Devil's Knot was filmed in Georgia in 2012 and premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 8, 2013. It received mostly negative reviews, with 26 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus noted that the story had already been covered by more compelling documentaries, and a Metacritic score of 42.

title: Wicked Minds
overview: Holden returns home from college and is surprised to find his overpowering competitive father married to a much younger woman Lana. Holden quickly falls for the beauty and charisma of his step mother. A passionate affair begins between son and stepmother.
plot:
Wicked Minds, also known as Paranoia, is a 2003 Canadian-American erotic thriller television film directed by Jason Hreno, whose credits also include Poison Ivy: The Secret Society, from a screenplay by Turi Meyer and Al Septien. Produced by Hearst Entertainment Productions, Incendo Productions and JB Media and running about 92 minutes, it stars Andrew W. Walker and Angie Everhart, with Winston Rekert, Amy Sloan, Frank Schorpion, Ellen David, Conrad Pla and Alan Fawcett in supporting roles. Although its DVD release was marketed as unrated, the film was made for television, and its fade-outs for commercial breaks remain visible.

Holden Price (Walker) comes home after his studies at Harvard and is surprised to discover that his father (Rekert), a wealthy, domineering and fiercely competitive man, has married Lana (Everhart), a woman much younger than himself. Their first meeting is an awkward one, as Holden walks in on her in the shower. Because his father is a workaholic who is seldom at home, Holden and Lana end up spending a great deal of time together, and he is soon drawn to her beauty and charisma. The two begin a passionate affair. When Holden learns that his hot-tempered father has been abusive toward Lana, he becomes visibly upset. Then his father is found dead, and both the son and his lover become suspects in the murder. The second half of the story turns into a whodunit built on a series of twists and double-crosses, in which the naive young man turns out to have been drawn into Lana's game.

The film drew middling notices. In The Great Canadian Guide to the Movies & TV, it received two and a half stars out of four and was described as a reasonably entertaining, noirish suspense drama with nice performances from Rekert and Everhart, though the reviewer felt the twists and double-crosses of its second half undermined the character drama established in the first. The Video Vacuum gave it two stars, finding the opening set-up solid and some of the romantic scenes effective, and crediting the chemistry between Everhart and Walker, who it said did a fine job as the naive son drawn into her game, but criticizing the dawdling pace of the second act and the telegraphed plot twists, and arguing that Hreno handled the seduction scenes better than the mystery and its tension.

title: Underdogs
tagline: There's only one team this summer.
overview: In the small village where Amadeo lives there is no one good enough to challenge his skills at Table Football. But, while Amadeo may be a genius as a table football player in real life he's a loser. He's in love with Lara, his childhood friend, but he's so shy that he can't bring himself to confess his love for her. So he just hangs out in his quaint, timeless village. When Amadeo beats the village bully Flash at Table Football. The scene is set for an epic rivalry. Consumed with anger Flash vows to get even and 10 years later he returns as an International Superstar, a Football Icon and Galatico determined to wreak his revenge.
plot:
Underdogs (Spanish: Metegol, meaning "table football"; released in the United Kingdom as The Unbeatables) is a 2013 Argentine-Spanish animated sports comedy film co-written, produced, directed and edited by Juan José Campanella. It is loosely based on the short story "Memorias de un wing derecho" ("Memoirs of a Right Winger") by Argentine writer Roberto Fontanarrosa, and Campanella developed the screenplay with co-writer and producer Gaston Gorali and Eduardo Sacheri, his collaborator on The Secret in Their Eyes. Costing $21 million, it became the most expensive Argentine film ever made and the most expensive Latin American animated feature.

A father tucking his son into bed tells him a story, asking him to use his imagination. Years earlier, in a quiet little town, a shy boy named Amadeo works in a bar and is the best table football player around. He is secretly in love with Laura, a girl he met there. One day a bully named Grosso challenges him to a match in front of her, and despite his reluctance Amadeo wins to the applause of the whole bar. The humiliated Grosso is soon taken on by a manager, and seven years later he returns as the most famous soccer player in the world, determined to avenge the only defeat of his life. He buys the entire town, sending the mayor fleeing by helicopter, builds a gigantic stadium on its site, plans to tear down the bar where he lost, takes possession of the old table and sets out to win Laura's affection. Just when Amadeo has lost everything, he discovers something magical: the little players of his table football game come to life, able to talk and make plans. Together they set off on an adventure to rescue Laura and save the town, and along the way they learn to become a real team. Amadeo then forms a soccer team of his own and challenges Grosso's squad to a match for the town's future, in which skill, teamwork and sportsmanship are put to the test against Grosso's arrogance.

Released by Universal Pictures in Argentina on 18 July 2013, the film opened at number one with a record opening for an Argentine film, outperforming Despicable Me 2 and Monsters University. An English version reached British cinemas in August 2014, while the North American version, voiced by a cast including Ariana Grande, Nicholas Hoult and Mel Brooks, was released on Netflix and on DVD in 2016 after a planned theatrical release was scrapped. The original version was well received, while the American version earned mixed reviews.

title: The Angry Birds Movie
tagline: Why so angry?
overview: An island populated entirely by happy, flightless birds or almost entirely. In this paradise, Red, a bird with a temper problem, speedy Chuck, and the volatile Bomb have always been outsiders. But when the island is visited by mysterious green piggies, it’s up to these unlikely outcasts to figure out what the pigs are up to.
plot:
The Angry Birds Movie is a 3D animated comedy-adventure film directed by Fergal Reilly and Clay Kaytis, and produced by Sony Pictures Animation. The movie was released on May 20, 2016.

In the beginning of the story, we are introduced to the main character, Red (voiced by Jason Sudeikis), a hot-headed but lovable bird who lives in a forest filled with birds. Red is known for his temper and his ability to get into fights with other birds. However, he has a soft spot for his friends, particularly Chuck (voiced by Josh Gad) and Bomb (voiced by Danny McBride).

The story takes a turn when the evil pig, Hamish (voiced by Bill Hader), steals the magical crystal that keeps the forest's ecosystem in balance. The crystal is hidden on an island called Bird Island, which is inhabited by birds who are obsessed with being perfect and following rules.

Red, Chuck, and Bomb decide to embark on a journey to retrieve the crystal and save their home from destruction. Along the way, they meet new friends, including Matilda (voiced by Maya Rudolph), a wise-cracking bird who becomes Red's love interest, and Guy (voiced by Danny McBride), a laid-back bird who is initially hesitant to join the group.

As they journey through the forest, the birds encounter various obstacles and challenges, including treacherous terrain, fierce predators, and rival birds. However, with their unique skills and teamwork, they are able to overcome these challenges and get closer to their goal.

Meanwhile, Hamish's plan is revealed: he intends to use the crystal to take over the world by building a massive fortress on Bird Island. The birds must stop him before it's too late.

The plot development of the movie takes a dramatic turn when Red discovers that his temper is actually a strength in disguise. He learns to control his emotions and work with his friends to overcome their differences and achieve their goal.

In the end, the birds successfully retrieve the crystal and defeat Hamish's fortress. However, instead of destroying it, they decide to use its power to create a new ecosystem that balances nature and technology. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Red and Matilda sharing a romantic moment, and the other birds learning to appreciate their unique qualities.

Overall, The Angry Birds Movie is a fun and entertaining film that explores themes of friendship, teamwork, and self-acceptance. With its colorful animation, witty humor, and lovable characters, it's a great movie for both kids and adults.

title: The Tower
tagline: Tower Sky. 108 Stories. Survive at any cost.
overview: On Christmas Eve at Tower Sky, an ultra-luxurious building complex, a White Christmas party is held to dazzle its equally high-end tenants and VIP guests. Dae-ho, the manager of the building and single father, is forced to cancel plans with his daughter Hana to work the event. His Christmas is saved when Yoon-hee, the food mall manager with a secret crush on Dae-ho, offers to babysit Hana during the party. Meanwhile, Young-ki the legendary fire chief of Yoido Station has finally promised his first holiday date night to his long suffering wife. The party is in full swing with the spectacular sight of two helicopters flying overhead just to spray snow on the partygoers and make everything perfect. When unthinkable disaster strikes, Dae-ho and Young-ki must summon all their strength and courage to save the lives of thousands but at what cost to themselves and their loved ones?
plot:
The Tower (Korean: 타워) is a 2012 South Korean disaster thriller directed by Kim Ji-hoon. Sol Kyung-gu, Son Ye-jin and Kim Sang-kyung star, with Ahn Sung-ki, Do Ji-han and Jo Min-ah among the supporting cast. Often compared to the American disaster classic The Towering Inferno, it depicts a fire that engulfs a luxury skyscraper in central Seoul on Christmas Eve after a helicopter accident. The film was released in South Korean cinemas on 25 December 2012.

Lee Dae-ho is a widowed father and the facilities manager of Tower Sky, a towering twin-tower residential and commercial complex in the Yeouido district of Seoul. He has promised to spend Christmas Eve with his young daughter Ha-na, but he is ordered to oversee preparations for a lavish party hosted by the building's owner for tenants, VIPs and politicians. Dae-ho has feelings for Seo Yoon-hee, the restaurant manager who agrees to look after Ha-na while he works. During inspections he discovers that the sprinkler system in one tower is not working because of frozen pipes, but the owner and his safety chief ignore the risk and strong wind forecasts and insist that the event go ahead.

During the party, helicopters scattering artificial snow over the building are caught in powerful updrafts and lose control. One crashes into the tower, setting off a fire and explosions that spread quickly through the upper floors, trapping hundreds of people, including Ha-na and Yoon-hee. Firefighters led by the veteran captain Kang Young-ki, a dedicated officer who has spent Christmas on duty rather than with his wife, race to the building. As the fire spreads and the structure weakens, Dae-ho uses his knowledge of the complex to lead a group of survivors toward safety, while Young-ki and his crew, including an inexperienced rookie, risk their lives in increasingly desperate rescue attempts, and the authorities consider drastic measures to keep the burning tower from collapsing onto its twin.

The Tower was a commercial success in South Korea, attracting more than five million admissions, and it was praised for its visual effects, which were produced largely in-house and were considered a technical milestone for Korean disaster films. Critics found the story familiar but enjoyed its large-scale action sequences and the performances of the leads.

title: The Drop
overview: Bob Saginowski finds himself at the center of a robbery gone awry and entwined in an investigation that digs deep into the neighborhood's past where friends, families, and foes all work together to make a living - no matter the cost.
plot:
The Drop is a 2014 American crime drama film directed by Michaël R. Roskam and written by Dennis Lehane, based on his own novel of the same name.

The story revolves around Tom Hardy's character, Bob Saginowski (also known as "Sagi"), a bartender at a small bar in Brooklyn, New York. Sagi is a quiet, introverted man who lives with his cousin, Nick (James Gandolfini), and their mother, Auntie Peg (Catherine Keener). The three of them form an unlikely family unit.

The plot begins with Sagi's life seemingly ordinary: he works at the bar, hangs out with his friends, and takes care of his aunt. However, everything changes when a young man named Toby Flender (Tom Hardy) walks into the bar, looking for a place to hide from some unsavory characters. Sagi takes pity on Toby and offers him a place to stay.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Toby is in deep trouble with some local gangsters who are demanding money from him. Sagi's life begins to spiral out of control as he tries to help Toby avoid his debtors. The situation escalates when Toby's associates start showing up at the bar, looking for him.

Meanwhile, Nick's health begins to decline, and Auntie Peg becomes increasingly dependent on Sagi. As the tension builds, Sagi finds himself caught between his loyalty to his family and his desire to protect Toby from harm.

The plot reaches its climax when Sagi discovers that Toby is in grave danger. In a tense confrontation, Sagi must use all his wits and resourcefulness to outsmart the gangsters and keep Toby safe. The film's ending is both heart-wrenching and redemptive, as Sagi finds a way to save Toby but ultimately loses himself in the process.

Throughout the film, Tom Hardy delivers a nuanced performance as Sagi, bringing depth and complexity to his character. James Gandolfini also shines as Nick, conveying a sense of vulnerability and desperation. The supporting cast, including Catherine Keener and David Dastmalchian, add to the film's emotional resonance.

The Drop is a gripping drama that explores themes of family, loyalty, and redemption. With its tight script, strong performances, and tense plot, it's no wonder this film received critical acclaim upon its release.

title: The Equalizer
tagline: What do you see when you look at me?
overview: McCall believes he has put his mysterious past behind him and dedicated himself to beginning a new, quiet life. plot:
The Equalizer is a 2014 American action-thriller film directed by Antoine Fuqua and written by Richard Wenk. The movie stars Denzel Washington as Robert McCall, a retired CIA operative who uses his skills to help those in need.

The story begins with Robert McCall (Denzel Washington), a quiet and unassuming man living in Boston. He spends most of his days working at Home Depot, where he befriends a young woman named Susan Plummer (Chloë Moretz). Susan is being harassed by her abusive boyfriend, Teddy Madsen (Marton Csokas), who has also been threatening her family.

When Susan's life is in danger, Robert steps in to help her. He uses his skills and resources to gather information about Teddy's past and expose him for the manipulative and violent person he is. As Robert delves deeper into Teddy's world, he discovers that he was involved in a human trafficking ring and has been using his wealth and influence to exploit vulnerable women.

As Robert gets closer to the truth, he attracts the attention of Teddy's associates, who begin to hunt him down. With the help of Susan and her family, Robert must use his skills as a former CIA operative to take down Teddy and his cohorts.

Throughout the movie, Robert's character is revealed through flashbacks, showing his time in the CIA and his experiences during the Cold War. We see that he was once a highly skilled operative who worked undercover, but after leaving the agency, he retired from the spy game and tried to live a quiet life.

As the story unfolds, Robert faces off against Teddy's men in a series of intense battles. He uses his knowledge of hand-to-hand combat and marksmanship to take down his opponents, often using unconventional methods to outsmart them.

In the climactic final confrontation, Robert faces off against Teddy in a tense showdown. With the help of Susan and her family, Robert is able to expose Teddy's true nature and bring him to justice.

The movie ends with Robert reflecting on his actions and the consequences of his decisions. He realizes that he has been living a lie, pretending to be an ordinary man when in reality, he was always meant for something more. The film concludes with Robert walking away from the chaos, ready to start anew and leave his past life behind.

Overall, The Equalizer is a gripping action-thriller that showcases Denzel Washington's signature style and charisma. With its intricate plot and well-developed characters, the movie keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

plot:
The Kings of Summer is a 2013 American coming-of-age comedy-drama film directed by Jordan Vogt-Roberts. The movie follows the story of Joe Toy, a teenager who runs away from home with his best friend Patrick to build a shelter in the woods and live off the land.

At its core, The Kings of Summer explores themes of rebellion, self-discovery, and the struggle for independence. Joe's decision to leave home is motivated by a desire to break free from the constraints of his family life and forge his own path in life. As he navigates the challenges of living in the wilderness, Joe must confront his own vulnerabilities and learn to rely on himself and his friend.

The film also delves into the complexities of male friendship and the ways in which boys navigate their relationships with each other during adolescence. Patrick's character serves as a foil to Joe's, highlighting the tensions and conflicts that can arise when two friends are forced to confront their own desires and needs.

Furthermore, The Kings of Summer touches on themes of identity and belonging. As Joe and Patrick try to create a new life for themselves in the woods, they must also navigate their relationships with the outside world and figure out where they fit into it. This is particularly evident in the character of Joe's father, who represents a more traditional and established way of life that Joe feels stifling.

Throughout the film, Vogt-Roberts uses humor and wit to explore these themes, often using satire and irony to highlight the absurdities and challenges of adolescence. Ultimately, The Kings of Summer is a heartwarming and relatable portrayal of growing up, self-discovery, and the power of male friendship.

title: Death Race: Inferno
tagline: Welcome to the Inferno
overview: Carl Lucas / Frankenstein has won four of his races and needs to win one more to win his freedom. Before his final race, Lucas and his team, car and all, are transferred to another prison where they will compete in a Death Race in the desert. Also, at the same time, Ceaser runs into a marketer who wants to franchise the Death Race program.
plot:
Death Race: Inferno, also titled Death Race 3: Inferno, is an American science fiction action film of 2013 directed by Roel Reiné and produced by Paul W. S. Anderson. The third entry in the Death Race series, it is set between Death Race 2 (2010) and the original Death Race (2008). Luke Goss returns as Carl Lucas, the masked driver Frankenstein, with Tanit Phoenix as Katrina Banks, Danny Trejo as Goldberg, Fred Koehler as Lists, Ving Rhames as R. H. Weyland, Dougray Scott as Niles York, Robin Shou as 14K and Hlubi Mboya as Satana.

Weyland has lost the rights to the Death Race through a hostile takeover by York, a British billionaire who moves the event to South Africa. Before leaving, Weyland arranges for Lucas's disfigured face to be repaired. Lucas is a single win from freedom, and York, fearing the loss of Frankenstein's huge fan base, threatens to kill him if he wins. In South Africa a brawl knocks off Lucas's mask, showing Katrina, Goldberg and Lists that he has been hiding behind it all along, and Katrina turns away from him. Female navigators fight to the death in a gladiatorial contest, and every racer is implanted with a GPS tracker so that escape means death. In the first race, across the Kalahari Desert, Razor beats Frankenstein. Goldberg begins a romance with the show's surgeon, Olivia, and Lucas privately wins back his team's trust, telling them he has made a new deal.

Lucas takes the second race, but Goldberg seems to die in an explosion caused by stray gunfire from local warlords. York warns Lucas to lose the final race or Katrina will be tortured, while Satana learns York means to push her aside. In the last race 14K's flares deflect a missile York fires at Lucas, who then abandons his lead to 14K and drives with Katrina into the control room, where Satana has handcuffed York. In hospital a burned survivor screams that he is York, but his tracker identifies him as Frankenstein. Lucas had secretly allied with Weyland, whose insider Olivia faked Goldberg's death and planted Frankenstein's tracker in York; Lucas and Katrina leapt clear before the crash and are declared dead. Weyland regains the race and frees the team, who head for a beach resort, while York must race as Frankenstein on Terminal Island.

The film went straight to home video in January 2013, followed by Death Race: Beyond Anarchy in 2018. Reviews were mixed; DVD Talk called it great mindless fun, while DVD Verdict found it a loud and tedious chore.
