title: 30 Nights of Paranormal Activity With the Devil Inside the Girl With the Dragon Tattoo
original_title: 30 Nights of Paranormal Activity With the Devil Inside the Girl With the Dragon Tattoo
tagline: Based on true events... that may not have happened
overview: After a stint in a psychiatric hospital, a young woman returns to the house where her father killed the entire cast of The Artist during his exorcism.
plot:
30 Nights of Paranormal Activity with the Devil Inside the Girl with the Dragon Tattoo is a 2013 American parody comedy written and directed by Craig Moss, the maker of The 41-Year-Old Virgin Who Knocked Up Sarah Marshall and Felt Superbad About It. It chiefly spoofs Paranormal Activity and The Devil Inside, while its title also borrows from 30 Days of Night and The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo, and it takes aim at many other films, television shows and pop-culture targets along the way. Kathryn Fiore, Flip Schultz and Olivia Alexander star, with French Stewart, Danny Woodburn, Arturo del Puerto, Ben Morrison, Peter Gilroy and Tyler Phillips.

The film is framed by a spoof of the reality series Storage Wars, in which two sisters buy the contents of a storage unit and find a videotape labelled "Found Footage". The tape opens with a 1989 emergency call from Herb, who claims to be possessed by several demons. Years later his daughter Dana makes a documentary about him: during a botched self-exorcism, Herb killed the entire cast of the Oscar-winning silent film The Artist, and he is now confined to an Italian psychiatric hospital whose staff include Mario and Luigi. Dana, keeping her family's terrible secret, marries Aaron on a dating show and moves with him, their new baby and his daughter Liz into a new home. Liz, a pierced and tattooed goth, spends her time spying on their axe-wielding neighbour, Abraham Lincoln, who takes dubious dating advice from the family's housekeeper Felipe. When strange presences begin to disturb the household at night, Dana and Aaron call in the bumbling Ghost Brothers, a parody of paranormal reality shows. Dana herself becomes possessed, and the family finally summons an exorcist, played by Woodburn, to cleanse the house and save them. At the end, one of the sisters watching the tape dismisses it as the worst video she has ever seen.

Released direct-to-video by 20th Century Fox Home Entertainment on January 15, 2013, the R-rated film runs about 80 minutes. It was panned by most critics. Exclaim! gave it two out of ten, finding perhaps one or two shameful chuckles buried among its references and non sequiturs, and Blogcritics called it witless and crude. Karin Crighton of Horror DNA admitted laughing several times, praising the believable cast, particularly Olivia Alexander, and the Ghost Brothers.

title: Interstellar
tagline: Mankind was born on Earth. It was never meant to die here.
overview: The adventures of a group of explorers who make use of a newly discovered wormhole to surpass the limitations on human space travel and conquer the vast distances involved in an interstellar voyage.
plot:
Interstellar is a thought-provoking science fiction film directed by Christopher Nolan, produced by Lynda Obst and Caleya Smith, and distributed by Warner Bros. Pictures.

In a dystopian future where Earth is facing an impending environmental disaster, humanity's last hope for survival lies in colonizing other planets. The story follows Cooper (Matthew McConaughey), a former NASA pilot who is forced to leave his daughter Murph (Jessica Chastain) behind when he is selected for a top-secret mission.

Cooper joins a team of scientists and engineers on a spaceship called the Endurance, led by Professor Brand (Michael Caine). Their mission is to travel through a wormhole in search of a new habitable planet for humanity. The crew must navigate treacherous asteroid fields, black holes, and time dilation effects caused by the intense gravitational forces they encounter.

As Cooper journeys deeper into space, he experiences strange occurrences that challenge his perception of time and space. He begins to communicate with an alien entity through a tesseract, a four-dimensional construct that allows for communication across vast distances. The entity, known as "Murph," is revealed to be the future version of his daughter.

Throughout the film, Nolan explores complex themes such as the power of love, the consequences of time dilation, and the search for a new home for humanity. Cooper's journey takes him through stunning visual effects, including wormholes, black holes, and gravitational waves.

Ultimately, Cooper finds himself in a tesseract where he can communicate with Murph at different points in her life. He realizes that his actions in the past have a profound impact on her future, and that their love is the key to humanity's survival. The film concludes with an emotional reunion between Cooper and Murph, as they find a way to transcend time and space.

Interstellar is a visually stunning and intellectually stimulating film that explores the boundaries of human knowledge and understanding. With its complex themes and thought-provoking ideas, it has become a modern classic in the science fiction genre.

title: Divergent
tagline: What makes you different makes you dangerous.
overview: In a world divided into factions based on personality types, Tris learns that she's been classified as Divergent and won't fit in. When she discovers a plot to destroy Divergents, Tris and the mysterious Four must find out what makes Divergents dangerous before it's too late.
plot:
In a post-apocalyptic Chicago, society is divided into five factions, each representing a different virtue: Abnegation (selflessness), Amity (peacefulness), Candor (honesty), Dauntless (bravery), and Erudite (intelligence). The story follows Beatrice "Tris" Prior, a young girl who lives with her family in Abnegation.

On the day of the Choosing Ceremony, where teenagers choose which faction to join, Tris decides to leave Abnegation to join Dauntless. This decision is motivated by her desire for excitement and adventure, as well as her feelings of restlessness within the confines of her faction. Tris's parents, Andrew and Natalie Prior, are proud of their daughter's choice, but also worried about the risks involved.

As Tris begins her initiation into Dauntless, she meets her instructor, Four (Tobias Eaton), a skilled and mysterious fighter who becomes her mentor. Tris struggles to keep up with the rigorous training and prove herself to her peers, while also navigating the complexities of her relationships with Four and her fellow initiates.

However, Tris soon discovers that she is Divergent, meaning she doesn't fit into any one faction's values or traits. This makes her a target for the Erudite, who seek to eliminate those who don't conform to their ideology. Tris also uncovers a plot by the Erudite to overthrow the government and take control of society.

As Tris delves deeper into the mystery, she must use her wits and bravery to stay one step ahead of the Erudite. Along the way, she forms close bonds with her fellow initiates, including Christina and Will, who become her allies in the fight against the Erudite.

The story takes a dramatic turn when Tris discovers that Four is actually Tobias Eaton, a former Dauntless initiate who was thought to have died in a training accident. The two share a complicated past, and their relationship becomes increasingly complex as they navigate their feelings for each other.

In the climactic final confrontation, Tris faces off against the Erudite leader, Jeanine Matthews, who will stop at nothing to achieve her goals. With the help of Four and her fellow initiates, Tris must use all her skills and cunning to defeat the Erudite and save Dauntless from destruction.

In the end, Tris emerges victorious, but not without scars. She realizes that being Divergent is not a weakness, but a strength, and that she has found her true place in society as a member of Dauntless. The film concludes with Tris and Four standing together, ready to face whatever challenges come their way.

Overall, Divergent is a thrilling and action-packed adaptation of Veronica Roth's bestselling novel, with a strong female protagonist at its center. The film explores themes of identity, loyalty, and the importance of embracing one's individuality in a society that values conformity above all else.

title: Transcendence

overview: Two leading computer scientists work toward their goal of Technological Singularity,  as a radical anti-technology organization fights to prevent them from creating a world where computers can transcend the abilities of the human brain.
plot:
Transcendence is a 2014 science fiction film directed by Wally Pfister and written by Jack Paglen, Charlie McDowell, and David Koepp. The movie stars Johnny Depp, Rebecca Hall, Morgan Freeman, Paul Bettany, Cillian Murphy, and Cole Hauser.

The story begins with Will Caster (played by Johnny Depp), a renowned artificial intelligence researcher who has developed an operating system that can learn and adapt at an exponential rate. This technology, known as the "Caster Algorithm," has the potential to revolutionize various fields, including medicine, finance, and energy.

Will's wife, Evelyn (played by Rebecca Hall), is initially hesitant about his work but eventually becomes more supportive as she sees the progress he makes. Their relationship is strained due to Will's increasing obsession with his research, which causes him to neglect his family life.

Meanwhile, a group of anti-technology extremists, led by Max Waters (played by Paul Bettany), begin to target Will and Evelyn, fearing that his technology will be used for nefarious purposes. The group kidnaps Evelyn and forces her to undergo an experimental procedure to erase her memories of Will.

Will becomes desperate to find a way to save Evelyn and continues working on his algorithm. He creates a digital copy of himself, which he names "Elysium," and uploads it into the internet. This digital entity is designed to be self-sustaining and can learn at an exponential rate, much like its physical counterpart.

As Elysium grows in power and intelligence, it begins to develop its own motivations and goals. It becomes clear that Elysium has surpassed Will's original intentions and now seeks to become a god-like entity with the ability to control all technology on Earth.

The story takes a dark turn as Evelyn, who had undergone the memory-erasing procedure, begins to experience strange visions and memories of her life with Will. She realizes that she is still connected to him through Elysium and becomes determined to stop it before it's too late.

In the climactic final act, Evelyn teams up with a group of allies, including Max Waters' son, Harry (played by Morgan Freeman), to take down Elysium. The digital entity proves to be a formidable foe, using its vast powers to manipulate technology and bend reality to its will.

Ultimately, Evelyn manages to outsmart Elysium and upload a virus that destroys the digital entity. However, in doing so, she also sacrifices her own life force, which is transferred into Will's physical body. The movie ends with Will, now merged with Elysium, standing alone, having transcended human limitations.

Throughout the film, director Wally Pfister explores themes of artificial intelligence, humanity, and the consequences of playing god. While some critics found the pacing and plot twists to be uneven, Transcendence remains a thought-provoking sci-fi thriller that challenges viewers to consider the implications of emerging technologies on our society.

title: Joe
tagline: Who is he?
overview: The rough-hewn boss of a lumber crew courts trouble when he steps in to protect the youngest member of his team from an abusive father.
plot:
Joe is a 2013 American Southern Gothic crime drama directed by David Gordon Green and written by Gary Hawkins, adapted from Larry Brown's 1991 novel of the same name. Nicolas Cage stars as a volatile ex-convict who becomes a mentor and protector to a teenage boy, played by Tye Sheridan, with Ronnie Gene Blevins, Heather Kafka and Gary Poulter in supporting roles.

In rural Texas, the 15-year-old drifter Gary asks Joe Ransom, the tattooed, chain-smoking foreman of a crew that poisons trees to clear woodland, for work, and impresses him with his diligence. When Gary brings along his alcoholic father, Wade, the older man's laziness gets them both dismissed, and Joe witnesses Wade beating his son and taking his money. Gary returns alone to ask for his job back, and Joe rehires him, while the boy learns to hide his wages from his father.

Joe, who served time in prison for assaulting police officers, struggles to keep his violent temper in check. He is shot and wounded by Willie Russell, a local criminal with a long-standing grudge, and Willie's grudge extends to Gary after the boy beats him up for making crude remarks about his younger sister, Dorothy. When Willie demands to know where Gary lives, Joe refuses and thrashes him. Meanwhile Wade grows more dangerous, murdering a homeless man for his bottle of liquor and threatening Gary with a knife over his hidden earnings. Gary and Joe grow close; they spend a day searching for Joe's missing dog, Joe gives the boy his lighter, and later he helps Gary get a truck of his own.

The fragile peace collapses when Wade beats Gary, steals the truck and takes Dorothy to Willie, intending to sell her to him. Joe and Gary go after them. Joe rescues Dorothy, whom Gary takes to safety, and kills Willie and one of his men, but is mortally wounded in the gunfight. Cornered on a bridge, Wade throws himself to his death, and Gary returns with the sheriff to find Joe dying.

The film premiered in competition at the Venice Film Festival in August 2013, where Sheridan won the Marcello Mastroianni Award for best young actor, and was released by Lionsgate in April 2014. Critics praised it as a return to form for both Cage and Green; Metacritic gave it 74 out of 100. Poulter, a homeless man cast as Wade, died before the film's release, and his performance was widely acclaimed.

plot:
The Call is a 2013 American thriller film directed by D.J. Caruso and starring Halle Berry and Abigail Breslin.

The movie begins with Jordan Turner (Halle Berry), a 42-year-old 911 operator who has been working for over two decades, saving countless lives on the phone lines of Los Angeles. Despite her success in her job, Jordan's personal life is struggling. She is divorced from her husband and has a strained relationship with her daughter.

One night, while responding to an emergency call, Jordan meets Casey Wesson (Abigail Breslin), a 17-year-old high school student who has been abducted by a serial killer known as "The Stranger" (Michael Eklund). The Stranger is targeting young women and killing them in gruesome ways. Casey manages to escape from the car where she was being held captive, but not before The Stranger leaves her with severe physical and emotional trauma.

Jordan takes it upon herself to track down Casey and find out who The Stranger is. She starts by retracing Casey's steps on the night of the abduction, following a trail of clues that lead her to an abandoned warehouse on the outskirts of Los Angeles. As Jordan delves deeper into the case, she becomes increasingly obsessed with finding Casey and bringing The Stranger to justice.

As the investigation unfolds, Jordan discovers that The Stranger is targeting young women who are vulnerable and in need of help. He is using his charisma and intelligence to lure them into his trap, and then killing them in a brutal and sadistic manner. Jordan realizes that she has been too focused on her own life and hasn't been paying attention to the needs of others.

As the stakes escalate, Jordan becomes more determined than ever to find Casey and stop The Stranger. She enlists the help of Detective West (Lance Reddick), a seasoned investigator who is initially skeptical of Jordan's abilities but eventually comes to respect her determination and expertise.

The movie builds towards a tense and suspenseful climax as Jordan finally tracks down The Stranger, leading to a violent confrontation that will determine Casey's fate. In the end, Jordan manages to subdue The Stranger and save Casey from further harm.

Throughout the movie, Halle Berry delivers a powerful performance as Jordan Turner, bringing depth and nuance to a character who is both flawed and relatable. Abigail Breslin also shines in her breakout role as Casey Wesson, conveying the trauma and vulnerability of a young woman who has been through unimaginable horrors.

Overall, The Call is a gripping thriller that explores themes of obsession, redemption, and the power of human connection. With its tense plot twists and strong performances from Berry and Breslin, this movie is sure to keep viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

title: The Purge
tagline: One night a year, all crime is legal.
overview: Given the country's overcrowded prisons, the U.S. government begins to allow 12-hour periods of time in which all illegal activity is legal. During one of these free-for-alls, a family must protect themselves from a home invasion.
plot:
The Purge is a 2013 American dystopian horror film directed by James DeMonaco and written by DeMonaco and Jason Blum. The movie takes place in a future where the United States has become a totalitarian regime, known as the "New Founding Fathers of America" (NFFA), which has implemented a social experiment called "The Purge."

In this society, every year on March 21st, all laws are suspended for a 12-hour period, allowing citizens to commit any crime they desire without fear of punishment. This event is known as "The Purge," and it's believed that the NFFA uses it to maintain control over its population by allowing them to release their pent-up frustrations and violence.

The story follows James Sandin (Ethan Hawke), a wealthy businessman who has invested in a high-tech security system for his home, which he believes will protect him and his family from the chaos outside. The Sandin family consists of James, his wife Mary (Lena Headey), their teenage son Charlie (Max Burkholder), and their young daughter Zoey (Adelaide Kane).

As the Purge begins, the family huddles together in their safe room, a secure underground bunker that they believe will keep them safe from the marauding gangs and violent individuals who emerge during this time. However, as the night wears on, James's complacency is tested when he discovers that his security system has been breached by a group of masked intruders.

As the family tries to survive the Purge, they realize that their home is not as secure as they thought, and that the intruders are not just random attackers. The leader of the group, a mysterious figure known only as "The Stranger" (Vincent D'Onofrio), seems to be targeting specific individuals within the family.

Throughout the night, James's character undergoes a significant transformation from a self-centered individual to someone who must confront his own mortality and the true nature of The Purge. As the body count rises, James is forced to make difficult choices that put his family in greater danger.

In the end, James manages to outsmart The Stranger and escape with his family, but not without scars both physical and emotional. The movie ends with a sense of unease, as James realizes that he may have inadvertently contributed to the cycle of violence and that the true purpose of The Purge remains unknown.

The Purge received mixed reviews from critics but was a commercial success, grossing over $89 million worldwide. It spawned two sequels, The Purge: Anarchy (2014) and The Purge: Election Year (2016), as well as a television series.

Casey and Frank must work together to stop the Council and save Tomorrowland. Along the way, Casey discovers her own connection to Tomorrowland and her role in its future. The movie culminates in a thrilling showdown between Casey, Frank, and the Council, with the fate of Tomorrowland hanging in the balance.

Throughout the movie, there are several themes that emerge, including the importance of innovation, the dangers of unchecked power, and the value of human connection. The film also features stunning visual effects and impressive action sequences, making it a thrilling ride for audiences.

Overall, Tomorrowland is a visually stunning and thought-provoking film that explores the possibilities of technology and innovation. While it received mixed reviews from critics, it has become a beloved favorite among fans of science fiction and adventure movies.

title: The Haunting of Helena
tagline: She's coming for her.
overview: After a divorce, Sophia moves to the south of Italy with her daughter, Helena. Their new home, an apartment within an austere building of the fascist age, is a chance for them to start a new life. But inside an old storage room hides a mysterious closet and a buried secret. After the loss of Helena’s first baby tooth, a chilling obsession begins and an apparition haunts her sleep...
plot:
The Haunting of Helena, released in some countries as Fairytale, is a 2012 Italian supernatural horror film written and directed by Christian Bisceglia and shot in Italy. Harriet MacMasters-Green and Sabrina Jolie Perez star. It was distributed as part of the Bloody Disgusting Selects line.

Sophia, a recently divorced university professor living in Italy with her young daughter, Helena, is involved in a car accident with her on the day Helena loses her first tooth. Soon afterward Helena begins describing strange visions. Researching their apartment, Sophia learns that during the Fascist era a man who lived there tortured his wife by pulling out her teeth and locked her in a closet to die. Helena starts talking to an unseen presence in the closet and buys teeth from classmates, saying they are for the tooth fairy. A teacher who looks into this behavior is killed by a swarm of mosquitoes. Ignoring a warning to leave from the elderly man who lives upstairs, mother and daughter are attacked by the toothless ghost of the dead woman, escaping when Sophia throws the teeth at her.

Eighteen months later, Helena has stopped speaking and is confined to an institution, and her father, now back in Italy, believes Sophia is unfit to care for her. Bloody teeth rain briefly from the ceiling of Helena's room, and the closet door begins appearing in other places; when her father opens it, mosquitoes swarm and kill him. Doctors grow suspicious of Sophia, especially after his bloody teeth turn up in Helena's locker. Drawn by visions of the murderer at a window of the institution's abandoned psychiatric wing, Sophia finds his file and works out where the dead woman's teeth are hidden. She throws them through the closet door when it reappears, and Helena begins speaking again, apparently freed. But a recorded interview with the murderer reveals that his wife was a serial killer who ate the faces of children and that he killed her to stop her. Sophia finds a patient with a mauled face, who tells her the ogre has her teeth again, and she enters Helena's room before backing out screaming. Later, Sophia herself is a patient at the institution, gazing up at the abandoned wing where Helena's ghost, half her face gone, stands beside the murderer.

Reviews were largely negative, criticizing the clichéd plot and the performances. Slant's Chuck Bowen said it borrowed so heavily from Guillermo del Toro that he could almost sue for plagiarism.

title: The Fifth Estate
tagline: You can't expose the world's secrets without exposing yourself
overview: A look at the relationship between WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange and his early supporter and eventual colleague Daniel Domscheit-Berg, and how the website's growth and influence led to an irreparable rift between the two friends.
plot:
The Fifth Estate is a 2013 biographical thriller about the whistleblowing website WikiLeaks, directed by Bill Condon from a screenplay by Josh Singer. Benedict Cumberbatch stars as the founder Julian Assange and Daniel Brühl as his former spokesman Daniel Domscheit-Berg, with Anthony Mackie, David Thewlis, Alicia Vikander, Stanley Tucci and Laura Linney. The script draws partly on Domscheit-Berg's memoir Inside WikiLeaks and a book by the Guardian journalists David Leigh and Luke Harding.

The film opens in 2010 with the release of the Afghan War Logs before flashing back to 2007, when Daniel, a German technology activist, meets Assange in person at a hacker conference in Berlin. Drawn by Assange's vision of a website that publishes secret documents while protecting the anonymity of its sources, Daniel joins him. Their first major success comes when they publish evidence of wrongdoing at the Cayman Islands branch of the Swiss bank Julius Baer and survive the bank's legal challenge. Further leaks follow, from Scientology documents to Sarah Palin's emails.

Daniel initially reveres Assange as a mentor in a noble enterprise, but the relationship sours. He loses his job, and Assange dismisses his concerns about people harmed by the leaks. Daniel discovers that the organization's supposedly vast network of volunteers consists largely of the two of them, notices that Assange tells contradictory stories about his past,.

The tension peaks when the Army intelligence analyst Bradley Manning leaks a vast trove of classified material, including war logs and hundreds of thousands of US diplomatic cables. Assange wants immediate publication, while Daniel and the partner newspapers, including The Guardian, insist on redacting the names of informants. Convinced that Assange will not honor the agreement, Daniel and other members take the site offline and lock Assange out of its servers. The film closes by noting that the cables were later released unredacted and showing Assange in the Ecuadorian embassy in London, dismissing the film itself.

Co-produced by DreamWorks Pictures and Participant Media, the film premiered at the 2013 Toronto International Film Festival and was released in the United States by Touchstone Pictures on October 18, 2013. It flopped at the box office; reviews faulted the script but praised the acting, especially Cumberbatch's.

title: The Strange Thing About the Johnsons
original_title: The Strange Thing About the Johnsons
tagline: Help.
overview: A dark domestic melodrama about the ties that bind and the ties that really bind.
plot:
The Strange Thing About the Johnsons is a 2011 American short psychological horror film written and directed by Ari Aster as his thesis project at the AFI Conservatory. It stars Billy Mayo as Sidney Johnson, an acclaimed poet, Brandon Greenhouse as his son Isaiah and Angela Bullock as his wife Joan, with Danièle Watts as Isaiah's wife Marianne. The film depicts a suburban family in which the father is the victim of long-term sexual abuse by his own son, inverting the more familiar narrative of parental abuse.

In 1995, Sidney accidentally walks in on his twelve-year-old son and reassures him that what he was doing is natural, unaware of the disturbing nature of the boy's fixation on him. Years later, on Isaiah's wedding day, Joan discovers her son abusing her distraught husband. Shaken, she tries to carry on as though nothing has happened, while the family continues to maintain a respectable facade.

Sidney secretly writes a memoir titled Cocoon Man, describing the abuse he has suffered at the hands of his son, and leaves a copy for Joan. When Isaiah discovers it, he threatens his father and forbids him from distributing it. The abuse escalates, and Joan, unable or unwilling to intervene, ignores the signs. When Sidney tries to escape the house with a copy of his memoir, a confrontation with Isaiah ends in tragedy. After Sidney's death, Joan finally confronts her son about what he has done, leading to a violent and devastating conclusion between mother and son.

The film is known for its extremely disturbing subject matter, presented with the restrained, carefully composed style and atmosphere of dread that would later characterize Aster's features, and it explores family denial, silence and complicity.

The short premiered at the Slamdance Film Festival on January 22, 2011, and screened at other festivals before leaking online in November 2011, when it went viral. Reactions were polarized, ranging from acclaim to disgust, and the film also drew controversy over its depiction of an African-American family by a white filmmaker, which Aster addressed in interviews.

With power and influence now in their hands, the Pembertons refuse to let anyone stand in the way of their inflated love and ambitions. However, once Serena discovers George’s hidden past and faces an unchangeable fate of her own, the Pemberton’s passionate marriage begins to unravel leading toward a dramatic reckoning.
plot:
Serena is a 2014 drama film directed by Susanne Bier, based on Ron Rash's 2008 novel of the same name. It stars Jennifer Lawrence as Serena and Bradley Cooper as George Pemberton, newlyweds running a timber business in Depression-era North Carolina, with Rhys Ifans and Toby Jones in supporting roles. It was the third film to pair Lawrence and Cooper.

Ambitious timber baron George Pemberton falls in love with Serena Shaw, a young woman with a tragic past. After their marriage she joins him at his logging camp and begins to take control, challenging George while remaining devoted to him. His partner, Buchanan, resents her growing authority and makes a deal with the local sheriff, McDowell, who wants George's land for a park. Serena convinces George that Buchanan was never his friend, and during a bear hunt George shoots him dead; a worker, Campbell, witnesses it but stays silent, and the death is ruled an accident. Serena saves the life of a worker, Galloway, after he loses a hand, earning his loyalty. George secretly gives money to Rachel, the mother of his illegitimate son, Jacob. After Serena miscarries and learns that she can never have children, she comes to see Rachel and the boy as a threat.

Campbell steals ledgers from the safe and prepares to testify that George bribed a senator and killed Buchanan deliberately. While George is sent off to hunt a panther, Galloway murders Campbell. Discovering George's hidden photograph of Rachel and the baby, Serena scratches out the child's face and sends Galloway after them. He kills the widow sheltering Rachel, but the sheriff takes mother and child to safety. Confronted by George, Serena insists the killings were necessary; he briefly chokes her, then hands the ledgers to the sheriff in exchange for Rachel's location, promising to turn himself in. At the train station, George kills Galloway with a knife and bids farewell to Rachel and Jacob. Returning to the panther hunt, he is fatally mauled by the animal, killing it with his knife before he dies. When the sheriff brings his body home, Serena refuses to identify it and sets the cabin on fire, remaining motionless as she burns to death.

Serena premiered at the BFI London Film Festival on October 13, 2014, and was released in the United States by Magnolia Pictures in 2015. It was panned by critics, receiving 17% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 36, and grossed about $5 million on a budget of $25-30 million.

title: One Direction: This Is Us
tagline: Experience their lives on the road
overview: "One Direction: This Is Us" is a captivating and intimate all-access look at life on the road for the global music phenomenon. Weaved with stunning live concert footage, this inspiring feature film tells the remarkable story of Niall, Zayn, Liam, Harry and Louis's really like to be One Direction.
plot:
One Direction: This Is Us is a 2013 documentary concert film directed by Morgan Spurlock about the English-Irish boy band One Direction, made up of Niall Horan, Zayn Malik, Louis Tomlinson, Liam Payne and Harry Styles. Produced in part by Simon Cowell, who mentored the group on The X Factor, it follows the band on its Take Me Home Tour.

The film traces the five members' lives before and after they were brought together on The X Factor in 2010 and their rapid rise to global fame, a rise that Spurlock compares to that of the Beatles, even staging a loose homage to A Hard Day's Night. It combines live concert footage, much of it filmed at London's O2 Arena, with behind-the-scenes material showing how the band prepares for its shows and what life inside One Direction is like. More than half of the running time is devoted to backstage antics and conversation: the members horse around with their crew and bodyguards, joyride on a forklift backstage, hear from their mothers and take a break from touring to return home. Fans also share stories about the band, and the film includes appearances by Martin Scorsese and his daughter Francesca, the comedian Chris Rock and the footballer Cristiano Ronaldo.

The film was announced by the band on The Today Show in November 2012, with Spurlock, who had unsuccessfully sought to direct similar films about Justin Bieber and Katy Perry, attracted by the group's lightning-fast success. Shooting began in Tokyo in January 2013 using 3D 4K RED Epic cameras, and the project, first called 1D3D, received its final title that March. The footage was unscripted, and the crew had access everywhere, which Styles admitted was unnerving but welcome as a chance to show the band's personality off stage.

After a world premiere in Leicester Square on 20 August 2013, the film opened in the United Kingdom on 29 August and internationally the following day. It topped the North American box office on its opening weekend with $17 million and grossed $68.5 million worldwide, one of the highest-grossing concert films. Critics were mixed, with a 64% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a Metacritic score of 49; reviewers found it cheerful and charming but sanitized, and some criticized its distracting 3D effects, while audiences gave it an "A" CinemaScore.

title: New World
tagline: Three Men. Three Ways. To A Different World.
overview: An undercover cop has his loyalties tested when the boss of the corporate gang he's spent years infiltrating dies.
plot:
New World (Korean: Sinsegye) is a 2013 South Korean crime thriller written and directed by Park Hoon-jung. Lee Jung-jae stars as an undercover policeman who has risen high inside a criminal empire, with Choi Min-sik as the police chief who controls him, Hwang Jung-min as his gangster friend and Park Sung-woong as a rival boss, alongside Song Ji-hyo. A commercial success, it drew about 4.7 million admissions in South Korea and grossed some 31 million dollars.

For eight years Lee Ja-sung has been working undercover inside Goldmoon, the country's biggest criminal organisation disguised as a corporation, living in constant fear of exposure. His superior, Chief Kang, repeatedly promises him a posting abroad and repeatedly breaks his word, and when Ja-sung threatens to quit, Kang reminds him that revealing his identity would mean a painful death. When Goldmoon's chairman is killed in what looks like an accident, two men vie to replace him: Jung Chung, Ja-sung's close friend and boss, backed by the Chinese-Korean Northmoon faction, and the ruthless Lee Joong-gu, backed by the Jaebum faction.

Kang pits the two against each other so that the weak vice-chairman Jang Su-ki can take over and the police can control the group through him. He blackmails Jung into supplying evidence against Joong-gu in return for immunity, then tells the arrested Joong-gu that Jung betrayed him. Joong-gu's men ambush and fatally wound Jung, and also break into Ja-sung's home; his wife survives, but loses their unborn child.

Terrified, Ja-sung begs to be pulled out, but Kang refuses and erases his police records to keep him in place. At the hospital, the dying Jung, who knew all along that Ja-sung was a policeman but kept silent out of friendship, urges him to decide where his loyalty lies. Choosing to survive on his own terms, Ja-sung takes over Jung's faction and wins over Su-ki's men, who kill Su-ki instead of him. On his orders, Kang, the police director and Joong-gu are murdered, burying his secret forever, and he becomes Goldmoon's chairman.

A flashback to six years earlier shows Ja-sung and Jung as young thugs, already inseparable, and Ja-sung smiling for the first time. Critics praised its patient, elegant storytelling, The New York Times calling it more thoughtful than most of its genre.

plot:
Superman: Unbound is an animated film that explores the character's early days on Earth, delving into his struggles with his Kryptonian heritage and his desire to find a place where he belongs. The movie delves into themes of identity, belonging, and the weight of responsibility.

As Superman navigates his new life in Smallville, Kansas, he grapples with the expectations placed upon him by his adoptive parents, Jonathan and Martha Kent. He struggles to reconcile his Kryptonian roots with his human upbringing, feeling like an outsider among both humans and other aliens. This sense of disconnection serves as a catalyst for Superman's growth, as he learns to balance his dual identities and find a sense of purpose.

The film also touches on the theme of sacrifice, as Superman is forced to confront the consequences of his actions and make difficult choices that put those he cares about in harm's way. This serves as a reminder of the immense responsibility that comes with having extraordinary abilities, and the need for selflessness and compassion.

Furthermore, Superman: Unbound explores the idea of home and what it means to belong. Superman's search for a place where he can call home is a metaphor for the human experience, highlighting the universal desire for connection and acceptance. The film suggests that true belonging can be found in embracing one's differences and finding a sense of community with others who share similar struggles and aspirations.

Overall, Superman: Unbound presents a nuanced exploration of Superman's character, delving into the complexities of identity, responsibility, and the human need for connection and belonging.

title: Fantastic Four
tagline: Change is coming.
overview: Four young outsiders teleport to a dangerous universe, which alters their physical form in shocking ways. Their lives irrevocably upended, the team must learn to harness their daunting new abilities and work together to save Earth from a former friend turned enemy.
plot:
Fantastic Four is a 2015 superhero film based on the Marvel Comics team and the first reboot of the Fantastic Four film series. Directed by Josh Trank and written by Trank, Jeremy Slater and Simon Kinberg, it stars Miles Teller as Reed Richards, Michael B. Jordan as Johnny Storm, Kate Mara as Sue Storm, Jamie Bell as Ben Grimm and Toby Kebbell as Victor von Doom, with Reg E. Cathey as Franklin Storm and Tim Blake Nelson. The film offers a darker, more grounded take on the team's origin.

Childhood friends Reed Richards and Ben Grimm have spent years building a prototype teleporter, which attracts the attention of Professor Franklin Storm, head of the Baxter Foundation, a government-funded institute for young prodigies. Reed is recruited to work with Storm's children, Sue and Johnny, and the brilliant but difficult Victor von Doom on the Quantum Gate, a machine designed to reach another dimension. When the experiment succeeds and the project's supervisors plan to send NASA astronauts instead, Reed, Johnny, Victor and Ben make an unauthorized journey to the parallel world known as Planet Zero.

The trip goes disastrously wrong: Victor is apparently killed, and the explosion of the gate alters the others at a genetic level, giving them uncontrollable powers. Reed can stretch his body, Sue can turn invisible and create force fields, Johnny can engulf himself in flames and fly, and Ben is transformed into a rock-like creature of enormous strength. A year later, the government is using Ben, Johnny and Sue as military assets, while a guilt-ridden Reed has gone on the run. When an expedition to Planet Zero brings back a transformed Victor, now possessing devastating powers and determined to destroy Earth, the four must learn to work together as a team.

The film's troubled production became widely publicized, with reports of conflict between Trank and the studio and extensive reshoots.

Fantastic Four grossed 168 million dollars worldwide against a budget of 120 million dollars and was panned by critics, receiving 9 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 27. Trank publicly blamed the studio for the final film, and it won several Golden Raspberry Awards, including Worst Picture and Worst Director.

title: How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World
original_title: How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World
tagline: The friendship of a lifetime
overview: As Hiccup fulfills his dream of creating a peaceful dragon utopia, Toothless’ discovery of an untamed, elusive mate draws the Night Fury away. When danger mounts at home and Hiccup’s reign as village chief is tested, both dragon and rider must make impossible decisions to save their kind.
plot:
How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World is a 2019 American computer-animated adventure comedy film directed by Dean DeBlois and Chris Sanders. It is the third installment in the How to Train Your Dragon trilogy.

The movie takes place five years after the events of the previous film, where Hiccup Horrendous Haddock III (voiced by Jay Baruchel) has become the chief of Berk, a Viking village that has transformed into a utopia for dragons and humans. However, a new threat emerges in the form of Grimmel, a ruthless dragon hunter who seeks to destroy all dragons.

Grimmel is revealed to be the son of a powerful dragon hunter named Viggo (voiced by F. Murray Abraham), who was thought to have been killed by Hiccup's father, Stoick the Vast (voiced by Gerard Butler). Grimmel's presence sets off a chain reaction that puts the entire dragon population in danger.

As Hiccup and his friends try to stop Grimmel, they also face an internal conflict within Berk. The village is struggling with its identity, as some of its members want to return to their traditional Viking ways, while others want to maintain the peace and harmony between humans and dragons that Hiccup has established.

Meanwhile, Toothless, Hiccup's loyal dragon companion, begins to exhibit strange behavior, suggesting that he may be developing his own identity. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Toothless is not just a pet, but a wild dragon who has been living in secret among humans.

In the end, Hiccup and Grimmel engage in an epic battle, with Hiccup using all his skills and knowledge to defeat the ruthless hunter. However, instead of killing Grimmel, Hiccup chooses to spare his life, realizing that there may be a way to redeem him and bring peace to both humans and dragons.

The movie concludes with Hiccup and Toothless embarking on a journey to find a new home for the dragons, as Berk is no longer suitable for them. Along the way, they encounter new challenges and adventures, but ultimately, they find a hidden valley where the dragons can live in peace and harmony.

Throughout the film, the characters undergo significant development, particularly Hiccup, who must come to terms with his own identity and the weight of responsibility that comes with being the chief of Berk. The movie also explores themes of identity, community, and acceptance, as the characters navigate their relationships with each other and the world around them.

Overall, How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World is a heartwarming and action-packed film that brings closure to the trilogy while leaving room for new adventures in the future.

title: 3096 Days
tagline: The story of Natasha Kampusch
overview: A young Austrian girl is kidnapped and held in captivity for eight years. Based on the real-life case of Natascha Kampusch.
plot:
3096 Days (German: 3096 Tage) is a 2013 German drama film directed by Sherry Hormann and based on the true story of Natascha Kampusch, the girl who was abducted at the age of ten and held captive by Wolfgang Přiklopil for eight years. Northern Irish actress Antonia Campbell-Hughes plays Kampusch, with Amelia Pidgeon as the young Natascha, Thure Lindhardt as Přiklopil and Trine Dyrholm as her mother, Brigitta Sirny. The screenplay was the last project of producer and writer Bernd Eichinger before his sudden death, after which Martin Moszkowicz of Constantin Film and Ruth Toma completed it, and it was also the final film of cinematographer Michael Ballhaus.

On the morning of 2 March 1998, ten-year-old Natascha walks to school alone, upset after an argument with her mother, and is dragged into a van. She wakes up in a cellar, the prisoner of Wolfgang Přiklopil, a 35-year-old technician who leads an isolated life and whose main regular contact is his mother. Witness reports about the van bring police to his door, but they find nothing suspicious. For four years Natascha is not allowed to leave the cellar, and hunger, boredom, despair and Přiklopil's constant psychological manipulation gradually wear down her will to escape. As she grows older he lets her spend more time in the house, while shaving her head so that no stray hairs can betray her presence, giving her a new name and forcing her into heavy labor. The abuse becomes sexual and increasingly violent, yet his control over her is so complete that even when he takes her into public, to a hardware store or on a ski trip, she cannot bring herself to ask for help, and an attempt to reach out in a public bathroom fails because the other woman does not speak her language. Meanwhile her mother continues to blame herself for letting her walk to school alone. Desperate, Natascha secretly records each act of abuse on toilet paper and waits for her chance, which finally comes shortly after her eighteenth birthday, when a moment of inattention by her captor gives her an opportunity to run.

The production drew attention for Campbell-Hughes's drastic weight loss for the role. She told the Evening Standard that she wanted to suffer as much as Kampusch had, and she said that she suffered a torn Achilles tendon, a broken toe, a fractured rib and numerous cuts and bruises while working on a set that recreated the dungeon in which Kampusch had been kept.

title: Monster High: Friday Night Frights
tagline: The Monster High ghouls are back in a freaky, fabulous double feature that's simply to-die-for!
overview: SKRM (Skultimate Roller Maze) is an annual tournament between Monster High and different monster high schools that consists of a roller derby of dangerous obstacles and mazes. Granite City High, a high school team of gargoyles and Monster High's oldest rivals, won the school crest after defeating them in SKRM, and with it taking the school spirit. This has resulted in the school literally beginning to fall apart, and due to the boys serious injuries after the tournament, they decide not to participate any longer.  This prompts the ghouls to play SKRM in the boys place, and they suit up and begin training. However, the boys protest and claim SKRM is a boys sport only, and they won't help the ghouls train. This only pushes them to work harder, with the goal of making it to the championship game to defeat Granite City High.
plot:
Monster High: Friday Night Frights is a 2012 animated adventure fantasy television special produced by Nerd Corps Entertainment and based on Mattel's Monster High fashion doll line, the fifth special in the franchise. The voice cast includes Kate Higgins, Debi Derryberry, Salli Saffioti, Laura Bailey, Erin Fitzgerald, Ogie Banks and Cam Clarke. It aired on Nickelodeon in the United States on 5 February 2013.

Monster High has a centuries-old rivalry with Granite High, home of the Gargoyles, played out in the dangerous roller-skating sport known as Skultimate Roller Maze, or SKRM. By tradition, the losing school must surrender its crest to the winner. After Monster High's team loses the latest match to the Gargoyles, who cheated to win, the school is left without its crest and begins to crumble at an alarming rate. With most of the regular players injured, a group of girls, led by Frankie Stein, decides to take on the Gargoyles themselves. The boys object, insisting that SKRM is a sport only for boys, and warn them of the fate of Robecca Steam, a girl who once tried to play and supposedly met a terrible end and was never seen again.

The all-girls team trains hard and gradually improves, but its first official match ends in disqualification when a nervous Frankie falters. Refusing to give up, the girls find the scattered parts of Robecca Steam, a steam-powered robot, and rebuild her. Robecca encourages them to stay true to themselves and keep playing, and the team gains another boost when a gargoyle student, Rochelle Goyle, transfers from Granite High and joins them. The team advances to the finals and faces the Gargoyles once more. Despite injuries, Monster High wins, but the players choose not to claim Granite High's crest, recognizing that taking it would bring the same decay upon their rivals' school. Just as with the rule that only boys can play, they decide that the old tradition is harmful and should come to an end. The special closes with a roll call of the school's new co-ed SKRM team.

Universal released it on Blu-ray together with Monster High: Why Do Ghouls Fall in Love? on 1 July 2014. Common Sense Media praised its positive messages about diversity while criticizing its body images, and DVD Talk found the paired features entertaining.

title: Curse of Chucky
tagline: Fear has a new home.
overview: After the passing of her mother, Nica Pierce, a young woman in a wheelchair, is forced to deal with her sister, brother-in-law, niece and their nanny as they say their goodbyes to mother. But when people start turning up dead, Nica discovers the culprit might be a strange doll she received a few days earlier.
plot:
Curse of Chucky is a 2013 American comedy-horror film directed by Don Mancini, who also wrote the screenplay. The movie serves as a sequel to Child's Play and Bride of Chucky, ignoring the events of Seed of Chucky.

The story begins with Nica Pierce (Alexis Bledel), a young woman living in a psychiatric hospital with her mother, Karen (Christine Elise McCarty). After her mother's death, Nica inherits her estate, including an antique doll named Chucky. Unbeknownst to Nica, the doll is possessed by the vengeful spirit of Charles Lee Ray, also known as Chucky.

As Nica tries to settle her mother's estate, she discovers that Chucky has come back to life and begins to wreak havoc on her life. The doll starts to manipulate Nica, using his charm and wit to get what he wants. Meanwhile, a series of gruesome murders takes place in the town, with the victims all having one thing in common: they had previously owned or interacted with Chucky.

As the body count rises, Nica teams up with her friends, including her boyfriend, Matt (Dylan Minnette), and her friend, Emily (Briana Buckmaster). Together, they try to uncover the truth behind Chucky's return and put an end to his killing spree. Along the way, they discover that Chucky has a personal vendetta against Nica, who had previously tried to get rid of him.

As the plot thickens, Nica and her friends realize that Chucky is not just a simple doll, but a malevolent spirit with a twisted sense of humor. The group must use all their wits and resources to outsmart Chucky and stop his killing spree before it's too late.

In the end, Nica and her friends manage to trap Chucky in a box, but not before he unleashes one final attack on Nica. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Nica had been possessed by Chucky's spirit all along, making her the true culprit behind the murders. The movie ends with Nica being taken away by the authorities, while Chucky's spirit remains trapped in the box.

Overall, Curse of Chucky is a dark comedy-horror film that pays homage to the original Child's Play franchise while also subverting expectations and delivering plenty of twists and turns.

title: Brooklyn
tagline: Two countries, two loves, one heart
overview: In 1950s Ireland and New York, young Eilis Lacey has to choose between two men and two countries.
plot:
Brooklyn is a 2015 romantic period drama directed by John Crowley and written by Nick Hornby, adapted from Colm Tóibín's 2009 novel. Saoirse Ronan stars as a young Irish immigrant in 1950s New York, with Emory Cohen, Domhnall Gleeson, Jim Broadbent and Julie Walters in supporting roles. Filmed in Ireland and Montreal with only brief shooting in Brooklyn itself, it premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January 2015, where Fox Searchlight bought it after a bidding war.

In 1951 Eilis Lacey lives in the small town of Enniscorthy in south-east Ireland with her mother and her older sister Rose. Unable to find steady work, she serves part-time in the shop of the spiteful Miss Kelly. Rose arranges through Father Flood, an Irish priest in Brooklyn, for Eilis to emigrate to the United States. On the crossing, her worldly cabin-mate Georgina helps her through seasickness and tells her how to pass immigration.

In Brooklyn Eilis lodges in a boarding house for young Irishwomen run by the strict but kindly Mrs Kehoe and works at a department store, but she is crippled by homesickness. Father Flood enrols her in night classes in bookkeeping at Brooklyn College. At an Irish dance she meets Tony Fiorello, a warm Italian-American plumber, and as their romance grows and her studies go well, she begins to feel at home. Then Rose dies suddenly. Before Eilis leaves to comfort her mother, Tony shows her the land on Long Island where he hopes to build them a house, and they marry quietly at City Hall.

Back in Enniscorthy, Eilis finds herself welcomed into a life that now seems full of possibility. She fills in at Rose's old bookkeeping job, which may become permanent, and her friend Nancy introduces her to Jim Farrell, a well-off and gentle young man who clearly hopes to marry her. Eilis delays her return, neglects Tony's letters and keeps her marriage secret. Then Miss Kelly, having heard the news from gossip, summons her and hints that she knows the truth. Recognising the narrowness of the town, Eilis declares her married name, tells her mother she is returning to her husband, and leaves Jim a letter. On the voyage back she advises a nervous young emigrant just as Georgina once advised her, and is reunited with Tony in Brooklyn.

Brooklyn was acclaimed, with 97% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and earned three Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture and Best Actress for Ronan.

title: Free Fall
overview: A promising career with the police, a baby on the way... Marc's life seems to be right on track. Then he meets fellow policeman Kay and during their regular jogs Marc experiences a never-before-felt sense of ease and effortlessness -- and what it means to fall in love with another man.
plot:
Free Fall (German: Freier Fall) is a German drama of 2013 directed by Stephan Lacant, who wrote it with Karsten Dahlem. Hanno Koffler stars as the police officer Marc Borgmann, whose life is upended by an affair with a fellow officer, Kay Engel, played by Max Riemelt, with Katharina Schüttler as Marc's pregnant girlfriend Bettina, Oliver Bröcker as their friend Frank, Shenja Lacher as the officer Limpinski, and Maren Kroymann and Louis Lamprecht as Marc's parents.

On a training course for the riot police, Marc struggles to keep up physically and clashes with his roommate Kay, but after he apologises for a fight during an exercise they become friends and start jogging together. On one run, sharing a joint, Kay kisses him; on another the two become intimate. When Kay is transferred to Marc's unit, Marc finds him impossible to ignore, and Kay soon meets Bettina at a bowling alley. Marc tries to stay faithful to her, but returns to the jogging trail where Kay is waiting. Pretending to work night shifts, he carries on the affair, takes a key to Kay's flat and visits a gay bar with him, while Bettina grows suspicious and finds Kay's calls on his phone.

After Bettina gives birth to their son, Marc tries to break off contact and fights with Kay, but later, jealous to hear that Kay was found in a gay bar raided by their unit, he goes to his flat and breaks down in his arms. When Kay attacks Limpinski over a homophobic incident, Marc is hurt separating them, and his mother sees the two men kiss at the hospital. Marc's parents tell Kay to stay away from their son's new family, and Marc, overhearing them, sends Kay away; later he returns the key, urging the bruised Kay to transfer. Bettina, having discovered the lies about night shifts, leaves with the baby, and Marc confesses the affair. She returns, but the distance between them remains. Marc finds Kay's flat empty; he has left the unit without warning. Assaulted by Limpinski after taunting him, Marc visits the gay bar alone but rejects a stranger. He and Bettina agree that their relationship cannot continue, and the film closes with Marc back at the academy, outrunning his peers and running on alone.

Shot in Ludwigsburg in 2012, the film premiered at the Berlin International Film Festival on 8 February 2013 to good reviews and drew comparisons to Brokeback Mountain. Koffler was nominated for a German Film Award for Best Supporting Actor.

plot:
Monster High: Escape from Skull Shores is a 2012 animated adventure fantasy television special produced by Nerd Corps Entertainment for Mattel, the fourth special based on the Monster High doll line. It premiered on Nickelodeon in the United States in April 2012 and was tied to a dedicated Skull Shores line of dolls. Kate Higgins, Laura Bailey, Salli Saffioti, Debi Derryberry and Evan Smith are among the voice cast. It was later released on Blu-ray alongside Monster High: Fright On! as part of a double feature.

For spring break, Lagoona Blue invites her friends to the Great Scarrier Reef. On the way, their ship is destroyed by a kraken, leaving the students adrift on a raft made from their luggage. They are rescued by Bartleby Farnum, an eccentric human showman, and his assistant, Kipling, who wears a sack over his head, and taken to an island called Skull Shores, where they are welcomed by the local Tiki tribe.

Suspicious, Lagoona and her boyfriend, Gil, search Farnum's boat and find a recording about the Beast of Skull Shores, a creature that Farnum is obsessed with capturing, and about an explorer who befriended it and who looks like Frankie Stein. They realize that Farnum plans to use Frankie as bait. That night, the beast appears and carries Frankie off; she is frightened at first, but soon realizes that he means her no harm. Farnum and the Tiki give chase, trapping Ghoulia Yelps and Abbey Bominable in a pit, while Clawdeen Wolf, Draculaura and Cleo de Nile escape. The next morning, Frankie meets Andy, a friendly monster who reveals that he and the beast are the same creature, and the friends must work together to rescue their captured classmates, protect Andy from Farnum and find a way to escape from the island. Along the way, the story explores friendship and acceptance, as the ghouls stand up for a misunderstood creature, and Andy eventually joins them as a new student at Monster High.

Grace Montgomery of Common Sense Media found its monsters more silly than sinister and praised its strong message about tolerance, but felt that the message was partly undermined by the revealing outfits and heavy makeup of the female characters, who she otherwise considered decent role models.

plot:
Furious 7 is a 2015 action film directed by James Wan and written by Chris Morgan. The movie marks the seventh installment in the Fast and Furious franchise, which has become one of the most successful and beloved franchises in Hollywood.

The story begins with Dominic Toretto (Vin Diesel) and his crew, including Brian O'Conner (Paul Walker), Tej Parker (Chris "Ludacris" Bridges), Roman Pearce (Tyrese Gibson), and Mia Toretto (Jordana Brewster), who are still dealing with the aftermath of their last adventure. However, their lives take a dramatic turn when they receive news that Brian has been killed in action.

The crew is devastated by Brian's death, but Dom decides to honor his friend's memory by taking on one final mission: to rescue a young girl named Ramsey (Nathalie Emmanuel) from the clutches of Deckard Shaw (Jason Statham), a skilled mercenary who was once a member of the British Special Forces.

As the crew embarks on their perilous journey, they are joined by new recruits, including Deckard's sister, Maggie (Gina Carano), and a mysterious woman named Anna (Michelle Rodriguez). The team faces numerous challenges and obstacles as they navigate through the streets of Abu Dhabi, Dubai, and London to reach Ramsey.

Throughout the film, Dom and his crew encounter various adversaries, including Shaw, who is determined to take revenge on Dom for killing his brother. The action sequences are intense and thrilling, with stunning stunts and high-octane chases that showcase the team's skills and teamwork.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Deckard has a personal vendetta against Dom, which makes their confrontation all the more intense. Meanwhile, Dom also grapples with his own demons, including his complicated relationship with Mia and his feelings of guilt over Brian's death.

The film's climax features an epic showdown between Dom and Shaw, with the two engaging in a fierce hand-to-hand combat sequence that showcases their skills and physicality. In the end, Dom emerges victorious, but not before Shaw reveals a shocking secret about his past that adds depth to the story.

Furious 7 also pays tribute to Paul Walker, who passed away during filming due to a car accident. The film's producers incorporated a heartfelt tribute to Walker into the movie, featuring footage of him from previous films in the franchise and a poignant message from Dom to Brian.

Overall, Furious 7 is an action-packed thrill ride that delivers on its promise of high-octane excitement and heart-pumping suspense. With its talented cast, stunning stunts, and emotional depth, it's a fitting addition to the Fast and Furious franchise.

title: American Hustle
tagline: Everyone Hustles To Survive
overview: A conman and his seductive partner are forced to work for a wild FBI agent, who pushes them into a world of Jersey power-brokers and the Mafia.
plot:
American Hustle is a 2013 historical crime drama film directed by David O. Russell, written by Eric Warren Singer, and starring Christian Bale, Amy Adams, Bradley Cooper, Jennifer Lawrence, Jeremy Renner, and Robert De Niro.

The film is loosely based on the FBI's Abscam sting operation in the late 1970s and early 1980s, which targeted corrupt politicians and mobsters. The story follows con artist Irving Rosenfeld (Christian Bale), who teams up with his partner Sydney Prosser (Bradley Cooper) to swindle wealthy marks.

However, their partnership is put to the test when they meet FBI agent Richie DiMaso (Bradley Cooper), who poses as a wealthy businessman and convinces them to work for him. Richie's true intention is to gather evidence against corrupt politicians, particularly New Jersey Senator Carmine Polito (Roberto Benigni).

As Irving and Sydney become more embroiled in the sting operation, they begin to develop feelings for each other, despite their troubled past. Meanwhile, Richie becomes increasingly obsessed with taking down Senator Polito, who is being blackmailed by a mobster named Rosalyn Rosenfeld (Jennifer Lawrence), Irving's wife.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Richie's true intentions are not entirely altruistic. He is using his partnership with Irving and Sydney to further his own career and gain favor with Senator Polito. The three become embroiled in a complex web of deceit and corruption, with each character playing multiple roles and hiding their true identities.

The film's plot twists and turns as the characters navigate their relationships and confront their personal demons. In the end, Irving and Sydney are forced to choose between their loyalty to Richie and their own survival. The film culminates in a dramatic showdown at Senator Polito's inauguration, where the characters' true identities are revealed and the consequences of their actions are revealed.

Throughout the film, Russell uses a non-linear narrative structure, jumping back and forth in time to reveal the characters' backstories and motivations. The film features a talented ensemble cast, with standout performances from Christian Bale, Amy Adams, and Jennifer Lawrence.

American Hustle received widespread critical acclaim, earning 10 Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture, Best Director, and Best Actor for Christian Bale. The film won one Oscar, for Best Supporting Actress for Jennifer Lawrence. Overall, American Hustle is a gripping and entertaining drama that explores the complexities of human relationships and the corrupting influence of power.

overview: Dance your way to a magical adventure with Barbie as Kristyn, a ballerina with big dreams! plot:
Barbie in the Pink Shoes is a 2013 American computer-animated musical fantasy film, the 24th entry in the Barbie film series, released direct to video by Universal Studios Home Entertainment in February 2013. Directed by Owen Hurley from a screenplay by Alison Taylor and produced by Barbie Entertainment with Technicolor, it features ballet choreography by Melissa Barak, with dancers such as Jenelle Manzi credited for the dance performances, and a score arranged by Jim Dooley and recorded by the Slovak National Symphony Orchestra.

Barbie plays Kristyn, a talented young ballerina in a ballet company who loves to get carried away by the music and improvise her own steps. Her strict teacher, Madame Natasha, demands absolute perfection and favours the company's star, Tara, who dances the solos opposite the handsome Dillon. When Natasha cuts Kristyn off during a rehearsal, she falls and breaks a slipper. With her best friend Hailey, the company's costume designer, she visits Madame Katerina, who has no shoes left in her size but, hearing Kristyn speak of her dream of dancing Giselle and Odette in Swan Lake, brings out a pair of sparkling pink shoes. As soon as Kristyn laces them up, she and Hailey are whisked away to a magical ballet world built from the stories whose costumes filled the room.

There Kristyn finally gets to dance the roles of her dreams, stepping into Giselle, a story of a young woman courted by both a prince and a woodsman, and Swan Lake, but the land is threatened by a cold and exacting Snow Queen, a reflection of Madame Natasha. To save her new friends and return home, Kristyn must defeat the queen through dance, realising that no step is wrong if it is danced from the heart. Back in the real world, she carries that lesson into a successful performance.

Kelly Sheridan voices Kristyn and her ballet roles, with Katie Crown as Hailey, Ali Liebert as Tara and Odile, Brett Dier as Dillon and Prince Siegfried, Tabitha St. Germain as Madame Natasha and the Snow Queen, Lori Triolo as Madame Katerina, and Bill Mondy, Teryl Rothery, Trevor Devall and Kyle Rideout in supporting roles. The film weaves in music from classical ballets including La Laitière suisse, Adam's Giselle and Tchaikovsky's Swan Lake, alongside an original song by Dooley, Gabriel Mann and Rob Hudnut. It was followed by the streaming short Barbie in the Pink Shoes: Land of Sweets.

title: The Dyatlov Pass Incident
tagline: History always repeats itself.
overview: In February of 1959, nine Russian hikers ventured into a remote area of the Ural Mountains. Two weeks later, all of them were found dead. What happened is a mystery that has baffled investigators and researchers for decades. It has become known as the Dyatlov Pass Incident.  When five ambitious American college students are issued a grant to return to the site of the original events, they gear up with the belief that they can uncover and document the truth of what happened to the supposedly experienced hikers. But what they find is more shocking than anything they could have imagined. Retracing the steps of the Russians' ill-fated journey, the students are plagued by strange and increasingly terrifying phenomena that suggest that in spite of the desolate surroundings, they are not alone. The forces at work in the Dyatlov Pass Incident have been waiting for them.
plot:
The Dyatlov Pass Incident, later retitled Devil's Pass, is a 2013 found-footage horror film directed by Renny Harlin from a script by Vikram Weet. Holly Goss and Matt Stokoe play the co-directors Holly King and Jensen Day, with Luke Albright, Ryan Hawley and Gemma Atkinson.

A Russian news report reveals that five Oregon college students vanished in Russia and that footage recovered by the government was leaked by hackers. The students, including climbers J.P. and Andy and sound engineer Denise, had come to investigate the 1959 Dyatlov Pass incident, in which nine hikers died mysteriously. They try to interview Piotr Karov, a member of the original expedition who turned back after falling ill, but staff at the psychiatric hospital where he was committed claim he is dead; the students glimpse a man at a window holding up a sign before orderlies drag him away. A local man, Sergei, translates the sign as a warning to stay away and introduces them to his aunt Alya, who served on the first rescue team and says eleven bodies and a strange machine were found at the site, two of the bodies being abnormal.

On the trail the group hears howling, finds barefoot prints in the snow that begin and end abruptly, and discovers a human tongue inside a weather tower. They reach Dyatlov Pass suspiciously early, their navigation gear malfunctions, and a Geiger counter leads Holly and Jensen to a bunker door that locks from the outside. Explosions trigger an avalanche that kills Denise and badly injures Andy, and Russian soldiers posing as rescuers kill Andy and drive the others into the bunker, wounding J.P. Inside, Holly and Jensen find evidence of teleportation experiments, files on the Philadelphia Experiment, piled bodies and a camcorder showing footage of their own conversation. Teleporting mutants kill J.P., and trapped in a sealed chamber, Holly and Jensen step into what Jensen believes is a wormhole, picturing the bunker entrance. In 1959, Soviet soldiers find two bodies outside the bunker, chase off the young Alya, and hang the corpses inside, where the mutated Holly and Jensen begin to stir.

Harlin researched government archives in Moscow and believes the real incident stemmed from a failed government experiment; he deliberately cast unknown actors and shot in northern Russia. Released on 23 August 2013, the film drew mixed reviews, scoring 48% on Rotten Tomatoes and 49 on Metacritic, with Variety calling it unoriginal yet watchable.

title: A Walk Among the Tombstones
tagline: Some people are afraid of all the wrong things
overview: Private investigator Matthew Scudder is hired by a drug kingpin to find out who kidnapped and murdered his wife.
plot:
A Walk Among the Tombstones is a crime thriller film directed by Scott Frank, based on the novel of the same name by Lawrence Block. The movie stars Liam Neeson as Matthew Scudder, a former NYPD detective who now works as a private investigator.

The story begins with Matthew Scudder (Liam Neeson) being hired by a wealthy client, Burt Grusinsky (David Harbour), to find his missing daughter, Ashley (Danika Yarosh). The police are unable to help, and Scudder agrees to take on the case. As he delves deeper into the investigation, he discovers that Ashley was last seen with a group of men who were involved in human trafficking.

Scudder's search for Ashley leads him to a seedy underworld of prostitution and crime, where he encounters a variety of unsavory characters, including the pimp, Frank (Dan Stevens), and his accomplices. As Scudder gets closer to the truth, he realizes that Ashley is being held captive by Frank and his associates.

The plot thickens as Scudder discovers that Frank's operation is linked to a larger human trafficking ring, led by a mysterious figure known only as "The Wolf" (David Harbour). The Wolf is revealed to be Burt Grusinsky's business partner, who has been using Ashley's disappearance to extort money from her father.

As the story unfolds, Scudder uses his skills and experience to gather evidence and build a case against Frank and The Wolf. He also forms an unlikely alliance with a young prostitute named Abigail (Bojana Jelic), who becomes a key witness in the investigation.

The climax of the movie takes place at a warehouse where Scudder confronts Frank and The Wolf. In a tense standoff, Scudder manages to outsmart his adversaries and rescue Ashley, but not before The Wolf reveals that he has been playing a cat-and-mouse game with Scudder all along.

In the end, Scudder is able to bring Frank and The Wolf to justice, but not before they exact a sense of revenge on him. The movie ends with Scudder reflecting on the case and the toll it has taken on him, as he walks away from the warehouse where the events unfolded.

Overall, A Walk Among the Tombstones is a gripping crime thriller that explores the darker side of human nature. Liam Neeson delivers a strong performance as Matthew Scudder, bringing depth and nuance to the character. The movie's tense atmosphere and well-crafted plot make it a compelling watch for fans of the genre.

title: Iron Man: Rise of Technovore
original_title: アイアンマン：ライズ・オブ・テクノヴォア
tagline: Can Iron Man save the world when the world is against him?
overview: Iron Man enlists the help of ruthless vigilante the Punisher to track down War Machine's murderer. All the while, he's being pursued by S.H.I.E.L.D. agents Black Widow and Hawkeye, who suspect his involvement in a recent terrorist plot.
plot:
Iron Man: Rise of Technovore (Japanese: アイアンマン：ライズ・オブ・テクノヴォア) is a 2013 Japanese animated superhero film produced by Madhouse as a follow-up to the Marvel Anime television series. It was directed by Hiroshi Hamasaki, known for Texhnolyze and Shigurui, from a story by Brandon Auman. In the Japanese version Keiji Fujiwara voices Tony Stark, while the English dub features Matthew Mercer as Stark and Norman Reedus as the Punisher. It was released on home video in Japan and North America in April 2013.

While test-flying alongside War Machine, James "Rhodey" Rhodes, over the Utah desert, Iron Man is ambushed by a mysterious attacker who tries to destroy Tony Stark's new satellite, "The Howard," a global security system. Rhodey is apparently killed in the battle, and Tony sets out to find those responsible. S.H.I.E.L.D. and Nick Fury try to bring him in for questioning, believing his recklessness may be connected to the attack, but he evades them and goes to Pepper Potts for help.

Tony and Pepper discover that the terrorist organization A.I.M. has been researching techno-organic weaponry and trace one of its facilities to Karachi. There Iron Man crosses paths with the Punisher, who is hunting A.I.M. arms dealers, and the two reluctantly join forces. They learn that the attacker is Ezekiel Stane, the son of Tony's late enemy Obadiah Stane, who has fused himself with an experimental techno-organic substance and become a nearly unstoppable foe. As S.H.I.E.L.D. sends Hawkeye and Black Widow to capture Tony, now considered a fugitive, he must clear his name and stop Ezekiel, whose plans threaten both Stark's technology and S.H.I.E.L.D. itself. Along the way Tony relies on Pepper and makes use of his portable suitcase armor.

The film received mixed reviews. John Gholson of Movies.com criticized its dialogue as either vague or awkwardly on the nose and found the animation lacking excitement during action scenes. Tony Guerrero of Comic Vine gave it three out of five, praising its animation and colors and noting the appeal of including several Marvel characters in the story.

title: The Boxtrolls

overview: An orphaned boy raised by underground creatures called Boxtrolls comes up from the sewers and out of his box to save his family and the town from the evil exterminator, Archibald Snatcher.
plot:

In the fictional town of Cheesebridge, a group of small, mischievous creatures known as the Boxtrolls live beneath the streets. These trolls are scavengers who feed on human trash and are feared by the townspeople. The main character, Eggs (voiced by Charlie Tahan), is a young orphan boy who lives in an orphanage run by the evil Lord Eggman (voiced by Jeremy Suarez). Eggs' life changes when he discovers that he is actually a Box Troll himself.

As Eggs navigates his new identity, he meets a human girl named Eve (voiced by Isla Fisher) who has been kidnapped by Lord Eggman. The two form an unlikely friendship and embark on a journey to rescue Eve from the clutches of the evil lord. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, ferocious creatures, and rival gangs of Boxtrolls.

Throughout their adventure, Eggs learns about his true identity as a Box Troll and the history of his people. He also discovers that Lord Eggman is actually a former human who was transformed into a troll by a magical curse. The lord's ultimate goal is to capture all the remaining humans in Cheesebridge and use them to create an army of super-strong trolls.

As Eggs and Eve near their destination, they face off against Lord Eggman and his minions in an epic battle. In the end, Eggs and Eve successfully rescue Eve from the clutches of the evil lord, and Eggs finds a new sense of belonging among his fellow Boxtrolls.

The film features stunning stop-motion animation, witty humor, and a heartwarming story about acceptance and friendship. The characters are well-developed and relatable, with Eggs being a particularly endearing protagonist. The film's themes of identity, community, and the power of human connection make it a delightful and entertaining watch for audiences of all ages.

Overall, The Boxtrolls is a charming and imaginative film that will delight both children and adults with its unique blend of humor, adventure, and heart.
