title: The Marine 3: Homefront
tagline: He's back home from war, but the battle has just begun.
overview: A Marine must do whatever it takes to save his kidnapped sister and stop a terrorist attack masterminded by a radical militia group.
plot:
The Marine 3: Homefront is a 2013 American action film directed by John Stockwell and starring Taylor Kitsch, Wendy Malick, and James Remar. The movie is the third installment in The Marine film series.

The story begins with Mike Donnelly (Taylor Kitsch), a former U.S. Marine who has been presumed dead after being captured by enemy forces during a mission in Iraq. However, it turns out that he was rescued by a group of rebels and has been living in hiding ever since.

Mike returns to the United States, where he is reunited with his estranged wife, Carly (Wendy Malick), and their young daughter, Hannah. Mike struggles to adjust to civilian life and reconnect with his family, but his past soon catches up with him when a group of mercenaries, led by the ruthless Victor Vex (James Remar), begin to terrorize the small town where he lives.

Vex is seeking revenge against Mike for killing one of his men during a previous encounter. As Mike tries to protect his family and community from Vex's gang, he must also confront his own demons and learn to let go of his past in order to move forward with his life.

As the situation escalates, Mike finds himself at odds with the local sheriff, who is initially unwilling to believe that Vex's gang is a threat. However, when the gang begins to wreak havoc on the town, the sheriff is forced to team up with Mike in order to stop them.

Throughout the movie, Mike faces off against Vex and his men in a series of intense battles, using his military training and skills to take down the mercenaries one by one. Along the way, he also forms an unlikely alliance with a local woman named Sarah (Daniella Alonso), who helps him on his mission to protect her town.

As the final showdown approaches, Mike confronts Vex in a tense and violent battle. In the end, Mike emerges victorious, but not without scars both physical and emotional. The movie concludes with Mike finally finding some measure of peace and closure, having protected his family and community from harm.

Overall, The Marine 3: Homefront is an action-packed thrill ride that explores themes of redemption, loyalty, and the struggle to balance personal life with a past filled with violence and trauma.

overview: It's a jungle out there for Blu, Jewel and their three kids after they're hurtled from Rio de Janeiro to the wilds of the Amazon. As Blu tries to fit in, he goes beak-to-beak with the vengeful Nigel, and meets the most fearsome adversary of all: his father-in-law.
plot:
Rio 2 is a 2014 animated musical comedy-adventure film produced by Blue Sky Studios and distributed by 20th Century Fox. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2011 film Rio.

The story begins with Blu, a domesticated blue macaw who lives in Minnesota with his owner, Linda, and their daughter, Jewel. Blu is struggling to connect with Jewel, who is growing up too fast for him. Meanwhile, Jewel's father, Rafael, a wild blue macaw from Rio de Janeiro, has been keeping an eye on her from afar.

Rafael decides it's time to introduce Jewel to his family and friends in the Amazon rainforest. Blu reluctantly agrees to join them on this adventure, hoping that it will help him bond with Jewel. The group sets off on a journey through the Amazon, facing various obstacles and dangers along the way.

Upon arrival, they meet Rafael's father, Carlos, who is struggling to find his place in the family due to his lack of flying skills. Blu also meets Rafael's friends, including Tulio, a toucan, and Pedro, a parrot. The group soon discovers that the Amazon is under threat from human loggers and poachers.

As they navigate through the rainforest, Blu struggles to adapt to the wild environment and his own identity as a domesticated bird. He also begins to develop feelings for Jewel's mother, Jewel, who is a hybrid of a blue macaw and a blue-and-yellow macaw. However, their relationship is complicated by Blu's past experiences with Jewel's mother.

Throughout the journey, Blu learns valuable lessons about family, friendship, and self-acceptance. He also comes to terms with his own identity as a domesticated bird who has found a new sense of purpose in protecting Jewel and her family.

In the end, Blu and Rafael successfully defeat the loggers and poachers, saving the Amazon rainforest. The movie concludes with Blu finding a new sense of belonging among the wild birds, and he finally connects with Jewel on a deeper level.

Rio 2 features stunning animation, catchy musical numbers, and a heartwarming story that explores themes of identity, family, and acceptance. The movie is a delightful sequel to Rio, offering plenty of humor, action, and adventure for audiences of all ages.

title: Drinking Buddies
tagline: A comedy about knowing when to say when.
overview: Weekend trips, office parties, late night conversations, drinking on the job, marriage pressure, biological clocks, holding eye contact a second too long… you know what makes the line between “friends” and “more than friends” really blurry? Beer.
plot:
Drinking Buddies is a 2013 American comedy-drama written, directed and edited by Joe Swanberg, starring Olivia Wilde, Jake Johnson, Anna Kendrick and Ron Livingston, with filmmaker Ti West in a supporting role. Set at a real Chicago brewery and built largely on improvised dialogue, it premiered at the South by Southwest film festival in 2013 and also screened at the Maryland Film Festival.

Kate and Luke are co-workers at Chicago's Revolution Brewing, where she handles marketing and public relations and he works in production. They share the same goofy sense of humour and spend their evenings drinking with the rest of the brewery crew, and they seem made for each other, except that both are already in relationships. Kate is dating Chris, a reserved introvert, while Luke lives with Jill, a kind and practical woman who is gently pressing him to talk about marriage.

Chris invites Luke and Jill to join him and Kate for a weekend at his lakeside cottage. During a hike, Chris and Jill share a kiss, while back at the house Luke and Kate stay up drinking, build a bonfire and go skinny-dipping. Soon after the trip Chris, recognising how different he and Kate are, breaks up with her. Kate celebrates her new freedom on a night out with the brewery crew and ends up sleeping with a colleague, Dave, which leaves Luke irrationally angry with them both.

When Jill goes away for a week with old college friends, Luke and Kate grow closer. They share dinner, fall asleep together on the couch, and he spends the weekend helping her move apartments. The move goes badly: Luke badly cuts his hand, Kate proves squeamish and unhelpful, a confrontation with an impatient driver leaves him bruised, and when Kate drops their dinner plans to go drinking with Dave, the two argue bitterly. Luke returns home to find Jill back early and in tears. Tending his wounds, she confesses to kissing Chris, insists that she loves him and still wants to marry him, and Luke forgives her and says he feels the same.

At work the next day, Kate and Luke are awkward with each other until they sit down together at lunch, trading bits of food in a silent gesture that their friendship will survive. The film received positive reviews, holding an 84% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Hours
tagline: Every second counts.
overview: A father struggles to keep his infant daughter alive in the wake of Hurricane Katrina.
plot:
Hours is a 2013 American thriller written and directed by Eric Heisserer. Paul Walker stars as a father struggling to keep his newborn daughter alive in a deserted New Orleans hospital after the power fails in the aftermath of Hurricane Katrina, with Genesis Rodriguez, T. J. Hassan and Judd Lormand in supporting roles.

In 2005, Nolan Hayes rushes his wife, Abigail, to the hospital when she goes into labor five weeks early. She dies giving birth, and their daughter must stay on a ventilator for two days until she can breathe unaided. As Katrina strikes, the hospital is evacuated, but the ventilator cannot be moved, so Nolan stays behind with the baby, whom he names Abigail after her mother. A nurse promises to return with help, but flooding in the basement knocks out the power, and the only generator Nolan can find must be cranked by hand every three minutes to charge the ventilator battery, which holds less charge each time. His every movement becomes a race against the clock.

Nolan rescues a dog tangled in rope, names it Sherlock and shares his food with it. He signals a helicopter from the roof, but gunmen drive it off; he tries an ambulance radio and reaches only a recording; and a generator he finds in the flooded basement nearly electrocutes him. Exhausted, hungry and with his hand cut from cranking, he devises new ways to work the crank, using his foot and later a rod. Looters raid the hospital for food, drugs and saline, and Sherlock chases one from Nolan's room; Nolan later realizes that the man robbed and killed the nurse who was bringing help. After nearly two days without sleep, he injects himself with adrenaline to stay awake. When two more looters arrive searching for drugs, he overpowers one, takes his gun and shoots the other. After forty hours the crank finally breaks. Nolan gives his daughter mouth-to-mouth resuscitation before collapsing, and as the ventilator's alarm sounds he believes he has failed her. Sherlock leads paramedics to them, and as they wheel Nolan out, the baby begins to cry and is placed in his arms.

The film premiered at the South by Southwest festival in Austin on March 10, 2013, and opened on December 13, 2013, two weeks after Walker's death. Reviews were mixed, with 64% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 55; Variety's Joe Leydon said its ingeniously simple setup was exploited for maximum suspense.

title: It Boy
overview: Alice Lantins is 38, ambitious and so committed to her work that she neglects her personal life.  In short, she is the ideal candidate for the next editor of the magazine Rebelle, or would be were it not for the fact that she appears to be stuck in a rut.  When Balthazar, a charming 20-year-old, crosses her path, her colleagues begin to see her in a whole new light...
plot:
It Boy (20 ans d'écart) is a 2013 French romantic comedy co-written and directed by David Moreau, from an original idea by his co-writer Amro Hamzawi. Produced by Abel Nahmias for EuropaCorp with Echo Films, it stars Virginie Efira and Pierre Niney, with Charles Berling, Gilles Cohen, Amélie Glenn, Camille Japy, Michaël Abiteboul and Louis-Do de Lencquesaing in supporting roles.

Alice Lantins (Efira), 38, is a capable and ambitious journalist at the fashion magazine Rebelle and the obvious candidate to become its next editor-in-chief, except that her boss, Vincent Khan (Cohen), sees her as uptight and old-fashioned. Returning from a trip to Brazil, she sits next to Balthazar (Niney), an architecture student of about twenty who has landed in business class by chance. He finds a USB stick she dropped and, when she picks him up to retrieve it, he puts a helmet on her before giving her a ride on his pink scooter. Two colleagues snap a photo of the moment and post it online, and overnight Alice's image is transformed. Realizing that her boss suddenly sees her as daring, she decides to fake a romance with the younger man to secure the promotion.

Alice adopts a bolder style, visits Balthazar at university and goes out with him, and the pretense slowly turns into real feelings, leading to a passionate night together. Unable to tell him that she first approached him for her career, and afraid that he will one day find her too old, she breaks off the relationship, leaving him heartbroken while Vincent celebrates the "new Alice". When the head of the magazine group wants Balthazar for a photo shoot, he learns how Alice used him and confronts her in front of the whole team, and Vincent fires her for the deception. Alone, Alice revisits the places they shared and finally addresses Balthazar in a university lecture hall, admitting her mistakes and asking for a fresh start. They reunite, and she returns to her old dream of writing.

The film premiered at the Alpe d'Huez comedy festival in January 2013 and opened in France and Belgium on 6 March 2013. Critics welcomed it as a lively, well-written romantic comedy, with Première praising the charm of its two leads despite a predictable story. Niney won the Swann d'Or for best actor at the Cabourg Film Festival.

title: The English Teacher
tagline: Refuse To Live Life By The Book
overview: Teacher Linda Sinclair balances her staid home life with an incredible passion for her subject, but her routine is forever altered when a former star pupil and his unsupportive father reenter her life.
plot:
The English Teacher is a 2013 American romantic comedy-drama directed by Craig Zisk from a screenplay by Dan and Stacy Chariton. Julianne Moore stars as a lonely small-town teacher whose orderly life is upended by a former student, played by Michael Angarano, with Greg Kinnear, Lily Collins, Nathan Lane, Jessica Hecht and Fiona Shaw. The film premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on April 26, 2013, and was released in a handful of US cinemas on May 17.

Linda Sinclair is a devoted, popular English teacher at a high school in Kingston, Pennsylvania. She lives alone, in modest comfort, and, being an incurable romantic, finds that no real man can live up to the heroes of the books she loves. When her former star pupil, Jason Sherwood, returns home after graduating from New York University's playwriting programme, discouraged by his failure to break through, Linda is determined to help him. She and the school's drama teacher Carl Kapinas persuade him to let them stage his dark play at the school.

Jason's father, Dr. Tom Sherwood, wants his son to give up writing and go to law school, and Jason, with no other prospects, seems ready to agree. Things grow complicated when, in a burst of creative excitement, Linda and Jason have a sexual encounter on her classroom desk. Jealousies and rumours follow and spill over into rehearsals, until the school administration learns of the affair and Linda is fired on the spot.

Fleeing in embarrassment, Linda has a minor car accident and is treated at the hospital by Dr. Sherwood, and she guiltily confesses that she slept with his son. Strong advance ticket sales then change the school's mind, and with Carl temporarily incapacitated by stress, the administration asks Linda to return and direct the play. The school insists, however, on a new ending, since the original, with its murder and suicide, is considered too disturbing for parents.

Jason angrily refuses to change his work, so Linda writes a gentler ending herself. The production is a success, and Jason, seeing the audience's reaction, comes to accept it and goes on to write more plays, while Linda returns to teaching and recovers her reputation. Some time later she runs into Tom in her favourite bookshop; over coffee they discover that they have much more in common than they thought, and she cautiously accepts his invitation to a proper date.

The film received mixed reviews, with 46% approval on Rotten Tomatoes,.

title: Europa Report

overview: A crew of international astronauts are sent on a private mission to Jupiter's fourth moon.
plot:
Europa Report is a 2013 science fiction film directed by Sebastián Cordero and written by Dean Georgaris. The movie follows a team of astronauts on a mission to one of Jupiter's moons, Europa.

The story begins with the launch of the spaceship, Europa One, which is crewed by five astronauts: Amara (Michael Nyqvist), Chris (Sharlto Copley), Ash (Anamaria Marinca), Tom (Daniel Wu), and Captain Leckert (Julian Glover). The mission is to explore Europa's subsurface ocean, which is believed to contain liquid water and potentially support life.

Upon arrival at Europa, the crew begins their exploration of the moon's surface. They deploy a rover to collect samples from the ice crust and conduct experiments on the moon's geology. However, during one of these experiments, the rover malfunctions, causing it to crash into the ice.

The crew soon discovers that the malfunction has caused a catastrophic failure of the ship's life support systems, putting everyone's lives at risk. As they try to repair the damage and find a way to survive, they realize that their mission has become a fight for survival against time.

As tensions rise among the crew members, they must work together to overcome their differences and find a solution to their predicament. Meanwhile, Amara begins to suspect that something is amiss with the ship's systems, which puts her at odds with Captain Leckert.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when it becomes clear that the malfunction was not an accident, but rather a deliberate act of sabotage. The crew soon discovers that one of their own members has been secretly working against them, and they must figure out who is behind the betrayal before it's too late.

As the situation spirals out of control, the crew faces numerous challenges, including equipment failures, toxic gas leaks, and a rapidly deteriorating living environment. In the end, only two crew members manage to escape the ship in a lifeboat, leaving behind their colleagues to face an uncertain fate.

The movie ends with Amara and Chris floating away from Europa, unsure of what lies ahead but determined to survive. The final shot is of the lifeless body of Captain Leckert, who had been hiding a dark secret that ultimately led to his downfall.

Europa Report received critical acclaim for its realistic portrayal of space travel and exploration, as well as its tense and suspenseful plot. While it may not have achieved mainstream success, the movie has developed a loyal following among science fiction fans and is widely regarded as one of the best sci-fi films of the 2010s.

Overall, Europa Report is a gripping and thought-provoking film that explores the challenges and risks faced by astronauts on a mission to explore the unknown. With its realistic portrayal of space travel and its tense plot, it's a must-see for fans of science fiction.

title: Prison Break: The Final Break
tagline: Prepare yourself for the truth
overview: The movie covers the events which occurred in between the downfall of The Company and the finale of the TV series (SEASON 4). It details the arrest and incarceration of Sara Tancredi, the final escape plan which Michael devises for Sara, and reveals the ultimate fate of Gretchen Morgan.
plot:
Prison Break: The Final Break is a television film of 2009 in the Prison Break franchise, directed by Brad Turner and Kevin Hooks, which covers the events between the fall of the Company and the revelation of Michael Scofield's death in the fourth season's finale. Wentworth Miller plays Michael and Sarah Wayne Callies Sara Tancredi, with Dominic Purcell as Lincoln Burrows, William Fichtner as Alexander Mahone, Amaury Nolasco as Fernando Sucre, Robert Knepper as T-Bag, Jodi Lyn O'Keefe as Gretchen Morgan and Lori Petty as the inmate Daddy.

The pregnant Sara is arrested for murdering Christina Scofield and held in an overcrowded Miami prison where Gretchen is also an inmate, while T-Bag and General Krantz are locked in the adjacent men's wing. The General places a $100,000 bounty on Sara, who survives a poisoning and learns that her baby will be taken from her after birth. When the warden refuses to protect her, Michael resolves to break her out with Lincoln and Sucre. Gretchen spots them and demands to be included. Mahone, offered his FBI job back if he can incriminate Michael, offers his help, while FBI agent Todd Wheatley searches Michael's flat and finds prison plans. Inside, Sara joins the gang of an inmate called Daddy, and Gretchen protects her, hoping to escape and see her daughter, Emily.

Michael devises a plan to parachute into the prison, paying T-Bag with the bounty money, stolen by Lincoln and Sucre, to set off a fire alarm. Mahone leaks the parachute plan to Wheatley, but on escape night the FBI shoots a dummy while Michael slips in beneath the agent's car. Gretchen stalls the guards and is taken away, leaving Sara a necklace for Emily. When the money transfer falls through, T-Bag betrays them and the alarms are shut off, as Michael had expected. Unable to open an electronic lock, Michael sends Sara on and short-circuits the door, electrocuting himself. Sara escapes to Lincoln, Sucre and Mahone, who reveals he was part of Michael's real plan all along. As Lincoln and Sara sail for the Dominican Republic, they watch a video in which Michael reveals that his brain tumour had returned and asks them to look after each other and the child.

Made available shortly after the series finale, the film aired on Sky1 in the United Kingdom on 27 May 2009 and was released on DVD and Blu-ray in the United States on 21 July. MovieWeb praised Callies' spirited performance.

As they near their destination, Luffy and Nami discover that the WOD are being hunted by the World Government, which seeks to exploit their powers for its own gain. The duo must use all their skills and cunning to evade capture and reach the WOD before it's too late.

Throughout the film, Luffy's character development is on full display as he grapples with his newfound powers and the weight of his responsibilities as a pirate. His relationships with Nami and other characters are also explored in depth, adding an emotional layer to the story.

title: Like Father, Like Son
tagline: At what point does a father truly become a father?
overview: Ryota Nonomiya is a successful businessman driven by money. He learns that his biological son was switched with another child after birth. He must make a life-changing decision and choose his true son or the boy he raised as his own.
plot:
Like Father, Like Son is a Japanese drama film of 2013 from writer, director and editor Hirokazu Kore-eda, giving Masaharu Fukuyama his first part as a father. Machiko Ono plays his wife Midori, with Keita Ninomiya as their son Keita, Shōgen Hwang as Ryūsei, Yōko Maki and Lily Franky as Yukari and Yūdai Saiki, and Jun Fubuki, Isao Natsuyagi, Jun Kunimura and Kirin Kiki in supporting roles.

Ryōta Nonomiya is a successful architect so absorbed by his career that he neglects Midori and their son Keita. One day Midori tells him that the hospital where Keita was born urgently wants to see them. There they learn that their biological son, Ryūsei, was switched with Keita at birth, and once DNA tests confirm the mistake, they face an agonising choice: keep the boy they have raised or exchange him for the child who is theirs by blood. They meet the other family, the Saikis, a small-town couple who lack Ryōta's money and ambition but understand far better the bond between parents and children, and for the first time see photographs of Ryūsei. After a series of meetings, the families begin swapping the boys for weekend visits. Since the Saikis have two other children, Ryōta tactlessly proposes that he and Midori raise both boys, deeply offending them.

The couples sue the hospital, and in court a nurse confesses that she switched the babies on purpose: newly married and struggling with her stepchildren, she envied the Nonomiyas' happiness. The statute of limitations protects her from prosecution. The families finally agree to exchange the boys permanently, but all four parents grieve for the sons they have lost, and both children withdraw, until Ryūsei runs away back to the Saikis and Ryōta has to fetch him home. When the nurse sends money as an apology, Ryōta goes to return it and confront her, only for her stepson to step in to defend her. Slowly Ryōta and Midori begin to bond with Ryūsei. Then, looking through his camera, Ryōta finds a series of pictures Keita secretly took of him, mostly asleep, and breaks down in tears. Visiting the Saikis, he follows the fleeing Keita, apologises for failing him as a father, and the two reconcile before both families go into the house together.

The film premiered in competition at the Cannes Film Festival in May 2013, where it received a long standing ovation and won the Jury Prize. It topped the Japanese box office for two weeks and passed three billion yen, and critics praised it highly, with 87% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: The Wizards Return: Alex vs. Alex
original_title: The Wizards Return: Alex vs. Alex
tagline: Everything is not what it seems.
overview: While visiting Italy with her family, a young wizard accidentally creates an evil version of herself.
plot:
The Wizards Return: Alex vs. Alex is a 2013 American television special based on the Disney Channel Original Series Wizards of Waverly Place, directed by Victor Gonzalez. Selena Gomez stars as Alex Russo, with Jake T. Austin, Jennifer Stone, Maria Canals-Barrera and David DeLuise reprising their roles from the series; David Henrie, who played Alex's brother Justin, does not appear, although the character is mentioned. Filmed mainly at Disney's studios in late 2012, the special premiered on the Disney Channel in the United States on 15 March 2013.

The Russo family, Alex's best friend Harper and Alex's werewolf boyfriend Mason throw a celebration for Justin, who has taken over as headmaster of the wizard school WizTech. Dominic, a WizTech student, arrives to explain that Justin is too busy to attend and flirts with Alex, making Mason jealous. Alex's father, Jerry, announces a family reunion in Tuscany. Alex magically creates a portal linking the family's Italian villa with their New York loft to save on travel, but Jerry scolds her for her selfishness and immaturity.

Hoping to prove that she is no longer the irresponsible wizard she once was, Alex casts a spell to rid herself of the negative parts of her personality, but it backfires and creates an evil double who emerges from a mirror and escapes to Italy. Meanwhile, Alex's brother Max chases after an Italian girl, unaware that she is his cousin, and their parents, Jerry and Theresa, follow him, starting the reunion early. Evil Alex, aided by a mysterious wizard, shrinks and imprisons Max, Jerry and Theresa. The accomplice is revealed to be Dominic, nephew of Gorog, the former leader of the Angels of Darkness. Following the trail to the Leaning Tower of Pisa, where Harper is also captured, Alex discovers that Dominic plans to use a spell replicator at the top of the tower to trap all mortals in tiny beads and take over the world, and he needs Alex's power to do it. Alex must face her evil reflection and defeat Dominic to save her family and the world.

The special drew 5.9 million viewers on its premiere in the United States. In the United Kingdom it attracted 575,000 viewers, making it at the time Disney Channel UK's third most-watched broadcast. It served as a reunion of the series, which had ended in 2012 after four seasons.

This exploration of masculinity is nuanced and multifaceted, highlighting the ways in which societal expectations can constrain individual expression.

Ultimately, Witching & Bitching is a film about finding one's place in the world and embracing one's true self, even if that means challenging the status quo. title: Odd Thomas
tagline: I might see dead people... But then, by God, I do something about it.
overview: In a California desert town, a short-order cook with clairvoyant abilities encounters a mysterious man with a link to dark, threatening forces.
plot:
Odd Thomas is a 2013 American supernatural thriller film written, directed and co-produced by Stephen Sommers, based on Dean Koontz's 2003 novel of the same name. Anton Yelchin stars as Odd Thomas, a short-order cook with psychic abilities, with Addison Timlin as his girlfriend Stormy Llewellyn, Willem Dafoe as Police Chief Wyatt Porter, Gugu Mbatha-Raw, Nico Tortorella and Patton Oswalt in supporting roles.

Odd works as a cook at a diner in the small desert town of Pico Mundo, California. He has the ability to see the spirits of the dead, who sometimes seek his help in finding justice, and he quietly solves crimes with the support of Chief Porter, one of the few people who know his secret. He can also see bodachs, invisible, shadowy creatures that feed on pain and suffering and gather in large numbers wherever death and violence are about to happen.

One day a strange man enters the diner surrounded by an unusually large swarm of bodachs. Odd nicknames him "Fungus Bob" because of his peculiar hair and follows him home, where he discovers files about mass murderers and evidence that Bob is planning something terrible. Odd also experiences disturbing visions of a massacre, involving men in bowling shirts and dead bodies. Chief Porter assigns deputies to watch Bob, and Odd, together with Stormy, whom he believes he is destined to marry, races to identify the target and the date of the coming attack. Bob is soon found dead, yet the bodachs continue to multiply across Pico Mundo, signaling that the danger has not passed and that others are involved in the plot. With the town's annual events approaching, Odd must determine who among the people around him is responsible before the tragedy he has foreseen comes to pass.

Although completed in 2013, the film was held up for years by legal disputes between its producers and financiers and received only a limited release in a few markets before reaching video on demand in the United States in 2016. Reviews were mixed: critics praised Yelchin's charismatic performance and the film's light, fast-moving tone, but some found its visual effects and storytelling uneven. Koontz himself publicly praised the adaptation.

title: We Are the Nobles
tagline: A falta de plata... Sale el cobre
overview: Tells the "riches to rags" story of the Nobles, three upper-class twenty-somethings that appear to have no limits to their checkbooks, and no direction in their lives. Until one day, their father tries to teach them a lesson by staging a financial scandal that forces the whole family to escape to an old house in the poor side of town, and leads the "kids" to do what they haven't done before: get jobs.
plot:
Nosotros los Nobles, released in English as The Noble Family and We Are the Nobles, is a 2013 Mexican comedy directed by Gary Alazraki in his feature debut. Gonzalo Vega stars as a wealthy businessman, with Luis Gerardo Méndez, Karla Souza and Juan Pablo Gil as his spoiled children and Ianis Guerrero, Karla Sofía Gascón and Mario Haddad in supporting roles. The film was loosely inspired by the 1949 Luis Buñuel comedy El gran calavera.

In modern Mexico City, the widowed construction magnate Germán Noble is so absorbed in his work that he has failed to notice that his three grown children are wasting their lives and his money. Javier nominally works at his father's company but spends his time partying and dreaming up absurd business schemes. Bárbara, a socialite, is about to become engaged to Peter, an older man with a string of failed businesses who is chiefly interested in her trust fund. The youngest, Carlos, has just been expelled from university after being caught with one of his professors.

After suffering a heart attack, Germán decides to teach his children a lesson. He tells them that an embezzling partner and union troubles have led the government to freeze his assets and that the whole family could be sent to prison. Convincing them to cut off contact with their friends, he moves the family into a dilapidated house that once belonged to his father in a modest neighborhood. For the first time in their lives, the children must get jobs: Carlos becomes a bank teller, while Lucho, the nephew of the family's former maid, helps Bárbara find work as a waitress and Javier as a bus driver. Struggling to pay bills in a crumbling house, the siblings begin to see the world differently. Bárbara realizes that Lucho, whom she once looked down on, is a good man; Javier recognizes that his old friends were shallow hangers-on; and Carlos finds discipline. Germán, meanwhile, discovers struggles his children had hidden from him and realizes how absent he was while they were growing up. His deception is threatened when Peter tracks down the family and learns the truth.

The film was a word-of-mouth phenomenon. It opened fourth at the Mexican box office before climbing to first place in its fourth weekend, briefly becoming the highest-grossing Mexican film of all time, and it ultimately grossed about $26 million. It was remade in Italy as Belli di papà, in Colombia as Malcriados and in France as Pourris gâtés.

title: The Raid 2
tagline: It's not over yet.
overview: After fighting his way through an apartment building populated by an army of dangerous criminals and escaping with his life, SWAT team member Rama goes undercover, joining a powerful Indonesian crime syndicate to protect his family and uncover corrupt members of his own force.
plot:
The Raid 2 (Indonesian title: The Raid 2: Berandal) is a 2014 Indonesian action thriller written, edited and directed by Welsh filmmaker Gareth Evans. A sequel to The Raid (2011), it brings back Iko Uwais as the tactical officer Rama, joined by Arifin Putra, Oka Antara, Tio Pakusadewo, Alex Abbad and Julie Estelle. As in Evans's earlier films, the fight scenes showcase the Indonesian martial art of pencak silat.

Hours after the first film, Rama brings his wounded colleague Bowo and the corrupt officer Wahyu to Lieutenant Bunawar, head of a secret unit investigating police corruption, who executes Wahyu and asks Rama to help expose the network of corrupt commissioner Reza. Rama refuses until he learns that his brother, Andi, has been killed by the rising gangster Bejo and that his own wife and son are in danger. To infiltrate the Bangun family, a crime syndicate that shares control of Jakarta with a Japanese yakuza clan led by Hideaki Gotō, Rama is sent to the same prison as Bangun's volatile son, Uco, and earns his trust by saving him during a riot. Rama then joins the family and, planting a bug in Uco's wallet, learns that the resentful Uco is secretly plotting with Bejo to provoke a war with the Gotō clan.

Bejo's assassins murder Bangun's loyal enforcer Prakoso and the killing is blamed on Gotō, but Bangun refuses to retaliate, and when Uco embarrasses him at a meeting with Gotō, Bangun cedes territory to keep the peace and later beats his son. Bejo's men then storm Bangun's office, where Uco kills his father and wounds Bangun's aide Eka. Rama, having just survived an ambush by Reza's officers, helps Eka escape but is captured and driven off to be killed; Eka rescues him and, dying, reveals that he too was an undercover officer, urging Rama to bring down the whole underworld. Learning that Reza has sided with Bejo and Uco, Gotō declares war on all three. Bunawar tells Rama that Reza is meeting the others at Bejo's restaurant, and Rama storms it alone. Uco, realizing he was manipulated, kills Reza and Bejo before Rama kills him. Badly hurt, Rama declines a deal from Gotō's son Keiichi, saying he is done.

Evans adapted it from Berandal, a 2009 script of his. The Raid 2 premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on 21 January 2014, and Sony Pictures Classics released it in North America on 28 March 2014. It sold more than 1.4 million tickets in Indonesia and earned about $6.8 million abroad. Critics praised it: 82% on Rotten Tomatoes and 71 on Metacritic.

title: Mercy
tagline: Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.
overview: A single mom and her two boys help take care of their grandmother with mystical powers.
plot:
Mercy is a 2014 American supernatural horror film directed by Peter Cornwell from a screenplay by Matt Greenberg, loosely based on Stephen King's short story "Gramma", collected in Skeleton Crew. Chandler Riggs stars as George, with Joel Courtney as his brother Buddy, Frances O'Connor as their mother Rebecca, Shirley Knight as their grandmother Mercy, Mark Duplass as their Uncle Lanning, Dylan McDermott as the neighbour and photographer Jim Swann, and Eddie Jones as the local pastor. Jason Blum produced it through Blumhouse Productions with McG, who brought Greenberg's script to Blum.

The film opens with a young Mercy nursing a child as her husband Frank kills himself with an axe. Years later, when the elderly Mercy suffers a medical episode and slips into a strange stupor, the single mother Rebecca brings George and Buddy to live in the old woman's isolated, dilapidated country house so the family can care for her rather than send her to a home. George loves his grandmother, but he soon senses that something supernatural is wrong with her. By questioning the pastor and his hard-drinking, wisecracking uncle, he gradually pieces together the dark family secrets connected to a mysterious book of black magic: unable to have children, Mercy once read from the forbidden Necronomicon and made a pact with a demon named Hastur so that she could become a mother.

In a sequence drawn most directly from King's story, Rebecca takes Buddy to the hospital and George is left alone in the house with his grandmother. He believes she has died, only to be assailed by her witchcraft, and he flees to look for help, discovering that Jim, who has grown close to Rebecca, is not the ally he seemed. In the climax, the demon tries to drive George to kill himself in the same way as his grandfather, but he turns the axe on Mercy instead, and the family later buries her beneath a tree, a different ending from the short story's.

Mercy was eventually issued straight to DVD, Blu-ray and video on demand by Universal Pictures Home Entertainment on October 7, 2014. Reviews were largely unfavourable. Dread Central called it an absorbing if quirky suspense drama with strong performances, especially Knight's, but found its story unoriginal and its CGI excessive, and CinemaBlend argued that it buried King's personal, atmospheric tale under invented subplots and lacked any real scares.

title: Child 44
tagline: How do you find a killer who doesn’t exist?
overview: Set in Stalin-era Soviet Union, a disgraced MGB agent is dispatched to investigate a series of child murders -- a case that begins to connect with the very top of party leadership.
plot:
Child 44 is a 2015 mystery thriller directed by Daniel Espinosa and written by Richard Price, adapted from Tom Rob Smith's 2008 novel. The ensemble cast features Tom Hardy, Gary Oldman, Noomi Rapace, Joel Kinnaman, Paddy Considine, Jason Clarke and Vincent Cassel. Both the novel and the film are very loosely based on the case of the Soviet serial killer Andrei Chikatilo.

In the Soviet Union of the early 1950s, under Stalin, Leo Demidov, a war hero and an agent of the Ministry of State Security (MGB), encounters a series of brutal child murders, but his superiors refuse to call them murders because official doctrine holds that serial killers are a product of capitalism. Leo's wife, Raisa, is accused of disloyalty, a charge Leo suspects was engineered by his ambitious rival, Vasili Nikitin. When Leo refuses to denounce her, he is demoted to the militia in the town of Volsk under General Mikhail Nesterov, and Raisa is forced to work as a janitor. Vasili urges Raisa to leave Leo for him and, when she refuses, has her mistreated.

When more murdered children are found in Volsk, Raisa joins Leo's investigation, and together they persuade Nesterov and his wife, Inessa, that a serial killer is at work. They discover at least 44 victims and realize that the killer travels the railways. On a secret trip to Moscow to interview a witness, Raisa realizes that a former colleague they turn to is an informer, and Leo kills him. Arrested on their return to Volsk, the couple are sent by train to a labor camp, where passengers attack them on Vasili's orders. They kill their attackers, jump from the train and make their way to Rostov, where most of the victims were found. By matching factory workers' travel records with the dates and places of the murders, Leo identifies Vladimir Malevich, a tractor factory worker, as the killer. Malevich surrenders, but Vasili, who has followed them, shoots him dead and tries to execute the couple, who kill him in a struggle. Leo blames Vasili's death on Malevich, whom the MGB falsely brands a Nazi agent. Reinstated, Leo asks to set up a homicide division in Moscow, and he and Raisa adopt two orphaned girls whose parents Vasili had executed.

Filmed in the Czech Republic and Romania, the film was released on 17 April 2015 but was withdrawn from Russian cinemas over its depiction of Soviet history. It grossed only $13 million on a $50 million budget, with critics praising Hardy but giving it 30% on Rotten Tomatoes and 41 on Metacritic.

title: Night at the Museum: Secret of the Tomb
original_title: Night at the Museum: Secret of the Tomb
tagline: One Final Night to Save the Day.
overview: When the magic powers of The Tablet of Ahkmenrah begin to die out, Larry Daley spans the globe, uniting favorite and new characters while embarking on an epic quest to save the magic before it is gone forever.
plot:
Night at the Museum: Secret of the Tomb is a 2014 American fantasy comedy directed by Shawn Levy and written by David Guion and Michael Handelman. The third and final live-action instalment of the Night at the Museum series, it stars Ben Stiller as the night guard Larry Daley and as the Neanderthal Laaa, with Robin Williams as Theodore Roosevelt, Owen Wilson as Jedediah, Steve Coogan, Rami Malek as Ahkmenrah, Dan Stevens as Sir Lancelot, Rebel Wilson and Ben Kingsley.

In 1938, archaeologists in Egypt uncover the Tablet of Ahkmenrah, despite warnings that removing it will bring "the end". Seventy-six years later, Larry is still the night guard at New York's Museum of Natural History, where exhibits come alive at night. During a gala to reopen the Hayden Planetarium, a creeping corrosion on the tablet causes the exhibits to run amok, while a new Neanderthal figure modelled on Larry treats him as his father. Former guard Cecil Fredericks, whose father found the tablet, says its magic is dying and that only Ahkmenrah's parents, displayed in the British Museum, may be able to save it.

Larry gets the curator, Dr. McPhee, to let him take Ahkmenrah to London with his son Nick, and finds that Roosevelt, the miniatures Jedediah and Octavius, Sacagawea, Attila the Hun, Dexter the monkey and Laaa have stowed away. Slipping past the guard Tilly, they bring the British Museum's exhibits to life and are joined by a wax figure of Sir Lancelot, while the American exhibits begin to stiffen and lose their memories. Ahkmenrah's parents explain that moonlight can recharge the tablet, but Lancelot steals it, believing it to be the Holy Grail, and bursts onstage during a performance of the musical Camelot, where he learns that King Arthur and his court are only legend. Told he can still have a life, he returns the tablet, and moonlight restores it. The exhibits agree that Ahkmenrah and the tablet should stay with his family, though it means they will no longer come alive, and Larry bids his friends farewell at dawn. Three years later, Larry has become a schoolteacher, and when Tilly brings the tablet to New York with a travelling exhibition, he smiles from across the street as the exhibits awaken once more.

Shot in London and British Columbia and released by 20th Century Fox in December 2014, the film grossed $363.2 million worldwide on a $127 million budget. Reviews were mixed. It features the final performances of Robin Williams and Mickey Rooney and is dedicated to them.

title: Star Wars: The Last Jedi
tagline: Darkness rises... and light to meet it
overview: Rey develops her newly discovered abilities with the guidance of Luke Skywalker, who is unsettled by the strength of her powers. Meanwhile, the Resistance prepares to do battle with the First Order.
plot:
Star Wars: The Last Jedi is a 2017 science fiction film directed by Rian Johnson, written by Johnson and Mark Hamill, and produced by Kathleen Kennedy, J.J. Abrams, and Dave Filoni.

The film takes place immediately after the events of The Force Awakens (2015). The Resistance, led by General Leia Organa (Carrie Fisher), is on the run from the First Order, a new evil force risen from the ashes of the Galactic Empire. Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamill), the legendary Jedi Master, has gone into exile on the planet Ahch-To, where he hopes to rebuild the Jedi Order.

The story begins with Rey (Daisy Ridley) searching for Luke, hoping to find a way to restore balance to the Force and defeat the First Order. She encounters Finn (John Boyega), a former Stormtrooper who has defected to the Resistance, and Poe Dameron (Oscar Isaac), a skilled pilot. The trio embarks on a perilous journey to find Luke, facing numerous challenges along the way.

Meanwhile, Kylo Ren (Adam Driver), the conflicted leader of the First Order, is struggling with his own identity and loyalties. He is torn between his allegiance to the dark side and his lingering connection to Rey, who he believes may be strong in the Force.

As Rey searches for Luke, she encounters a series of cryptic clues and visions that lead her to Canto Bight, a luxurious casino planet where she meets DJ (Benicio del Toro), a skilled hacker. However, their encounter is short-lived, as they are pursued by Kylo Ren's forces.

Rey eventually finds Luke on Ahch-To, but he is reluctant to return to the Jedi Order, fearing that he will only lead to more suffering and conflict. Rey convinces him to train her in the ways of the Force, and they embark on a journey to confront their pasts and find redemption.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the Resistance and the First Order, with Luke using his newfound connection to the Force to help turn the tide of the battle. However, Kylo Ren ultimately discovers Rey's true identity as strong in the Force, leading to a confrontation that leaves both characters severely injured.

In the aftermath, Rey sets out on her own journey, determined to find a new purpose and bring balance to the Force. Luke, meanwhile, is left to grapple with his own guilt and regret, realizing too late that he may have inadvertently contributed to the rise of the First Order.

The film concludes with a poignant moment between Leia and Rey, as they share a heartfelt goodbye before Leia's passing. The final shot is of Rey standing on the deck of the Resistance ship, looking out at the stars, ready to embark on her own journey into the unknown.

Overall, Star Wars: The Last Jedi is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores complex themes of identity, loyalty, and redemption in a galaxy far, far away.

plot:
Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker is a 2019 science fiction film directed by J.J. Abrams, written by Abrams and Chris Terrio, and produced by Lucasfilm Ltd.

The film takes place nine years after the events of The Last Jedi (2017) and follows the story of Rey (Daisy Ridley), Finn (John Boyega), Poe Dameron (Oscar Isaac), and Kylo Ren (Adam Driver). The Resistance, led by General Leia Organa (Carrie Fisher in a previously recorded performance), is on the run from the First Order, which has taken over the galaxy.

The film begins with Rey discovering that she is strong in the Force, but also struggling to understand her connection to it. She sets out on a journey to find Luke Skywalker (Mark Hamill), who has gone into exile after the events of The Last Jedi. Along the way, she encounters Ben Solo, Kylo Ren's father, who was thought to be dead.

As Rey searches for Luke, she is pursued by Kylo Ren and his allies, including Supreme Leader Snoke's (Andy Serkis) clone, Emperor Palpatine (Ian McDiarmid). The film's plot thickens as it becomes clear that Palpatine has returned from the dead and is seeking to reclaim his power over the galaxy.

Meanwhile, Finn and Poe are on a mission to disable the First Order's ability to track the Resistance. They team up with Rose Tico (Kelly Marie Tran), who has discovered a way to disable the tracking device using a code from an ancient Sith temple.

As the story unfolds, Rey discovers that she is the granddaughter of Emperor Palpatine and that she has the potential to become a powerful Force user. However, she also struggles with her connection to the dark side, which is represented by Kylo Ren.

The film's climax features an epic battle between the Resistance and the First Order on the planet Exegol, where Rey confronts Palpatine and Kylo Ren. In a surprising twist, it is revealed that Emperor Palpatine had been manipulating events from behind the scenes to bring about his own return to power.

In the end, Rey uses her connection to the Force to defeat Palpatine and destroy him once and for all. However, in doing so, she also sacrifices herself, as she becomes one with the Force. The film ends on a hopeful note, with Finn, Poe, and Rose mourning the loss of their friend, but also celebrating their victory over the First Order.

Throughout the film, there are many nods to classic Star Wars characters and storylines, including a memorable appearance by Emperor Palpatine's iconic theme music. The film's climax features an epic lightsaber duel between Rey and Kylo Ren, which is reminiscent of the iconic duels between Luke Skywalker and Darth Vader in the original trilogy.

Overall, Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker is a satisfying conclusion to the sequel trilogy, bringing together many of the storylines and characters from the previous two films. While it has its flaws, the film's epic scope, memorable characters, and nostalgic value make it a must-see for fans of the franchise.

title: Enemy
tagline: You can’t escape Yourself!
overview: A mild-mannered college professor discovers a look-alike actor and delves into the other man's private affairs.
plot:
Enemy is a psychological thriller film directed by Denis Villeneuve, released in 2013. The movie follows the story of Adam Bell (played by Jake Gyllenhaal), an academic who teaches at a university in Toronto.

The film begins with Adam's mundane life as he lectures to his students and navigates his relationships with his colleagues and friends. He is particularly close to his colleague, Mary Svevo (played by Mélanie Laurent). However, their friendship seems unfulfilling, and Adam feels an emptiness within himself.

One day, while walking down the street, Adam encounters a man who bears an uncanny resemblance to him - Anthony St. Claire (also played by Jake Gyllenhaal). The doppelganger is charming, confident, and seemingly more fulfilled than Adam. Despite initial reservations, Adam becomes fascinated with Anthony and starts to secretly meet him.

As their relationship deepens, Adam begins to question his own identity and sense of self. He becomes increasingly obsessed with Anthony, who represents a life that Adam feels he has never truly lived. The two men start to swap lives, with Adam taking on Anthony's persona and vice versa.

The plot thickens as Adam starts to notice discrepancies between his life and Anthony's. He discovers that Anthony is married to Mary Svevo, which further complicates their relationship. As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Anthony is not just a doppelganger but also a representation of Adam's darker impulses and desires.

Throughout the film, Villeneuve masterfully explores themes of identity, duality, and the human condition. The cinematography is stunning, with a muted color palette that adds to the overall sense of unease and tension.

As the story reaches its climax, Adam is forced to confront the consequences of his actions. He must choose between embracing his true self or continuing to live a life that is not authentic to him. In the end, Adam makes a decision that will change his life forever.

The ending of Enemy is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the nature of identity and reality. The film's final shot of Adam walking away from Anthony's apartment suggests that he has finally found a sense of self-acceptance, but the viewer is left wondering if this is truly the case.

Overall, Enemy is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that explores the complexities of human psychology. With its masterful direction and outstanding performances, it is a must-see for fans of psychological thrillers.

plot:
Justice League: The Flashpoint Paradox is a 2013 animated superhero film produced by Warner Bros. Animation, based on the DC Comics storyline "The Flash of Two Worlds" and "Flashpoint". The movie takes place in an alternate universe where Barry Allen, aka The Flash (Ezra Miller), has become a crime lord in Central City.

In this reality, Barry's life took a dark turn after his mother, Nora Allen, was murdered by a man named Reverse-Flash (Tom Cavanagh). This event led to Barry becoming obsessed with stopping the villain and eventually discovering he had superhuman speed. However, instead of using his powers for good, Barry became a ruthless crime lord who terrorized Central City.

The story begins with Barry's life as a crime lord, where he is feared by everyone in the city. Meanwhile, in the Justice League headquarters, Superman (James Arnold Taylor) and Batman (Kevin Conroy) are discussing the threat of Darkseid, an intergalactic warlord who seeks to conquer Earth. However, their conversation is interrupted by the arrival of Barry Allen, who has come to join the Justice League.

Upon meeting the team, Barry's presence causes a rift in the timeline, creating a new reality where Superman and Batman are not present. In this reality, Darkseid has taken over Central City, and Barry must navigate his way through the city to stop him.

As Barry navigates this new world, he meets a young version of himself (Ezra Miller) who is struggling to control his powers. The two Barrys form an alliance to take down Darkseid's army and ultimately face off against the villain himself.

Throughout the movie, the Flashpoint Paradox storyline unfolds, revealing that Barry's actions in this reality have created a catastrophic timeline where Superman and Batman are not present. The team must work together to find a way to restore the original timeline and bring balance back to the universe.

In the climactic final battle, Barry and his allies face off against Darkseid's army, while also dealing with the consequences of their actions in this reality. Ultimately, they succeed in defeating Darkseid and restoring the original timeline.

The movie concludes with Barry returning to his own reality, where he is reunited with his mother's spirit (voiced by Kari Wahlgren). The film ends on a hopeful note, as Barry reflects on the lessons he learned from his journey through Flashpoint Paradox.

title: Capturing Avatar
overview: Capturing Avatar is a feature length behind-the-scenes documentary about the making of Avatar. It uses footage from the film's development, as well as stock footage from as far back as the production of Titanic in 1995. Also included are numerous interviews with cast, artists, and other crew members. The documentary was released as a bonus feature on the extended collector's edition of Avatar.
plot:
Capturing Avatar is a 2010 American feature-length documentary directed by Laurent Bouzereau and produced by Mob Scene about the making of James Cameron's science fiction epic Avatar. Running about 98 minutes, it was released on 16 November 2010 as the centrepiece of the bonus material on the second disc of 20th Century Fox's three-disc Avatar: Extended Collector's Edition on DVD and Blu-ray, which presented three versions of the film along with deleted scenes and extensive production archives.

The documentary traces the long evolution of the project and Cameron's journey in bringing it to the screen, combining footage shot during development and production with archive material reaching back to 1995, before the making of Titanic. Cameron and producer Jon Landau recall and demonstrate their original tests of performance capture technology in that period, explain how the project was then set aside for about ten years, and describe how Fox finally gave the go-ahead for production to begin in 2007. Comments from the late visual effects pioneer Stan Winston are also included.

A major thread is the development of the groundbreaking performance capture techniques that allowed actors to drive every movement of the digital Na'vi characters on screen, and the film follows how these methods advanced over the course of production. It includes footage of the 2006 auditions and screen tests of Sam Worthington, Zoe Saldaña and Joel Moore, and a moment in which Cameron explains to Sigourney Weaver that her character's surname will have to change from Shipley to Augustine so that audiences do not confuse her with Ripley, her role in Aliens.

Interviewees include Cameron, Landau, Worthington, Saldaña, Weaver, Stephen Lang, Giovanni Ribisi and Michelle Rodriguez, alongside casting director Margery Simkin and many of the artists and crew members who worked on the film. Reviewers of the collector's edition singled the documentary out among its extras; Slant Magazine described it as a groovy survey of the film's evolution and the filmmaker's journey, and Hollywood in Hi-Def highlighted its archival material on the early performance capture experiments and casting.

title: Crush
tagline: Careful what you wish for
overview: A secret admirer's crush on a high school athlete takes a fatal turn.
plot:
Crush is a 2013 American direct-to-video thriller directed by Malik Bader from a screenplay by Sonny Mallhi. The film stars Lucas Till, Crystal Reed and Sarah Bolger, with Caitríona Balfe, Reid Ewing, Leigh Whannell and Holt McCallany in supporting roles. It follows a popular high school athlete who discovers that someone has become dangerously obsessed with him. Millennium Entertainment released it on DVD, Blu-ray and video on demand in the United States in April 2013.

Scott is a talented soccer player who hopes his skill on the field will earn him an athletic scholarship. He also has a gift for art, but he puts it aside to concentrate on sport, even after a leg injury threatens his playing career. His best friend Jules has romantic feelings for him, yet Scott keeps her at a distance so as not to spoil their friendship. Bess, a quiet classmate who notices and admires his artistic side, is also drawn to him; she in turn is pursued by a classmate named Jeffrey, whose interest she ignores as her fixation on Scott deepens.

Before long an unseen stalker begins to intrude on Scott's life, and the incidents grow steadily more menacing. A teacher who flirted with him is attacked and badly hurt, and Jules narrowly escapes being killed at a party. Scott suspects Bess, knowing how she feels about him, but has no way to prove it. The situation takes a sharp turn when Scott, driving one evening, accidentally strikes Andie, a young woman who works with Bess, and offers to drive her home because she has hurt her leg. Inside her house the truth comes out: Andie is the stalker, and she knocks Scott unconscious and imprisons him in her basement, deliberately aggravating his injured leg to keep him from escaping. Scott's struggle to get free, and the efforts of the people around him to work out what has happened, lead to the film's violent climax.

Reviews were generally unfavorable. Scott Weinberg, writing for FEARnet, praised the performances of the three leads but criticized the thin premise and a script he considered derivative, noting its similarity to Mallhi's earlier screenplay for The Roommate and arguing that the film offered little in the way of suspense, character or surprise.

title: [REC]⁴ Apocalypse
tagline: It’s time to leave.
overview: Ángela Vidal, the young television reporter who entered the building with the firemen, manages to make it out alive. plot:
[REC]⁴ Apocalypse (Spanish: [REC] 4: Apocalipsis) is a Spanish action horror film of 2014 and the fourth and final instalment of the [REC] series, directed by Jaume Balagueró, co-director of the first two films. A direct sequel to [REC]², it picks up immediately afterwards, with Manuela Velasco reprising her role as the television reporter Ángela Vidal, alongside Paco Manzanedo as Guzmán, Héctor Colomé as Dr. Ricarte, Ismael Fritschi as the technician Nic and Críspulo Cabezas as Lucas.

A special forces team storms the quarantined apartment building to rescue Ángela and destroy the site; only two soldiers, Lucas and Guzmán, survive the infected residents. Ángela wakes chained to a bed aboard an isolated ship at sea, remembering nothing. Ricarte assures her she is not infected while his team studies the virus in an onboard laboratory, and Nic reconstructs the footage from her camera. During a power cut an infected test monkey escapes and bites the cook, who contaminates the food, turning most of the crew and guards. Ángela, Guzmán, Lucas and an elderly survivor of a wedding outbreak make for the bridge, but the old woman turns and Lucas is forced to shoot her.

Ricarte realises that an antidote requires an unmutated strain, and the reconstructed footage reveals that Ángela was orally infected with a worm-like parasite by the original carrier. He tries to cut it out of her, but an infected attack lets her escape, and she bites him. It emerges, however, that the parasite passed to Guzmán during the rescue. Guzmán traps Ángela below decks as Ricarte sets the ship to self-destruct; Lucas is killed trying to restart an engine, and Nic knocks out Ricarte to seize his lifeboat. Nic and Ángela kill a pack of infected monkeys with an outboard motor, then fight off Guzmán as he tries to pass the parasite back to her, killing him with a harpoon gun. The pair leap into the sea as the ship explodes, the parasite is swallowed by a fish, and they end up in a taxi whose driver jokes about the wild party they must have been to.

The film premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2014, screened at Sitges and opened in Spain on 31 October. Reviews were mixed to positive, welcoming Velasco's return though some found it a weak finale, and it holds 68% on Rotten Tomatoes.

Entourage is a 2015 American satirical comedy-drama film written, directed and produced by Doug Ellin as a continuation of the HBO television series he created, which ran from 2004 to 2011. The film reunites the show's principal cast: Adrian Grenier as the movie star Vincent Chase, Kevin Connolly as his manager and best friend Eric "E" Murphy, Kevin Dillon as Vince's brother Johnny "Drama" Chase, Jerry Ferrara as Turtle and Jeremy Piven as Ari Gold. Haley Joel Osment and Billy Bob Thornton play new characters, and as in the series, many celebrities appear as themselves.

The film picks up shortly after the series finale. Vince's marriage has quickly ended, and he and his friends gather on a yacht to cheer him up. Ari, who has given up being an agent to become head of a film studio, offers Vince the lead in his first production, a futuristic take on Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde called Hyde. Vince agrees on the condition that he can direct it, with Drama in a supporting role.

Eight months later the film is in post-production and badly over budget, and Vince needs another $10 million to finish it. Ari flies to Texas to persuade the film's co-financiers, the wealthy Larsen McCredle and his son Travis, to provide more money. Travis travels to Los Angeles to see a cut, but Vince, unsure of the result, keeps postponing screenings. When Travis finally watches it, he demands major changes, including cutting Drama's scenes, while also showing a jealous interest in Vince's relationship with the model Emily Ratajkowski. With Ari's career and the film's future at stake, the friends must deal with the financier's escalating demands. Meanwhile E prepares to become a father with his ex-fiancée Sloan while juggling other romantic complications, Turtle pursues the MMA fighter Ronda Rousey, and Drama faces a personal scandal involving a leaked video.

Released by Warner Bros. in June 2015, Entourage received negative reviews from critics, who found it a self-indulgent extension of the series with little appeal beyond its fans, and it was criticized for its treatment of women. It grossed about $49 million worldwide against a budget of roughly $30 million, a disappointing result for a franchise continuation.

The Enterprise is severely damaged in the battle, and the crew is forced to make an emergency landing on a nearby planet. The ship is later repaired by a group of locals, who also reveal that Krall has been using the Federation's technology to build a massive fleet of ships.

As the crew tries to repair the Enterprise, they discover that Krall's true intention is to use the ship's technology to destroy entire planets and civilizations. Meanwhile, Spock is struggling with his Vulcan heritage and his human emotions, which are becoming increasingly difficult to control.

As the battle between the Enterprise crew and Krall's fleet reaches its climax, Kirk and his crew face off against Krall in an epic space battle. Meanwhile, Spock must confront his own identity and find a way to reconcile his human and Vulcan sides.

title: 3 Days to Kill
tagline: The question is... kill or die?
overview: A dangerous international spy is determined to give up his high stakes life to finally build a closer relationship with his estranged wife and daughter. But first, he must complete one last mission - even if it means juggling the two toughest assignments yet: hunting down the world's most ruthless terrorist and looking after his teenage daughter for the first time in ten years, while his wife is out of town.
plot:
3 Days to Kill is a 2014 action thriller film directed by McG and written by Luc Besson and Adi Hasak. Kevin Costner stars as Ethan Renner, a CIA agent dying of cancer who hopes to retire and rebuild his relationship with his estranged family, with Amber Heard as the elite agent Vivi Delay, Hailee Steinfeld as his sixteen-year-old daughter Zooey, Connie Nielsen as his ex-wife Christine, Richard Sammel as the German arms trafficker known as the Wolf, and Tómas Lemarquis as the Wolf's lieutenant, the Albino.

During an operation in a Belgrade hotel to capture the Albino, who is helping the Wolf sell a dirty bomb to terrorists, Renner becomes dizzy, wounds the Albino in the leg and blacks out, letting him escape. Vivi, assigned by the CIA Director to kill the Wolf, suspects Renner has unknowingly seen him. Renner is diagnosed with terminal glioblastoma that has spread to his lungs and is told he will not live to the following Christmas. Having kept his work secret from Christine and Zooey for decades at the cost of losing them, he returns to Paris to make amends, only to find an African family squatting in his apartment whom the police say he cannot evict until after winter. Christine lets him reconnect with Zooey and leaves her in his care while she travels on business. Vivi then offers him an experimental drug that could greatly extend his life in exchange for hunting down the Wolf, and he reluctantly agrees. Working through the gang's limousine driver and accountant, he pursues the Albino while battling hallucinations brought on by the drug whenever his heart rate rises, which he can only control with alcohol, and while handling Zooey's lies and school troubles. Gradually he wins back his daughter's trust. After killing the Albino in the subway, Renner discovers that the father of Zooey's boyfriend is the Wolf's business partner, and at a party there he protects his family and sends the Wolf plunging down an elevator shaft. Facing the injured Wolf, Renner cannot pull the trigger, citing his promise to his wife to quit, and Vivi kills the Wolf herself. Renner lives to spend Christmas at a beach house with his family and receives a gift of more of the medicine, as Vivi watches from a nearby hill.

Released in February 2014, the film grossed $53.3 million against a $28 million budget. Reviews were mixed, with a 27% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a consensus finding its action accomplished but its family conflict underdeveloped.

The government's actions are driven by a desire for power and control, which puts them at odds with those who value freedom and individuality.

Throughout the film, Captain Harlock remains a symbol of resistance against an oppressive regime. His actions are motivated by a sense of justice and a desire to protect those who cannot defend themselves. The character's backstory is also explored, revealing his troubled past and his reasons for becoming a space pirate.

The climax of the film features an epic battle between Harlock's crew and the EDF. In the end, Harlock emerges victorious, but not without sacrifices. Mika's fate is revealed, and the consequences of her visions are made clear.

The ending of Space Pirate Captain Harlock sets the stage for a new beginning, as Harlock and his crew look to the future and the challenges that lie ahead. The film concludes with a sense of hope and renewal, as Harlock remains committed to his values of freedom and justice.

Overall, Space Pirate Captain Harlock is a thrilling adventure that explores themes of resistance, individuality, and the power of the human spirit. With its stunning animation and engaging storyline, this film is a must-see for fans of science fiction and anime.

plot:
Kite (also called A Kite) is a 2014 South African-American action thriller directed by Ralph Ziman from a screenplay by Brian Cox, adapted from Yasuomi Umetsu's controversial 1998 anime of the same name. India Eisley stars as a young vigilante assassin hunting the people behind her parents' murder, with Callan McAuliffe and Samuel L. Jackson.

In a dystopian, crime-ridden society where gangs rule the streets and children are abducted and sold into trafficking rings, Sawa's mother and her father, a police officer, are killed in a double homicide. Taken under the wing of her father's former partner, Lieutenant Karl Aker, she becomes an assassin who targets criminals, posing as a prostitute to get close to her marks, with the trafficking boss known as the Emir as her ultimate target. After each killing she takes Amp, a drug supplied by Aker that dulls her pain but also wipes away her memories. When she infiltrates the Emir's operation, she kills his father and extracts information on where trafficked victims are sent, and she is confronted by Oburi, a young man from her past who begs her to stop taking Amp, though she does not remember him. Together they rescue a kidnapped child from the Emir's men and track down one of his business partners, but Sawa is nearly killed when her cover is blown. Aker, angry that her vendetta is escalating, cuts off her Amp, and as she suffers withdrawal Oburi takes her in and helps her recover the memories the drug had erased. The truth emerges: her father had uncovered evidence of corruption, and Aker, the man who raised her, was behind her parents' deaths. Aker kills Otis, a witness to the conspiracy, and confesses that he meant to use Sawa to destroy the Emir so that the two of them could take over the trafficking trade. Sawa turns on him, and the film ends with her and Oburi heading for a refuge for orphaned children.

Eisley plays Sawa, with McAuliffe as Oburi, Jackson as Aker, Carl Beukes as Vic Thornhill, Deon Lotz as Detective Prinsloo, Zane Meas as the Emir and Lionel Newton as Otis Breedlove. A live-action version had been in development since about 2003; David R. Ellis was attached to direct but died in January 2013, and Ziman took over, shooting in Johannesburg that February. Released abroad from June 2014 and on video in North America by Anchor Bay that August, it grossed about $0.5 million. Critics savaged it, giving it 0% on Rotten Tomatoes and calling it a derivative, clichéd slog.

Riggan Thomson became famous playing the superhero Birdman in a trilogy of films between 1989 and 1992, and he is still haunted by the mocking voice of his former alter ego, which urges him to return to blockbusters; at times he even seems to levitate or move objects with his mind. The production is produced by his best friend and lawyer, Jake, and co-stars his girlfriend Laura and newcomer Lesley, while his daughter Sam, a recovering addict, works as his assistant. When a falling light injures one of the actors just before previews, Lesley's boyfriend Mike Shiner, a brilliant but volatile method actor, takes over the role and immediately begins to dominate the production, sabotaging previews and even taking credit in the press for Riggan's personal motivations. Riggan's relationships with Mike and Sam grow strained, an accident leaves him stranded in his underwear in Times Square during a performance, and an influential critic, Tabitha Dickinson, promises to destroy the play without having seen it. As opening night approaches, Riggan's grip on reality loosens, and the line between his role, his ambition and his fantasies of flight becomes increasingly difficult to draw.

Birdman grossed more than $103 million worldwide and received critical acclaim for its screenplay, direction, cinematography and performances. It holds a 91% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 87 out of 100, indicating "universal acclaim". At the 87th Academy Awards it won four Oscars, for Best Picture, Best Director, Best Original Screenplay and Best Cinematography, from nine nominations, and Keaton won the Golden Globe for Best Actor in a Musical or Comedy.

As the story unfolds, his sense of self is constantly tested and challenged, leading to a profound exploration of what it means to be human.

The film also examines the theme of morality and the gray areas that exist between right and wrong. The characters in Collide are multidimensional and often flawed, making it difficult for the audience to distinguish between good and evil. This moral ambiguity serves as a commentary on how our perceptions of others can be skewed by circumstance and our own biases.

Furthermore, Collide touches on the theme of loneliness and disconnection in modern society. The characters in the film are all outsiders in their own way, struggling to form meaningful connections with others. This sense of isolation is palpable throughout the movie, adding to the overall sense of tension and unease.

Overall, Collide is a gripping thriller that explores complex themes and ideas through its intricate plot and well-developed characters.

title: Barbie Mariposa & the Fairy Princess
tagline: Friendship overcomes any obstacle.
overview: Mariposa becomes the Royal Ambassador of Flutterfield, and is sent to bring peace between her fairy land and their rivals, the Crystal Fairies of Shimmervale. While Mariposa doesn't make a great first impression on  the King, she becomes fast friends with his shy daughter, Princess Catania. plot:
Barbie Mariposa & the Fairy Princess is a 2013 computer-animated fantasy film directed by William Lau and written by Elise Allen, produced by Barbie Entertainment with Rainmaker Entertainment and released direct to video by Universal. The 25th film in the Barbie series, it is a sequel to Barbie Mariposa and part of the Fairytopia line. The voice cast includes Kelly Sheridan, Maryke Hendrikse, Tabitha St. Germain, Kathleen Barr, Alessandro Juliani and Russell Roberts, and the music was composed by Douglas Pipes, with songs including "Only a Breath Away", "Fly High" and "Be a Friend".

Since her last adventure, the butterfly fairy Mariposa has become royal historian of Flutterfield. On the recommendation of Prince Carlos, Queen Marabella appoints her ambassador to the Crystal Fairies of Shimmervale. Centuries earlier, Shimmervale's king accused the butterfly fairies of stealing Crystallite, the source of light and warmth for his realm, and the two peoples have lived as enemies ever since, each spreading rumors about the other. Doubting herself, Mariposa receives from Carlos a glowing flower holding Flutterfield's most precious magic and sets off with her furry companion Zee.

In Shimmervale, the suspicious King Regellius gives her a cold welcome, but she quickly befriends his shy daughter, Princess Catania, and learns that outsiders are forbidden to touch Crystallite, above all the powerful Heart Crystal. Catania confides that eight years earlier the dark fairy Gillion, refused a piece of Crystallite by her father, tried to kidnap her; her wings were broken in the attack, and although they healed she has not flown since. Mariposa also realizes that the king only invited her because he believes butterfly fairies are warriors who could teach his army. As a token of friendship, Catania gives Mariposa her Crystallite pendant, and Mariposa gives her the glowing flower.

At the Crystal Ball, guests spot the pendant and accuse Mariposa of theft, and the king banishes her despite Catania's defense. Gillion then attacks, turning the kingdom's crystals and people to stone. Encouraged by Mariposa, Catania overcomes her fear of flying, and together they restore the Heart Crystal, which rewards both with new wings. Catania chooses to forgive Gillion and offers her Crystallite, restoring her youth, and the king, admitting he misjudged Mariposa, makes peace with Flutterfield.

The film was released on DVD in the United States on 27 August 2013.

title: Annie
