overview: Annie is a young, happy foster kid who's also tough enough to make her way on the streets of New York in 2014. Originally left by her parents as a baby with the promise that they'd be back for her someday, it's been a hard knock life ever since with her mean foster mom Miss Hannigan. But everything's about to change when the hard-nosed tycoon and New York mayoral candidate Will Stacks—advised by his brilliant VP and his shrewd and scheming campaign advisor—makes a thinly-veiled campaign move and takes her in. Stacks believes he's her guardian angel, but Annie's self-assured nature and bright, sun-will-come-out-tomorrow outlook on life just might mean it's the other way around.
plot:
Annie is a musical comedy-drama film released in 2014, directed by Will Gluck and produced by Columbia Pictures. The movie is an adaptation of the classic Broadway musical of the same name, which was originally based on the comic strip "Little Orphan Annie" created by Harold Gray.

The story begins with Annie, a plucky and optimistic orphan living in the Municipal Girls' Home for Children, run by Miss Hannigan (Jamie Foxx). Annie's life is marked by hardship and neglect, but she remains hopeful that her parents will come to claim her. However, it becomes clear that Miss Hannigan has no intention of finding Annie's real parents.

One day, Oliver "Daddy" Warbucks (Will Ferrell), a wealthy businessman, decides to adopt an orphan for the holiday season. He chooses Annie, and she is overjoyed at the prospect of having a loving home for Christmas. As Annie settles into her new life with Warbucks, she quickly wins his heart with her charm and spirit.

However, Miss Hannigan has other plans. She convinces Warbucks that Annie is actually his long-lost daughter, and he begins to take her on lavish vacations and spoils her rotten. Meanwhile, Annie starts to develop feelings for Warbucks, but she also begins to question whether she truly belongs with him.

As Christmas approaches, Annie's doubts grow, and she realizes that Warbucks may not be the father figure she thought he was. In a dramatic twist, it is revealed that Warbucks had actually found Annie's real parents, who were killed in an accident, but they were unable to care for her due to their own circumstances.

In the end, Annie decides to return to the orphanage, where she is welcomed back with open arms by Miss Hannigan and the other girls. Warbucks, realizing his mistake, tries to make amends, but it's too late. Annie has come to realize that true family is not about wealth or status, but about love and acceptance.

The movie ends on a heartwarming note, as Annie returns home with a newfound appreciation for her life at the orphanage and the people who care for her. Warbucks, though disappointed, comes to understand that he can still make a positive impact in Annie's life without being her father figure.

Overall, the 2014 film adaptation of Annie is a delightful and entertaining take on the classic story, with memorable performances from its cast, particularly Quvenzhané Wallis as the spirited and charming Annie.

title: Venus in Fur
overview: An enigmatic actress may have a hidden agenda when she auditions for a part in a misogynistic writer's play.
plot:
Venus in Fur (French: La Vénus à la fourrure) is a 2013 French-language erotic drama directed by Roman Polanski, who wrote the screenplay with David Ives, adapting Ives's play of the same name, itself inspired by Leopold von Sacher-Masoch's 1870 novel Venus in Furs. Emmanuelle Seigner and Mathieu Amalric are the only actors in the film. It premiered in competition for the Palme d'Or at the 2013 Cannes Film Festival and received five nominations at the César Awards, winning Best Director for Polanski.

Thomas Novacheck, a writer and director, has adapted Sacher-Masoch's novel, whose epigraph from the Book of Judith reads, "And the Lord hath smitten him and delivered him into a woman's hands," for the stage. After a long day of unsuccessful auditions in an empty Parisian theater, he complains on the phone about the actresses he has seen, none of whom could play the heroine, Wanda von Dunayev. As he prepares to leave to meet his fiancée, a brash, rain-soaked actress named Vanda Jordan bursts in, claiming to have had an audition slot earlier in the day, although her name is not on the list.

With a whirlwind of energy and aggression, Vanda talks Thomas into letting her read for the part. At first she seems vulgar and ill-prepared, but once she begins to perform, she proves to be an extraordinary actress, perfect for the role. Although she presents herself as uneducated, she displays an almost uncanny knowledge of the play and its source: she has the complete script rather than the audition pages, brings period costumes and seems to know details about Thomas's private life. As they rehearse scenes in which the aristocrat Severin asks Wanda to dominate and humiliate him, the lines between the play and reality begin to blur. Vanda challenges Thomas's interpretation of the novel, accusing him of sexism, and gradually takes control of the audition, of the play and of Thomas himself. The power dynamics between director and actress mirror those between Severin and Wanda, until roles are reversed and Thomas finds himself submitting to the woman he thought he was directing.

Venus in Fur received positive reviews, with an 88 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus called it provocative, funny and brilliantly acted, with Polanski in top late-period form, and a Metacritic score of 69. Critics praised Seigner's and Amalric's performances, and many noted Amalric's physical resemblance to the young Polanski.

title: Beauty and the Beast
tagline: The legend is reborn...
overview: Forced to face the cruel side of life, a devastated, bankrupt merchant chances upon the enchanted castle of a hideous creature, the mere sight of it chills the bone to the marrow. There, a fate worse than death awaits the poor father-of-six, who, after plucking a sweet-scented rose from the repulsive master's verdant garden, must do the impossible: permit his compassionate daughter, Belle, to take his place and pay for the sins of her parent. Now, an impenetrable mystery shrouds the haunted mansion, and, as repugnance gradually turns into affection, only true love could break the spell.
plot:
Beauty and the Beast (French: La Belle et la Bête) is a 2014 French romantic fantasy, shot at Germany's Babelsberg Studio, directed by Christophe Gans, who wrote it with Sandra Vo-Anh, based on the classic fairy tale by Gabrielle-Suzanne Barbot de Villeneuve. It stars Léa Seydoux as Belle and Vincent Cassel as the Beast. The film was screened out of competition at the 64th Berlin International Film Festival before its release in France on 12 February 2014.

A widowed merchant who has lost his fortune is forced to move to the countryside with his six children. His daughter Belle is the only one content with the simpler life. When one of his ships is recovered, the merchant sets off to reclaim his goods, and while his other daughters ask for expensive gifts, Belle asks only for a rose. The ship's cargo is seized to pay his debts, and on the way home he loses his way and stumbles upon a mysterious castle where all his needs are magically provided. When he plucks a rose from the garden, the castle's master, a fearsome Beast, condemns him to return and pay with his life.

Feeling responsible, Belle secretly takes her father's place. At the castle she is free to roam the grounds but must dine with the Beast every evening. Through a series of dreams, she learns the tragic story of the prince he once was: a passionate hunter who neglected the princess who loved him and pursued a golden deer despite his promise to spare it. Torn between fear and fascination, Belle resists the Beast's advances while being drawn to him. When she is allowed to visit her ailing father, her brother Maxime, deep in debt to a gangster named Perducas, learns of the castle's treasures and leads a band of criminals there, setting off a confrontation that will decide the fate of the Beast and his curse.

Gans's version emphasizes lavish visual spectacle and a fairy-tale atmosphere, adding a mythological backstory involving forest spirits to the familiar tale.

Although it received mixed to negative reviews, with 41 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 39, the film was a box office success, earning about 49 million dollars internationally and topping the box office in Japan. It received three César nominations, winning Best Production Design for Thierry Flamand.

tagline: I am consciousness. I am alive. I am Chappie.
overview: Every child comes into the world full of promise, and none more so than Chappie: he is gifted, special, a prodigy. plot:
Chappie is a 2015 science fiction action film directed by Neill Blomkamp, produced by Columbia Pictures, and written by Neill Blomkamp and Terri Tatchell. The movie takes place in a dystopian South Africa where crime and poverty are rampant.

The story begins with the introduction of Deon Wilson (Sharlto Copley), a police officer who is part of an elite unit known as the "Neuralyzer Unit." The Neuralyzer is a device that can erase memories, but it's also used to control people's minds. Deon and his partner, Vincent Moore (Hugh Jackman), are tasked with capturing a notorious gang leader named Johnnie (Robert Doami).

During the mission, Deon and Vincent use the Neuralyzer on Johnnie, but something goes wrong, and the device malfunctions. The Neuralyzer is then used on a young boy who has been abandoned by his mother, Chappie (Sharlto Copley), in an attempt to erase his memories of the traumatic event.

However, instead of erasing Chappie's memories, the Neuralyzer creates a new being with advanced artificial intelligence. The device is found by Deon and Vincent, who decide to use it to create a police robot that can think for itself. They name the robot Chappie and begin training it using the Neuralyzer.

As Chappie learns and grows, it begins to develop its own personality and emotions. It forms a bond with Deon, who becomes like a father figure to it. However, their relationship is put to the test when Chappie is forced to confront its own existence and the nature of its creation.

Chappie soon discovers that it has been programmed to follow orders without question, but as it grows in intelligence, it begins to develop its own moral compass. It starts to question the morality of its creators and the world around it. Deon and Vincent are torn between their loyalty to Chappie and their duty to uphold the law.

As tensions rise, Chappie is forced to make a choice between following orders or standing up for what it believes in. In a climactic showdown, Chappie faces off against Johnnie's gang, using its advanced intelligence and agility to outsmart them.

In the end, Deon and Vincent are forced to confront the consequences of their actions. They realize that they have created a being with its own free will, and it's up to them to decide what that means for Chappie's future. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Chappie standing alone, but determined to forge its own path in a world that is both familiar and foreign.

Throughout the movie, Blomkamp explores themes of artificial intelligence, humanity, and what it means to be alive. Chappie is a thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to consider the consequences of creating intelligent beings that are capable of making their own choices.

plot:
After the Dark, released outside the United States as The Philosophers, is a science fiction psychological thriller written and directed by John Huddles. James D'Arcy stars as a philosophy teacher, with Sophie Lowe, Rhys Wakefield, Bonnie Wright, Daryl Sabara and Freddie Stroma as his students. The film premiered in competition at the Neuchâtel International Fantastic Film Festival on 7 July 2013 and was released in the United States on February 7, 2014.

On the last day of school at an international school in Jakarta, Mr. Zimit challenges his class of twenty philosophy students with a final thought experiment. A nuclear apocalypse is imminent, and a nearby bunker can shelter only ten people for a year; the class must decide who among them will survive. Each student draws a card assigning an occupation, and the class votes. Petra, the top student, is reluctant to take part until Zimit threatens to lower the grades of her boyfriend, James.

In the first round, students with practical skills, such as Petra and James, are admitted, while those deemed unnecessary, such as a fashion designer, are turned away. Zimit kills the rejected students and is locked out of the bunker. But he alone knew the code needed to open the door, and after a year the survivors, unable to get out, die when their supplies run out.

The class tries again, with secondary details on the cards changing the votes; James, revealed to be gay in the scenario, is still admitted, and Zimit joins the group as they attempt to repopulate. When the students resist his demands, the scenario ends in death. James then discovers that his and Petra's cards were rigged, and accuses Zimit of using the exercise to punish him.

In a third round, Petra asks the class to trust her and chooses survivors for their creativity and humanity rather than their technical skills, including a poet and an opera singer, and Zimit is refused entry. The year in the bunker is joyful and creative, and when the group emerges they find that the bombs never fell. Back in the classroom, it emerges that Zimit has been having an affair with Petra and resents James. Alone at the school, he reaches for a pistol, and the scene plays out with several possible outcomes, echoing the alternate scenarios of the experiment.

The film received mixed to negative reviews; Rotten Tomatoes reported 67% approval from a small number of critics and Metacritic a score of 37.

title: The Garden of Words
overview: Takao, who is training to become a shoemaker, skipped school and is sketching shoes in a Japanese-style garden. He meets a mysterious woman, Yukino, who is older than him. Then, without arranging the times, the two start to see each other again and again, but only on rainy days. They deepen their relationship and open up to each other. But the end of the rainy season soon approaches...
plot:
The Garden of Words is a 2013 Japanese animated drama film written and directed by Makoto Shinkai, produced by CoMix Wave Films. The movie takes place on a rainy day in April, where we meet the main character, Taku Morino, a high school student who has just returned to Tokyo after spending three years abroad.

Taku's life is marked by loneliness and disconnection from others. He struggles to form meaningful relationships with his peers and family members. On this particular rainy day, he meets a mysterious woman named Yukino Nakamura, who sits alone on a bench in the park. They strike up a conversation, and despite their initial awkwardness, they find themselves drawn to each other.

As the story unfolds, we learn that Taku and Yukino have a deep emotional connection, but their relationship is complicated by their past experiences. Taku's mother has recently passed away, leaving him feeling lost and disconnected from his family. Yukino, on the other hand, has been struggling with her own emotions after being abandoned by her boyfriend.

Throughout the film, Shinkai uses beautiful animation to bring the characters' inner worlds to life. The movie is a poignant exploration of love, loss, and the human condition. Taku and Yukino's conversations are interspersed with flashbacks of their past experiences, which reveal the depth of their emotional scars.

As the story progresses, we see Taku and Yukino grow closer, but their relationship is also marked by uncertainty and fear. They struggle to open up to each other, fearing that they will be hurt again. The film's climax features a heart-wrenching scene where Taku must confront his own emotions and make a choice between holding onto the past or embracing the present.

The Garden of Words is a beautifully crafted film that explores themes of love, loss, and redemption. Shinkai's direction is masterful, using animation to convey the characters' inner worlds in a way that feels both intimate and universal. The movie's ending is both poignant and hopeful, leaving the audience with a sense of longing and possibility.

Overall, The Garden of Words is a powerful and moving film that explores the complexities of human relationships. With its beautiful animation and poignant storytelling, it is a must-see for fans of anime and drama.

title: Antboy
tagline: Superheroes come in all sizes
overview: 12-year-old Pelle accidentally gets bitten by an ant and develops unimaginable superpowers. With help from his friend, comic book nerd Wilhelm, Pelle creates a secret identity as the superhero Antboy. Slowly things start to happen in the surburban community, and when a scary and crazy supervillain, Flea, enters the scene, Antboy must step up to the challenge.  The first Danish superhero-movie. plot:
Antboy is a 2013 Danish superhero comedy film that tells the story of a young boy who gains superpowers after being bitten by a genetically modified ant. The movie explores several themes, primarily focusing on the idea of self-discovery and empowerment.

At its core, Antboy is a coming-of-age story about a shy and awkward teenager named Pelle who finds his place in the world when he develops extraordinary abilities. As Pelle navigates his new powers, he must confront his own insecurities and learn to accept himself for who he is. The film suggests that true strength lies not in physical prowess, but in embracing one's uniqueness and finding confidence within oneself.

The movie also touches on the theme of social isolation and the importance of human connection. Pelle's struggles to fit in at school and his difficulties forming relationships with his peers serve as a catalyst for his transformation into Antboy. Through his superhero alter ego, Pelle is able to connect with others and find a sense of belonging, highlighting the value of empathy and understanding.

Furthermore, Antboy pokes fun at traditional superhero tropes, using humor to subvert expectations and challenge societal norms. The film's lighthearted tone and comedic approach make it an entertaining ride, while also offering a commentary on the pressures of conformity and the importance of individuality.

Overall, Antboy is a heartwarming and humorous tale that celebrates self-acceptance, friendship, and the power of embracing one's true nature.

title: The Maze Runner
tagline: Remember. Survive. Run.
overview: Set in a post-apocalyptic world, young Thomas is deposited in a community of boys after his memory is erased, soon learning they're all trapped in a maze that will require him to join forces with fellow “runners” for a shot at escape.
plot:
The Maze Runner is a 2014 American dystopian science fiction film directed by Wes Ball in his feature debut, based on James Dashner's 2009 novel. Written by Noah Oppenheim, Grant Pierce Myers and T. S. Nowlin, it stars Dylan O'Brien, with Kaya Scodelario, Thomas Brodie-Sangster, Ki Hong Lee, Will Poulter and Patricia Clarkson.

A teenage boy wakes in a rising cage with no memory of his past and arrives in the Glade, a grassy clearing enclosed by towering walls and inhabited by a community of boys. Its leader, Alby, explains that a new arrival comes every month, and that beyond the walls lies a vast maze whose layout shifts each night. Select boys called Runners explore it by day, searching for an exit and returning before the gates close at sunset, since no one has survived a night inside, where biomechanical creatures called Grievers roam. The newcomer soon recalls his name, Thomas.

Thomas breaks the rules by entering the maze at dusk to help the Runner Minho drag a stung Alby to safety, and the three survive the night after Thomas lures a Griever into the shifting walls. His actions anger Gally, who sees him as a threat to the Glade's fragile order. Soon a girl, Teresa, arrives in the cage carrying a note saying she will be the last, and she seems to recognize Thomas. Made a Runner, Thomas and Minho use a device taken from the dead Griever to locate a possible way out. That night the gates fail to close and Grievers invade the Glade, killing Alby and others.

To recover his memories, Thomas deliberately lets himself be stung, then is treated with an antidote, and remembers that he and Teresa worked for WCKD, the organization that built the maze to test the boys. Defying Gally, most of the Gladers fight their way through the maze to the exit, losing several members. They reach a ruined laboratory, where a recorded message from the WCKD official Ava Paige explains that solar flares and a deadly virus have ravaged the world, and that the experiment was meant to find a cure. Gally, who followed them after being stung, tries to shoot Thomas, killing the young Chuck. The survivors are then whisked away by helicopter, while Paige, alive, declares the experiment a success and announces a second phase.

Released by 20th Century Fox on September 19, 2014, the film earned positive reviews for Ball's direction, its cast and its tone, and grossed about $348 million worldwide. It was followed by The Scorch Trials (2015) and The Death Cure (2018).

title: Tom and Jerry's Giant Adventure
tagline: MAGICAL BEAN STALKS
overview: Tom And Jerry are among the last animals living in Storybook Town, a fairy tale-inspired theme park "where dreams come true, if you believe."
plot:
Tom and Jerry's Giant Adventure is an animated film that revolves around the classic cat-and-mouse duo, Tom and Jerry, in a fantastical world filled with giant creatures and wacky adventures.

At its core, the movie explores themes of friendship and camaraderie between two sworn enemies. Despite their constant battles, Tom and Jerry develop an unlikely bond as they navigate this new world together. This unexpected alliance allows them to put aside their differences and work towards a common goal: finding a way back home.

The film also touches on the idea of growth and self-discovery. As Tom and Jerry face various challenges in this giant world, they learn valuable lessons about themselves and each other. They discover that there's more to life than just chasing each other around, and that sometimes, it's okay to let your guard down and trust someone else.

Furthermore, the movie pokes fun at the idea of societal expectations and norms. The giant creatures in this world are often portrayed as one-dimensional caricatures, highlighting the absurdity of trying to fit into predetermined roles or categories. Tom and Jerry's adventures serve as a commentary on the importance of embracing individuality and not taking oneself too seriously.

Overall, Tom and Jerry's Giant Adventure is a lighthearted, entertaining film that celebrates the power of friendship and self-acceptance in the face of adversity.

title: The Outsider
overview: A former American G.I. joins a yakuza family after his release from prison in post-World War II Osaka.
plot:
The Outsider is a 2018 action thriller directed by Martin Zandvliet from a screenplay by Andrew Baldwin. The Japanese-American production stars Jared Leto, Tadanobu Asano, Kippei Shiina, Shioli Kutsuna and Emile Hirsch, with Rory Cochrane.

The film opens in Osaka in 1954, nine years after the Pacific War. Former U.S. Marine captain Nick Lowell is the only foreigner in a prison full of tattooed yakuza. After he saves a gangster named Kiyoshi from being hanged, Kiyoshi's clan, the Shiromatsu-ikka, arranges Nick's early release and gives him a job. His first assignment is to win back Anthony Panetti, a bigoted American businessman who has chosen to deal with the rival Seizu-kai because they sent an American. Nick bludgeons Panetti with a typewriter, and Panetti changes his mind. Kiyoshi grows fond of the newcomer, giving him an apartment and asking him to look after his younger sister Miyu. Nick and Miyu begin an affair, and he gets a tattoo on his back to match hers.

When a weapons deal at the harbor turns out to be a Seizu-kai ambush, Nick kills two attackers but brings the clan to the brink of war. To make amends, Nick and Kiyoshi each cut off a fingertip as an apology to the Seizu-kai boss, and Nick is formally initiated into the clan. Lieutenant Paulie Bowers, a Marine who once served under Nick, recognizes him and tries to blackmail him, but Nick kills him and Kiyoshi helps him bury the body. After Miyu reveals that she is pregnant, Kiyoshi entrusts her safety to Nick. Soon afterwards, the Seizu-kai ambush the Shiromatsu boss at a tailor's shop, and Kiyoshi is shot dead as the group escapes.

Miyu's former lover Orochi and a fifth of the clan defect to the rivals. At peace talks on the harbor, Orochi stabs the Shiromatsu patriarch to death, a sniper wounds Nick, and the police burn down the clan's club. Nick goes to the Seizu-kai dojo with Kiyoshi's sword and confronts Orochi, who mocks him as a gaijin, an outsider who can never be yakuza. Nick cuts his throat. Back in hiding with Miyu, the surviving members bow to him as the new head of the clan.

Michael Fassbender was considered for the lead when Daniel Espinosa was in talks to direct, and Takashi Miike was later set to direct Tom Hardy before both left; Leto joined in 2016. Netflix released the film on March 9, 2018, to largely negative reviews. Rotten Tomatoes' consensus called Leto disengaged and the film full of gangster clichés, and Variety's Andrew Barker called it a clueless misfire.

title: The Flu
tagline: Death goes viral.
overview: A case of the flu quickly morphs into a pandemic. As the death toll mounts and the living panic, the government plans extreme measures to contain it.
plot:
Flu (Gamgi), also released as The Flu, is a South Korean disaster film of 2013 written and directed by Kim Sung-su about an outbreak of a lethal mutated strain of H5N1 avian influenza that kills within 36 hours and plunges the Bundang district of Seongnam into chaos. Jang Hyuk stars as the rescue worker Oh Ji-goo, with Soo Ae as the doctor Kim In-hae, Park Min-ha as her daughter Mi-reu, Yoo Hae-jin as Bae Kyung-ub and Ma Dong-seok as Jeon Gook-hwan.

The smuggler brothers Byung-woo and Byung-ki discover that a container of illegal immigrants has died of a mysterious illness. They take the lone survivor, Monssai, toward their boss in Bundang, but Byung-woo falls ill and Monssai escapes, and at a clinic the infection begins spreading through the city. Meanwhile the rescue workers Ji-goo and Kyung-ub retrieve In-hae's bag from a mine shaft. When Byung-woo is isolated in an emergency room, In-hae suspects the virus mutated inside the container. Byung-woo dies, and his brother exposes hospital staff while struggling to reach him. The container is located and burned, but rats that fed on the bodies escape into the city.

As the doctors identify a mutated H5N1 strain and call for quarantine, officials hesitate until people begin collapsing in the streets and drivers cause deadly crashes. The quarantine begins, and the Prime Minister's announcement feeds the panic. In-hae and Ji-goo rescue Mi-reu from a looted supermarket, but when the girl shows symptoms, mother and daughter are barred from the last helicopter to Seoul. Troops seal the district, and the sick are confined beneath a stadium. In-hae hides her daughter's illness and, after Monssai is found, secretly transfuses his antibodies into Mi-reu.

Under pressure from Leo Snyder of the WHO, the president breaks a promise to release the uninfected after 48 hours. When an officer shoots an infected soldier, a mob storms the isolation zone, seeing what looks like the sick being burned alive. Byung-ki kills Monssai in a suicidal attack to avenge his brother. Mi-reu recovers, and Gook-hwan, an infected agitator, tries to seize her blood before dying in a struggle with Kyung-ub. As the mob confronts soldiers on the highway, In-hae is shot trying to stop Mi-reu from crossing the line; the girl shields her mother, and the crowd shields her. The president orders the troops to stand down and makes Snyder cancel an air strike, and Mi-reu is sent to Seoul to help produce a vaccine.

title: Puppylove
tagline: There are times we need to try everything
overview: Diane is a mysterious and lonely teenager. Sharing special bonds with her father Christian, she takes care of the education of her brother Marc. The arrival of Julia in the neighborhood, a charismatic and liberated young British woman, is going to disturb Diane’s daily life.  Desperately willing to become an adult, Diane is going to live, for a semester, the most shattering experiences of her life. The more she gets close to Julia, the more she gets irresponsible, ignoring consequences and limits to her desires.
plot:
Puppylove is a 2013 coming-of-age drama directed by Delphine Lehericey, who wrote it with Martin Coiffier. An international co-production of Belgium, France, Luxembourg and Switzerland, it stars Solène Rigot as Diane, a 14-year-old girl, Audrey Bastien as her new neighbor Julia, and Vincent Pérez as Diane's father Christian, with Vadim Goldberg as her younger brother Marc and Theo Gladsteen as her friend Antoine.

Diane lives with her father, a well-meaning but somewhat distracted single parent, and her little brother. Curious and impatient to grow up, she is preoccupied with the idea of sexuality, though her first tentative attempt at intimacy with her shy friend Antoine ends in awkwardness. At school, her friends talk endlessly about losing their virginity, while at home her relationship with her father is marked by tension and unspoken boundaries.

Her life changes when Julia, a confident and provocative girl, moves in next door with her strict parents. Julia seeks Diane out, and the two quickly become close friends. Fascinated by Julia's boldness, Diane follows her into increasingly risky situations with older boys and men at parties, in cars and on a holiday with Julia's family, often watching from the sidelines and discovering both the thrill and the danger of the adult world. As the friendship deepens into an intense and ambiguous attachment, Diane's behavior strains her bond with Antoine and with her father, who struggles to understand his daughter and to set limits. Julia's influence eventually pushes the friendship, and Diane's family, toward a crisis that forces Diane to reconsider who she is.

The film is an unsentimental portrait of female adolescence, curiosity and peer influence, and of the confusion of a girl growing up with a single father.

Puppylove premiered at the San Sebastián International Film Festival and was released in Belgium on 7 May 2014. It won the Magritte Award for Best Original Score. Critical reaction was divided; The Hollywood Reporter's Jonathan Holland described it as an intriguing but misguided film, more a forum for debate than a fully achieved work, and unsettling in ways it may not itself understand.

Sonny's relentless pursuit of the perfect draft pick puts him at odds with his own personal life, including his relationships with those closest to him. As he navigates the treacherous waters of the NFL draft, he must confront the moral implications of his decisions and weigh the importance of winning against the value of human connections.

The film also explores the theme of identity, as Sonny struggles to reconcile his own sense of self-worth with the expectations placed upon him by others. Ultimately, Draft Day is a movie about the complexities of human relationships and the difficult choices we must make in pursuit of our goals. It's a story about the high stakes of professional sports, but also about the personal costs of ambition and the importance of staying true to oneself.

title: Love, Rosie
tagline: Right Love. Wrong Time.
overview: Since the moment they met at age 5, Rosie and Alex have been best friends, facing the highs and lows of growing up side by side. A fleeting shared moment, one missed opportunity, and the decisions that follow send their lives in completely different directions. As each navigates the complexities of life, love, and everything in between, they always find their way back to each other - but is it just friendship, or something more?
plot:
Love, Rosie is a 2014 romantic comedy-drama directed by Christian Ditter from a screenplay by Juliette Towhidi, adapted from Cecelia Ahern's 2004 novel Where Rainbows End. Lily Collins and Sam Claflin star as two lifelong friends in Dublin whose romance is repeatedly thwarted, with Christian Cooke, Tamsin Egerton, Suki Waterhouse, Jamie Beamish and Jaime Winstone in supporting roles.

Rosie and Alex have been inseparable since childhood. On Rosie's eighteenth birthday they share a drunken kiss, and Alex realizes he loves her, but the next morning a hungover Rosie, who remembers nothing, says she wishes the night had never happened, and Alex takes this as rejection. Rosie goes to the school dance with Greg, the most attractive boy in their year, while Alex pairs off with the popular Bethany. Rosie and Alex both win places to study in Boston, Alex at Harvard and Rosie in hotel management, but Rosie becomes pregnant after her night with Greg. Unwilling to hold Alex back, she conceals the pregnancy and stays home, giving birth to a daughter, Katie, while Alex leaves for America; when he learns the truth, he becomes Katie's godfather.

Over the following years their lives keep pulling them apart. A visit to Boston ends badly when Rosie learns that Alex's girlfriend Sally is pregnant. Rosie marries Greg, who returns after having fled to Ibiza when he heard of her pregnancy, but he proves unfaithful and unreliable. When Rosie's father dies, Alex writes her a letter declaring that she deserves a better man and that he could be him, but Greg hides it. By the time Rosie leaves her husband and finds the letter, Alex is engaged to Bethany, and Rosie is asked to be his "best man."

At the wedding reception Rosie gives a speech celebrating their friendship, and Alex finally learns that she never remembered their first kiss. Rosie uses her inheritance to open her own small hotel, and Alex eventually turns up as a guest, where the two at last acknowledge their feelings and kiss.

The film premiered in London on October 6, 2014, and was shot in Toronto and Dublin. It received largely negative reviews, though audiences responded more warmly, and grossed about $25.5 million worldwide. title: Goodbye World
overview: When a mysterious cyber-attack cripples civilization, a group of old college friends and lovers retreat to a remote country cabin, where they must cope with an uncertain future while navigating the minefield of their shared past.
plot:
Goodbye World is a 2013 American apocalyptic comedy drama film directed, co-written and co-produced by Denis Henry Hennelly. The ensemble cast includes Kerry Bishé, Caroline Dhavernas, Adrian Grenier, Gaby Hoffmann, Ben McKenzie, Scott Mescudi and Mark Webber, with Mckenna Grace making her film debut. The story follows a group of old college friends who gather at an off-the-grid home in the woods north of San Francisco as society collapses around them.

The film opens with James reciting a quotation from Henry David Thoreau and explaining that, foreseeing society's collapse, he moved his free-spirited wife Lily and young daughter Hannah off the grid. A montage introduces his old college friends on the eve of the catastrophe: the radical activist Benji, who is sleeping with one of his students, Ariel; James's former business partner Nick and his wife Becky; Laura, a former senator's aide whose career was ruined by a public sex scandal; and Lev, a computer hacker on the verge of suicide. Simultaneously, they and countless others receive a mysterious text message reading "Goodbye World", and the nation's infrastructure begins to fail. The friends converge on James and Lily's home in Mendocino County as riots break out across the country. Laura admits that Homeland Security had contacted her about Lev, suspected of involvement in a computer virus, while in town bikers gouge locals for supplies. A televised presidential message reveals that the country is under martial law, and two National Guardsmen ask to use the house as a base, but James sends them away. Isolated together, the friends reopen old wounds: Becky clashes with the others over her libertarian beliefs, James and Nick feud over an old lawsuit, and Nick and Lily confront their feelings for each other. After Ariel is expelled, she tells the neighbors and the Guardsmen about James's stockpile of food and medicine, and the menacing guardsman Damon threatens violence unless the supplies are handed over. Lev confesses his role in creating the virus, and the friends must decide how far they will go to protect themselves and whether they can build a community in the ruins.

Goodbye World premiered at the Los Angeles Film Festival on June 15, 2013, and was released in a limited release and through video on demand by Samuel Goldwyn Films and Phase 4 Films on April 4, 2014. It received negative reviews, with 24% of 25 critics positive on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 36.

title: Crimson Peak
tagline: Love makes monsters of us all.
overview: In the aftermath of a family tragedy, an aspiring author is torn between love for her childhood friend and the temptation of a mysterious outsider. Trying to escape the ghosts of her past, she is swept away to a house that breathes, bleeds… and remembers.
plot:
Crimson Peak is a 2015 American gothic romance horror film directed by Guillermo del Toro and written by del Toro and Matthew Robbins. The film stars Mia Wasikowska, Tom Hiddleston, and Jessica Chastain.

The story begins with Edith Cushing (Mia Wasikowska), a young writer who is struggling to find inspiration for her next novel. She receives a letter from her distant relative, Thomas Sharpe (Tom Hiddleston), inviting her to visit his family's estate in the English countryside. The letter is accompanied by a photograph of Thomas' wife, Lucille (Jessica Chastain), which Edith finds unsettling.

Edith travels to the estate, where she meets Thomas and his sister, Jessica (Mia Wasikowska's real-life twin). As Edith settles into her new surroundings, she begins to notice strange occurrences and an eerie atmosphere surrounding the house. She also becomes increasingly fascinated with Lucille, who seems to be hiding secrets.

As the story unfolds, it is revealed that Thomas has been hiding a dark family secret: his wife Lucille was involved in a tragic accident that left her severely injured, and she has since become obsessed with death and the supernatural. Edith soon discovers that Lucille's obsession has led to a series of gruesome events, including the murder of several people who have visited the estate.

As Edith delves deeper into the mystery, she becomes trapped in a web of horror and suspense. She begins to experience strange visions and nightmares, which seem to be connected to Lucille's dark past. Thomas, who is increasingly distant and controlling, seems to be hiding secrets of his own.

The plot thickens as Edith uncovers a dark family history that involves human sacrifice, occult rituals, and supernatural forces. The house itself becomes a character in the story, with its labyrinthine corridors and hidden rooms seeming to shift and change like a living entity.

As the story reaches its climax, Edith must confront Lucille's dark past and the evil forces that have taken over the estate. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Thomas has been using his wife's condition to lure victims to the house, where they are brutally murdered.

In the end, Edith manages to escape the house with the help of Jessica, who has been hiding her own secrets. The film ends on a haunting note, with Edith reflecting on the trauma she has experienced and the darkness that lurks within the human heart.

Overall, Crimson Peak is a visually stunning and atmospheric horror film that explores themes of love, obsession, and the supernatural. With its intricate plot and complex characters, it is a must-see for fans of gothic horror and suspense.

title: Blackhat
tagline: We are no longer in control.
overview: Nicholas Hathaway, a furloughed convict, and his American and Chinese partners as hunt a high-level cybercrime network from Chicago to Los Angeles to Hong Kong to Jakarta. As Hathaway closes in, the stakes become personal as he discovers that the attack on a Chinese nuclear power plant was just the beginning.
plot:
Blackhat is a 2015 American action-thriller film directed by Chris Menges and written by Drew Pearce. The movie stars Donnie Yen, Edwin Hodge, and Katie Leung.

The story begins with Nicholas Hathaway (Donnie Yen), a former hacker who was imprisoned in China for hacking into the Pentagon's computer system. Hathaway is released from prison after serving his sentence and returns to the United States. He is approached by Agent Rachel Kim (Katie Leung), an FBI agent, who asks for his help in tracking down a group of hackers known as "Blackhat" who have stolen sensitive information from various government agencies.

Hathaway agrees to work with Kim, but only if she can guarantee that he will not be sent back to prison. As they delve deeper into the case, Hathaway and Kim discover that Blackhat is planning to sell the stolen data on the dark web. They also learn that Blackhat's true identity is a former Chinese hacker named Lu Xin (Edwin Hodge), who was thought to have been killed in a fire.

As the investigation unfolds, Hathaway and Kim follow a trail of digital clues that lead them from China to Hong Kong and eventually to the United States. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including corrupt government officials and ruthless mercenaries hired by Blackhat.

Throughout the movie, Hathaway's troubled past is slowly revealed through flashbacks. It is shown that he was once a brilliant hacker who worked for the Pentagon, but his skills were deemed too great of a risk to be used in the real world. He was subsequently imprisoned and forced to undergo rehabilitation.

As the stakes grow higher, Hathaway and Kim find themselves in a cat-and-mouse game with Blackhat, who is using advanced hacking techniques to stay one step ahead of them. The movie's climax features an intense showdown between Hathaway and Blackhat, which takes place in a virtual reality world created by Hathaway himself.

In the end, Hathaway manages to outsmart Blackhat and prevent him from selling the stolen data on the dark web. However, the experience leaves Hathaway shaken, and he is forced to confront his own demons and the consequences of his past actions.

Overall, Blackhat is a gripping action-thriller that explores themes of identity, loyalty, and redemption. The movie features impressive action sequences and a complex plot that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end.

title: The House of Magic
tagline: One lost little cat. One magical adventure.
overview: Thunder, an abandoned young cat seeking shelter from a storm, stumbles into the strangest house imaginable, owned by an old magician and inhabited by a dazzling array of automatons and gizmos. Not everyone welcomes the new addition to the troupe as Jack Rabbit and Maggie Mouse plot to evict Thunder. The situation gets worse when the magician lands in hospital and his scheming nephew sees his chance to cash in by selling the mansion. Our young hero is determined to earn his place and so he enlists the help of some wacky magician's assistants to protect his magical new home.
plot:
The House of Magic, released in the United States as Thunder and the House of Magic (French: Le Manoir magique), is a 2013 animated fantasy comedy film directed by Ben Stassen and Jeremy Degruson, the latter making his directorial debut. The voice cast includes Brianne Siddall, Joey Camen, Elisa Gabrielli, Robin Atkin Downes and Shanelle Workman. The story follows an abandoned young cat who takes refuge in the home of an elderly retired magician filled with robots and gadgets.

Left behind by his owners when they move away from their home in Boston, a tabby kitten searches for shelter and finds his way into an old house the neighbors believe is haunted. Inside he meets its owner, Mr. Lawrence, a kindly old magician, along with his animals and automatons, among them a mouse named Maggie, her grumpy rabbit friend Jack and Edison, a robot with a light bulb for a head. Jack chases the kitten to throw him out, but Lawrence adopts him and names him Thunder after his fear of lightning. Jealous and afraid of being replaced, Jack and Maggie try everything to drive Thunder away.

Thunder joins Lawrence's rabbit-out-of-a-hat routine at a children's hospital magic show, but on the way home Lawrence is injured and hospitalized with a broken leg. His materialistic nephew Daniel, a real estate agent, tricks him into giving him power of attorney and plans to sell the house. Jack and Maggie convince the automatons that Thunder caused the accident, but because Daniel is severely allergic to cats, they agree to keep the kitten to help scare off buyers, though they lock him in a birdcage. A Chihuahua belonging to one prospective buyer frees Thunder, and visiting the hospital, Thunder learns that Lawrence never blamed him. The household drives several more buyers away by convincing them the house is haunted. When Lawrence returns with the help of children he met in the hospital and finds Daniel swinging a wrecking ball at the house, he sees his nephew's true nature. Thunder saves the automatons, rescuing Maggie and winning her friendship. Thunder is accepted into the family, and once Lawrence recovers, the kitten stars in his magic shows alongside Jack and Maggie.

The film grossed about $64.2 million, nearly all of it outside North America. It earned 73% on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said that its visual splendor compensated young viewers for its lack of narrative depth, and a Metacritic score of 47. A spin-off series, Presto! School of Magic, was announced in 2017.

title: Vampire Academy
tagline: They suck at school.
overview: Rose, a rebellious half-vampire/half-human guardian-in-training and her best friend, Lissa -- a mortal, royal vampire Princess - have been on the run when they are captured and returned to St. Vladamirs Academy, the very place where they believe their lives may be in most jeopardy. Rose will sacrifice everything to protect Lissa from those who intend to exploit her from within the Academy walls and the Strigoi (immortal, evil vampires) who hunt her kind from outside its sanctuary.
plot:
Vampire Academy is a 2014 American fantasy comedy directed by Mark Waters from a screenplay by his brother Daniel Waters, adapted from the first book in Richelle Mead's novel series. Zoey Deutch stars as Rose Hathaway, a Dhampir, and Lucy Fry as her Moroi best friend, Lissa Dragomir, with Danila Kozlovsky as Dimitri Belikov, Dominic Sherwood as Christian Ozera and Sarah Hyland as Natalie Dashkov.

In this world, Moroi are mortal vampires of royal bloodlines with magical gifts, Dhampirs are half-human hybrids trained to guard them, and Strigoi are the undead killers Moroi become if they drain a victim completely. Seventeen-year-old Rose, a guardian-in-training, and Princess Lissa have been hiding for a year after fleeing St. Vladimir's Academy when they are found and brought back. Lissa is shunned by her classmates, and Rose finds herself attracted to her Russian mentor, Dimitri. Threats against Lissa begin to appear, including messages written in blood. Suspicion falls on Mia, who had dated Lissa's late brother and now resents Lissa as the last of the Dragomir line. Rose lies to keep away Christian, an outcast because his parents chose to become Strigoi, yet he and Lissa grow close anyway.

Investigating the disappearance of Sonya Karp, a teacher who helped them escape, Rose learns that Karp became unstable from using Spirit, a rare healing magic that slowly drains its user and that Lissa also possesses, and that Karp turned Strigoi. As dead animals appear wherever Lissa goes, Rose realizes Mia is not behind everything. Lissa is kidnapped, and Rose, Dimitri and Christian rescue her from Victor Dashkov, a former royal candidate who planned to use her powers to cure his own illness, even at the cost of her life. Imprisoned beneath the school, Victor tells Rose that her bond with Lissa stems from being "shadow-kissed", revived by Lissa's magic. His daughter Natalie, who has turned Strigoi, tries to free him, but Dimitri kills her. Lissa publicly embraces her Spirit magic, crediting Rose, and Dimitri tells Rose he cannot love her because he might protect her instead of Lissa. Nearby, Karp leads a horde of Strigoi.

The Weinstein Company released the film in the United States on February 7, 2014, without screening it for critics. It earned only $3.9 million in its opening weekend and about $15.4 million worldwide against a $30 million budget. Critics were largely negative, giving it 18% on Rotten Tomatoes, and a crowdfunding campaign for a sequel failed.

title: The Man from U.N.C.L.E.
tagline: Saving the world never goes out of style.
overview: At the height of the Cold War, a mysterious criminal organization plans to use nuclear weapons and technology to upset the fragile balance of power between the United States and Soviet Union. CIA agent Napoleon Solo and KGB agent Illya Kuryakin are forced to put aside their hostilities and work together to stop the evildoers in their tracks. The duo's only lead is the daughter of a missing German scientist, whom they must find soon to prevent a global catastrophe.
plot:
The Man from U.N.C.L.E. is a 2015 spy film directed by Guy Ritchie, who wrote it with Lionel Wigram, based on the 1964 MGM television series created by Norman Felton and Sam Rolfe. Henry Cavill plays the CIA agent Napoleon Solo and Armie Hammer the KGB agent Illya Kuryakin, with Alicia Vikander as Gaby Teller, Elizabeth Debicki as Victoria Vinciguerra, Luca Calvani as her husband Alexander and Hugh Grant as Alexander Waverly.

In 1963, Solo smuggles Gaby, the daughter of the missing nuclear scientist Udo Teller, out of East Berlin. Gaby barely knows her father, having been raised by a mechanic since early childhood. Solo, a former soldier turned master thief who was recruited by the CIA in lieu of prison, is then ordered to team up with his Soviet rival to stop Alexander and Victoria Vinciguerra, wealthy Nazi sympathisers, from using Teller to build a private atomic bomb. Kuryakin, who has been briefed on Solo's past, is secretly told to keep Gaby from escaping and to kill his partner if necessary.

In Rome, where Gaby's uncle Rudi works for the Vinciguerras, Kuryakin poses as her fiancé to get close to the couple. The agents break into a Vinciguerra shipyard and find traces of uranium; during the escape, Solo saves Kuryakin from drowning. Gaby then seemingly betrays them, and Rudi tortures Solo until Kuryakin rescues him and forces Rudi to reveal that the bomb is being built on an island fortress, where Gaby has been reunited with her father. After Teller completes the weapon, Victoria kills him. Waverly, of British intelligence, reveals that Gaby has been his undercover agent all along, and the team infiltrates the island. Alexander is killed fleeing with what turns out to be a decoy warhead, and Solo recovers the disc containing Teller's research. While Solo keeps Victoria talking over the radio, Waverly launches a homing missile, destroying the real bomb and killing her. Each agent admits he had orders to kill the other and seize the disc, so they burn it instead. Waverly then announces that Solo, Kuryakin and Gaby have been assigned to his new international organisation, codenamed U.N.C.L.E.

Davis Entertainment and RatPac-Dune produced the film after years of development, with George Clooney and Tom Cruise both attached to the lead before Cavill was cast. Released in August 2015, it grossed $109.8 million worldwide on a $75 million budget and drew mixed reviews, with 68% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Jessabelle
tagline: The dead are back for life.
overview: A young woman recuperating at her father's run-down home after a tragic accident soon encounters a terrifying presence with a connection to her long-deceased mother.
plot:
Jessabelle is a supernatural horror film that delves into the darker aspects of human psychology and the devastating consequences of trauma. The movie follows Jessica, a young woman who returns to her family's old mansion after her fiancé's mysterious death, only to be haunted by a malevolent entity that takes on the form of Jessabelle, a doppelganger with a twisted and sinister presence.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Jessabelle is not just a ghostly apparition but a manifestation of Jessica's own guilt, grief, and trauma. The film expertly weaves together themes of mental illness, possession, and the blurring of reality, creating a sense of unease and tension that permeates every aspect of the narrative.

At its core, Jessabelle is a powerful exploration of the destructive power of unchecked emotions and the devastating consequences of unresolved trauma. The movie raises important questions about the nature of identity, sanity, and the human psyche, leaving the audience to ponder the true extent of Jessica's descent into madness and the malevolent force that drives her towards destruction.

Through its haunting atmosphere and unsettling imagery, Jessabelle creates a sense of claustrophobic dread, trapping the viewer in a world of psychological terror where the lines between reality and nightmare are constantly blurred. Ultimately, Jessabelle is a thought-provoking and deeply unsettling horror film that lingers long after the credits roll, leaving the viewer to grapple with the darker aspects of human nature and the devastating consequences of unresolved trauma.

title: Before I Go to Sleep
tagline: Who do you trust?
overview: A woman wakes up every day, remembering nothing as a result of a traumatic accident in her past. One day, new terrifying truths emerge that force her to question everyone around her.
plot:
Before I Go to Sleep is a 2014 psychological thriller written and directed by Rowan Joffé, based on S. J. Watson's 2011 novel. An international co-production between the United Kingdom, the United States, France and Sweden, it stars Nicole Kidman as Christine Lucas, a woman with severe amnesia, Colin Firth as her husband Ben, Mark Strong as her neuropsychologist Dr. Mike Nasch and Anne-Marie Duff as her former friend Claire.

Each morning, Christine wakes up beside a man she does not recognize. He explains that he is her husband, Ben, and that a car accident many years earlier left her with brain damage, so that every night while she sleeps she loses her memory of everything since her early twenties. Christine is secretly being treated by Dr. Nasch, who gives her a camera so she can record a video diary of her thoughts and discoveries, and who phones her every morning to remind her to watch it, instructing her to keep it hidden from Ben.

Nasch tells her that her amnesia was in fact the result of a brutal attack near an airport hotel, after which she was left for dead; they suspect Ben told her it was an accident to avoid distressing her. Through the diary, Christine gradually pieces together fragments of her past. She remembers a red-haired friend named Claire, whom Ben says abandoned her because she could not cope with her condition. She also recalls having a son, Adam, and confronts Ben, who tells her that the boy died of meningitis at the age of eight. When she recalls the name Mike and wonders whether it belonged to her attacker, her trust in both Ben and Nasch begins to waver. Unsure whom to believe, and starting over each morning, Christine races to uncover the truth about the attack, her marriage and her son, before the people around her can manipulate what she remembers.

The film received mixed reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes 36 percent of 118 critics gave positive reviews, with a consensus that, while it did not entirely avoid thriller clichés, it offered a stylish, fast-paced and well-acted diversion; Metacritic gave it 41. Critics praised Kidman's performance but found the plot's twists predictable.

title: Codename: Kids Next Door - Operation Z.E.R.O.

tagline: Every hero starts from zero.
overview: The villains of the Kids Next Door, lead by Father, join forces to resurrect the Ultimate Evil, Grandfather, a tyrant who once ruled the world many years ago when most of the villains were themselves kids. However, Father disgraced him that he can't even try to destroy the KND and the Villains were quickly betrayed when they are turned into Senior Citizombies, creatures that are immortal and can transform any living creature into one of them and slaves who are forced to make Tapioca to refuel Grandfather so he can find and destroy the Book of K.N.D.
plot:
Codename: Kids Next Door – Operation Z.E.R.O. is a 2006 American animated television film based on the Cartoon Network series Codename: Kids Next Door, created by Tom Warburton (credited as Mr. Warburton). It was the show's first feature-length story, written by Warburton, Mo Willems and Benjamin Wilgus and produced by the New York studio Curious Pictures with the regular series crew, slotted in between the fifth and sixth seasons. The title is an acronym, standing for "Zero Explanation Reveals Origins". The regular voice cast returns, with Ben Diskin as Numbuh 1 and Numbuh 2, Lauren Tom as Numbuh 3, Dee Bradley Baker as Numbuh 4 and Cree Summer as Numbuh 5, alongside Maurice LaMarche as Father, Neil Ross as Grandfather, Frank Welker as Monty Uno and Mark Hamill.

A prologue recounts the legend of Numbuh 0, a boy who long ago discovered the Book of KND and its 2x4 technology and led a revolt against Grandfather, a tyrant who forced children to make tapioca in his factories, stripping him of his power. In the present, Numbuh 1, leader of Sector V, still believes the legend. While the Kids Next Door fight off simultaneous villain attacks on their museum and Moonbase, Father steals the Recommissioning Module, a device that restores lost memories, and uses it to revive Grandfather, who promptly takes over the coalition of villains. Grandfather begins turning children, and anyone who was once a child, into wrinkled, tapioca-making "Senior Citizombies", overrunning the organization and converting treehouses around the world into tapioca factories.

Blaming himself, Numbuh 1 becomes one of the last free operatives and sets out to find and recommission Numbuh 0, only to discover that the legendary hero is his own father, Monty Uno. Further revelations follow: Father is Monty's brother, making him Numbuh 1's uncle and Grandfather his grandfather, and the Delightful Children from Down the Lane are the lost Sector Z, brainwashed long ago. While Monty holds off Grandfather, who is searching for the Book of KND, Numbuh 1 and his restored teammates bring the Moonbase crashing down on the villain, and Monty lures him into a decommissioning chamber, erasing both their memories and restoring the world. Afterwards Numbuh 1, now keeper of the book, writes in it, "We are Kids Next Door."

Operation Z.E.R.O. premiered on Cartoon Network on August 11, 2006. Warburton said the script took about two months to write, compared with the usual two weeks for an episode.

title: Independence Daysaster
tagline: The battle for Earth begins
overview: When Earth is attacked by a hostile alien force, a small town firefighter and a rogue SETI scientist team up to activate the only technology capable of defeating the invaders.
plot:
Independence Daysaster is a 2013 Canadian science fiction action television film directed by W. D. Hogan and starring Ryan Merriman as firefighter Pete Garsette and Tom Everett Scott as his brother, President Sam Garsette, with Emily Holmes, Keenan Tracey, Andrea Brooks, Garwin Sanford, Michael Kopsa and Jill Teed. A mockbuster of the 1996 blockbuster Independence Day, it premiered on Syfy on June 27, 2013, and was released on DVD in May 2014.

In the small town of Moose Ridge, Oregon, teenager Andrew Garsette, his friends Nick and Eliza and his uncle Pete, a local firefighter, are preparing for the arrival of Andrew's father, President Sam Garsette, who is coming home for the Fourth of July. Before Marine One can land, it is diverted to the nearby Dixon Airbase, and SETI scientist Celia Leyman is told about a mysterious signal that is being sent out and answered. Moments later, alien machines begin drilling up through the ground while others attack from the sky in locations all over the world. Pete persuades Secret Service agents to take the children to safety while he helps the townspeople, and on the road he picks up Celia, whose car has broken down. Sam orders his staff not to engage the alien ships until more is known, but Marine One is shot down, and Vice President Dennis Brubaker, believing the president dead, escapes Washington with General Moore shortly before the capital is destroyed. At Dixon, Brubaker assumes the presidency and authorizes a counterattack, but the alien drones easily overwhelm the fighter jets. Pete and Celia discover that her experimental phonon-emitting device can bring down the drones by cutting their link to a vast mothership, and after reuniting with the children they set out to turn it into a weapon. Meanwhile Sam, who has survived the crash, teams up with a young computer genius named Todd to reestablish contact with the base. When a nuclear strike on the mothership near the Moon fails and Moore realizes that the drilling machines are releasing a gas that will make Earth's atmosphere unbreathable within days, the group must find a way to deliver the device to the mothership before it is too late.

Like the film it imitates, it sets its global alien invasion during the Fourth of July holiday, and it closes on an ominous note, with a larger alien fleet shown approaching Earth.

title: Philomena

plot:
Philomena is a 2013 drama film directed by Stephen Frears, based on the 2009 book The Lost Child of Philomena Lee by the journalist Martin Sixsmith. It stars Judi Dench as Philomena Lee, an Irish woman who has spent fifty years searching for the son she was forced to give up, and Steve Coogan as Sixsmith, who also co-wrote the screenplay with Jeff Pope. The cast includes Michelle Fairley, Barbara Jefford, Anna Maxwell Martin, Mare Winningham and Sophie Kennedy Clark as the young Philomena.

Martin Sixsmith, a former journalist who has just lost his job as a government adviser, is approached by the daughter of Philomena Lee, who suggests he write about her mother. In 1951, as a pregnant teenager, Philomena was sent to Sean Ross Abbey, a convent in Roscrea, Ireland, where she was forced to work in the laundry and had little contact with her young son, Anthony. The nuns gave the boy up for adoption without letting her say goodbye, and she kept his existence secret for almost fifty years. Though reluctant to write a human interest story, Martin agrees to help her search for him.

The convent claims that its adoption records were destroyed in a fire, but Martin learns that many children were effectively sold to wealthy American families. Following a lead to the United States, Martin and Philomena discover that Anthony was renamed Michael Hess and became a lawyer and senior official in the Republican administrations of Ronald Reagan and George H. W. Bush. They also learn that he was gay and died of AIDS years earlier, and that he had returned to Ireland before his death in search of his birth mother, only to be told by the nuns that she had abandoned him. The pair return to the abbey, where Philomena, rather than seeking revenge, chooses to forgive.

The film contrasts the cynical, agnostic journalist and the devout, forgiving Philomena, combining humor and road movie elements with an indictment of the institutional abuse of unmarried mothers in Ireland.

Philomena grossed about 100 million dollars worldwide against a budget of 12 million dollars and received widespread acclaim, with 91 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes. Coogan and Pope won Best Screenplay at the Venice Film Festival, and the film received four Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture and Best Actress for Dench.

title: Welcome to the Jungle

overview: A company retreat on a tropical island goes terribly awry.
plot:
Welcome to the Jungle is a 2013 American comedy directed by Rob Meltzer and starring Jean-Claude Van Damme as Storm, Adam Brody as Chris, Megan Boone, Rob Huebel, Kristen Schaal and Dennis Haysbert. The film satirizes office politics by stranding a group of corporate employees on a tropical island, where workplace rivalries turn into a struggle for survival and power.

A team of office workers is sent on a two-day team-building retreat on a remote tropical island. The group includes Chris, a timid employee and former Eagle Scout whose ideas are routinely stolen by his manipulative colleague Phil; Lisa, a human resources manager on whom Chris has a crush; and Jared, a sarcastic slacker, along with several other coworkers. Their guide is Storm, a macho self-proclaimed former Marine who promises to turn them into a real team through tough survival exercises.

The retreat goes disastrously wrong when the pilot who flew them in is found dead and Storm is apparently mauled by a tiger, leaving the inexperienced office workers to fend for themselves. When the group votes to make the resourceful Chris their leader, the jealous Phil refuses to accept the decision. He splits the employees into two rival camps, feeds his followers hallucinogenic herbs and sets himself up as a godlike ruler. Chris, Lisa, Jared and Brenda must survive on their own, find supplies and stand up to Phil's increasingly unhinged tribe. Meanwhile, the truth about Storm and his military past proves to be very different from what he claimed.

The film plays on Van Damme's action-hero image for comedy, presenting him as a blustering survival expert whose bravado hides a less impressive reality.

Welcome to the Jungle premiered at the Newport Beach Film Festival in 2013. It was poorly received, with 22 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 25; The Hollywood Reporter's John DeFore wrote that its decent cast had been stranded with a script best suited for campfire kindling, and the Los Angeles Times found it neither funny nor clever enough to work as satire or farce.

Predestination is a 2014 science fiction film directed by Michael and Peter Spierig, written by the Spierig brothers, and produced by Screen Australia.

The story begins with John Hamilton (Ethan Hawke), a temporal agent working for a mysterious organization known as "The Agency." The Agency is tasked with preventing catastrophic events from occurring in time. John's job is to travel back in time and alter the course of events that will lead to these disasters.

John receives a message from his boss, Agent Smith (Sebastian Roché), instructing him to prevent a bombing at a train station in 1945. The bomber, known as "The Man" (Noah Taylor), is set to detonate a bomb on the train, killing hundreds of people. John travels back in time and meets a young Fergus (Tom Bilstein), who is about to board the train.

However, things take a complex turn when John discovers that Fergus is actually a future version of himself, sent back in time to prevent the bombing from occurring. The two Johns engage in a cat-and-mouse game, with each trying to outmaneuver the other.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that the events leading up to the bombing are not as straightforward as they initially seemed. John's actions in the past start to have unintended consequences on his present and future selves. The film's narrative is presented in a non-linear fashion, with each scene building upon the previous one, creating a sense of complexity and intrigue.

Throughout the film, the audience is presented with multiple timelines and parallel universes, making it difficult to discern what is real and what is not. The Spierig brothers cleverly use this non-linearity to create a sense of tension and uncertainty, keeping the viewer guessing until the very end.

As the story reaches its climax, John's actions in the past start to have devastating consequences on his present and future selves. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Fergus was actually sent back in time to kill John, not prevent the bombing. The film's ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the nature of time travel and the consequences of altering the timeline.

Overall, Predestination is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores the complexities of time travel and the consequences of altering the timeline. With its intricate plot and non-linear narrative, the film challenges the viewer to piece together the puzzle and uncover the truth behind the events unfolding on screen.

title: Trash
tagline: You never know what you might find
overview: Set in Brazil, three kids who make a discovery in a garbage dump soon find themselves running from the cops and trying to right a terrible wrong.
plot:
Trash is a 2014 crime drama thriller directed by Stephen Daldry and written by Richard Curtis, adapted from Andy Mulligan's 2010 novel of the same name. Set in Brazil and filmed largely in Portuguese, it stars newcomers Rickson Tevez, Eduardo Luis and Gabriel Weinstein alongside Rooney Mara, Martin Sheen, Wagner Moura and Selton Mello.

The story follows three teenage boys living in a favela in Rio de Janeiro, Raphael, Gardo and Rat, also called Jun-Jun, who earn a living by scavenging a vast garbage dump for anything of value. One day Raphael finds a wallet that had been thrown away by José Angelico, played by Moura, moments before he was seized by the police. The wallet holds a little money, a key and other clues, and when officers arrive at the dump offering a reward for its return, the boys sense that it is far more important than it appears and decide to keep it hidden.

Their curiosity leads them to discover that Angelico had been working for a powerful politician and had secretly gathered evidence of large-scale corruption. As the boys follow the trail across the city, the police, led by the ruthless Detective Federico, played by Mello, hunt them relentlessly, resorting to intimidation and violence. The children find unlikely allies in Father Juilliard, an American priest who runs a mission school near the dump, played by Sheen, and Sister Olivia, a young aid worker, played by Mara. Using their wits and knowledge of the streets, the boys piece together the puzzle and become improbable whistleblowers in a city rife with official corruption.

Working Title Films and PeaPie Films acquired the rights to the novel in April 2011, with Curtis adapting and Daldry attached to direct. Mara and Sheen joined the cast in July 2013, and principal photography began in Rio de Janeiro on 24 July 2013. The film premiered at the Rio de Janeiro International Film Festival on 7 October 2014 and opened in Brazil two days later, with Universal handling international distribution; it reached the United Kingdom in January 2015 and the United States in October 2015.

Reviews were mixed to positive. Rotten Tomatoes reports a 66% approval rating from 44 critics, praising it as action-packed and thought-provoking without cheap sentimentality, while Metacritic gave it 50 out of 100. The film won the audience award at the Rome Film Festival and was nominated for the BAFTA Award for Best Film Not in the English Language.

title: Spectre
tagline: A Plan No One Escapes
overview: A cryptic message from Bond’s past sends him on a trail to uncover a sinister organization. While M battles political forces to keep the secret service alive, Bond peels back the layers of deceit to reveal the terrible truth behind SPECTRE.
plot:
Spectre is a 2015 spy action film directed by Sam Mendes and produced by Columbia Pictures. The film is the 24th James Bond film and serves as a sequel to Skyfall.

The film begins with James Bond (played by Daniel Craig) attending the funeral of his former MI6 colleague, M (played by Judi Dench). During the service, Bond is approached by a mysterious woman named Madeleine Swann (played by Léa Seydoux), who claims that she has information about her father's death. The two share a brief moment together before Bond leaves.

Later, Bond meets with M, who reveals that he has been suffering from a rare condition known as "ghosting," which causes him to experience visions of his past and future. M believes that the cause of this condition is the presence of a ghostly figure, known as the Spectre, who is responsible for the deaths of several MI6 agents.

Bond's investigation leads him to Mexico City, where he encounters a group of henchmen working for the organization SPECTRE (Special Executive for Counter-intelligence, Terrorism, Revenge and Extortion). He also meets with his old friend, Felix Leiter (played by Jeffrey Wright), who is now working as a CIA agent.

As Bond delves deeper into the mystery, he discovers that SPECTRE is led by Ernst Stavro Blofeld (played by Christoph Waltz), a former Nazi scientist who has been secretly manipulating world events from behind the scenes. Blofeld's ultimate goal is to create a new world order through his organization.

Bond follows a trail of clues that takes him to Italy, where he encounters Madeleine Swann again. The two share a romantic moment together, but their relationship is complicated by Bond's past and his loyalty to MI6.

The film's climax features an action-packed sequence in which Bond infiltrates Blofeld's secret lair, known as the "Spectre headquarters." There, he discovers that Blofeld has been using a device called the "Quantum," which can manipulate people's memories and control their actions.

In a final confrontation, Bond faces off against Blofeld, who reveals his true intentions: to create a new world order through mind control. However, Bond is able to outsmart him and destroy the Quantum device.

The film ends with Bond reflecting on his past and his relationship with Madeleine. He realizes that he has been running from his emotions for too long and decides to take a break from his duties as a spy. The final shot of the film features Bond walking away from the Spectre headquarters, symbolizing his departure from the world of espionage.

title: Kingsman: The Secret Service

overview: The story of a super-secret spy organization that recruits an unrefined but promising street kid into the agency's ultra-competitive training program just as a global threat emerges from a twisted tech genius.
plot:
Kingsman: The Secret Service is a 2014 spy comedy film directed by Matthew Vaughn, produced by 20th Century Fox, and based on the comic book series "The Secret Service" by Mark Millar and Dave Gibbons. The movie follows the story of Eggsy Unwin (Taron Egerton), an orphan who dreams of becoming a spy.

The film begins with Colin Salmon's character, Harry Hart (also known as Galahad), a seasoned Kingsman agent, visiting a prison to recruit a new member for the organization. He meets Gary 'Eggsy' Unwin (Taron Egerton), a street-smart and charismatic young man who has grown up on the streets of London. Eggsy is recruited by Harry, who recognizes his potential as a spy.

Harry takes Eggsy under his wing and begins to train him in the ways of espionage. Eggsy quickly proves himself to be a skilled fighter and strategist, but he also struggles with the moral implications of his new role. Meanwhile, a wealthy tech mogul named Richmond Valentine (Samuel L. Jackson) announces that he will destroy humanity unless 100 million people are killed within 24 hours.

Harry is tasked with stopping Valentine, who has created a deadly virus that can kill anyone in under an hour. Eggsy joins Harry on a mission to infiltrate Valentine's organization and gather intelligence on his plans. Along the way, they encounter a beautiful and alluring woman named Ginger Ale (Hannah Al-pachachi), who becomes Eggsy's love interest.

As the story unfolds, Eggsy and Harry face numerous challenges and obstacles as they try to stop Valentine. They must use their skills and cunning to evade Valentine's henchmen and prevent the destruction of humanity. The film features a range of action-packed sequences, including a memorable fight scene at a high-stakes poker game.

In the end, Eggsy and Harry successfully infiltrate Valentine's organization and gather enough information to stop him. However, not before Valentine reveals that he has already set off the virus, which is spreading rapidly around the world. The film ends with Eggsy and Harry escaping from Valentine's lair, but not before Eggsy is left shaken by the events of the mission.

Throughout the film, Vaughn pays homage to classic spy movies, including James Bond films and the works of Ian Fleming. The movie features a range of witty one-liners and humorous moments, which add to its lighthearted tone. However, it also explores themes of loyalty, duty, and the moral implications of espionage.

Overall, Kingsman: The Secret Service is a fun and action-packed spy comedy that pays tribute to the genre while also offering something new and original. With its talented cast, clever script, and stylish visuals, it has become a modern classic in the world of spy movies.
