title: Inferno
tagline: His greatest challenge. Humanity's last hope.
overview: After waking up in a hospital with amnesia, professor Robert Langdon and a doctor must race against time to foil a deadly global plot.
plot:
Inferno is a 2016 American action thriller film directed by Ron Howard and starring Tom Hanks as Robert Langdon, a symbologist who becomes embroiled in a global conspiracy. The movie is the third installment in the Robert Langdon series, following Angels & Demons (2009) and Da Vinci Code (2006).

The story begins with Dr. Sienna Brooks (Felicity Jones), a brilliant scientist who has been working on a cure for Alzheimer's disease. She is kidnapped by a mysterious organization known as the "Benedictus" group, led by Abigail Holmes (Amanda Seyfried). The group demands that Langdon find a specific text written in ancient Sumerian, which they believe will unlock the secrets of the universe.

Langdon soon discovers that he has been chosen for this task because of his expertise in symbology. He is given a cryptic message by Abigail, who reveals that she is working to prevent a global pandemic caused by a deadly virus known as the "Benedictus virus." The virus is said to be created by a mysterious figure known only as "The Architect," who has been manipulating world events from behind the scenes.

As Langdon delves deeper into the mystery, he teams up with Sienna's sister, Dr. Vittoria (Irène Jacob), and together they embark on a perilous journey across Europe to uncover the truth about the virus and The Architect's identity. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including deadly traps, puzzles, and cryptic clues left behind by The Architect.

As the story unfolds, Langdon discovers that the Benedictus virus is linked to an ancient text known as the "Inferno," which holds the secrets of the universe. He also learns that Abigail is not what she seems, and that her true intentions are far more sinister than he initially thought.

The movie's climax features a thrilling showdown between Langdon and The Architect (Vincent Cassel), who reveals himself to be a former scientist turned mad by his own ambition. In the end, Langdon and Sienna manage to stop the pandemic and uncover the truth about The Architect's identity, but not before many lives are lost.

Throughout the movie, Howard weaves together intricate plot twists, clever puzzles, and stunning visuals to create an engaging narrative that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats. While some critics felt that the movie's pacing was uneven and the plot was overly complex, fans of the series will appreciate the thrilling adventure and intellectual challenge that Inferno provides.

Overall, Inferno is a gripping action thriller that explores themes of science, faith, and the power of human ingenuity. With its breakneck pace, clever plot twists, and stunning visuals, it's a must-see for fans of the Robert Langdon series and action enthusiasts alike.

title: Stonehearst Asylum
tagline: No one is what they seem.
overview: A Harvard Medical School graduate takes a position at a mental institution and soon becomes obsessed with a female mental patient, but he has no idea of a recent and horrifying staffing change.
plot:
Stonehearst Asylum, originally titled Eliza Graves, is a 2014 American gothic psychological thriller directed by Brad Anderson and written by Joseph Gangemi, loosely based on Edgar Allan Poe's 1845 short story "The System of Doctor Tarr and Professor Fether". It stars Kate Beckinsale, Jim Sturgess, Ben Kingsley, Michael Caine, David Thewlis and Brendan Gleeson, and was released on October 24, 2014.

In 1899, during a lecture at Oxford, a professor demonstrates the case of Eliza Graves, a woman diagnosed with hysteria who insists that she is sane. A young man in the audience later arrives at the remote Stonehearst Asylum introducing himself as Dr. Edward Newgate, an Oxford graduate seeking a residency. He is admitted by an armed group led by Mickey Finn and taken to the superintendent, Dr. Silas Lamb. Lamb rejects drugs and restraint and believes that patients' delusions should be indulged if they make them happy.

Newgate is captivated by Eliza, now a patient there. At the Christmas Eve feast she secretly prevents him from drinking a toast and urges him to leave, but he will not go without her. He then finds the asylum's real staff, among them the former superintendent Dr. Benjamin Salt, locked in the boiler room. They reveal that Lamb and Finn are patients who drugged them and seized control, and warn that Lamb was a military surgeon who killed his own patients.

Newgate tries to work against the inmates from within. Lamb forces Newgate to administer electroshock treatment to Salt, leaving him amnesiac. When Newgate attempts to drug the inmates' champagne during the New Year celebration, he is caught and prepared for the same treatment.

Newgate tells Eliza that he came to Stonehearst to rescue her after seeing her at the Oxford lecture. When Lamb is confronted with a photograph of one of his wartime victims, he breaks down, and the patients, frightened of Finn's brutality, rise against him. Finn dies by electrocution, starting a fire from which Eliza leads the inmates to safety, and flashbacks reveal that Lamb killed wounded soldiers out of a misguided sense of mercy.

When Eliza's husband and the Oxford professor later arrive to take her home, the professor reveals that he is the real Edward Newgate, and that the young man was an escaped mental patient. The lovers are last seen happily together in Italy. Reviews were mixed, with 54% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and the film grossed 3.2 million dollars.

title: The Art of the Steal
tagline: It takes a great artist to pull off the perfect con
overview: Crunch Calhoun, a third-rate motorcycle daredevil and part-time art thief, teams up with his snaky brother to steal one of the most valuable books in the world. But it's not just about the book for Crunch — he's keen to rewrite some chapters of his own past as well.
plot:
The Art of the Steal, previously titled The Black Marks and The Fix, is a 2013 Canadian heist comedy written and directed by Jonathan Sobol. It stars Kurt Russell, Jay Baruchel, Chris Diamantopoulos, Matt Dillon and Katheryn Winnick, with Terence Stamp, and premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 11, 2013.

Art thief Crunch Calhoun is betrayed by his brother and partner, Nicky, when a "smooth switch" of a Gauguin for a forgery at a museum in Warsaw goes wrong: the forger's last-minute touch-up is noticed and Nicky trips the alarm. To avoid a 20-year sentence, Nicky returns the painting and informs on others, and Crunch spends years in a Polish prison. Released, he scrapes by performing motorcycle stunts, joined by Lola, the charmer, and Francie, the apprentice. Meanwhile Interpol agent Bick, aided by informant Sam Winters, interrogates Nicky at an airport about a famous stolen Seurat that a colleague of Nicky's has been carrying.

Seeking work with his old associate "Uncle" Paddy, Crunch finds Nicky there with the Seurat. Paddy proposes stealing a priceless book, the second ever printed on the Gutenberg press, from a customs warehouse for a $1.5 million payout. Crunch refuses at first, scolding Nicky for picking the pockets of the defenseless, but Lola persuades him, and with Parisian forger Guy and a plan devised by Nicky, the team smuggles the real book into the warehouse inside a giant sculpture and swaps it for a replica. Inspired by Guy's tale of a legendary forger who sold copies of the Mona Lisa in 1911, Nicky convinces the others to commission multiple forgeries to sell to several buyers, investing $300,000 himself, but he secretly orders cheaper fakes from another forger, Dirty Ernie, to sell first and split the money two ways. When he calls the buyers, none of them has heard of the deal. Crunch reveals that the book scheme was a ruse to steal the Seurat from Nicky using his own idea, Interpol receives an anonymous tip about Nicky and the painting he took from a double-crossed partner, and Sam is rewarded with the genuine Seurat upon his parole.

Shot partly in Bucharest, with Budapest standing in for Warsaw in aerial shots, the film received mixed reviews, with 46% on Rotten Tomatoes and 53 on Metacritic; critics enjoyed the cast but found the formula familiar.

Through the characters' perspectives, the film conveys the emotional turmoil that followed the assassination, as people struggled to come to terms with the sudden loss of a leader and the senseless killing of an innocent man.

The movie also examines the role of media in shaping public perception and the way events are remembered over time. The character of Abraham Zapruder, who captured the infamous "Zapruder film" of the assassination, serves as a symbol of the power of documentation and the importance of preserving historical moments.

Furthermore, Parkland touches on the theme of conspiracy theories and the lingering questions surrounding the assassination. The film raises questions about the official narrative and invites viewers to consider alternative perspectives, leaving room for interpretation and debate.

Ultimately, Parkland is a thought-provoking exploration of the human experience in the face of tragedy, highlighting the complexities and nuances that arise when individuals are forced to confront the darker aspects of human nature.

The story begins with the disappearance of Amy, who goes missing on the day of her fifth wedding anniversary. Nick reports her missing to the police, but as the investigation unfolds, it becomes clear that nothing is as it seems. The media has a field day, portraying Amy as a manipulative and unstable woman who had been planning her disappearance for months.

The couple's friends and family members also reveal that they had grown tired of Amy's manipulative tactics, which included pretending to be a victim in order to get attention.

She had been feeling suffocated by Nick's lack of emotional support and his inability to connect with her on a deeper level. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Amy had faked her own death in order to frame Nick for her murder.

As the investigation continues, Nick becomes the prime suspect, but he maintains his innocence. Meanwhile, Amy is hiding in plain sight, using her charm and wit to manipulate those around her. She creates an alternate identity for herself, complete with a new name, appearance, and backstory.

In the end, it is revealed that Amy had been planning her revenge against Nick all along. She had been manipulating him throughout their marriage, using her intelligence and cunning to get what she wanted. In a stunning finale, Nick discovers the truth about Amy's disappearance and confronts her in a dramatic showdown.

Throughout the film, Fincher masterfully builds tension and suspense, keeping the audience guessing until the very end. The performances by Affleck and Pike are outstanding, bringing depth and nuance to their characters. The film's themes of marriage, identity, and the unreliability of appearances are timely and thought-provoking.

Overall, Gone Girl is a gripping and twisty thriller that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats until the very end. With its complex characters, clever plot twists, and masterful direction, it is a must-see for fans of psychological thrillers.

plot:
Monster High: 13 Wishes is a 2013 American computer-animated fantasy film based on Mattel's Monster High fashion doll franchise, produced by Mattel with animation by Nerd Corps Entertainment. Directed by Steve Sacks with Andrew Duncan and Audu Paden, and written by Ted Zizik and Mike Montesano, it runs 73 minutes and was released on DVD and Blu-ray on 8 October 2013 before airing on Nickelodeon on 25 October. It tied in with the 13 Wishes and Haunt the Casbah doll lines and a video game, and its score is by Paul Robb and Michael Kotch.

A prologue set a thousand years earlier shows the genie Gigi Grant breaking the rules of her lantern to stop her shadow sister, Whisp, from using an eclipse to seize power through the last wish of a finder. In the present, a new school year begins at Monster High, and Clawdeen Wolf's little sister Howleen, tired of being overlooked, is determined to become popular. Serving detention in the school attic with Frankie Stein, Clawdeen, Draculaura, Lagoona Blue and Ghoulia Yelps, she discovers the lantern and frees Gigi, who grants her not three but thirteen wishes, unwittingly releasing Whisp as well.

Howleen first uses her wishes to help her friends, getting the ghouls out of detention, making Abbey Bominable student body president and putting Clawd and his friends on a dangerous television show. Under Whisp's secret influence, however, she wishes herself popular, turns Cleo de Nile into a nobody and banishes Clawdeen into the lantern, leaving a shadow double behind. Each wish has a dark side, and the school turns upside down. Gigi, forbidden to influence her finder, confides in Frankie, revealing that Whisp plans to use the coming eclipse to replace everyone with shadow versions and rule the world. Frankie, Draculaura and Ghoulia have Howleen wish them into the lantern, where they rescue Clawdeen and search for the shards of a shattered magic mirror. Returning on magic carpets in time for the eclipse, they join Howleen's shy shadow friend Twyla, who assembles the mirror and breaks Whisp's spell. Howleen undoes her earlier wishes and spends the last one freeing Gigi while letting Whisp become a real genie of the lantern.

The voice cast includes America Young as Howleen, Jonquil Goode as Gigi, Whisp and Twyla, Salli Saffioti as Clawdeen and Cleo, Kate Higgins as Frankie, Debi Derryberry as Draculaura and Erin Fitzgerald as Abbey. The film was also released in several European countries that October.

overview: Wallace, who is burned out from a string of failed relationships, forms an instant bond with Chantry, who lives with her longtime boyfriend. Together, they puzzle out what it means if your best friend is also the love of your life.
plot:
The F Word, released in some countries as What If, is a 2013 romantic comedy directed by Michael Dowse from a screenplay by Elan Mastai, based on the play Toothpaste and Cigars by TJ Dawe and Michael Rinaldi. It stars Daniel Radcliffe as Wallace and Zoe Kazan as Chantry, with Adam Driver, Mackenzie Davis, Megan Park and Rafe Spall. A Canadian and Irish co-production, it explores whether a man and a woman can remain just friends.

Wallace is a young Englishman living in Toronto who dropped out of medical school after a painful breakup and has since withdrawn from social life. His best friend Allan persuades him to come to a party, where Wallace meets Allan's cousin Chantry, an animator, and the two immediately hit it off. As he walks her home, however, he learns that she has been living with her boyfriend for years. When they meet again by chance at a cinema, they spend the evening talking about everything from love to an absurdly extravagant sandwich, and they decide to become friends.

Wallace soon meets Chantry's boyfriend Ben, a lawyer who works for the United Nations, and accidentally knocks him out of a window, sending him to the hospital. When Ben accepts a six-month posting in Dublin, Wallace and Chantry spend even more time together, and their bond deepens. Wallace struggles to hide his growing feelings, while Allan and his impulsive new girlfriend Nicole urge him to be honest. As Chantry is offered an important career opportunity abroad and her relationship with Ben reaches a turning point, both Wallace and Chantry must decide whether to risk their friendship for something more.

The film is a dialogue-driven comedy marked by rapid, witty banter about love, food and friendship, and it was praised for the chemistry between its leads.

The F Word premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 7, 2013, and was released in 2014. It won the Canadian Screen Award for Best Adapted Screenplay among several nominations, including Best Picture. Reviews were generally positive, with about 74 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, while Metacritic gave it a score of 59.

Chef is a 2014 road comedy-drama film written, produced and directed by Jon Favreau, who stars as Carl Casper, a celebrity chef who starts a food truck business with his friends and young son. The ensemble cast includes Sofía Vergara, John Leguizamo, Scarlett Johansson, Oliver Platt, Bobby Cannavale, Amy Sedaris, Emjay Anthony and Dustin Hoffman, with Robert Downey Jr. in a cameo. Favreau wrote the script after a run of big-budget films, wanting to go "back to basics" with a movie about cooking, with chef Roy Choi as co-producer.

Carl, born in Miami, is head chef at Gauloises, an upscale restaurant in Brentwood, Los Angeles, where he frequently clashes with the owner, Riva, who insists on a safe, traditional menu. At home, his relationships with his wealthy ex-wife Inez and their tech-savvy young son Percy are strained. When the influential critic and blogger Ramsey Michel comes to dine, Riva forces Carl to abandon his bold new menu at the last minute, and the result is a scathing review. Ted 2 is a 2015 American fantasy comedy directed by Seth MacFarlane, who co-wrote it with Alec Sulkin and Wellesley Wild. A sequel to Ted (2012), it stars MacFarlane as the voice of Ted, Mark Wahlberg as John Bennett, Amanda Seyfried as Samantha Jackson, Jessica Barth as Tami-Lynn, Giovanni Ribisi as Donny and Morgan Freeman as Patrick Meighan.

Ted, a living teddy bear, marries Tami-Lynn, while John is now divorced from Lori. A year later, the marriage is strained, and the couple decide that a baby could save it. Since Ted cannot father a child, he and John search for a sperm donor, and after several failed attempts John offers his own. When Tami-Lynn proves to be infertile because of past drug use, they try to adopt. The adoption process leads Massachusetts to declare that Ted is property rather than a person. He loses his job, his accounts and his marriage. John and Ted decide to sue, and a leading lawyer hands the case to his niece Sam, a novice attorney. She knows nothing about pop culture, but the three bond over their love of marijuana.

Meanwhile, Ted's old stalker Donny, now a janitor at Hasbro's headquarters, persuades an executive to back his plan to kidnap Ted and mass-produce living teddy bears. The court rules against Ted. The trio turn to Patrick Meighan, a renowned civil rights lawyer, and on the trip to New York, John and Sam fall in love. Meighan sympathizes but turns them down, saying Ted has contributed little to humanity. Angry and jealous of John's new romance, Ted storms off into New York Comic Con, where Donny, disguised as a Ninja Turtle, abducts him. John and Sam arrive just as Donny is about to cut Ted open. As they leave, Donny sends a model of the Starship Enterprise swinging toward Ted, and John pushes him aside and is struck. In the hospital, John appears to die but has merely been revived and is pranking them. News footage of Ted's grief and John's sacrifice persuades Meighan to take the case, and he wins by showing that Ted is self-aware and capable of empathy. Ted and Tami-Lynn remarry and adopt a son.

A dropped drug-smuggling storyline left no room for Mila Kunis's Lori. Filming began in Massachusetts in July 2014. Universal released the film on June 26, 2015. Its $33.5 million opening disappointed, but it grossed $217 million worldwide on a $68 million budget. Reviews were mixed to negative. Rotten Tomatoes reported 45% approval, saying enjoyment would depend on tolerance for its sophomoric, scatological humor.

title: Easy Sex, Sad Movies
overview: Buenos Aires screenwriter Pablo is hired to write a new romantic comedy. As he begins his story, he visualizes his characters living in Madrid. Pablo creates a meet-cute between Marina and Víctor, a cute couple in Madrid who are soon totally in love. Yet as Pablo gets more and more into the script, he finds it difficult to separate his movie characters from what is happening in his own real life – specifically, his own love life.
plot:
Easy Sex, Sad Movies (Spanish: Sexo fácil, películas tristes; released in Argentina as El amor y otras historias) is a 2014 Argentine-Spanish romantic comedy written and directed by Alejo Flah, an Argentine filmmaker based in Madrid. Produced with the participation of TVE alongside Lazonafilms, Icónica and Utópica, it stars Ernesto Alterio as the screenwriter Pablo, Quim Gutiérrez as Víctor and Marta Etura as Marina, with Julieta Cardinali, Carlos Areces and Bárbara Santa-Cruz. Gutiérrez and Etura had first worked together in AzulOscuroCasiNegro (2006).

The film is a romantic meta-comedy built on several levels. In Buenos Aires, Pablo, a novelist who enjoyed great success in his youth and now, in middle age, is going through both a creative and an emotional crisis, is hired to write a conventional romantic comedy. Because the project is an Argentine-Spanish co-production, with a scene in France for a French co-producer, he sets his story in Madrid. There he imagines the meet-cute between Víctor, a skeptic who drifts through life without commitment, and Marina, who are soon completely in love, with a secondary couple played by Areces and Santa-Cruz serving as confidants for the protagonists' doubts. As Pablo works through his script, which piles cliché upon cliché yet still works, he finds it harder and harder to separate his characters from his own life, as he is in the midst of a separation from his partner, played by Cardinali, and must find inspiration for a happy ending in fiction. Gradually it emerges that the story of Pablo and his wife could be a projection of the fictional romance, with the characters perhaps the same people fifteen years later.

Flah described the film as both biographical and anti-biographical, explaining that he wanted to explore how fiction feeds on reality while reality needs fiction as an escape. It was released in Argentina on 16 October 2014, screened at the Málaga Film Festival, and opened in Spanish cinemas through Filmax on 24 April 2015. In El País, Javier Ocaña described a curious three-level work that admits to falling into stereotype while paying tribute to it, praising the excellent cast and the dialogue more than its plain direction and photography, and valuing a final twist that turns the apparent happy ending into something more ambivalent. Other Spanish critics found it likable and entertaining, with good chemistry between Gutiérrez and Etura, but predictable.

title: Moebius
tagline: Hell hath no fury like a woman scorned.
overview: A wife, overwhelmed with hatred for her husband, inflicts an unspeakable wound on their son, as the family heads towards horrific destruction.
plot:
Moebius (Korean: 뫼비우스) is a 2013 South Korean arthouse horror drama film written and directed by Kim Ki-duk. It is told entirely without spoken dialogue, subtitles or intertitles; the characters communicate through sounds and intense gazes, and non-diegetic sound is limited to the opening and closing scenes. Cho Jae-hyun plays the father, Seo Young-joo the son and Lee Na-ra both the mother and the father's mistress, with Kim Jae-hong as a gang leader.

Discovering that her husband is having an affair, a mother tries to castrate him in revenge. When she fails, she mutilates her teenage son instead and flees into the night, passing a man praying on the street. The guilt-ridden father becomes obsessed with helping his son find sexual pleasure in other ways, including painful alternative practices, and researches penis transplants. As rumors spread, the son is bullied and assaulted, and in an attempt to reclaim his standing he takes part in a gang's assault on his father's mistress, though he only pretends to participate. Jailed, he is beaten by other inmates, until it is established that he could not physically have committed the crime and he is released.

The son returns to the mistress's workplace and becomes drawn into a violent, sadomasochistic relationship with her and the gang leader, ending with the mistress castrating the gang leader. The father, learning of an experimental procedure, has his own organ transplanted to his son, but the son struggles to respond, and the mistress turns to the gang leader instead. When the mother finally returns home and tries to reconcile with her husband, she learns what he has done. Discovering that the transplanted organ responds instinctively to the mother, she turns her attention to her son, driving the father into a jealous rage; after a failed attempt to take back what he gave, he kills the mother and himself. The son destroys the organ with a gun and turns to a spiritual life, apparently becoming the praying man glimpsed at the start.

Moebius screened out of competition at the 70th Venice International Film Festival. In South Korea, the Korea Media Rating Board twice gave it a "restricted release" rating, an effective ban, over its depiction of incest between mother and son; Kim cut or altered 33 scenes in total before it was cleared for adult audiences and released in September 2013. Critics described it as daring and deeply disturbing.

The story begins with Sean (Alex Pettyfer), his girlfriend Hannah (Debora Franks-Costelo), and their friend Hunter (Matt Walsh) driving to Oklahoma to chase a severe thunderstorm. They are accompanied by Sean's father, Joe (Richard Armitage), who is also a storm chaser. The group is equipped with cameras and weather equipment to capture the storm from different angles.

As they drive into the heart of the storm, the group becomes increasingly reckless, ignoring warnings from meteorologists and local authorities. They are determined to get as close to the storm as possible, despite the risks. As the storm intensifies, the group's vehicle is damaged, and they become stranded in a field.

The group decides to split up and try to find shelter, but their efforts are hindered by the treacherous terrain and the storm's unpredictable behavior. Sean and Hannah go one way, while Hunter and Joe go another. As the storm rages on, the group members begin to experience terrifying and unexplained phenomena, including strange lights, loud noises, and bizarre visions.

As the night wears on, Sean and Hannah become separated from each other, and they must navigate the treacherous landscape to find shelter. Meanwhile, Hunter and Joe are caught in a tornado that lifts their vehicle into the air. The two men are forced to cling to each other as they are tossed around like ragdolls.

As the storm reaches its climax, Sean and Hannah stumble upon an abandoned farmhouse, where they take refuge. However, they soon realize that they are not alone, and the house is infested with a mysterious entity that seems to be connected to the storm.

The movie's climax features a series of intense and suspenseful sequences as the group members try to survive the storm and find each other again. In the end, Sean and Hannah manage to escape the farmhouse, but Hunter and Joe are nowhere to be found.

As the storm begins to subside, Sean and Hannah reflect on their terrifying experience and the true cost of their adventure. The movie ends with a sense of uncertainty, leaving the audience wondering what happened to Hunter and Joe.

Overall, Into the Storm is a tense and suspenseful thriller that explores the dangers of reckless behavior and the power of nature. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has developed a cult following among fans of disaster films and storm chasers.

title: Left Behind
tagline: The end begins
overview: A small group of survivors are left behind after millions of people suddenly vanish during the rapture and the world is plunged into chaos and destruction.
plot:
Left Behind is a 2014 American Christian apocalyptic thriller film directed by Vic Armstrong and written by Paul LaLonde and John Patus, based on the 1995 novel by Tim LaHaye and Jerry B. Jenkins. The second film adaptation of the first book in the Left Behind series, it stars Nicolas Cage, Chad Michael Murray, Cassi Thomson, Nicky Whelan, Jordin Sparks and Lea Thompson. Unlike the novel, it is set largely on an airplane.

Chloe Steele, a college student, flies home to New York to surprise her father, airline pilot Rayford Steele, for his birthday, only to learn that he has been called in to fly to London. At the airport she meets the investigative journalist Cameron "Buck" Williams. Chloe resents the religious fervor of her mother, Irene, a recent convert, and suspects that her parents' marriage is in trouble after seeing Rayford flirting with the flight attendant Hattie Durham and noticing that he is not wearing his wedding ring.

While Chloe is at a mall with her young brother, he vanishes in her arms, leaving his clothes behind. Millions of people around the world, including all children, disappear in an instant, and chaos erupts. On Rayford's flight to London, his co-pilot, a flight attendant and every child on board have also vanished, and he struggles to keep the frightened passengers under control while trying to make contact with the ground. A pilotless plane collides with his aircraft, damaging the fuel line, and he turns back toward New York.

At home, Chloe finds that her mother is also gone, and at Irene's church the pastor explains that the faithful have been taken to heaven while he was left behind because he never truly believed. Rayford reaches the same conclusion after finding Bibles among the belongings of his missing crew. In despair, Chloe climbs a bridge intending to end her life, but receives a call from her father and Buck: with the New York airports closed and fuel running out, Rayford needs somewhere to land. Chloe uses a truck to clear a road under construction and guides him to it, and he brings the plane down safely. As the survivors look out at a burning world, Buck remarks that it looks like the end, and Chloe replies that it is only the beginning.

Left Behind was panned by critics, with Rotten Tomatoes reporting 0% approval and Metacritic a score of 12. It received three Golden Raspberry Award nominations, including Worst Picture and Worst Actor for Cage.

title: Alexander and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Very Bad Day

tagline: One day can change everything.
overview: Alexander's day begins with gum stuck in his hair, followed by more calamities. plot:
Alexander and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Very Bad Day is a heartwarming film that explores the complexities of family dynamics, sibling relationships, and the challenges of growing up. The movie delves into the emotional struggles of its protagonist, Alexander, as he navigates a day filled with mishaps and misfortunes.

At its core, the film is a poignant portrayal of the imperfections and quirks that make families unique. It highlights the importance of love, acceptance, and understanding in the face of adversity. Through Alexander's experiences, the movie shows how even the most trying days can be transformed into opportunities for growth, connection, and laughter.

The film also touches on themes of sibling rivalry, teasing, and the challenges of navigating different personalities within a family. However, it does so in a way that is relatable and endearing, rather than confrontational or preachy. Ultimately, Alexander and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Very Bad Day is a film about finding joy and humor in the everyday moments, even when things don't go according to plan.

The movie's tone is lighthearted and humorous, with a touch of satire that pokes fun at the absurdities of family life. The characters are well-developed and memorable, particularly Alexander, who is both frustrating and lovable at the same time. Overall, the film is a delightful and entertaining exploration of what it means to be a part of a loving but imperfect family.

title: Freaks of Nature
tagline: Get out undead or alive.
overview: In the town of Dillford, humans, vampires and zombies were all living in peace - until the alien apocalypse arrived. Now three teenagers-one human, one vampire, and one zombie-have to team up to figure out how to get rid of the visitors.
plot:
Freaks of Nature is a 2015 American comedy horror film directed by Robbie Pickering and written by Oren Uziel. It stars Nicholas Braun as Dag, Mackenzie Davis as Petra and Josh Fadem as Ned, with Joan Cusack, Bob Odenkirk, Keegan-Michael Key, Ed Westwick, Patton Oswalt, Vanessa Hudgens and Denis Leary. The story follows three high-school outcasts in a town where humans, vampires and zombies live side by side until an alien invasion turns the species against one another.

The small town of Dillford, Ohio, is home to three groups that barely tolerate each other. Vampires sit at the top of the social ladder and are the coolest kids at school; zombies are kept in a ghetto and allowed out only with special collars that keep them docile; and humans are somewhere in between. Dag, a nerdy human teenager, is desperate to lose his virginity to Lorelei, the most popular girl in school, and is humiliated by Rick Wilson, the baseball coach who also runs the local meat factory and has replaced its human workers, including Dag's mother, with cheap zombie labor.

Meanwhile, Petra, a social outcast, is seduced and bitten by Milan, the school's playboy vampire, who then abandons her to cope alone with her new condition. Ned, Dag's former best friend and one of the smartest people in town, is so tired of being ostracized by his family and teachers that he lets a zombie bite him so that he will no longer have to think. Just as Dag finally seems about to win over Lorelei, aliens invade Dillford, and the residents, believing they are being attacked by the other species, plunge into an all-out war. Dag, Petra and Ned, now a human, a vampire and a zombie, must put aside their differences, uncover the aliens' plans and unite the town against the real enemy.

The film uses its supernatural premise to satirize high-school cliques, prejudice and social hierarchies.

Freaks of Nature was given a limited release by Columbia Pictures on October 30, 2015. It received negative reviews, with none of the five critics counted by Rotten Tomatoes giving it a positive review; The SciFi Movie Page suggested watching it only for the scenes featuring Key, Leary, Odenkirk and Oswalt.

plot:
Planes: Fire & Rescue is a 2014 animated adventure comedy film produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios and directed by Bobs Gannaway. The movie takes place in the fictional town of Piston Peak, where planes live and work together to maintain order and safety.

The story begins with Dusty Crophopper (voiced by Dane Cook), a hotshot fire plane who has just returned from his first big rescue mission. However, he soon realizes that being a hero isn't all it's cracked up to be, as he struggles to live up to the expectations of his friends and family.

Meanwhile, a series of devastating wildfires is sweeping across Piston Peak, threatening the town and its inhabitants. The fire department, led by Captain Skipper (voiced by Ed Harris), is stretched thin trying to keep up with the blazes. Dusty sees this as an opportunity to prove himself and joins the fire department.

However, things take a turn when a new plane, Lil' Dipper (voiced by Curtis Armstrong), arrives in Piston Peak. Lil' Dipper is a rescue plane who specializes in water rescues, but he's also a bit of a show-off and a rival to Dusty. The two planes engage in a series of competitions and one-upmanship, which distracts them from the real issue at hand.

As the wildfires intensify, Dusty and Lil' Dipper are forced to put aside their differences and work together to save Piston Peak. Along the way, they meet a new character, Windlifter (voiced by Wes Studi), a veteran fire plane who becomes a mentor to Dusty.

The movie's climax features an epic rescue mission as Dusty and Lil' Dipper team up to save a group of planes trapped in a burning hangar. The film's ending is heartwarming, as Dusty learns the value of teamwork and humility, and Lil' Dipper finds redemption for his past mistakes.

Throughout the movie, there are plenty of humorous moments, including cameos from other Disney characters, such as Felix (voiced by Brad Garrett) and Maru (voiced by Curtis Armstrong). The animation is colorful and vibrant, with a mix of realistic and fantastical elements that bring the world of Piston Peak to life.

Overall, Planes: Fire & Rescue is a fun and action-packed adventure that explores themes of teamwork, humility, and redemption. While it may not be as well-known as some other Disney movies, it has its own unique charm and is sure to delight fans of animation and adventure films.

title: Zombie Night
tagline: Tonight, at sundown... the dead will rise again
overview: Zombies come out at night and two families must survive until morning.
plot:
Zombie Night is a 2013 American made-for-television zombie horror film directed by John Gulager, written by Keith Allan and Delondra Williams from a story by Richard Schenkman, and produced by The Asylum for the Syfy channel. Anthony Michael Hall and Daryl Hannah star as Patrick and Birdy Jackson, a couple trying to keep their family alive through a single night, with Alan Ruck, Jennifer Taylor, Rachel G. Fox and Shirley Jones in supporting roles.

In a small California town, Patrick is driving home with his teenage daughter Tracie and her friend Rachel when they hit a man who turns out to be one of the walking dead. The corpse chases Rachel into a cemetery, and as Patrick and Tracie search for her they discover that the dead are rising from their graves. Rachel is killed, and the town quickly descends into chaos. At home, Birdy and her mother Barbara, known as Nana, arm themselves and take in an injured woman, Janice, while a police officer, Lopez, fights his way through the streets. Nearby, the family's neighbour Joe Madden barricades his wife Karin, their young son Nathan and their teenage son Perry, Tracie's boyfriend, inside a house equipped with a panic room and supplies. After Nana dies and returns as a zombie, Patrick and Tracie reunite with Birdy, but when the group goes to the Maddens' house for shelter, Joe refuses to let them in. Forced to fight their way inside at heavy cost, they find that the infected Perry has killed his father, and the survivors flee once more through the night. When dawn finally comes, only Patrick, Birdy, Tracie and Nathan are left alive, and the zombies fall still, leaving the family to wonder what will happen when the sun goes down again.

Filmed in Pasadena on a reported budget of about one million dollars, the production favoured practical effects, and Gulager cast amputees as some of the zombies; co-writer Allan appears as a looter. The film premiered on Syfy on October 26, 2013 and was released on DVD on December 10, 2013.

Reviews were largely negative. Brian Lowry of Variety dismissed it as a brain-dead exploitation picture and an almost comically amateurish effort, complaining that Hall and Hannah sleepwalk through their roles, and Michael Storey of the Arkansas Democrat-Gazette found it a sub-par zombie film lacking humour or camp. Andrew Dowler of Now was more generous, writing that it brought enough energy, skill and gore to its basic Night of the Living Dead story to provide light entertainment.

title: Police Story: Lockdown
overview: A man looking for the release of a long-time prisoner takes a police officer, his daughter, and a group of strangers hostage.
plot:
Police Story: Lockdown, released in China as Police Story 2013, is a 2013 Chinese-Hong Kong neo-noir action thriller written and directed by Ding Sheng, who had previously made Jackie Chan's Little Big Soldier. The sixth installment and another reboot of the Police Story series, it casts Chan not as a Hong Kong cop, as in the earlier films, but as a police officer from mainland China, and like New Police Story it stands alone with a much darker tone than the comedic originals.

Detective Zhong Wen goes to Wu Bar, a nightclub, to see his estranged daughter Miao Miao, who is dating its owner, Wu Jiang, and the two argue over the relationship. Before he can make peace with her, Zhong is knocked out and wakes up tied to a chair with wire, as Wu reveals himself as the mastermind of a hostage-taking that traps the bar's customers, Miao among them. Wu demands a ransom from the police and a meeting with the prisoner Wei Xiaofu. Breaking free, Zhong finds Wu's secret room, filled with pictures of a teenage girl and of Wu as a young kickboxer nicknamed "Spider", along with plans showing that he has wired the bar with explosives. Recaptured when Wu threatens to plunge Miao's hand into a tank of piranhas, Zhong wins the release of three hostages by beating one of Wu's fighters despite a broken finger, and then brings Wei to the bar.

Wu explains that Zhong, Wei and several hostages all witnessed the death of his younger sister years earlier, when Wei, trying to steal medicine for his mother, held her at knifepoint in a pharmacy and the pregnant girl killed herself with his blade. Zhong had arrived but could not save her, and the bartender reveals that he was her boyfriend. When the police storm the club, the bombs go off and Wu escapes with Miao into a subway tunnel. There he offers Zhong a choice between shooting himself to save his daughter or shooting Wu. Zhong pulls the trigger on himself, but the gun is empty, and Wu, satisfied, releases Miao and stands before an oncoming train, which is switched onto another track at the last moment. Wu is arrested, and Zhong reconciles with his daughter.

Jackie Chan plays Zhong Wen, with Liu Ye as Wu Jiang and Jing Tian as Miao Miao. Filmed in Beijing from November 2012 to February 2013, it was shown at the Beijing International Film Festival and released in China on 24 December 2013. Well Go USA distributed it in the United States as Police Story: Lockdown in June 2015. Reviews were mixed, with a 44 on Metacritic.

title: Coherence
tagline: Rearrange Your Brain
overview: On the night of an astronomical anomaly, eight friends at a dinner party experience a troubling chain of reality bending events.
plot:
Coherence is a 2013 science fiction thriller film written and directed by James Ward Byrkit. The movie takes place on a single evening in Chicago, Illinois, where a group of friends gather for dinner at a restaurant.

The story begins with a dinner party hosted by Tom (played by Maury Sterling), where his girlfriend, Emily (played by Alex Manugian), is expecting their first child. The guests include Tom's brother, Brian (played by Jake Weary), and his girlfriend, Sarah (played by Emily Foxler). As the evening progresses, the group discusses their relationships, careers, and life choices.

As the dinner party reaches its climax, a series of strange events occur, which seem to be connected to an alternate reality or parallel universe. The guests begin to experience strange visions and hallucinations, which are not explained by any external factor. These events disrupt the normal flow of time, causing the characters' perceptions of reality to become distorted.

As the night wears on, the group's relationships with each other become increasingly complicated. Brian becomes obsessed with a mysterious woman who appears in his vision, while Sarah starts to question her own identity and purpose. Emily, meanwhile, is struggling to come to terms with her pregnancy and the changes it brings to her life.

Throughout the film, Byrkit employs a non-linear narrative structure, jumping back and forth between different moments in time. This creates a sense of disorientation and confusion, mirroring the characters' experiences as they navigate the strange events unfolding around them.

As the evening reaches its climax, the group discovers that their dinner party has been interrupted by an alternate version of themselves from a parallel universe. In this reality, Tom is not with Emily, but with Sarah, who is now pregnant with his child. The guests are forced to confront the consequences of their choices and the paths they have taken in life.

The film's ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to ponder the nature of reality and the consequences of the characters' actions. Byrkit has stated that he intended for the film to be a thought-provoking exploration of the complexities of human relationships and the fragility of reality.

Overall, Coherence is a mind-bending thriller that challenges its viewers to question their perceptions of reality. With its complex narrative structure and thought-provoking themes, the film has become a cult classic among fans of science fiction and psychological thrillers.

plot:
The Smurfs: The Legend of Smurfy Hollow is a 2013 animated comedy film produced by Sony Pictures Animation. The movie takes place in the fictional village of Smurfville, where the lovable blue creatures live.

The story begins with Papa Smurf (voiced by Jonathan Winters) announcing that he has chosen a new Smurfberry harvest site for the year, which is located in a hollow tree called Smurfy Hollow. The Smurfs are excited to start their annual tradition of harvesting Smurfberries, but things take a turn when they discover that the hollow tree is inhabited by a ghostly spirit.

The ghost, known as the "Ghost of Smurfy Hollow," is said to be the spirit of a young Smurf who died in the hollow many years ago. The Ghost is determined to scare away the living Smurfs and keep them from harvesting their Smurfberries. The Smurfs are initially frightened by the Ghost's presence, but they soon realize that it's just trying to protect its home.

As the story progresses, Brainy Smurf (voiced by Danny Pudi) discovers that the Ghost is actually a manifestation of his own guilt and regret over not being able to save the young Smurf who died in the hollow. The Ghost is trying to find peace and move on from its past, but it's stuck in the hollow due to its unfinished business.

The Smurfs decide to help the Ghost by completing its unfinished task: finding a way to forgive itself and let go of its guilt. Along the way, they learn valuable lessons about friendship, forgiveness, and the importance of moving forward.

As the story unfolds, the Smurfs face various obstacles and challenges as they try to help the Ghost find peace. They also have to deal with Gargamel (voiced by Hank Azaria), who's trying to capture the Ghost and use its energy for his own evil purposes.

In the end, the Smurfs successfully help the Ghost find closure and move on from its past. The Ghost is finally able to rest in peace, and the Smurfs are able to harvest their Smurfberries without any further issues. The movie ends with a heartwarming moment of the Smurfs celebrating their success and looking forward to a bright future.

Overall, The Smurfs: The Legend of Smurfy Hollow is a charming and entertaining film that explores themes of forgiveness, friendship, and moving on from past mistakes. With its lovable characters, engaging storyline, and beautiful animation, it's a must-see for fans of the Smurfs franchise.

title: Rurouni Kenshin Part II: Kyoto Inferno
original_title: るろうに剣心 京都大火編
tagline: Fate Hangs On His Sword.
overview: Kenshin has settled into his new life with Kaoru and his other friends when he is approached with a request from the Meiji government. plot:
Rurouni Kenshin: Kyoto Inferno, released in North America as Rurouni Kenshin Part II: Kyoto Inferno, is a 2014 Japanese jidaigeki action film based on the Rurouni Kenshin manga and the second installment of the live-action series that began with Rurouni Kenshin (2012). Directed by Keishi Ōtomo, it stars Takeru Satoh as the wandering swordsman Himura Kenshin, with Emi Takei, Munetaka Aoki, Yū Aoi and Kaito Oyagi, and Tatsuya Fujiwara as the villain Shishio Makoto.

In a mine in Hyōgo Prefecture, police led by Saitō Hajime are ambushed and massacred by the men of Shishio, who had helped overthrow the Tokugawa shogunate before being betrayed. Kenshin, living at Kamiya Kaoru's dojo, at first refuses the government's request to stop Shishio, but agrees after the official Ōkubo Toshimichi is assassinated by Shishio's underling Seta Sōjirō. On the road, Kenshin meets Makimachi Misao, an aspiring ninja, and defends a village from Shishio's men, revealing his past as the assassin Hitokiri Battōsai. Brought before Shishio, he duels Sōjirō, who breaks Kenshin's reverse-blade sword.

In Kyoto, Kenshin stays at an inn run by Okina, a semi-retired ninja of the Oniwabanshū, who warns him that Shinomori Aoshi, who has already beaten Sanosuke in Tokyo, is determined to kill him. Kaoru, Yahiko and Sanosuke follow Kenshin to Kyoto. The swordsmith who made his blade has died, but his son Seikū gives Kenshin a twin of the old sword after Kenshin defeats Shishio's warrior Sawagejō Chō, who had kidnapped Seikū's baby. Learning that Shishio plans to burn Kyoto that night, the police, Kenshin, the ninja and his friends fight Shishio's forces, while Okina is defeated in a duel with his former pupil Aoshi. Kenshin realizes the attack on Kyoto is a diversion and that Shishio actually plans to set Tokyo ablaze. He pursues Sōjirō, who has kidnapped Kaoru, to Shishio's departing ship and battles Shishio until Kaoru is thrown overboard and he leaps into the sea after her. A mysterious man later finds Kenshin unconscious on a beach and carries him away.

Shot across Japan with more than 5,000 extras, the film was released by Warner Bros. Pictures Japan on August 1, 2014. It was the third highest-grossing film of 2014 in Japan, earning ¥5.22 billion, and critics praised its action and Kenji Tanigaki's fight choreography. The Legend Ends followed a month later.

title: Rurouni Kenshin Part III: The Legend Ends
original_title: るろうに剣心　伝説の最期編
tagline: Every battle has an end… but some legends live forever.
overview: Shishio sets sail in his ironclad ship to bring down the government. In order to stop him, Kenshin trains with his old master to learn his final technique.
plot:
Rurouni Kenshin: The Legend Ends is a 2014 Japanese period action film directed by Keishi Ōtomo and based on Nobuhiro Watsuki's manga Rurouni Kenshin. The third installment of the live-action film series and a direct sequel to Rurouni Kenshin: Kyoto Inferno, released earlier the same year, it stars Takeru Satoh as Himura Kenshin, Emi Takei as Kaoru Kamiya, Munetaka Aoki as Sanosuke Sagara, Yūsuke Iseya as Aoshi Shinomori, Yōsuke Eguchi as Saitō Hajime and Tatsuya Fujiwara as the villain Makoto Shishio.

The story continues immediately after the events of Kyoto Inferno. Kenshin, a former assassin who has sworn never to kill again, washes ashore and is found by his old master, Hiko Seijūrō, who once rescued him as an orphaned boy. Fearing that Kaoru has died, Kenshin asks Hiko to teach him the final technique of the Hiten Mitsurugi sword style so that he can defeat Shishio, a vengeful former government assassin who was betrayed and burned by his masters and now plans to overthrow the Meiji government.

As Kenshin undergoes his master's harsh training and confronts the fact that he has lost his will to live, Shishio arrives off the coast of Tokyo aboard an ironclad warship and forces the government to negotiate. He demands that the authorities publicly brand Kenshin, the legendary Battōsai, a criminal and hand him over, threatening to expose the government's past crimes if they refuse. Kenshin's friends learn that he is alive and that Kaoru has survived, and they set out to help him. Arrested and facing execution, Kenshin must prepare for a final confrontation on Shishio's warship, where he and his allies face Shishio's elite warriors, including the swift Sōjirō Seta, in an epic battle to decide the future of Japan.

The film is noted for its elaborate sword-fighting choreography and the climactic battle aboard the battleship, bringing the Kyoto arc of the manga to a close.

The Legend Ends was released in Japan by Warner Bros. on September 13, 2014. It spent four weeks at number one at the Japanese box office and was one of the five highest-grossing films of 2014 in Japan. The series was later continued with Rurouni Kenshin: The Final and Rurouni Kenshin: The Beginning in 2021.

title: Wer
tagline: The legend reborn
overview: A defense attorney begins to suspect that her client, who is charged with the murders of a vacationing family, might be more than meets the eye.
plot:
Wer is a 2013 American horror film directed by William Brent Bell, who co-wrote it with Matthew Peterman. A.J. Cook stars as an American defence attorney in France who comes to suspect that her client is a werewolf, with Simon Quarterman, Vik Sahay, Sebastian Roché and Brian Scott O'Connor. The film was released in Japan in November 2013 and reached video on demand in the United States in August 2014.

An American family on holiday in rural France are savagely attacked by an unseen creature, killing Henry Porter and his young son Peter. His wife Claire survives long enough to tell police, led by Captain Klaus Pistor, that the attacker looked like a man, and she later dies of her injuries. The authorities arrest Talan Gwynek, a huge, hirsute local recluse. Kate Moore, an expatriate lawyer, takes on his defence, assisted by her investigator Eric Sarin and by Gavin Flemyng, an English animal-attack expert and her former lover. During an interview at the police station a scuffle breaks out, and Talan scratches Gavin.

At the Gwyneks' isolated home, Talan's Romanian-born mother insists he is too frail to kill anyone because of a hereditary condition affecting the men in her family, and claims the police are persecuting him because the state wants their land for a nuclear waste site. The defence team suspects porphyria, while Gavin grows steadily sicker after his scratch and tension rises between him and Eric over Kate. During a medical examination, flashing strobe lights trigger Talan, who displays monstrous strength, slaughters almost everyone present and escapes.

A manhunt corners him in an abandoned building, where he is filmed transforming and survives an eight-storey fall. After killing more officers he is gunned down, but revives during transport and goes on a rampage. Gavin, now realising he shares Talan's affliction, kills Mrs. Gwynek and fully transforms. Furthermore, Crystal Lake Memories: The Complete History of Friday the 13th touches upon the theme of nostalgia and its relationship with horror. The film's nostalgic value lies not only in its portrayal of the original films but also in its exploration of how the franchise has become an integral part of popular culture, influencing countless other horror movies and TV shows.

title: The Fault in Our Stars

The Fault in Our Stars is a romantic drama film based on John Green's novel of the same name. The movie follows the story of two teenagers, Hazel and Augustus, who meet at a cancer support group.

Hazel (Shailene Woodley) is a 16-year-old girl who has thyroid cancer that requires her to carry an oxygen tank with her everywhere she goes. She is a bookworm and spends most of her time reading and writing in her online blog, where she shares her thoughts on life, death, and everything in between.

Augustus (Ansel Elgort), on the other hand, is a 17-year-old boy who lost his leg to bone cancer. He is charming, witty, and has a passion for music. Augustus is also a bit of a hopeless romantic, which makes him an instant hit with Hazel.

The two meet at a support group for kids with cancer, where they bond over their shared experiences as teenagers dealing with life-threatening illnesses. They quickly become inseparable, and their friendship blossoms into something more.

As they spend more time together, Augustus and Hazel embark on a journey to Amsterdam to attend a cancer conference, where they hope to meet other people who are going through similar struggles. Along the way, they discuss the meaning of life, death, and everything in between.

One day, while on their trip, Augustus reveals that he has been diagnosed with a rare form of bone cancer called osteosarcoma. He is given only a short time to live, which makes him realize how precious every moment is.

Hazel, who has also lost her leg due to cancer, is devastated by the news. However, she tries to stay positive and focus on making the most of their remaining time together. The two decide to take a trip to Amsterdam's famous Vondelpark, where they share a romantic kiss under the stars.

As the story unfolds, Augustus and Hazel face numerous challenges, including the harsh realities of mortality, the complexities of love, and the difficulties of living with cancer. Through their journey, they learn valuable lessons about life, death, and the importance of human connection.

In the end, Augustus's condition worsens, and he is forced to confront his own mortality. Hazel is devastated by the news, but she tries to stay strong for her loved one. The movie ends with a heart-wrenching scene where Augustus passes away in Hazel's arms, surrounded by their love and memories.

The Fault in Our Stars is a poignant and emotional film that explores the complexities of life, death, and love. Through its powerful storytelling and outstanding performances, the movie has captured the hearts of audiences worldwide, making it one of the most beloved films of recent years.

Aloha is a 2015 American romantic drama film directed by Cameron Crowe. The movie explores complex and often conflicting emotions, particularly in the context of love, loyalty, and cultural identity.

The protagonist, Allison Ng (played by Emma Stone), is a young lawyer who returns to her hometown on the island of Oahu after years away, only to find herself rekindling an old flame with her former best friend, Captain Steve Edwards (played by Bradley Cooper). As their relationship deepens, Allison must confront the choices she made in the past and the consequences that have shaped her present.

The film also grapples with issues of cultural identity and the complexities of belonging. The character of Captain Steve is a quintessential American, while Allison's family has been deeply rooted in Hawaiian culture for generations. This dichotomy serves as a backdrop for exploring themes of assimilation, tradition, and the tension between preserving one's heritage and embracing change.

Furthermore, Aloha touches on the theme of guilt and redemption. The character of Captain Steve is haunted by past mistakes, particularly those related to his business dealings with Allison's family. As their relationship progresses, he must confront these demons and find a way to make amends and start anew.

Throughout the film, Crowe masterfully weaves together these themes, creating a nuanced and thought-provoking exploration of the human experience. The result is a movie that is both poignant and humorous, with a strong focus on character development and emotional depth.

plot:
Sausage Party is a 2016 American adult animated comedy film directed by Greg Tiernan and Conrad Vernon, produced by Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg. The movie takes place in a grocery store where food items are alive.

The story begins with Frank (voiced by Seth Rogen), a hot dog sausage who lives on a shelf in the grocery store. Frank is content with his mundane life, surrounded by other food items like Brenda (voiced by Kristen Wiig), a bun, and Sammy Bagel Jr. (voiced by Jonah Hill), a bagel. However, Frank's life takes a dramatic turn when he meets Karla (voiced by Maya Rudolph), a human woman who works at the store.

Frank becomes obsessed with Karla and sets out on a journey to understand her world beyond the confines of the grocery store. Along the way, he befriends Barry (voiced by Bill Hader), a talking tortilla chip, and Douchebag (voiced by David Krumholtz), a douche bag who serves as their guide.

As Frank navigates this new world, he discovers that Karla is not just a human but also the key to understanding his own existence. He learns that food items are created in factories and then shipped to stores like the one where he lives. The movie takes a dark turn when Frank realizes that his fellow food items are being consumed by humans.

The plot thickens as Frank, Barry, and Douchebag embark on a mission to stop the evil grocery store manager, Trevor (voiced by Nick Kroll), who is determined to sell Karla to a human. Along the way, they encounter various obstacles, including treacherous landscapes like the "Meatpacking District" and the "Dairy Aisle."

As Frank's journey progresses, he develops feelings for Karla, but their love is forbidden due to the nature of their relationship. In the end, Frank must make a choice between his life in the grocery store or joining Karla in her world.

The movie culminates in an action-packed finale where Frank and his friends face off against Trevor and his minions. In the end, Frank makes the ultimate sacrifice to save Karla and ensure that she can live her life freely. The movie ends on a bittersweet note, with Frank's fate left uncertain but his legacy living on through Karla.

Throughout the movie, Sausage Party tackles mature themes like existentialism, consumerism, and the human condition. The film features a talented voice cast, witty humor, and stunning animation that brings the world of food to life. Overall, Sausage Party is a thought-provoking and hilarious animated comedy that will leave audiences laughing and pondering the meaning of life.

title: That Awkward Moment
tagline: When you realize getting some means wanting more.
overview: Best pals Jason and Daniel indulge in casual flings and revel in their carefree, unattached lives. plot:
That Awkward Moment (released as Are We Officially Dating? in Australia, New Zealand and Indonesia) is an American romantic comedy-drama of 2014 written and directed by Tom Gormican in his debut. Zac Efron, Miles Teller and Michael B. Jordan star as the friends Jason, Daniel and Mikey, with Imogen Poots as Ellie, Mackenzie Davis as Chelsea and Jessica Lucas as Mikey's wife Vera.

Waiting on a bench in New York, Jason explains in voice-over that every relationship reaches the "So..." moment, when one partner wants to get serious, and that for him it marks the end. He and Daniel design book covers at a publishing house. When their friend Mikey, a young doctor married since college, learns that Vera wants a divorce, the three head out to celebrate his freedom with Daniel's wingwoman, Chelsea. Jason charms Ellie but, mistakenly concluding that she is a prostitute, flees her apartment in the morning, only to discover the next day that she is a new author whose book cover he is pitching. The friends vow to stay single together.

Each promptly breaks the pact in secret. Jason wins Ellie back with an apology drawn as a comic strip and begins seeing her, even getting along well with her father; Daniel falls for Chelsea; and Mikey rekindles his marriage after Vera complains that he lacks spontaneity. Everything unravels at Thanksgiving. When Ellie's father dies, Jason, unwilling to commit, skips the funeral and loses her; Vera admits she no longer loves Mikey; and Daniel, caught out, denies that he is dating Chelsea, ending that romance too. The friends quarrel over their secrecy and then patch things up. Mikey calls a woman he met on the first night, and Daniel reunites with Chelsea after being hit by a taxi. Two months later, at one of Ellie's book readings, Jason makes a public scene, recalling how they met and asking her to start over in Gramercy Park, where he once gave her a stolen key. After four hours on the bench, Ellie sits down beside him and he begins, "So..."

The script appeared on the 2010 Black List of the best unproduced screenplays under its original title. Released by Focus Features on 31 January 2014, the film drew largely negative reviews, scoring 23% on Rotten Tomatoes, though Efron won the MTV Movie Award for Best Shirtless Performance.

title: Macbeth
tagline: All hail Macbeth that shall be king
overview: Feature film adaptation of Shakespeare's Scottish play about General Macbeth whose ambitious wife urges him to use wicked means in order to gain power of the throne over the sitting king, Duncan.
plot:
Macbeth is a 2015 historical drama directed by Justin Kurzel and adapted from William Shakespeare's tragedy by Todd Louiso, Jacob Koskoff and Michael Lesslie. A British and French co-production, it stars Michael Fassbender as the Scottish lord and Marion Cotillard as Lady Macbeth, with Paddy Considine, Sean Harris, David Hayman, Jack Reynor, Elizabeth Debicki and David Thewlis in supporting roles. Kurzel and Fassbender reimagined Macbeth as a soldier scarred by war and grief, adding a prologue, absent from the play, in which the couple bury their young child.

After leading King Duncan's army to a costly victory in a civil war, in which even boy soldiers die, Macbeth and his comrade Banquo meet three mysterious women who hail Macbeth as Thane of Cawdor and future king, and Banquo as the father of kings. When Duncan grants Macbeth the title of the executed traitor Cawdor, Lady Macbeth urges her husband to make the rest of the prophecy come true while the king is their guest. Guided by the ghost of a dead boy soldier, Macbeth murders Duncan in his tent; the king's son Malcolm flees, and Macbeth kills the servants framed for the crime and is crowned.

Haunted by the prophecy that Banquo's heirs will rule, Macbeth has his friend murdered, but Banquo's son Fleance escapes, and at a feast the king raves at Banquo's ghost. The witches warn him to beware Macduff but promise that he will reign until Birnam Wood comes to Dunsinane and that no man born of woman can harm him. When Macduff flees to join Malcolm, Macbeth has his wife and children burned alive. Consumed by guilt, Lady Macbeth dies, and Macbeth descends into despair. Malcolm's forces set fire to Birnam Wood, sending its smoke towards the castle, and Macduff, who reveals that he was cut from his mother's womb, kills Macbeth in single combat. As Malcolm is hailed king, Fleance takes up Macbeth's sword and runs into the smoke.

Filmed in Scotland and England, including the Isle of Skye, Bamburgh Castle and Ely Cathedral, Macbeth competed for the Palme d'Or at the 2015 Cannes Film Festival and was released by StudioCanal that autumn. Critics praised its visual style, its battle scenes and the performances of Fassbender and Cotillard, although some found the accents and diction hard to follow. It grossed about $16 million worldwide against a budget of around $20 million.

title: In Your Eyes
tagline: Two strangers. One extraordinary connection.
overview: Two seemingly unconnected souls from different corners of the United States make a telepathic bond that allows them to see, hear and feel the other's experiences, creating a bond that apparently can't be broken.
plot:
In Your Eyes is a 2014 American independent paranormal romance directed by Brin Hill and written by Joss Whedon, the second feature produced by Whedon's company Bellwether Pictures. It stars Zoe Kazan as Rebecca Porter and Michael Stahl-David as Dylan Kershaw, with Nikki Reed, Steve Harris, Mark Feuerstein as Rebecca's husband Phillip and Jennifer Grey. The film follows two strangers living on opposite sides of the United States who share an inexplicable psychic connection.

As children, Rebecca, in New Hampshire, and Dylan, in New Mexico, experience a strange moment of connection: when Rebecca crashes her sled and is knocked unconscious, Dylan is thrown from his school desk at the same instant. Twenty years later, Rebecca is married to Phillip, a successful and controlling doctor, while Dylan has recently been released from prison and is trying to stay out of trouble. One night Dylan is hit with a pool cue in a bar fight, and Rebecca, far away at a dinner party, is suddenly flung to the floor, to her husband's embarrassment.

The two soon discover that they can hear each other when they speak aloud, see what the other sees and feel what the other feels. Convinced that they are not imagining it, they begin talking every day, showing each other their surroundings, sharing memories and dreams, and introducing themselves by looking into mirrors. The bond becomes a source of comfort and intimacy for two lonely people, and they gradually fall in love. But their connection attracts unwelcome attention: Rebecca's strange behavior alarms her husband, who eventually has her forcibly institutionalized, while Dylan's parole and his old associates threaten his fresh start, and the two must find a way to be together despite the distance separating them.

The film combines romance with a light supernatural premise, focusing on the intimacy of a relationship built entirely on conversation and shared perception.

In Your Eyes premiered at the Tribeca Film Festival on April 20, 2014, and immediately afterward was self-distributed online rather than receiving a theatrical release. It received mixed to positive reviews, with 61 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes; ScreenDaily praised its balance of humour, tenderness and danger.

title: Legendary: Tomb of the Dragon
overview: Travis and his team travel to China in search of what isn't supposed to exist ... their mission to capture a Cryptid which is wreaking havoc in a remote village and they need to do this before it is killed by Harker, the legendary bounty hunter.
plot:
Legendary: Tomb of the Dragon (also released simply as Legendary) is a 2013 British-Chinese creature adventure film directed by Eric Styles from a screenplay by Andy Briggs. Starring Scott Adkins, Dolph Lundgren and Huang Yi, it was produced by companies including China Film Group, Midsummer Films and Ripken Productions on an estimated budget of about 12 million dollars, shot on location in China with cinematography by Shu Yang, scored by Paul Leonard-Morgan, and released in May 2013. It was also presented in 3D.

Adkins plays Travis Preston, a cryptozoologist who wants to capture rare and supposedly mythical animals alive for scientific study. When an expedition after a giant bear goes wrong and a colleague is killed, he is buried in lawsuits and withdraws from the field, nursing a bitter rivalry with Harker (Lundgren), a cigar-chomping trophy hunter interested only in the glory of the kill. Travis is drawn back by Doug (James Lance), a wealthy lawyer, who shows him video footage of a huge reptile filmed in a remote part of China, where a creature has been killing local workers. Reuniting his team, Katie (Lydia Leonard) and Brandon (Nathan Lee), he travels to the village to determine whether the primeval lizard is real.

On arrival the team finds that Harker, hired to destroy the beast, has already reached the key sites. The two camps clash, at one point coming to blows at an excavation, while Travis's group investigates the killings, mounts night-time boat searches and plans to trap the animal in a large cylindrical cage. Travis also finds an ally in Dr. Lan Zeng (Huang), an associate of Harker's, with whom he escapes Harker's men on a motorcycle. The hunt culminates in the discovery of the creature's cave lair, where the rivals face off, one side trying to take the animal alive and the other trying to kill it.

Critical reception was mixed to negative. Vic's Movie Den found it an enjoyable, tongue-in-cheek B-movie with a brisk pace, likable humour and an amusing Lundgren, comparing it to The Ghost and the Darkness and Jurassic Park while finding the creature effects unconvincing. INFLUX Magazine praised the scenery and cinematography but called the script contrived and likened the film to a better-funded Syfy television movie. German reviewers similarly criticised its lack of originality and weak computer effects while noting attractive nature photography and an entertaining rivalry between the leads.

Horrible Bosses 2 is a 2014 American comedy film directed by Seth Gordon and written by Michael Markowitz, John Francis Daley, and Jonathan Goldstein. The movie serves as a sequel to the 2011 film Horrible Bosses.

The story begins with Nick Hendricks (Jason Bateman), Dave Harken (Kevin Spacey), and Kurt Buckman (Jennifer Aniston) having successfully killed their terrible bosses, but they soon realize that their newfound freedom comes with its own set of problems. They are now struggling to find new jobs and deal with the consequences of their actions.

Meanwhile, a new character, Bobby Pellit (Colin Farrell), is introduced as the son of the late Mr. Pellit, who was one of the original bosses in the first film. Bobby is a ruthless and cunning businessman who has taken over his father's company, Pellit Inc. He becomes the target of Nick, Dave, and Kurt, who are determined to take him down.

As the story unfolds, the three friends concoct a plan to kill Bobby, but things don't go as smoothly as they had hoped in the first film. The plot thickens when Bobby's girlfriend, Sarah (Jamie Foxx), becomes involved with one of the main characters, and the group must navigate their personal relationships while trying to take down Bobby.

Throughout the movie, the characters face various obstacles, including a series of hilarious misadventures and unexpected twists. In the end, Nick, Dave, and Kurt must confront their own flaws and weaknesses in order to succeed in their mission.

The film features an ensemble cast, including Charlie Day as Dean "Fist" Jones, a new character introduced in this sequel. The movie also includes several comedic set pieces, including a memorable scene at a Las Vegas casino.

Overall, Horrible Bosses 2 is a raunchy and irreverent comedy that explores the consequences of taking revenge on one's terrible bosses. While it may not be as sharp or original as its predecessor, the film delivers plenty of laughs and entertaining moments for fans of the genre.

title: Monster High: Fright On!
overview: See what happens when the student bodies of an all-vampire school and an all-werewolf school integrate with Monster High.
plot:
Monster High: Fright On! is a 2011 animated fantasy comedy television special based on Mattel's Monster High fashion doll line, broadcast on Nickelodeon in the United States on October 30, 2011. The second Monster High special after New Ghoul @ School, it is tied to the "School's Out" and "Dead Tired" doll ranges. The voice cast includes Kate Higgins as Frankie Stein, Salli Saffioti as both Cleo de Nile and Clawdeen Wolf, Debi Derryberry as Draculaura, Laura Bailey as Lagoona Blue and Headmistress Bloodgood, Erin Fitzgerald as Abbey Bominable and Ogie Banks as Clawd Wolf.

Headmistress Bloodgood announces that Monster High will merge with two other schools, the all-vampire Belfry Prep and the werewolf-only Crescent Moon High, hoping to unite all monsters and eventually the human world. Frankie welcomes the plan, but Draculaura, a vampire dating the werewolf Clawd, is nervous, and the first day proves a disaster. Vampires and werewolves carve out separate territory, the vampire Gory clashes with Cleo by trying to take over the Fear Squad, and Clawd's childhood friend Romulus is dismayed that he loves a vampire. Frankie's plan for a unifying dance is ruined by Administrator Van Hellscream, the human official for monster relations, who takes over the school with his assistant Crabgrass and secretly inflames the feud while claiming to keep the peace. Clawd's insecure younger sister Howleen joins the conflict, rival support groups form, and Romulus quietly drives Clawd and Draculaura apart.

Frankie discovers that Crabgrass has turned Bloodgood to stone with gorgon dust and taken her place, the real headmistress now standing as a statue in the courtyard. Learning from Deuce how to reverse the curse, she frees Bloodgood, but Van Hellscream traps the girls over a pit in the catacombs. With Draculaura and Howleen missing, the vampires and werewolves blame each other and plan a midnight showdown in the gym, which Van Hellscream hopes will convince the authorities that monsters must be kept apart. Abbey frees the girls, and with help from Operetta, Clawdeen and Clawd they escape; Draculaura shields Howleen from a gargoyle, changing her mind about vampires. The girls reach the gym before the fight begins, and Frankie's speech brings the students together. Van Hellscream and Crabgrass try to flee, but Deuce turns them to stone, and Romulus makes peace with Clawd and befriends Draculaura.

Critical coverage was sparse; CineMagazine rated it 2.5 stars.

title: Unbroken
tagline: Survival. Resilience. Redemption.
overview: A chronicle of the life of Louis Zamperini, an Olympic runner who was taken prisoner by Japanese forces during World War II.
plot:
Unbroken is a biographical war drama film directed by Angelina Jolie, released in 2014. The film is based on the life of Louis Zamperini, an American Olympic athlete and World War II prisoner of war.

The film begins with Louis Zamperini (played by Jack O'Connell) as a young boy growing up in Torrance, California, during the Great Depression. He is a rebellious and troubled child who finds solace in track and field, inspired by his father's athletic career. Louis becomes an Olympic athlete, competing in the 1936 Summer Olympics in Berlin.

After the Olympics, Louis joins the United States Army Air Forces (USAAF) and is assigned to the 20th Air Force, which is tasked with bombing Japanese cities. In May 1943, Louis' plane crashes on the Pacific Ocean, leaving him stranded for 47 days with two fellow crew members, Russell Phillips (played by Domhnall Gleeson) and Francis McNulty (played by Finn Wittrock). The three men survive on coconuts and rainwater, but eventually, they are rescued by the Japanese Navy.

Louis is taken prisoner by the Japanese and sent to a series of POW camps in Japan. He endures brutal treatment, including forced labor, starvation, and physical abuse. Despite the harsh conditions, Louis maintains his faith and becomes an inspiration to his fellow prisoners.

In 1944, Louis is transferred to a camp where he meets a Japanese guard named Mutsuhiro Watanabe (played by Takashi Yamaguchi), who becomes his captor and tormentor. Watanabe subjects Louis to physical and emotional abuse, including being forced to dig graves for dead Allied soldiers.

As the war ends in August 1945, Louis is finally released from the POW camp. He returns to the United States, where he struggles to adjust to civilian life. He becomes a motivational speaker and writer, sharing his story of survival and resilience with others.

The film ends with Louis' reunion with his family, including his wife, Cynthia (played by Melissa Leo), and their two children. Despite the trauma he experienced during the war, Louis finds peace and redemption through his faith and his relationships with those around him.

Throughout the film, Angelina Jolie's direction weaves together themes of hope, resilience, and the human spirit. The film features stunning cinematography, capturing the beauty of the Pacific Ocean and the harsh conditions of the POW camps. The performances by the cast, particularly Jack O'Connell and Domhnall Gleeson, are also noteworthy.

Overall, Unbroken is a powerful and moving film that tells an incredible true story of survival and redemption.
