plot:
Paranormal Activity: The Marked Ones is a 2014 American supernatural horror film directed by Fede Alvarez and written by Christopher Landon. The movie is the fourth installment in the Paranormal Activity franchise, which began with the 2007 film Paranormal Activity.

The story follows Jesse (Jorge Lendeborg Jr.), a high school student who moves to Los Angeles from El Paso, Texas, with his family. Jesse's cousin, Alex (Javier Botet), is struggling to adjust to life in LA after being bullied at school. The two cousins bond over their shared experiences as outsiders.

One night, while exploring the neighborhood, Jesse and Alex stumble upon a mysterious figure lurking around an abandoned house. They soon discover that the house has been marked with strange symbols, which seem to be connected to an ancient ritual. As they delve deeper into the mystery, they begin to experience terrifying supernatural events, including unexplained noises, movements, and visions.

As the events escalate, Jesse becomes increasingly obsessed with uncovering the truth behind the markings and the mysterious figure. He enlists the help of his friends, including Marisol (Claudia Geilfuss), a local artist who is familiar with the history of the house. Together, they research the symbols and try to understand their significance.

The group soon discovers that the markings are connected to an ancient cult that was active in the area. The cult believed that certain individuals were "marked" by the supernatural forces, and these individuals would be chosen for a dark purpose. As Jesse becomes more deeply embroiled in the mystery, he realizes that he is one of the marked ones.

As the events reach a climax, Jesse's friends are picked off one by one, and he is left to face the mysterious figure alone. In a desperate bid to survive, Jesse uses his knowledge of the ancient ritual to try and defeat the supernatural forces.

The movie culminates in a shocking twist: Jesse discovers that Alex is not just an innocent bystander but is actually the chosen one, destined for a dark purpose. The film ends with Jesse's fate uncertain, leaving the audience wondering if he will survive or succumb to the supernatural forces.

Throughout the movie, Fede Alvarez masterfully builds tension and suspense, using clever camera work and sound design to create an atmosphere of unease. The cast delivers strong performances, particularly Jorge Lendeborg Jr., who brings a sense of vulnerability and determination to his character.

Overall, Paranormal Activity: The Marked Ones is a tense and unsettling horror film that explores themes of identity, community, and the supernatural. While it may not be as well-known as some of its predecessors in the franchise, it offers a unique take on the paranormal activity genre and is sure to leave viewers on the edge of their seats.

title: Anna
tagline: Don't let her in.
overview: A man with the ability to enter peoples' memories takes on the case of a brilliant, troubled sixteen-year-old girl to determine whether she is a sociopath or a victim of trauma.
plot:
Mindscape, also released as Anna, is a 2013 psychological science fiction thriller and the feature directorial debut of the Spanish filmmaker Jorge Dorado, written by Guy Holmes. An international co-production, it stars Mark Strong as John Washington, a memory detective, Taissa Farmiga as Anna Greene, Brian Cox as his superior Sebastian and Noah Taylor. The film follows an investigator who must determine whether a troubled teenager is a sociopath or a victim.

In a world where some people, known as viewers, have developed the psychic ability to enter other people's memories, John Washington works for Mindscape, an agency that uses such talents to help solve criminal cases, though its findings are not admissible in court. Still grieving the death of his wife, John suffers a stroke during a failed session and is left unable to work for two years. Financially desperate, he asks Sebastian for a new assignment.

He is given the case of Anna, a brilliant but troubled sixteen-year-old who is on a hunger strike and whose stepfather wants her institutionalized. As John explores her memories of her time at a prestigious girls' school, he uncovers a series of disturbing incidents, including accusations against a teacher and the poisoning of classmates, for which Anna blames a mysterious girl nicknamed Mousey. Increasingly drawn to Anna and convinced that she is a victim of abuse, John begins to suspect the adults around her, while signs emerge that Anna may be manipulating him and altering her own memories. When violence erupts at Anna's home, John finds himself accused of a crime and must discover the truth about the girl he has been trying to help.

The film is a puzzle thriller about memory, manipulation and the unreliability of perception.

Mindscape premiered at the 46th Sitges Film Festival in October 2013, with StudioCanal handling international sales and distribution in several European countries. It grossed about 1.1 million dollars and received mixed reviews, with 33 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 42.

title: Project Almanac

overview: A group of teens discover secret plans of a time machine, and construct one. However, things start to get out of control.
plot:
Project Almanac is a 2015 American science fiction thriller film directed by Dean Georgaris and written by Dean Georgaris and Jeremy M. Johnson. The movie stars Jonny Weston, Allen Leinman, and Brittany Snow.

The story begins with three high school friends - Jake (Jonny Weston), Will (Allen Leinman), and Chris (Brittany Snow) - who are struggling to find their place in the world after graduation. They decide to make a time capsule that will be opened on December 31, 2015, as a way to cope with their impending adulthood.

While working on the project, they stumble upon an unusual equation that seems to defy the laws of physics. Intrigued, they begin to experiment with it, and after several failed attempts, they finally succeed in creating a functioning time machine.

Excited by their discovery, the friends decide to use the time machine to alter events from their past, hoping to improve their lives. However, as they start making changes, they realize that every decision has unintended consequences, and their actions begin to unravel the fabric of reality.

As the night wears on, Jake becomes increasingly obsessed with using the time machine to change his own life, while Will tries to keep a level head and maintain control over the situation. Chris, who had initially been hesitant about the project, begins to see the potential benefits of altering their past.

The friends' actions start to have catastrophic consequences, causing events from their past to unfold in unexpected ways. They soon realize that they are trapped in a time loop, reliving the same night over and over again as they try to fix their mistakes.

As the night wears on, Jake becomes more and more reckless, using the time machine to alter events for his own gain. Will tries to intervene, but Jake's actions become increasingly erratic, putting everyone at risk.

In a desperate attempt to break the cycle, Will uses the time machine to send Chris back in time, hoping that she will be able to prevent the catastrophic events from occurring. However, this plan ultimately fails, and the friends are left with no choice but to try and destroy the time machine before it's too late.

In the end, Jake is killed by a car while trying to use the time machine, and Will manages to destroy the device in an attempt to prevent further chaos. As the night comes to a close, Will reflects on the events that have transpired, realizing that some things are meant to be and that altering the past can have devastating consequences.

The movie ends with Will standing alone, looking out at the cityscape, as the clock strikes midnight, marking the end of 2015. The final shot is of the time capsule, which has been left untouched, a reminder of the friends' failed attempt to alter their lives and the unpredictable nature of time itself.

The film showcases the deep connection that develops between Winter and Sawyer, as they work together to help her overcome her challenges. This friendship serves as a reminder of the importance of empathy, compassion, and understanding in our relationships with others.

title: Justin Bieber's Believe
overview: A backstage and on-stage look at Justin Bieber during his rise to super stardom.
plot:
Justin Bieber's Believe is a 2013 American concert documentary directed by Jon M. Chu, who also staged the Canadian singer's Believe Tour, and the follow-up to Justin Bieber: Never Say Never (2011). Combining tour performances, rehearsal and backstage footage and fresh interviews with the star, it traces Bieber's continuing rise to global fame and his attempts to cope with growing up in the spotlight. Open Road Films distributed it in the United States and Canada.

The film moves between the making of the tour and the shows themselves. It opens on Bieber casually improvising at a piano and joking in a dressing room, then follows the large dance auditions held to cast the tour, the rehearsals, and his collaborations with his creative team, including a comic sequence about the courting of Chu himself to direct the production. On stage, Bieber makes his entrance dressed in white, descending above the crowd on giant wings fashioned from guitars, drums and other instruments, and he reaches out to fans at the front, sometimes bringing one up to be serenaded. Interspersed are home videos of young fans reacting hysterically to receiving concert tickets and shots of devotees camping on pavements to buy them. Stanley's character, in particular, grapples with the notion of authenticity versus artifice, as he struggles to reconcile his public persona with his true feelings for Sophie.

The movie also explores the theme of vulnerability, highlighting the difficulties of opening oneself up to love and intimacy. Through Stanley's journey, the film shows how even those who have built walls around themselves can find it challenging to let go and be truly vulnerable.

Ultimately, Magic in the Moonlight is a romantic comedy that uses humor and wit to explore deeper themes about human connection, identity, and the complexities of love.

title: Minions: Training Wheels
overview: Margo, Edith, and Agnes spot an ice cream truck.The three of them go after the truck but Agnes falls as she attempts to pedal to the truck. The Minions, seeing her so upset by this, decide to build her a unicorn-themed motorcycle. Agnes goes for a little ride around town.
plot:
Minions: Training Wheels is a 2013 American computer-animated short comedy film produced by Illumination as a companion piece to Despicable Me 2. Directed by Eric Favela and Régis Schuller from a story by Brett Hoffman, it was one of three new shorts, alongside Puppy and Panic in the Mailroom, included as bonus material on the Blu-ray, Blu-ray 3D and DVD release of Despicable Me 2, which Universal Pictures Home Entertainment issued on 10 December 2013. The parent film, directed by Chris Renaud and Pierre Coffin, follows the retired supervillain Gru, and the short turns the spotlight onto his three adopted daughters and the yellow, gibberish-speaking Minions who serve him.

The story is a simple, almost wordless comic episode. When an ice cream truck rolls through the neighbourhood, Margo, Edith and little Agnes race after it on their bicycles. Agnes, the youngest, still struggles on her bike and falls behind, then takes a tumble while pedalling, leaving her disappointed and in tears. A trio of Minions, moved by her distress, decides to help her catch up. Applying their usual eccentric ingenuity, they put her through a training regimen, with one Minion acting as her coach, and build her a gleaming unicorn-themed motorcycle.

Riding her new machine, Agnes finally reaches her sisters, but just as she is about to get her ice cream, a jewel thief hijacks the ice cream van and speeds off. Furious at losing her treat, Agnes chases the van through town, shouting for her ice cream, and inadvertently causes the thief to crash, which makes her a local hero. Her motorcycle is wrecked in the process, but in the end she manages to ride her old bicycle without stabilisers and declares that she likes it better anyway, not least because the Minions have secretly fitted it with a button that transforms it into a robotic suit.

The short reunites much of the feature's voice cast. Miranda Cosgrove voices Margo, Dana Gaier voices Edith and Elsie Fisher voices Agnes, while Pierre Coffin provides the voices of the Minions. Dave Rosenbaum voices the ice cream vendor, co-director Régis Schuller voices the jewel thief, and Steve Carell appears uncredited as Gru. Like the other bonus shorts made for the franchise's home video releases, it extends the slapstick, dialogue-light humour of the Minions into a self-contained story built around a single gag-driven situation.

The film delves into the psychological effects of trauma on individuals, particularly those who have experienced loss or betrayal. Alton's journey is marked by his struggle to come to terms with his father's death and his own sense of identity.

The movie also touches upon the theme of power dynamics, as Alton navigates a world where he is both vulnerable and resourceful. His interactions with the KGB agent, Simo, serve as a catalyst for exploring the blurred lines between good and evil, highlighting the moral ambiguities that often accompany human relationships.

Alton's actions are driven by his desire to protect himself and those he cares about, rather than any grandiose sense of duty or responsibility. This nuanced portrayal of heroism adds depth to the narrative, inviting viewers to reevaluate their own perceptions of courage and sacrifice.

Ultimately, Big Game presents a thought-provoking exploration of human resilience in the face of adversity, encouraging audiences to reflect on their own capacity for survival and redemption.

title: Tarzan
tagline: The legend starts here
overview: One of the most classic and revered stories of all time, Edgar Rice Burroughs' Tarzan returns to the big screen for a new generation. Tarzan and Jane face a mercenary army dispatched by the evil CEO of Greystoke Energies, a man who took over the company from Tarzan's parents, after they died in a plane crash in the African jungle.
plot:
Tarzan is a 2013 English-language German animated action-adventure film written, directed and produced by Reinhard Klooss, based on the Tarzan stories by Edgar Rice Burroughs. Kellan Lutz voices John Greystoke Jr., the jungle-raised Tarzan, and Spencer Locke voices Jane Porter, with Trevor St. John as William Clayton, the scheming chief executive of Greystoke Energies and Les Bubb, Joe Cappelletti and Brian Huskey also in the cast.

In prehistoric times a meteor strikes the Earth and wipes out the dinosaurs. In the present, the industrialist John Greystoke funds an expedition to Uganda, aided by the scientist James Porter, to find the meteor and harness its energy. When the search fails, he leaves with his family, but over a semi-active volcano their helicopter's instruments go haywire and they land on the meteor. Taking a sample of its glowing rock, John sets off a reaction that awakens the volcano, and the helicopter crashes as they flee, leaving only the boy alive. The mountain gorilla Kala, who has just lost her own baby, adopts him, and he grows up among the animals under a name he invents, Tarzan. When Porter's daughter Jane is bitten by a viper during a safari, the young Tarzan carries her to shelter and cures her. Unsettled by contact with people, he leaves his gorilla family to live at the crash site. Years later, the apes' abusive leader Tublat accidentally activates the helicopter's emergency beacon, alerting Greystoke Energies, and Clayton persuades Jane, now a conservationist, to join him in Africa. Disgusted by his greed, Jane wanders into the jungle and finds the grown Tarzan. When Clayton discovers that the Greystoke heir is alive, he opens fire, and the couple flee into a valley where the meteor has mutated plants and animals into monsters. At the meteor Tarzan finds his father's pickaxe, and Jane realizes who he is. Tarzan returns to his troop, defeats and exiles Tublat, and he and Jane admit their love. Clayton turns Porter's camp into an armed base, Kala is shot protecting the couple, and Clayton rigs the meteor with explosives, but Tarzan rescues Jane and her father, summons his animal friends and escapes as the mountain collapses and Clayton and his men fall to their deaths.

Tarzan premiered in Russia on 17 October 2013 and was released in Germany by Constantin Film on 20 February 2014. Despite largely negative reviews, including a 20% Rotten Tomatoes rating, it grossed €44.1 million worldwide on a €25 million budget.

title: Pirates of the Caribbean: Tales of the Code: Wedlocked
original_title: Pirates of the Caribbean: Tales of the Code: Wedlocked
tagline: That scoundrel! Thinks he can marry the both of us!
overview: Wenches Scarlett and Giselle fix each other up for their wedding, in which they would each marry their groom. Upon realizing that both their grooms were the same man, Jack Sparrow, the two wenches found themselves in an auction led by the Auctioneer. This short film serves as a prequel to The Curse of the Black Pearl, and explains just why Jack Sparrow's boat the Jolly Mon was seen sinking at the beginning of the whole story; why the wenches were so upset with him; and how Cotton lost his tongue.
plot:
Pirates of the Caribbean: Tales of the Code: Wedlocked is a 2011 American live-action short film directed by James Ward Byrkit and written by Ted Elliott and Terry Rossio, the screenwriters of the Pirates of the Caribbean trilogy, with Jerry Bruckheimer as executive producer. Running about ten minutes, it is a prequel to The Curse of the Black Pearl centered on Scarlett and Giselle, the two Tortuga wenches from the films, played again by Lauren Maher and Vanessa Branch. John Vickery plays the Auctioneer, a character drawn from the Disneyland attraction, and David Bailie returns as Cotton, speaking on screen for the first time, with Walter Williamson, Fred Maske, Ric Sarabia, Jack Donner and Dale Dickey among the pirates and wenches.

In Shipwreck City, Scarlett and Giselle are preparing for their weddings in front of the same mirror when they realize they are about to marry the same man: both wear identical rings from Captain Jack Sparrow. A curtain then rises to reveal a room full of eager pirates and a banner announcing an auction of wenches as brides. The two women, who believe the money is being raised for them, compete for attention as the bids climb, then brawl on stage, which only drives the price higher, until the Marquis D'Avis buys them both for 700 pieces of silver and two goats. When the Auctioneer shackles them and declares that the proceeds are his, since Jack traded them to him fair and square under the Pirate Code, the crowd turns ugly. The stern guardian of the Code, Mungard, threatens anyone who disrespects it, but Giselle slaps him, a stray pistol shot sets off chaos, and Mungard, hearing Jack's name, fires and hits the Code book itself. He orders the shocked pirates to keep silent on pain of losing their tongues, and Cotton promptly assures him that "mum's the word". Escaping by boat, the brides vow to slap Jack when they next see him, and Scarlett reveals that she pulled four nails from his boat, explaining why it is sinking when he first appears in The Curse of the Black Pearl.

Byrkit, a conceptual consultant on the trilogy, shot the short in late 2006 in three days on the Shipwreck Cove sets left over from At World's End before they were demolished. It was released on 18 October 2011 as an exclusive in the Pirates of the Caribbean Four-Movie Collection Blu-ray set. Reviewing it, Chronique Disney called it funny, respectful and well paced, faithful to the spirit of the first three films.

At its core, the film is a poignant exploration of the emotional toll that being a superhero takes on individuals. Both Tony Stark and Bruce Banner struggle with their own personal demons, which often lead to destructive outbursts. The movie highlights the difficulties of balancing one's ego with the need for selflessness and responsibility.

Tony Stark's character, in particular, is driven by a desire to prove himself as a hero and earn the respect of those around him. Meanwhile, Bruce Banner's struggles with his alter ego serve as a reminder that even the most well-intentioned individuals can be consumed by their darker impulses.

Furthermore, the film explores the idea of what it means to be a true hero. Is it about having incredible powers or abilities? Or is it about making sacrifices and putting the needs of others before one's own? The movie raises these questions through the characters' interactions and relationships, ultimately suggesting that true heroism lies in finding a balance between personal ambition and selflessness.

Overall, Iron Man & Hulk: Heroes United is a thought-provoking animated film that offers a nuanced exploration of complex themes and character dynamics.

plot:
Blended is a 2014 American romantic comedy film directed by Frank Coraci and written by Ivan Menchell. The movie stars Adam Sandler and Drew Barrymore as two single parents who end up on a disastrous blind date, which ultimately leads to them spending the entire summer together with their kids.

The story begins with Jim Friedman (Adam Sandler), a divorced father of three, who is trying to find love again. He meets Lauren Reynolds (Drew Barrymore) at a singles bar, where they agree to go on a blind date. However, things don't go as planned, and the two end up getting drunk together, leading to a series of awkward moments.

Despite the initial disaster, Jim and Lauren decide to give their relationship another chance and meet again with their kids in tow. They spend the summer together at a family resort, where they try to navigate their feelings for each other while also dealing with their own personal issues.

As the summer progresses, Jim and Lauren start to develop feelings for each other, but their past relationships and fears hold them back. Meanwhile, their kids, who are initially hesitant about their parents' relationship, eventually warm up to the idea of having two moms or dads.

Throughout the movie, Jim and Lauren face various challenges, including a series of hilarious misadventures with their kids, a rival suitor for Lauren's affections (played by Kevin Nealon), and their own personal demons. Despite these obstacles, they continue to grow closer and eventually realize that they have fallen in love.

The movie culminates with Jim and Lauren confessing their feelings to each other and sharing a romantic kiss. The film ends on a heartwarming note, with the two couples (Jim's kids and Lauren's kids) embracing their blended family and looking forward to a bright future together.

Overall, Blended is a lighthearted, comedic take on love, family, and relationships. With its witty dialogue, relatable characters, and hilarious moments, it's a fun and entertaining movie that will leave audiences smiling.

title: Ratchet & Clank
tagline: Kick Some Asteroid.
overview: When the galaxy comes under the threat of a nefarious space captain, a mechanic and his newfound robot ally join an elite squad of combatants to save the universe.
plot:
Ratchet & Clank is a 2016 animated science fiction action comedy film based on the Insomniac Games video game series, directed by Kevin Munroe. James Arnold Taylor and David Kaye reprise their roles from the games as Ratchet and Clank, alongside Jim Ward as Captain Qwark and Armin Shimerman as Doctor Nefarious, with Paul Giamatti, John Goodman, Bella Thorne, Rosario Dawson and Sylvester Stallone. The film offers an original story loosely based on the first game in the series, released in 2002.

In the Solana Galaxy, Chairman Drek and his species, the Blarg, are dismantling entire planets to build a new artificial world to replace their polluted home planet. At a factory producing Drek's war robots, a defective robot is created and escapes to warn the heroic Galactic Rangers. He crash-lands on the planet Veldin and meets Ratchet, a young lombax mechanic who dreams of becoming a Ranger. Ratchet names the robot Clank, and together they save the Rangers from an attack, becoming instant celebrities.

Pressured by their popularity, the vain Ranger leader, Captain Qwark, recruits Ratchet and Clank to the team. Jealous of their fame, Qwark secretly agrees to help Drek, who is preparing to destroy more planets with his superweapon, the Deplanetizer. When Drek's scientist, Doctor Nefarious, reveals his own scheme to take control of the weapon and destroy the entire galaxy, Ratchet and Clank must stop him and persuade Qwark to choose the right side.

The film was produced at Rainmaker Entertainment's studio in Vancouver, with Insomniac contributing to its screenplay, characters and animation assets; the screenplay was co-written by the series' former senior writer T. J. Fixman. A re-imagined version of the first game was released as a tie-in.

Ratchet & Clank was released in the United States by Gramercy Pictures on April 29, 2016. It was a box office failure, grossing 14.4 million dollars against a 20 million dollar budget, and received generally negative reviews, with 22 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 29.

title: Pride
tagline: Based on the inspirational true story.
overview: In 1984, a group of LGBT activists decide to raise money to support the National Union of Mineworkers during their lengthy strike. There is only one problem: the Union seems embarrassed to receive their support.
plot:
Pride is a 2014 historical comedy-drama written by Stephen Beresford and directed by Matthew Warchus. Based on a true story, it follows the lesbian and gay activists who raised money for mining families during the 1984 miners' strike, the start of the Lesbians and Gays Support the Miners campaign. It premiered in the Directors' Fortnight at Cannes, where it won the Queer Palm, and opened in British cinemas on 12 September 2014.

Watching news coverage of the strike, London activist Mark Ashton notices that the police have shifted their harassment from gay people to the miners. After a bucket collection at the Pride march, he founds LGSM, joined by the closeted 20-year-old student Joe and by Jonathan and Gethin, whose bookshop Gay's the Word becomes its base. Frustrated by the lack of response, the group takes its donations directly to the Welsh village of Onllwyn. Local spokesman Dai Donovan gives a moving speech of thanks in a gay bar, and although Maureen leads a walkout when LGSM first visits, Hefina and the outspoken newcomer Siân James help win the village round, especially after Jonathan's legal knowledge frees detained miners.

Maureen leaks the story to a tabloid, and the activists answer by staging the "Pits and Perverts" benefit concert headlined by Bronski Beat. But a hastily brought-forward union vote rejects further help, Mark is shaken by a former lover's hint that he has AIDS, Gethin is badly beaten, and Joe is outed to his parents. When the strike ends in March 1985, Joe leaves home and Mark rejoins the group, and at the 1985 Pride march LGSM is joined by hundreds of miners. An epilogue recounts the union's support for gay rights within the Labour Party and Mark's death from AIDS at 26.

Ben Schnetzer plays Mark, Bill Nighy plays Cliff, Paddy Considine plays Dai and Imelda Staunton plays Hefina, with Dominic West, Andrew Scott, George MacKay and Joseph Gilgun. Critics were highly positive, with 92% approval on Rotten Tomatoes and comparisons to The Full Monty and Billy Elliot, and the film earned more than £3.2 million in the UK in its first four weekends. It was nominated for the Golden Globe for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy and for three BAFTAs, and a stage musical version premiered in Cardiff in 2026.

title: Time of EVE: The Movie
original_title: イヴの時間 劇場版
tagline: Are you enjoying the time of EVE?
overview: In the not-too-distant future, androids have come into common usage. However, treating androids on the same level as humans is frowned upon, and there is constant paranoia surrounding the possibility of robots defying humans, their masters. Those who appear too trustworthy of their androids are chided and labeled as "android-holics". Rikuo Sakisaka, who has taken robots for granted for his entire life, one day discovers that Sammy, his home android, has been acting independently and coming and going on her own. He finds a strange phrase recorded in her activity log, "Are you enjoying the time of EVE?". He, along with his friend Masakazu Masaki, traces Sammy's movements and finds an unusual café. Nagi, the barista, informs them that the café's main rule is to not discriminate between humans and androids. While Rikuo tries to reveal Sammy's intentions, he begins to question the legitimacy of the fear that drives humans to regard androids as nothing more than mere tools.
plot:
Time of EVE: The Movie (Japanese: Ivu no Jikan Gekijōban) is a 2010 Japanese animated science fiction drama directed by Yasuhiro Yoshiura. It is the theatrical version of Time of Eve, a six-episode original net animation that Yoshiura created and that streamed on Yahoo! Japan between 2008 and 2009. Produced by Directions, Inc. and animated by Studio Rikka, it features character designs by Ryusuke Chayama and music by Tohru Okada, with the voices of Jun Fukuyama, Rie Tanaka, Kenji Nojima, Rina Sato, Yukana and Miyuki Sawashiro.

In a near future where androids have become everyday household appliances, treating them as equals is frowned upon, and an anti-robot group called the Ethics Committee campaigns for strict separation between humans and machines. High school student Rikuo Sakisaka, who has always taken robots for granted, notices that his family's android, Sammy, has been coming and going on her own, and finds a strange phrase in her activity log: "Are you enjoying the Time of Eve?" With his best friend Masaki, he traces her movements to a hidden café of that name, whose barista, Nagi, enforces a single rule: no discrimination between humans and androids. Inside, androids stop displaying the halo-like status rings that normally mark them as machines, and the door locks for a short time after each customer leaves so that no one can follow them.

Visiting the café again and again, the two boys meet its regulars, among them the chatty Akiko, the young couple Koji and Rina, who each hide their true nature from the other, and little Chie and her elderly guardian Shimei. Their conversations often play on Isaac Asimov's Three Laws of Robotics and their unexpected loopholes. Rikuo, who gave up the piano after being moved by a robot's performance, discovers that Sammy is far more human than he believed, while Masaki, whose father is an official of the Ethics Committee, must confront the childhood resentment that turned him against his own household robot, Tex. The film also hints at the history behind the café and the people who created it.

The movie premiered in Tokyo and Osaka on 6 March 2010, with a new theme song, "I have a dream", composed by Yuki Kajiura and performed by Kalafina. It was selected for the Pusan International Film Festival and received a Jury Recommended Work distinction at the 14th Japan Media Arts Festival. In 2013 a Kickstarter campaign for an international Blu-ray release raised more than ten times its goal.

title: Son of God
tagline: Their Empire. His Kingdom.
overview: The life story of Jesus is told from his humble birth through his teachings, crucifixion and ultimate resurrection.
plot:
Son of God is a 2014 American epic biblical film directed by Christopher Spencer and produced by Mark Burnett and Roma Downey. It retells the life of Jesus by adapting The Bible, the miniseries that aired on the History channel in March 2013, combining aired scenes with unaired footage. Scenes of Satan were cut from the feature after commentators claimed that the actor playing him resembled President Barack Obama. The film opened in the United States and Canada on February 28, 2014.

The elderly John, the last of Jesus' followers still alive, recounts the story from his exile. Born in Bethlehem to Mary and Joseph and visited by three wise men, Jesus begins his ministry in Galilee thirty years later, gathering Peter, James, John, Matthew and Mary Magdalene. His teachings and miracles draw huge crowds who call him the Messiah, while the Pharisees accuse him of blasphemy for forgiving sins. Entering Jerusalem on a donkey before Passover, he is hailed with palm leaves and overturns the tables of the money changers in the temple. The high priest Caiaphas, warned by the Roman governor Pontius Pilate that any unrest will lead him to close the temple and cancel the festival, resolves to stop him, and Judas agrees to help in exchange for thirty pieces of silver.

After the Last Supper, Judas betrays Jesus with a kiss in the Garden of Gethsemane. Tried at night and convicted of blasphemy when he confirms he is the Son of God, Jesus is handed to the Romans. Pilate finds no breach of Roman law and has him flogged, but Caiaphas sways the crowd to free Barabbas instead and demand crucifixion, and Pilate washes his hands of the matter. Jesus is crucified at Golgotha beneath a sign proclaiming him King of the Jews, and his death brings an earthquake that tears the temple curtain. Three days later Mary Magdalene finds the tomb empty and meets the risen Jesus, who appears to the disciples, convinces the doubting Thomas and ascends into heaven, later visiting the aged John to promise that he will return.

Diogo Morgado plays Jesus, with Roma Downey as Mary, Greg Hicks as Pilate, Adrian Schiller as Caiaphas, Darwin Shaw as Peter, Sebastian Knapp as John, Joe Wredden as Judas and Amber Rose Revah as Mary Magdalene. Critics were largely negative, with 17% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, though audiences gave it an A− CinemaScore. It opened to $26.5 million and grossed $70.9 million on a $22 million budget.

title: Marshland
tagline: Life, Death, Redemption.
overview: The Spanish deep South, 1980. A series of brutal murders of adolescent girls in a remote and forgotten town bring together two disparate characters - both detectives in the homicide division - to investigate the cases. With deep divisions in their ideology, detectives Juan and Pedro must put aside their differences if they are to successfully hunt down a killer who for years has terrorized a community in the shadow of a general disregard for women rooted in a misogynistic past.
plot:
Marshland is a Spanish crime drama film that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of corruption. The movie takes place in 1980, during a severe drought in Spain, and follows two detectives, Juan Marichal and José Luis Salinas, as they investigate a series of gruesome murders in the rural town of Marshland.

At its core, Marshland is a film about the corrupting influence of power and the devastating effects it can have on individuals and communities. The movie exposes the rotting underbelly of small-town Spanish society, where the wealthy elite exploit the poor and vulnerable, and the authorities turn a blind eye to their crimes.

The film also explores themes of masculinity, toxic masculinity, and the objectification of women. The characters are often portrayed as brutish and aggressive, with a deep-seated need for control and dominance. This toxic masculinity is reflected in the way the detectives treat the victims and each other, highlighting the darker aspects of male nature.

Furthermore, Marshland touches on the theme of social inequality and the struggles faced by rural communities. The movie portrays a society where the wealthy few live in luxury, while the poor struggle to survive. The drought serves as a metaphor for the economic and environmental crises that ravage the region, leaving many without access to basic necessities.

Throughout the film, the director weaves together these themes, creating a complex and thought-provoking narrative that challenges the viewer to confront the darker aspects of human nature.

title: Heaven Is for Real
tagline: Unlock the mystery
overview: The true story of the 4-year old son of a small-town pastor who, during emergency surgery, slips from consciousness and enters heaven. When he awakes, he recounts his experiences on the other side.
plot:
Heaven Is for Real is a 2014 American Christian drama film directed by Jon Erwin and produced by Kevin Downes, Andrew Erwin, and Scott Brickell. The movie is based on the 2008 memoir of the same name by Todd Burpo, which recounts his son's near-death experience (NDE) at the age of four.

The story begins with the Burpo family - Todd (Greg Kinnear), his wife Sonja (Kelly Reilly), and their four children, including their youngest son Colton (Tyler Perry). The family is living in Colorado when Colton falls into a coma after choking on a piece of food during dinner. During his time in the hospital, Colton claims to have seen Jesus Christ and experienced heaven.

As Colton's condition worsens, his parents are filled with anxiety and fear for their son's life. However, Colton remains calm and peaceful, often talking about what he saw in heaven. He describes a beautiful place with rolling hills, trees, and animals, where he met Jesus and other loved ones who had passed away.

Colton also shares stories of his experiences in heaven, including meeting a man named "Dad" who he believes is his deceased father. The family is skeptical at first, but as Colton's visions become more vivid and detailed, they begin to question the possibility that their son has truly seen heaven.

As Colton's condition improves, the Burpo family becomes increasingly fascinated by his experiences in heaven. They start to investigate the claims he made, including talking to other families who have experienced similar NDEs. The family also begins to experience strange and unexplained events, which they attribute to Colton's connection to heaven.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Colton's condition suddenly deteriorates, and he falls into another coma. This time, the family is faced with the possibility that their son may not survive. However, in a miraculous turn of events, Colton awakens from his coma and begins to recover.

As Colton recovers, the Burpo family reflects on the lessons they learned from his experiences in heaven. They come to realize that their son's NDE was a gift, one that allowed him to see beyond the veil of death and experience the love and presence of God.

The movie ends with the Burpo family returning to their normal lives, but forever changed by Colton's experiences in heaven. The film concludes on a hopeful note, suggesting that even in the darkest moments, there is always the possibility for redemption, forgiveness, and eternal life.

Overall, Heaven Is for Real is a powerful and moving movie that explores themes of faith, hope, and redemption. While some critics have questioned the accuracy of Todd Burpo's story, the film remains a testament to the human spirit's capacity for love, forgiveness, and transcendence.

title: The Cobbler
tagline: Saving the neighborhood one sole at a time.
overview: Max Simkin repairs shoes in the same New York shop that has been in his family for generations. Disenchanted with the grind of daily life, Max stumbles upon a magical heirloom that allows him to step into the lives of his customers and see the world in a new way. Sometimes walking in another man's shoes is the only way one can discover who they really are.
plot:
The Cobbler is a 2014 American magic realism comedy-drama film directed by Tom McCarthy, who co-wrote it with Paul Sado. Adam Sandler stars as a New York cobbler who discovers he can take on the appearance of anyone whose shoes he wears. The supporting cast includes Cliff "Method Man" Smith, Ellen Barkin, Melonie Diaz, Dan Stevens, Steve Buscemi and Dustin Hoffman.

In a 1903 prologue, the cobbler Pinchas Simkin uses a special stitching machine on the shoes of a thug harassing his neighbors. In the present, Pinchas's great-grandson Max Simkin runs the same shop with little enthusiasm, cares for his ailing mother, Sarah, and misses his father, Abraham, who vanished long ago. Jimmy runs the barber shop next door, and activist Carmen Herrera fights developers razing the neighborhood. When local thug Leon Ludlow brings in shoes for resoling and Max's own machine breaks, he uses the old family machine, tries the shoes on and turns into Ludlow. He experiments with other identities, and one evening wears his father's shoes so that his mother can enjoy a happy dinner with her husband once more.

After Sarah dies, Max follows Ludlow while in disguise, watches him extort local businesses, and finds hidden watches and weapons in his apartment. Ludlow catches him there, and Max, still looking like Ludlow, subdues him and ties him up, then poses as him among his henchmen to stop a man's murder. Ludlow later breaks free and attacks Max, who kills him with a stiletto heel during the struggle; the police find no evidence. Jimmy confronts Max and reveals that his father also used the machine before disappearing. With Carmen, Max targets slumlord Elaine Greenawalt, who is threatening an elderly tenant, and exposes her corruption, leading to her arrest. After Max returns the watches to Ludlow's girlfriend, the man he saved has him abducted, but the car is struck and Max wakes in Jimmy's barber shop. Jimmy reveals himself to be Abraham, who faked his death, and shows his son the family's shoe collection and legacy.

The Cobbler premiered in the Special Presentations section of the 2014 Toronto International Film Festival and was released in limited theaters and on demand on March 13, 2015. It earned only about $24,000 in its U.S. opening weekend, making it the weakest box-office performer of Sandler's career, and it grossed $6.5 million overseas against a $10 million budget. Critics panned it, giving it a 10% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a Metacritic score of 23.

title: Saving Santa
tagline: Adventures of a time traveling elf
overview: A lowly stable elf finds that he is the only one who can stop an invasion of the North Pole by using the secret of Santa's Sleigh, a TimeGlobe, to travel back in time to Save Santa - twice.
plot:
Saving Santa is a 2013 British animated Christmas musical comedy created and written by Tony Nottage and directed by Leon Joosen, produced by Nottage, Terry Stone and Nick Simunek. Martin Freeman voices Bernard, a lowly elf who works in Santa's stables, with Tim Curry as the villainous businessman Neville Baddington, Tim Conway as Santa Claus, Pam Ferris and Ashley Tisdale. It was released direct-to-video in November 2013.

At the North Pole, Bernard is a cheerful but clumsy elf whose job is mucking out the reindeer stables. He dreams of doing something more important and longs for the respect of his fellow elves, who regard him as a well-meaning nobody, but his chance to prove himself seems unlikely ever to come. Few people know how Santa manages to deliver presents to every child in the world in a single night; the secret lies in Santa's sleigh, which contains a magical TimeGlobe that allows it to travel through time.

Neville Baddington, a ruthless tycoon who heads a powerful corporation, becomes obsessed with discovering the location of Santa's workshop and the secret behind Santa's deliveries, so that he can exploit them for profit. When he and his private army invade the North Pole and capture Santa, Bernard, who is the only one to have discovered the secret of the sleigh, finds himself the only one able to stop them. Using the TimeGlobe, he travels back in time to warn everyone and prevent the invasion, but his efforts do not go as planned, and he is forced to go back a second time, encountering earlier versions of himself and complicating events further. With the help of his friends and his own ingenuity, Bernard must outwit Baddington, rescue Santa and save Christmas for children everywhere, proving to the other elves that even the humblest worker can be a hero.

Saving Santa received mixed to negative reviews, with a 17 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes based on six reviews. Critics praised the voice cast, particularly Freeman and Curry, but found the animation and story unremarkable compared with major studio holiday films.

title: Hunter x Hunter: The Last Mission
overview: Isaac Netero is the chairman of the Hunter Association. Decades ago he sealed away Jed, a Hunter who had mastered the use of On, the dark "shadow" of Nen. plot:
Hunter × Hunter: The Last Mission is a 2013 Japanese animated feature directed by Keiichiro Kawaguchi and released on December 27, 2013. The second film based on Yoshihiro Togashi's Hunter × Hunter manga, it features the voices of Megumi Han as Gon, Mariya Ise as Killua, Miyuki Sawashiro as Kurapika, Keiji Fujiwara as Leorio and Ichirō Nagai as Isaac Netero.

Decades before the main story, Netero, chairman of the Hunter Association, defeats a formidable enemy named Jed. In the present, hooded figures storm a prison and recruit its inmates. Gon and Killua, on a break from their expeditions, travel to Heaven's Arena with Wing and Biscuit to cheer on their friend Zushi in the Battle Olympia tournament, while Leorio is ambushed on his way to meet them. The intruders seize the tower: Gaki takes the place of Zushi's opponent and defeats him, Shura hijacks the security system, and Rengoku places a curse on Netero that seals his Nen and immobilizes him. Their leader hurls Gon and Killua from the tower, but they survive and fight their way back.

Netero identifies the leader as Jed, his former friend and head of Shadow, the Hunter Association's covert unit, which Netero destroyed after its members began using On, a forbidden power that is the opposite of Nen and is fueled by hatred. The descendants of Shadow, persecuted by the government after the group's fall, revived Jed through their hatred, and he trained them in On. Their aim is to force the Association to reveal the Black Report, a record of the crimes committed against them. As the battle spreads through the building, Gon and Killua defeat Gaki, who dies under the terms of his vow, and Kurapika, present as a bodyguard for his employer Neon, defeats Shura with Leorio's help, but is infected with Jed's blood, which seals his Nen. Hisoka is also present in the tower.

On the roof, Gon is infected too and embraces On to fight Jed, while Killua persuades Rengoku to let go of her hatred, freeing Netero from her curse. Netero chooses to absorb Jed's attacks rather than strike back, and Gon finally purifies the On within Jed with his own Nen, allowing his old enemy to die in peace. With Shadow defeated, the tournament goes ahead.

The film grossed about ¥850 million at the Japanese box office. It had its US premiere at the Japan Film Festival of San Francisco in July 2014, and Viz Media screened an English dub in US theaters in January 2019 before releasing it on home video that March.

title: Get on Up

overview: A chronicle of James Brown's rise from extreme poverty to become one of the most influential musicians in history.
plot:
Get on Up is a biographical musical drama film that tells the story of James Brown, an American singer, songwriter, and musician. The movie explores several themes that are deeply intertwined with the life and legacy of its protagonist.

One of the primary themes of Get on Up is the struggle for identity and self-expression. James Brown's early life was marked by poverty, racism, and personal turmoil, which he channeled into his music as a means of empowerment and rebellion. The film showcases how Brown's unique blend of gospel, blues, and R&B styles helped him to transcend his circumstances and become an iconic figure in American music.

Another significant theme is the power of perseverance and resilience. Despite facing numerous setbacks, including personal struggles with addiction and run-ins with the law, Brown continued to create and perform music that inspired generations of fans. The film highlights how he used his music as a means of healing and redemption, both for himself and others.

The movie also explores the theme of legacy and the impact one person can have on others. Through James Brown's story, Get on Up shows how an individual's influence can extend far beyond their own lifetime, shaping the course of music history and inspiring future generations of artists.

Finally, the film touches on the theme of redemption and personal growth. As James Brown navigates his later years, he grapples with the consequences of his past actions and seeks to make amends through his music and philanthropy. The movie suggests that it's never too late to change and find forgiveness, both for oneself and others.

title: The Best of Me

overview: A pair of former high school sweethearts reunite after many years when they return to visit their small hometown.

The movie begins with Lucy Miller (Scarlett Johansson), a young woman who has been diagnosed with a rare brain tumor that will kill her in six months. Desperate to make the most of the time she has left, Lucy's husband, John (Morgan Freeman), and his partner, Pierre (Pierre Morel), take her to a secret facility in Eastern Europe where scientists are experimenting with the human brain.

The scientists, led by Professor Samuel Norman (Min Skei), have developed a technology that allows people to access 100% of their brain capacity, essentially granting them superhuman abilities. Lucy is chosen for the experiment because she has a rare genetic makeup that makes her brain particularly receptive to the technology.

As Lucy undergoes the procedure, she begins to experience strange and vivid visions, which are revealed to be glimpses into other dimensions and parallel universes. She also starts to develop incredible physical abilities, such as superhuman strength and agility.

However, as Lucy's powers grow, so does her sense of self-awareness and consciousness. She begins to question the nature of reality and her place in the world. The scientists, who had intended for Lucy to be a test subject, are shocked by her rapid evolution and struggle to control her newfound abilities.

As Lucy's transformation accelerates, she becomes increasingly detached from her human form and begins to see the world as a vast, interconnected web of energy and consciousness. She also starts to experience strange visions of other dimensions and timelines, which threaten to overwhelm her.

The movie takes a dramatic turn when Lucy is attacked by a group of mercenaries who are seeking to exploit her powers for their own gain. In a thrilling sequence, Lucy uses her abilities to take down the mercenaries and escape from the facility.

In the end, Lucy's transformation is complete, and she has become a being of pure energy, capable of accessing all levels of human consciousness. The movie ends with Lucy floating in space, surrounded by a swirling vortex of colors and lights, as she contemplates her new existence and the infinite possibilities that lie before her.

Overall, Lucy is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores themes of identity, consciousness, and the nature of reality. Scarlett Johansson delivers a powerful performance as the titular character, bringing depth and nuance to a complex and fascinating story.

However, Abel's success is threatened when he is forced to pay a hefty sum of money to a local crime lord, Danny Nunis (David Dastmalchian), in order to maintain his business.

As the story progresses, it becomes clear that Abel is not just a simple businessman, but also a complex and nuanced individual who is driven by a desire to provide for his family. He is married to Anna (Jessica Chastain), a strong-willed and independent woman who is struggling to balance her own ambitions with her role as a mother.

Abel's situation becomes increasingly precarious when he is forced to deal with the machinations of Danny Nunis, who is determined to take control of Abel's business. Meanwhile, Abel also finds himself drawn into a world of violence and corruption, where he must navigate a complex web of alliances and rivalries in order to protect his family and his business.

As the plot thickens, it becomes clear that Abel is not just fighting for survival, but also for his dignity and self-respect. He is a man who has been forced to confront the harsh realities of the world around him, and he will stop at nothing to protect himself and those he loves.

Throughout the film, Oscar Isaac delivers a powerful performance as Abel Morales, bringing depth and nuance to a complex and multifaceted character. The supporting cast, including Jessica Chastain and David Dastmalchian, also deliver strong performances that add to the overall tension and suspense of the film.

The film's climax is both intense and emotionally resonant, as Abel finds himself facing off against Danny Nunis in a violent confrontation that will determine the fate of his business and his family. In the end, Abel emerges victorious, but not without scars - both physical and emotional.

Overall, A Most Violent Year is a gripping and thought-provoking film that explores themes of identity, community, and the human condition. With its strong performances, tense plot, and nuanced characters, it is a must-see for fans of crime dramas and anyone interested in exploring the complexities of the human experience.

title: The Prince
tagline: Mercy is for the Weak
overview: A family man who turns out to be a retired mob enforcer must travel across the country to find his daughter who has gone missing.
plot:
The Prince is a 2014 American action thriller film directed by Brian A. Miller and starring Jason Patric, Bruce Willis, John Cusack and Rain, with Jessica Lowndes and Gia Mantegna. Filmed in Mobile, Alabama, in and around the Battle House Hotel and the adjoining RSA Battle House Tower, it was given a limited theatrical release and a video-on-demand release by Lionsgate on August 22, 2014.

Paul is a mechanic whose daughter Beth is away at college. During a video chat she seems stressed and distracted but insists she is fine, and they make plans for her visit home after finals. Soon afterwards Paul receives a letter from the college saying that Beth has not paid her tuition, and when he calls her, a stranger answers her phone. Without contacting the police, he travels to her city to find her himself. In her apartment he finds a photograph of Beth with another young woman, Angela, whom he tracks down at a local bar. Angela reluctantly tells him that Beth has dropped out of school and fallen in with drug dealers, and Paul pays her to take him to New Orleans, Beth's last known location, and point out her dealer, Eddie. When one of Eddie's friends attacks him, Paul responds with startling brutality, and Eddie only agrees to talk after his uncle recognizes Paul as the man he once saw kill seven armed men two decades earlier. Eddie reveals that Beth has moved on to harder drugs and is living with a kingpin known as The Pharmacy. Angela insists on staying to help find her friend, and as thugs begin to pursue them, Paul finally explains his past: he was once a hit man for the crime boss Omar, and a botched attempt on Omar's life killed Omar's wife and daughter instead. Omar has never forgiven him, and Paul realizes that his old enemy intends to use Beth to get to him. Turning to an old friend and former partner, Sam, for help, Paul recovers his hidden weapons and prepares for a violent showdown to save his daughter.

The film was panned by critics. On Rotten Tomatoes, none of the 10 critics' reviews are positive, and Metacritic gave it a score of 19 out of 100, indicating "overwhelming dislike". Andrew Barker of Variety wrote that Cusack and Willis "yawn their way through this basic-cable-quality actioner", and the film grossed about $1.3 million internationally against an $18 million budget.

title: Incarnate
tagline: Faith has failed us.
overview: An exorcist comes up against an evil from his past when he uses his skills to enter the mind of a nine year old boy.
plot:
Incarnate is a 2016 American supernatural horror film directed by Brad Peyton and written by Ronnie Christensen, produced by Blumhouse Productions and WWE Studios. Aaron Eckhart stars as Dr. Seth Ember, a man who frees people from demonic possession by entering their minds, with Carice van Houten as Lindsay Sparrow, David Mazouz as her son Cameron, Catalina Sandino Moreno as Camilla Marquez, a Vatican representative, Keir O'Donnell and Emily Jackson as Ember's assistants Oliver and Riley, and Matt Nable as Cameron's father Dan.

Ember, who uses a wheelchair in the waking world, has an unusual way of dealing with possession: rather than performing exorcisms, he enters the subconscious of the possessed and helps them realize that they are dreaming, since demons cannot truly control their hosts but instead lull them into comforting dreams while using their bodies. His assistant Oliver warns him that the demons are adapting to his methods. When Camilla, sent by the Vatican, asks him to help 11-year-old Cameron, Ember refuses at first, until she suggests that the demon inside the boy may be one he knows. A priest confirms his suspicion that it is Maggie, the entity he has hunted for years, and offers him a vial of a possessed man's blood that would give him a few seconds of lucidity, just enough time to take his own life, an offer Ember declines. Ember and his team induce a near-death state that lets him synchronize with Cameron's brain, giving him only minutes before his heart fails. Inside the boy's dream, Ember finds Cameron with his father, and he insists that Dan, who left the family after breaking his son's arm in a drunken rage, be brought in to help, with tragic results. Pressed by Lindsay, Ember reveals that a possessed driver killed his wife and child in a car crash and left him unable to walk, and that he has been pursuing Maggie ever since. As he plunges again into Cameron's mind for a final confrontation, the line between dream and reality begins to blur, and Ember must decide how far he will go to destroy the demon.

Released in the United States on December 2, 2016, by Blumhouse Tilt and High Top Releasing, Incarnate grossed $2.5 million in its opening weekend, finishing ninth. Critics were largely negative: Rotten Tomatoes gives it 18% from 34 reviews, and Metacritic a score of 30.

overview: Alice Kingsleigh returns to Underland and faces a new adventure in saving the Mad Hatter.
plot:
Alice Through the Looking Glass is a 2016 American fantasy adventure film directed by James Bobin and written by Linda Woolverton, based on the 1865 novel "Through the Looking-Glass" by Lewis Carroll. The film serves as a sequel to the 2010 film Alice in Wonderland.

The story begins with Alice (Mia Wasikowska) living a mundane life in London, struggling to cope with the loss of her mother and the pressures of growing up. She is visited by the Red Queen's (Helena Bonham Carter) sister, the White Queen (Anne Hathaway), who informs Alice that she has been chosen to fulfill an ancient prophecy that will determine the fate of Wonderland.

The White Queen explains that the Red Queen's power is waning, and only Alice can restore balance to the kingdom by finding the three magical mirrors. The mirrors hold the secrets of Wonderland's past, present, and future, and their combined power can bring peace to the land.

Alice embarks on a perilous journey through the Looking Glass, facing various obstacles and creatures along the way. She encounters the Cheshire Cat (Barney Williams), who serves as her guide and confidant, and Tarrant Hightopp (Rhys Ifans), a charming but troubled pirate who becomes her ally.

As Alice navigates the fantastical world, she discovers that the Red Queen's power is fueled by the negative emotions of those around her. The more people fear and hate, the stronger the queen's magic becomes. Alice realizes that she must confront her own fears and doubts in order to break the curse and restore balance to Wonderland.

Throughout her journey, Alice encounters a range of characters, including the Mad Hatter (Johnny Depp), who is struggling with his own identity crisis, and the Tweedle brothers (Joseph Gordon-Levitt and Sonya Walger), who serve as comedic relief. She also meets the Queen of Hearts' (Helena Bonham Carter) loyal subjects, the playing cards, who are determined to stop Alice from fulfilling her destiny.

As Alice draws closer to finding the magical mirrors, she faces increasingly formidable challenges. The Red Queen's power grows stronger, and Alice must confront her own darkness in order to overcome the obstacles in her path.

In the end, Alice successfully retrieves the three mirrors and uses their combined power to break the curse that has been cast over Wonderland. The Red Queen's power is restored, but not at the cost of her own humanity. Alice returns home, forever changed by her experiences in Wonderland, with a newfound appreciation for the complexities of life and the importance of facing one's fears.

The film concludes with Alice reflecting on the lessons she learned during her journey, realizing that the true magic lies within herself and that the power to change the world begins with understanding oneself.

plot:
Run All Night is a 2015 American action thriller film directed by Jaume Collet-Serra and starring Liam Neeson, Joel Kinnaman, and Ed Harris.

The movie begins with Leo Kearns (Liam Neeson), a former hitman who has retired to a quiet life in Brooklyn with his wife, Veronica (Geraldine Viswanathan). However, their peaceful existence is disrupted when Leo's estranged son, Danny (Joel Kinnaman), and his pregnant girlfriend, Amanda (Bojana Jelic), arrive at their doorstep. Brock is a ruthless and cunning adversary who will stop at nothing to eliminate anyone who gets in his way. When Danny fails to pay off his debt to Brock, he sets out to collect on the loan by targeting Leo and his family.

Leo, who has been trying to leave his violent past behind him, finds himself drawn back into the world of crime when Danny's life is threatened. As the situation spirals out of control, Leo must use all his skills and experience to protect his son and his wife from Brock's henchmen. Overall, Run All Night is a tense and thrilling action movie that explores themes of family, loyalty, and redemption. While it may not be as original or groundbreaking as some other films in the genre, it delivers plenty of excitement and suspense for fans of Liam Neeson's brand of action heroics.

title: Cooties
tagline: Please don't feed the children.
overview: A mysterious virus hits an isolated elementary school, transforming the kids into a feral swarm of mass savages. An unlikely hero must lead a motley band of teachers in the fight of their lives.
plot:
Cooties is a dark comedy horror film that explores several themes that are both thought-provoking and unsettling. At its core, the movie delves into the idea of societal collapse and the breakdown of social norms in the face of chaos.

The film takes place in an elementary school where a mysterious virus causes children to become violent and aggressive, turning them into "cooties" that spread rapidly among the student body. As the situation spirals out of control, the adults are forced to confront their own vulnerabilities and weaknesses, revealing a deeper unease about their roles as caregivers and authority figures.

One of the primary themes of Cooties is the fear of losing control and the breakdown of social order. The film's portrayal of a school descending into chaos serves as a metaphor for the fragility of modern society, where even the most seemingly stable institutions can be brought to its knees by external forces.

The movie also explores the theme of toxic masculinity, particularly in the character of Duncan, who embodies a brand of aggressive, entitled masculinity that ultimately proves to be his downfall. As the situation escalates, Duncan's behavior becomes increasingly erratic and violent, highlighting the dangers of unchecked male aggression.

Furthermore, Cooties touches on the idea of the "other," particularly in the context of the virus, which serves as a symbol for the unknown and the uncontrollable. The film's portrayal of children as monstrous, zombie-like creatures taps into deep-seated fears about the vulnerability of our most innocent and defenseless members.

Overall, Cooties is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that explores themes of societal collapse, toxic masculinity, and the fear of the unknown, all set against a backdrop of chaos and horror.

title: As the Gods Will
tagline: Oh my God, please return my tedious everyday.
overview: High school student Shun Takahata is bored. Bored with the day-to-day monotony of school and life, he prays for change, for something exciting. Suddenly, he and his classmates are forced to play deadly children's games and facing terrifying creatures from a talking Daruma doll to a sharp-clawed lucky cat.
plot:
As the Gods Will (Japanese: Kami-sama no Iu Tōri) is a 2014 Japanese supernatural horror film directed by Takashi Miike and based on the first story arc of the manga by Muneyuki Kaneshiro and Akeji Fujimura. Sota Fukushi plays Shun Takahata, with Ryūnosuke Kamiki as Takeru Amaya, Hirona Yamazaki as Ichika Akimoto and Mio Yūki as Shoko Takase, and Lily Franky as a homeless man who is God.

Shun, a high school student bored with his ordinary life, is suddenly forced along with his class into a deadly version of the children's game daruma-san ga koronda. A Daruma doll at the front of the classroom kills anyone it sees moving, while a button on its back can end the game. Everyone in the class except Shun dies. Reunited with his childhood friend Ichika, Shun reaches the gym, where students must throw a giant bell into a hoop on the collar of a huge beckoning-cat doll or die. Shun and Ichika devise a trick that works with Amaya's help, but Amaya then kills the students who did not help, saying the unworthy do not deserve to live. As he and Shun fight, the cat knocks everyone out with sleeping gas.

Shun wakes in a giant cube floating over Tokyo with other students, including Takase. In a round of kagome kagome, blindfolded players must guess which of four floating kokeshi dolls stands behind them, and Shun wins by tricking his doll into revealing itself. Reunited with Amaya and Ichika, he faces a giant polar bear that demands truthful answers and has the group vote out suspected liars; Ichika, Takase and Amaya all admit liking Shun, and after deaths including Takase's, Shun realizes the bear itself is lying. In the final game, a hide-and-seek game with a can, hosted by matryoshka dolls, Amaya is the demon and captures every other player, but Shun chains him long enough to kick the can. The dolls declare that everyone survives and hand out ice cream, but the sticks are a lottery, and everyone except Shun and Amaya draws death. Standing atop the cube as crowds chant "God's children", Shun insists there is no god, but the dolls name each game host as a god, "and God", as a man appears behind him and Shun turns to face him.

The film premiered at the Rome Film Festival on October 18, 2014, opened in Japan on November 15 and earned $1.5 million there in its first weekend. Western critics gave mixed reviews, praising its effects but faulting its plot. After the 2021 release of Squid Game, the series was accused of copying the film, which its creator denied.

title: Barefoot
tagline: She's stepping out into the world.
overview: The "black sheep" son of a wealthy family meets a young psychiatric patient who's been raised in isolation her entire life. He takes the naive young woman home for his brother's wedding an improbable romance blooms, as she impresses everyone with her genuine, simple charms.
plot:
Barefoot is a 2014 American romantic comedy film directed by Andrew Fleming and written by Stephen Zotnowski. It is technically a remake of the 2005 German film Barfuss by Til Schweiger, although that film was itself based on Zotnowski's original screenplay. Evan Rachel Wood stars as Daisy Kensington, a young psychiatric patient raised in isolation, and Scott Speedman as Jay Wheeler, the black sheep of a wealthy family, with Treat Williams and Kate Burton as Jay's parents and J. K. Simmons as Dr. Bertleman. The film was produced by WhiteFlame Productions.

Jay, a ne'er-do-well working as a janitor at a Los Angeles psychiatric hospital as part of his probation, intervenes one night when a fellow janitor tries to assault a patient, Daisy, by pretending to be a doctor. Daisy, who was admitted to the hospital after being raised in isolation and has gone barefoot all her life, follows Jay when he leaves. Rather than return her, he takes her with him to his brother's wedding in New Orleans, hoping to convince his family that he has turned his life around, when in reality he needs money to pay off a loan shark. Daisy impresses his family, but she tells Jay that she was hospitalized for killing her mother, and when Jay's suspicious father presses her with questions, she suffers a panic attack. After admitting the truth to his parents, Jay sets out with Daisy in his father's vintage RV. Pursued by the authorities, the pair enjoy an unlikely road trip, outwitting a police officer along the way, and grow closer. When Daisy overhears Jay telling Dr. Bertleman that he will bring her back, she flees and crashes the RV. Jay learns that it was her mother, not Daisy, who heard voices, and that Daisy blames herself for her mother's death. Daisy is returned to the hospital and Jay is arrested. Released on bail, Jay finds his apartment ransacked by the loan shark and realizes that he wants to be with Daisy, devising a desperate plan to get back inside the hospital to see her.

Barefoot premiered at the Santa Barbara International Film Festival on February 2, 2014, and received a limited theatrical release by Roadside Attractions, alongside a video-on-demand release, on February 21, grossing only $15,071 in theaters. Critics gave it negative reviews, with a 19% Rotten Tomatoes rating and a Metacritic score of 22.

title: The Babadook
tagline: If it's in a word, or it's in a look, you can't get rid of the Babadook.
overview: A single mother, plagued by the violent death of her husband, battles with her son's fear of a monster lurking in the house, but soon discovers a sinister presence all around her.
plot:
The Babadook is a psychological horror film written and directed by Jennifer Kent, released in 2014. The movie follows the story of Amelia (Essie Davis), a widowed mother who struggles to cope with the loss of her husband, Tom (Noah Wiseman), in a car accident.

Amelia's son, Samuel (Noah Wiseman), is a shy and introverted six-year-old boy who has difficulty adjusting to his new life without his father. As Amelia tries to navigate her grief and care for her son, she begins to experience strange and terrifying events that suggest the presence of a supernatural entity known as the Babadook.

The Babadook is a monster from children's books that comes to life when read aloud. In this case, it appears in Samuel's room, manifesting as a dark figure with a menacing presence. As the story progresses, Amelia becomes increasingly unhinged and paranoid, convinced that the Babadook is a manifestation of her own guilt and grief.

As the events escalate, Amelia's relationship with Samuel deteriorates, and she begins to question her own sanity. The line between reality and fantasy blurs, and Amelia starts to see the world through the eyes of her son. She becomes obsessed with understanding the Babadook and its connection to their family's tragedy.

The film takes a dark and unexpected turn when Amelia discovers that Samuel has been reading the Babadook book repeatedly, which seems to be fueling the monster's presence. In a shocking twist, it is revealed that Samuel has been using his imagination to cope with his father's absence, and the Babadook represents his own grief and fear.

In the climactic final act, Amelia confronts her own demons and the Babadook, leading to a tragic and devastating conclusion. The film ends with Amelia, now fully embracing her grief, reading the Babadook book to Samuel, who has seemingly accepted the monster as a part of their reality.

Throughout the movie, Jennifer Kent explores themes of grief, trauma, and mental illness, raising questions about the nature of reality and the power of imagination. The Babadook is a masterclass in psychological horror, building tension through its slow-burning atmosphere and unsettling imagery.

The film received widespread critical acclaim for its performances, direction, and original storytelling. Essie Davis's portrayal of Amelia earned her numerous awards and nominations, including the AACTA Award for Best Actress.

title: Rage
tagline: The past never stays dead
overview: When the Russian mob kidnaps the daughter of a reformed criminal, he rounds up his old crew and seeks his own brand of justice.
plot:
Rage, released as Tokarev in most of Europe and Australia, is a 2014 American action crime thriller film directed by Paco Cabezas and written by Jim Agnew and Sean Keller. Nicolas Cage stars as Paul Maguire, a former Irish mobster turned legitimate businessman, with Rachel Nichols as his wife Vanessa, Aubrey Peeples as his daughter Caitlin, Peter Stormare as mob boss Frank O'Connell, Danny Glover as Detective Peter St. John, Max Ryan and Michael McGrady as Paul's old partners Kane and Danny, and Pasha D. Lychnikoff as the Russian boss Chernov.

As young men, Paul and his friends Kane and Danny belonged to a branch of the Irish mob, and one night they ambushed a Russian mobster carrying money to his boss. The robbery set off a bloody war between the Irish and the Russian mob, but the stolen cash allowed Paul to leave crime behind. Years later he has built a legitimate construction business in Mobile, Alabama, married the younger Vanessa and become a devoted father to his teenage daughter Caitlin, while remaining friends with Kane and Danny, who never managed to go straight. One night, while Paul and Vanessa attend a charity dinner, Caitlin is reported abducted from their home by masked men while her friends Evan and Mike were with her. Convinced that the crime is long-delayed revenge for the robbery, Paul ignores the police and turns to his old partners. When Caitlin's body is found in a storm drain, his search becomes a violent rampage against anyone connected to Chernov, the Russian boss whose money they stole, despite warnings from O'Connell that a man allowed to leave the mob should not return to its methods. Vanessa, who first supported him, comes to fear that he is becoming the killer he once was. As the bloodshed escalates, Chernov learns that the man killed in the old robbery was his own brother, Paul's friendships collapse under suspicion, and the discovery of a Tokarev pistol in Paul's closet, a relic of that night, leads him toward a devastating truth about what really happened to his daughter.

Rage received negative reviews from critics. It holds a 13% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus calls it depressingly dull and poorly made, a rare Cage action thriller lacking the energy to reach "so bad it's good" territory, and Metacritic gave it a score of 28 out of 100 based on 17 critics.

title: The Suspect
tagline: All evidences say he did it.
overview: Betrayed and on the run, a former North Korean agent tries to seek revenge on the man who killed his wife, find his missing daughter, and uncover the secrets hidden inside the eyeglasses of a dead man.
plot:
The Suspect (Korean: Yonguija) is a 2013 South Korean action spy film directed by Won Shin-yun and starring Gong Yoo, with Park Hee-soon, Jo Sung-ha, Yoo Da-in and Kim Sung-kyun in supporting roles. Gong was cast after Yoon Kye-sang dropped out of the lead role, and he prepared by dieting for three months, learning the Russian martial art Systema and performing car chases, rock climbing and skydiving over the Han River without stunt doubles. The film was partly shot in Puerto Rico.

Ji Dong-cheol was once one of North Korea's top special forces agents, but after a change in the political leadership he is abandoned by his government in the middle of a mission. Going on the run, he searches for his wife and daughter, who had been sold into slavery in China, only to find them dead. When he learns that a former colleague, Ri Kwang-jo, was behind their deaths, he defects to the South to hunt down the killer. Living incognito in the South, Dong-cheol searches for his enemy by day and works by night as the chauffeur of Chairman Park, a business executive with ties to Pyongyang. One night the chairman is attacked and killed by an assassin, but before he dies he hands Dong-cheol a special pair of glasses. A member of the South Korean intelligence service frames Dong-cheol for the murder, and a massive manhunt is launched, led by Min Se-hoon, an NIS operative who was demoted to drill sergeant after a failed mission in which Dong-cheol spared his life, and by Kim Seok-ho, a corrupt NIS director. With the help of Choi Kyung-hee, a documentary filmmaker making a film about North Korean defectors who comes to sympathize with his past, Dong-cheol must evade his pursuers while trying to recover the top-secret materials his dying employer wanted him to find and settle his score with the man who destroyed his family.

The Suspect opened in South Korea on December 24, 2013, and became a box office hit with 4.1 million admissions; its distribution rights were sold to seven territories. It holds a 75% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 63 out of 100, and the Los Angeles Times praised its "inspired and teeth-grittingly determined" set pieces.
