title: Ouija
tagline: Keep telling yourself it's just a game.
overview: A group of friends must confront their most terrifying fears when they awaken the dark powers of an ancient spirit board.
plot:
Ouija is a supernatural horror film directed by Stiles White and written by Mike Flanagan and Chad Hayes. The movie was released on October 24, 2014, by Universal Pictures.

The story begins with a group of teenagers who are friends since childhood, consisting of Olivia (Shelley Hennig), Andrea (Anika Noni Rose), Nora (Haley Murphy), and Lindsey (Liana Liberato). They have been inseparable since they met in kindergarten, but their friendship has started to fray due to the pressures of high school life.

One day, while exploring an abandoned house on a dare from Olivia's boyfriend, Peter (Benjamin Walker), the group stumbles upon an antique Ouija board. Despite initial reservations, they decide to use it for fun and ask questions about the future. However, their actions inadvertently awaken a malevolent spirit that has been trapped in the board.

As the night wears on, the group starts experiencing strange and terrifying occurrences, which they initially dismiss as mere coincidence or pranks gone wrong. However, when they start receiving ominous messages from an unknown entity, they realize that something is seriously amiss.

The group soon discovers that the Ouija board has become a portal to the spirit world, allowing them to communicate with a malevolent entity known only as "Zoey." Zoey claims to be a victim of a brutal murder and demands that the group help her find peace by solving a series of puzzles and riddles.

As the night descends into chaos, the group realizes that they are trapped in the house with no way out. The lines between reality and fantasy blur, and the group starts to turn on each other as paranoia sets in.

The movie takes a dark and unexpected turn when it is revealed that Peter's family has been hiding a sinister secret: his father, Paul (Doug Jones), was involved in a cult that performed human sacrifices, including Zoey. The group soon discovers that they are trapped in the house with a vengeful spirit who will stop at nothing to claim their souls.

In the climactic final act, the group must work together to outsmart Zoey and escape the house before it's too late. However, as the night wears on, it becomes clear that some of them may not make it out alive.

The movie ends with a haunting twist: Olivia is left alone in the house, but she soon realizes that she has become trapped in her own nightmare. The camera pans out to reveal that Olivia is now standing in front of the Ouija board, ready to continue the ritual and invite more spirits into her world.

Overall, Ouija is a tense and unsettling horror film that explores the dangers of meddling with forces beyond human control. With its creepy atmosphere, well-developed characters, and shocking plot twists, it's no wonder why this movie has become a cult classic among horror fans.

title: Nightcrawler
tagline: The city shines brightest at night
overview: When Lou Bloom, desperate for work, muscles into the world of L.A. crime journalism, he blurs the line between observer and participant to become the star of his own story. Aiding him in his effort is Nina, a TV-news veteran.
plot:
Nightcrawler is a psychological thriller film directed by Dan Gilroy, released in 2014 by Bold Films. The movie follows the story of Lou Bloom (played by Jake Gyllenhaal), a driven and ambitious young man who becomes obsessed with capturing violent and sensational footage for local news stations.

The film begins with Lou, a struggling young man living in Los Angeles, working as a janitor at a mortuary. He is desperate to make ends meet and find purpose in his life. One day, he stumbles upon an opportunity to work as a freelance videographer for a local news station, capturing footage of accidents and crimes. However, Lou soon realizes that the best-paying gigs are those involving violence and tragedy.

As Lou becomes more successful in his new career, he adopts a peculiar and unsettling persona, often dressing in dark attire and adopting a menacing tone to get the best shots. He befriends a local news anchor, Nina Romina (played by Rene Russo), who is initially hesitant about working with him but eventually warms up to his unique perspective.

Lou's obsession with capturing violent footage leads him to take risks that put himself and others in harm's way. He becomes fixated on capturing the most sensational and disturbing content, often at the expense of human life. His actions become increasingly erratic and disturbing, causing concern among those around him.

As Lou's career takes off, he attracts the attention of a rival videographer, Kessler (played by Bill Paxton), who is also vying for the top spot in capturing violent footage. The two engage in a series of escalating pranks and one-upmanship, pushing each other to new extremes.

Meanwhile, Lou's relationships with his colleagues and friends begin to deteriorate as he becomes more consumed by his work. His obsession with violence and sensationalism leads him to sacrifice his own humanity, causing those around him to question his motivations and morals.

The film builds towards a climactic confrontation between Lou and Kessler, which ultimately exposes the darker aspects of their rivalry and the true cost of Lou's ambition. In the end, Lou is forced to confront the consequences of his actions, and the audience is left wondering whether he has finally found redemption or succumbed to his own darkness.

Throughout the film, Dan Gilroy explores themes of capitalism, consumerism, and the commodification of violence. The movie raises questions about the ethics of sensational journalism and the impact it can have on society. Jake Gyllenhaal's performance as Lou Bloom is particularly noteworthy, capturing the complexity and nuance of a character who is both fascinating and repulsive.

Overall, Nightcrawler is a thought-provoking and unsettling film that challenges viewers to confront the darker aspects of human nature.

title: Batman: Assault on Arkham
tagline: Get ready to root for the bad guys.
overview: Batman works desperately to find a bomb planted by the Joker while Amanda Waller sends her newly-formed Suicide Squad to break into Arkham Asylum and recover vital information stolen by the Riddler.
plot:
Batman: Assault on Arkham is an animated thriller that delves into the darker aspects of Bruce Wayne's psyche and his struggle with the blurred lines between heroism and villainy. The film masterfully weaves together a complex narrative that explores the themes of obsession, madness, and the corrupting influence of power.

At its core, the movie is a thought-provoking commentary on the nature of evil and how it can manifest in even the most well-intentioned individuals. The Joker, as a character, serves as a catalyst for Bruce's inner turmoil, forcing him to confront the depths of his own psyche and the darkness that lurks within.

The film also touches upon the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals. Bruce's past experiences, particularly those related to his parents' murder, continue to haunt him, driving his crusade against crime and fueling his obsession with justice. This narrative thread serves as a poignant reminder of the long-term effects of trauma and the ways in which it can shape an individual's worldview.

Furthermore, Batman: Assault on Arkham raises questions about the morality of vigilantism and the fine line between heroism and vigilantism. Bruce's actions, though motivated by a desire to protect others, are often driven by a personal vendetta against those he perceives as evil. This moral ambiguity serves as a thought-provoking commentary on the complexities of justice and the difficult choices that must be made in the pursuit of it.

Overall, Batman: Assault on Arkham is a gripping thriller that explores the darker corners of the human psyche, raising important questions about the nature of evil, trauma, and morality.

title: When Marnie Was There
tagline: Promise we'll remain a secret, forever.
overview: Upon being sent to live with relatives in the countryside due to an illness, an emotionally distant adolescent girl becomes obsessed with an abandoned mansion and infatuated with a girl who lives there - a girl who may or may not be real.
plot:
Anna Sasaki is a 12-year-old girl with low self-esteem living in Sapporo with her foster parents, Yoriko and her husband. One day, Anna suffers an asthma attack at school. At the doctor's recommendation to send Anna to a place where the air is clean, Yoriko decides to have her spend summer break with Yoriko's relatives, Setsu and Kiyomasa Oiwa, who live in a rural seaside town located between Kushiro and Nemuro.

Anna investigates an abandoned mansion across a salt marsh. She recognizes it, but the tide ensnares her and keeps her there until Toichi, an elderly fisherman, finds her. Anna sees a blonde-haired girl in the mansion. On the night of the Tanabata festival, she meets the girl, Marnie. The two agree to keep their meetings secret. Marnie invites Anna to a party at the mansion, where she sees Marnie dancing with a boy named Kazuhiko. Anna sketches Marnie while there.

Anna meets Hisako, an older woman who paints. Hisako comments that Anna's sketches look like Marnie, whom she knew when she was young. A family moves into the mansion. During the move-in, Anna meets a girl named Sayaka, who gives her Marnie's diary that had been hidden in a drawer. Anna tells Marnie she found documents showing her foster parents are paid to care for her. She assumes that they only pretend to love her for the money and says she cannot forgive her biological family for leaving her behind and dying. Marnie shares how her parents are always traveling abroad, and how she is left behind with her cruel nanny. The maids bully her and threaten to lock her in the silo near the mansion. Anna leads Marnie to the silo to confront the latter's fear of it. Marnie conquers her fear, but begins referring to Anna as Kazuhiko. As a storm hits, Anna dreams of Marnie leaving and wakes up to discover her gone.
Sayaka finds the missing pages from Marnie's diary, which include passages about Kazuhiko and the silo. She and her brother find Anna unconscious with a high fever. They bring her back to the Oiwas, where Anna confronts Marnie, intending not to forgive her for leaving her in the silo. Marnie says she is sorry for leaving her and she cannot see Anna anymore. Before they part, Anna tells Marnie that she loves her and forgives her.
When Anna recovers, Hisako reveals Marnie's story: Marnie married Kazuhiko and had a daughter named Emily. Kazuhiko died from a sudden illness and Marnie committed herself to a sanatorium to cope with her loss. With no other family to care for her, Emily was sent to a boarding school. Marnie recovered, but as a preteen, Emily was resentful for her mother abandoning her. In her adulthood, Emily ran away from home to get married and had a daughter herself, but she and her husband were killed in a car accident when their daughter was just a baby. Marnie raised her granddaughter, who was placed in foster care after her death.

title: Step Up All In
tagline: Every Step Has Led To This
overview: All-stars from the previous Step Up installments come together in glittering Las Vegas, battling for a victory that could define their dreams and their careers.
plot:
Step Up All In is a 2014 American dance drama film directed by Jon M. Chu and written by Michael Genet. The movie serves as the fourth installment in the Step Up film series.

The story begins with Emily (Caitlin Stasey), a young dancer who has just moved to Los Angeles to pursue her dreams of becoming a professional dancer. She meets Tyler Gage (Shawn Mendes) and his crew, including Sean (Jordan Fisher), who are part of an underground dance crew called the "Los Angeles Kings." Emily is initially hesitant to join the group but eventually warms up to them.

As Emily becomes more confident in her dancing skills, she begins to form close bonds with Tyler's friends, particularly Sean. However, their budding friendship is put to the test when Tyler and his crew are challenged by a rival dance crew called "The Kings" (led by a ruthless dancer named Victor).

The rivalry between the two crews escalates into an all-out dance battle, with Emily and her new friends determined to prove themselves as the best. Along the way, Emily must navigate her feelings for Sean while also confronting her own self-doubt and fears.

As the competition heats up, Emily's skills are put to the test, and she finds herself facing off against Victor in a thrilling dance showdown. The movie culminates in an epic finale that showcases the talents of the entire cast, with Emily emerging as a rising star in the world of competitive dance.

Throughout the film, the characters face various challenges, including personal struggles, rivalries, and self-doubt. However, through their passion for dance and their determination to succeed, they learn valuable lessons about perseverance, teamwork, and believing in themselves.

The movie features a mix of contemporary and hip-hop dance styles, with impressive choreography that brings the story to life. The cast delivers strong performances, particularly Caitlin Stasey and Jordan Fisher, who bring depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Step Up All In is an inspiring and entertaining film that celebrates the power of dance and the importance of following your dreams. With its engaging storyline, memorable characters, and impressive dance sequences, it's a must-see for fans of the Step Up franchise and dance enthusiasts alike.

title: Poltergeist
tagline: They're here. And they know what scares you.
overview: A family's suburban home is invaded by angry spirits. When the terrifying apparitions escalate their attacks and take the youngest daughter, the family must come together to rescue her.
plot:
Poltergeist is a 2015 American supernatural horror film directed by Gil Kenan, written by David Lindsay-Abaire and produced by Sam Raimi, Rob Tapert and Roy Lee. A remake of the 1982 film of the same name, it is the fourth instalment overall in the Poltergeist franchise. Sam Rockwell and Rosemarie DeWitt star as Eric and Amy Bowen, with Saxon Sharbino, Kyle Catlett and Kennedi Clements as their children, Jared Harris as the television ghost hunter Carrigan Burke and Jane Adams as paranormal researcher Dr. Brooke Powell. Released in 3D after several date changes, the film opened in May 2015.

Facing financial difficulties after Eric loses his job, the Bowen family buys a suburban house that fits their reduced budget. Unknown to them, it was built on the site of an old cemetery whose remains were supposed to have been relocated by the developer. On their first night, they hear strange noises in the walls, and nine-year-old Griffin finds a box of creepy clown dolls left behind in the house. Lights and electronic devices begin switching on and off, and Griffin discovers his six-year-old sister Madison talking to the static on the television, warning that someone is coming.

The next evening, while Eric and Amy are at a dinner party, the paranormal activity intensifies dramatically. Teenage daughter Kendra is grabbed by a corpse's hand emerging from the floor, Griffin is attacked by a clown doll and dragged out of the house by a tree, and Madison vanishes after being drawn through her bedroom closet into another dimension. The desperate parents turn to a team of paranormal researchers led by Dr. Powell, who discover that the house has become a portal for restless spirits. Powell calls in her former partner Carrigan Burke, a reality television host with genuine experience of the supernatural, who explains that the spirits are using Madison to find their way into the light. The family must venture into the spectral realm to bring her back before she is lost forever.

The remake updates the original's story with contemporary technology such as smartphones, tablets and a camera-equipped drone used to explore the spirit world, while preserving key moments from the 1982 film.

Poltergeist received largely negative reviews, with about 29 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and critics considering it inferior to the original, though it was a moderate commercial success, grossing about 95 million dollars worldwide against a budget of 35 million.

title: The Lazarus Effect
tagline: Evil will rise.
overview: Medical researcher Frank, his fiancee Zoe and their team have achieved the impossible: they have found a way to revive the dead. After a successful, but unsanctioned, experiment on a lifeless animal, they are ready to make their work public. However, when their dean learns what they've done, he shuts them down. plot:
The Lazarus Effect is a thought-provoking sci-fi horror film that delves into the complexities of grief, trauma, and the blurred lines between life and death. At its core, the movie explores the theme of loss and the human desire to defy mortality.

The story follows a group of scientists who, after a tragic accident, discover a way to bring people back from the dead. However, as they delve deeper into their research, they begin to realize that their newfound power comes with a terrible cost. The film masterfully weaves together elements of horror, drama, and science fiction to create a narrative that is both unsettling and thought-provoking.

One of the primary themes of The Lazarus Effect is the exploration of grief and its various forms. The characters' experiences with loss serve as a catalyst for their research, but also lead to a deeper understanding of the human psyche's capacity for trauma and emotional pain. As they navigate the consequences of playing God, they are forced to confront the darkness within themselves and the true nature of their relationships.

The film also touches on the theme of identity and what it means to be alive. The Lazarus Effect raises questions about the essence of humanity and whether it can be replicated or recreated. The characters' experiences with the dead raise more questions than answers, leaving the audience to ponder the very definition of life and death.

Furthermore, the movie critiques the notion of scientific progress without moral responsibility. The scientists' pursuit of knowledge and power leads them down a dark path, highlighting the dangers of unchecked ambition and the importance of considering the consequences of one's actions.

Ultimately, The Lazarus Effect is a thought-provoking exploration of the human condition, delving into the complexities of grief, trauma, and the blurred lines between life and death.

title: Boys
tagline: How does it feel to win a race when you know you lost a love?
overview: Two teen track stars discover first love as they train for the biggest relay race of their young lives.
plot:
Boys (Dutch: Jongens) is a 2014 Dutch coming-of-age romantic drama directed by Mischa Kamp. Made for television, it stars Gijs Blom as a teenage athlete who falls in love with a teammate, played by Ko Zandvliet, with Jonas Smulders, Ton Kas and Stijn Taverne in supporting roles.

Fifteen-year-old Sieger lives with his widowed father, Theo, and his older brother, Eddy, who is still struggling with their mother's death and frequently clashes with their father. Sieger and his best friend, Stef, are members of the local athletics club, and together with two other boys, Tom and Marc, they are chosen to represent the club in the relay race at the national championships.

One day, while swimming in a nearby river, Sieger and Marc are left alone and share a kiss. Confused, Sieger insists that he is not gay, and Marc gently agrees. When Stef begins dating a girl named Kim, Sieger feels pressured to pursue her best friend, Jessica, while trying to suppress his feelings for Marc. On a training weekend, Sieger slips out one night and Marc follows him to the beach, where they spend the night together. Back home, afraid of being found out, Sieger ignores Marc at a fair, and when Jessica kisses him, he is left torn and miserable.

Sieger tries to make amends and arranges to go swimming with Marc, but his plans are derailed by a family crisis: Theo discovers that Eddy lost his job long ago and has been spending his days riding motorbikes, and he locks the bike away. Sieger goes after his brother instead of meeting Marc, and when they nearly run Marc over on the road, Sieger, fearful of being seen with him, walks away without an explanation. On the day of the relay, Sieger's bare apology is not enough for Marc, who tells him to go back to his charade, although the team still wins.

At a celebratory dinner, Theo returns Eddy's motorbike, and Stef quietly lets Sieger know that he knows about Marc and approves. When his father asks whether he is all right, Sieger admits that he is not, takes Eddy's motorbike and rides off. The film ends with Sieger and Marc riding together, Marc's arms around him, as Sieger embraces who he is.

Boys premiered on Dutch public television in early 2014 and proved so successful that it received a theatrical release in the Netherlands and was sold abroad. It screened at festivals including Seattle and Frameline, later reached Netflix, and won four awards at the Zlín youth film festival, including a youth acting prize for Blom.

overview: Overeducated and underemployed, 28 year old Megan is in the throes of a quarterlife crisis. Laggies is a 2014 American coming-of-age comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of female identity, relationships, and self-discovery. The movie delves into the theme of midlife crisis, as seen through the character of Megan (played by Keira Knightley), a 28-year-old woman who feels lost and uncertain about her life.

The film also touches on the idea of female friendship and the importance of finding one's tribe. Megan forms an unlikely bond with a 16-year-old girl named Alex (played by Chloë Moretz) and her family, which becomes a source of comfort and support for her. Through their interactions, the movie highlights the significance of these relationships in helping women navigate life's challenges.

Furthermore, Laggies critiques societal expectations placed on women, particularly those related to marriage, motherhood, and career goals. The film presents a nuanced portrayal of women who are struggling to find their place in the world, often feeling pressure to conform to traditional norms.

Ultimately, the movie is a heartwarming exploration of self-discovery, growth, and the power of human connection. It encourages viewers to reevaluate their own expectations and desires, embracing the complexity and uncertainty of life's journey.

title: Into the Grizzly Maze
tagline: Hunt or be hunted.
overview: Two estranged brothers reunite at their childhood home in the Alaskan wild. They set out on a two-day hike and are stalked by an unrelenting grizzly bear.
plot:
Into the Grizzly Maze, originally titled Red Machine and later Endangered and Grizzly, is a 2015 American action horror film directed by David Hackl from a screenplay by Guy Moshe and Jack Reher. It stars James Marsden as Rowan Moore, Thomas Jane as his brother Beckett, Piper Perabo as Beckett's wife Michelle, Scott Glenn and Billy Bob Thornton as the hunter Douglas. The film follows two estranged brothers stalked by a massive, relentless grizzly bear in the Alaskan wilderness.

As boys, Beckett and Rowan Moore had a terrifying encounter with a grizzly bear in a remote area of the Alaskan wilderness known as the Grizzly Maze. Years later, the brothers have grown apart: Beckett has become a local deputy, while Rowan has just been released from prison. Rowan returns home, and an old friend, Mary Cadillac, asks him to look for her missing husband Johnny. Meanwhile, an enormous grizzly begins killing people in the area, beginning with a group of hunters and then two loggers.

Rowan reunites with Beckett, who has married Michelle, a deaf wildlife photographer and conservationist. Rowan says he has come back to visit the Maze and pay his respects to their late father. When the killings are reported, Douglas, a hunter and butcher, warns that the animal is larger and more cunning than any ordinary bear and offers to track it. As Rowan and Michelle go missing in the Maze, Beckett sets out to find them with Rowan's former girlfriend Kaley. The brothers and their companions are soon trapped in the wilderness with the bear, which is hunting them one by one, and they must put aside their old resentments if they are to survive.

The film combines a creature-feature premise with a family drama about brothers reconciling, set against rugged forest landscapes.

The film's original distributor dropped the project, and Vertical Entertainment and Destination Films released it on video on demand on May 19, 2015, followed by a limited theatrical release on June 26, 2015. It received mixed to negative reviews, with 36 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 43.

At its core, the movie explores the theme of toxic masculinity, as embodied by the main character Jerry Palmer (played by Ryan Reynolds), who struggles with his own demons and finds solace in his inner voice. This voice, a wisecracking and manipulative alter ego named Gerald, serves as both a confidant and a catalyst for Jerry's destructive behavior.

The film also touches on the theme of loneliness and isolation, highlighting Jerry's disconnection from society and his inability to form meaningful relationships. Through Jerry's character, the movie critiques societal expectations of masculinity and the pressure to conform to traditional norms.

Furthermore, The Voices examines the concept of mental illness and the stigmatization that often accompanies it. Jerry's struggles with depression and anxiety are portrayed as a result of his own making, rather than a genuine medical condition. This portrayal raises questions about the nature of mental health and whether individuals can be held responsible for their own suffering.

Ultimately, The Voices is a thought-provoking exploration of the human psyche, delving into the darker aspects of human nature and the complexities that make us who we are.

title: The Captive
tagline: When hope is all you have.
overview: Eight years after the disappearance of Cassandra, some disturbing incidents seem to indicate that she's still alive. Police, parents and Cassandra herself, will try to unravel the mystery of her disappearance.
plot:
The Captive is a 2014 Canadian thriller directed by Atom Egoyan from a screenplay he co-wrote with David Fraser. Ryan Reynolds stars as a father whose daughter is abducted, with Mireille Enos as his wife, Scott Speedman and Rosario Dawson as police investigators, Kevin Durand as the kidnapper and Alexia Fast as the grown daughter, alongside Bruce Greenwood. Told out of chronological order across eight winters, it competed for the Palme d'Or at the 2014 Cannes Film Festival and opened in Canada in September 2014.

In Niagara Falls, Ontario, the detective Jeffrey Cornwall joins Nicole Dunlop's unit investigating online child exploitation. Soon afterwards, the contractor Matthew Lane picks up his nine-year-old daughter Cassandra from skating practice and leaves her in his truck for a few minutes while he buys a pie; when he returns, she has vanished. Jeffrey and Nicole doubt his story, and his wife Tina, devastated, turns against him.

Eight years later the couple are estranged, Tina still blaming Matthew, who spends his nights searching for Cassandra on his own, while Jeffrey and Nicole have become a couple. Cassandra is in fact being held by Mika, a member of a child pornography ring who no longer abuses her but uses her to lure younger children online. He torments her parents through hidden cameras, including in the hotel rooms Tina cleans, and Cassandra stays because she fears for them. When Jeffrey spots recent photos of her online and Nicole's work leads to a high-profile string of arrests, the ring decides to target Nicole.

Nicole is drugged and abducted at a dinner held in her honour by Mika's accomplice Vicky. Mika also stages a reunion between Matthew and Cassandra at a remote spot, watching as the girl refuses to leave, before tranquillising Matthew. Later, Matthew overhears Vicky questioning Cassandra's old skating partner, Albert, and follows her to a diner, where he plants his phone on Mika's car, deliberately causes a disturbance so that the staff call the police, and escapes a car chase in which the kidnappers shoot at him.

Tracking the phone, Jeffrey reaches Mika's house. He is shot by Vicky, who is killed by another officer, and he fatally wounds Mika. The Lanes are reunited with their daughter, Nicole is rescued, and Cassandra returns to skate at her old rink. Critics were largely negative, and the film grossed around two million dollars worldwide.

title: The Skeleton Twins
tagline: Family is a cruel joke.
overview: Estranged twins Maggie and Milo coincidentally cheat death on the same day, prompting them to reunite and confront the reasons their lives went so wrong. As the twins' reunion reinvigorates them, they realize the key to fixing their lives may just lie in repairing their relationship.
plot:
The Skeleton Twins is a dark comedy-drama film that explores the complexities of sibling relationships, mental health, and the human condition. At its core, the movie delves into the theme of existential crisis, where the two main characters, Maggie and Milo, are forced to confront their own mortality and the meaninglessness of life.

The film also examines the concept of identity and how it is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and traumas. As the twins navigate their way through a series of misadventures and personal struggles, they are compelled to re-examine their past choices and the decisions that have led them to this point in their lives.

Furthermore, The Skeleton Twins touches on the theme of family dynamics and the ways in which our relationships with others can both heal and harm us. The movie portrays a complex web of emotions, where love, anger, and resentment are intertwined, creating a rich tapestry of human experience.

Ultimately, the film suggests that it's never too late to find redemption, forgiveness, and a sense of purpose, even in the face of adversity and uncertainty. Through its nuanced portrayal of the human condition, The Skeleton Twins offers a thought-provoking exploration of what it means to be alive, and how we can find meaning in our own lives despite the darkness that surrounds us.

title: Whiplash
tagline: The road to greatness can take you to the edge.
overview: Under the direction of a ruthless instructor, a talented young drummer begins to pursue perfection at any cost, even his humanity.
plot:
Whiplash is a 2014 American drama film directed by Damien Chazelle and written by Chazelle. The film stars Miles Teller, J.K. Simmons, and Melissa Leo.

The story revolves around Andrew Neyman (played by Miles Teller), an aspiring jazz drummer who enrolls in a prestigious music conservatory, the Shaffer Conservatory, to study under the demanding instructor Terence Fletcher (played by J.K. Simmons). Fletcher is notorious for his brutal teaching methods, which push his students to their limits.

Initially, Andrew struggles to keep up with Fletcher's intense demands and is humiliated in front of his peers during a performance. However, he becomes determined to prove himself and earn Fletcher's respect. As the semester progresses, Andrew faces numerous challenges, including physical exhaustion, mental strain, and self-doubt.

Fletcher's unorthodox teaching methods involve pushing his students to their breaking points, often using verbal abuse and humiliation to motivate them. He demands absolute perfection from his students, both musically and physically. Andrew is forced to confront his own limitations and weaknesses, as well as the darker aspects of Fletcher's personality.

As the semester reaches its climax, Andrew finds himself at a crossroads. He can either continue to struggle under Fletcher's tutelage or risk everything to prove himself. In a dramatic showdown, Andrew delivers an outstanding performance that earns him Fletcher's respect and admiration.

Throughout the film, Chazelle explores themes of ambition, obsession, and the sacrifices one must make to achieve greatness. The film also delves into the complexities of mentorship and the blurred lines between love and hate. J.K. Simmons' portrayal of Terence Fletcher is particularly noteworthy, as he brings a depth and nuance to the character that makes him both terrifying and fascinating.

The film's climax features an intense drum solo performance by Andrew, which showcases his growth and development as a musician. The final scene, in which Andrew delivers a heartfelt speech about the sacrifices he made for music, serves as a poignant conclusion to the story.

Overall, Whiplash is a gripping and intense drama that explores the darker side of ambition and the pursuit of excellence. With outstanding performances from its cast, particularly J.K. Simmons, the film has become a modern classic in the world of cinema.

title: Suffragette
tagline: Mothers. Daughters. Rebels.
overview: Based on true events about the foot soldiers of the early feminist movement who were forced underground to evade the State.
plot:
Suffragette is a 2015 British historical drama about the struggle for women's suffrage in the United Kingdom, directed by Sarah Gavron and written by Abi Morgan. It stars Carey Mulligan as Maud Watts, a young laundry worker, Helena Bonham Carter as Edith Ellyn, Anne-Marie Duff as Violet Miller, Ben Whishaw as Maud's husband Sonny, Brendan Gleeson as Inspector Steed, Natalie Press as Emily Davison and Meryl Streep as Emmeline Pankhurst. It was the first feature film to be shot inside the Houses of Parliament.

In London in 1912, Maud, 24, has worked in a laundry since childhood. While delivering a package, she is caught up in a suffragette protest that includes her coworker Violet. When Violet is too badly beaten by her husband to testify before a parliamentary committee, Maud speaks in her place about the lives of working women. The government nonetheless refuses to extend the vote, and when Maud joins the protests she is arrested and jailed, where she meets Emily Davison, a close ally of Emmeline Pankhurst.

Her growing involvement costs Maud dearly. Facing hostility from neighbors and coworkers, she attends a secret rally where Pankhurst speaks, and her husband throws her out of their home and keeps their young son George from her. Dismissed from the laundry after her picture is published, she lashes out at the supervisor who had abused her and other girls for years. Inspector Steed tries to recruit her as an informer, but she refuses, and after learning that Sonny has given George up for adoption, she becomes more radical, joining the movement's campaign of bombings and sabotage, enduring prison and force-feeding during a hunger strike, and finally accompanying Emily to the Derby, where the suffragettes seek to draw the attention of the King.

The film focuses on the working-class women of the movement, showing the personal sacrifices behind the fight for political rights.

Suffragette premiered at the Telluride Film Festival in September 2015, opened the BFI London Film Festival on 7 October, and was released in the United Kingdom on 12 October 2015. It grossed 38 million dollars on a 14 million dollar budget and received generally favorable reviews, with 73 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 64.

title: Cloud 9
tagline: Nothing's Impossible.
overview: Set high atop snow-capped mountains in the adrenaline-fueled world of competitive snowboarding, the Disney Channel Original Movie “Cloud 9″ tells the inspiring story of two snowboarders who must overcome self-doubt to learn that achieving their dreams is possible.
plot:
Cloud 9 is a 2014 American sports romance drama television film directed by Paul Hoen and written by Justin Ware, set in the world of competitive snowboarding. Dove Cameron and Luke Benward star, with Mike C. Manning, Kiersey Clemons, Patrick Fabian and Jeffrey Nordling. It premiered on Disney Channel as a Disney Channel Original Movie on January 17, 2014, and was later shown on Disney channels around the world.

In Summit Valley, Colorado, Kayla Morgan is training for the Fire and Ice snowboarding competition with her boyfriend Nick Swift, son of the demanding team coach Sebastian Swift. One night Nick and his friends steal the sled of Will Cloud, a once-famous snowboarder, and persuade Kayla to ride it; when it runs out of control, Nick jumps off and Kayla crashes into the sign of a mountain lodge, wrecking it and the sled. She is thrown off the team and must work at the Cloud family's dog kennel, where Will now works after giving up the sport, until she can pay for a new sled.

Will tells Kayla she was only on the Swift team because her father owns the resort that employs Sebastian, and Nick confirms it before breaking up with her. Determined to compete, Kayla forms her own team from Will's old friends, naming it the Hot Doggers after the kennel, while the Swifts replace her with the star snowboarder Skye Sailor. Will at first refuses to coach her, but agrees after she offers to renovate the kennel, and under his guidance her riding improves rapidly, making Nick jealous.

Kayla asks Will to teach her the Cloud 9, the move he invented whose failure, captured on a viral video, ended his career. When he says she is not ready, she rides down the dangerous Tyson's Peak, unaware that it is being televised, and is buried by an avalanche; Will digs her out. He finally agrees to teach her, and after an argument about whether she still wants Nick back, the two kiss.

When Sebastian invites Kayla back to the Swifts, she accepts, but returns to the Hot Doggers just before the competition. Nick wins the men's title, and Skye's strong run means Kayla needs a near-perfect score. Her father apologises for doubting her, and Nick admits that his father forced him to drop her. Kayla lands the Cloud 9, earning a perfect score and winning the event for the Hot Doggers, as even Sebastian applauds. The Philadelphia Inquirer called it a quintessential Disney Channel movie aimed squarely at tweens.

title: Pawn Sacrifice
tagline: On the board he fought the Cold War. In his mind he fought his madness.
overview: American chess champion Bobby Fischer prepares for a legendary match-up against Russian Boris Spassky.
plot:
In 1972, Bobby Fischer tears apart his hotel room in a paranoid delusional state, believing he is being spied upon by the Soviet KGB.
Two decades earlier, in 1951 Brooklyn, Fischer's mother, a Soviet Jewish immigrant, explains to 8-year-old Bobby that the FBI has her under surveillance because she supports Marxist revolution in the U.S. She coaches Bobby on what to say to the FBI if he is ever approached.
Bobby immerses himself in chess and becomes an expert player. Despite her worries that chess is becoming an obsession, his mother takes him to an adult chess club, where he impresses the resident chess master and is accepted as a student. Bobby enters the world of professional chess championships and soon becomes the youngest grandmaster ever.
Bobby's hatred of distractions leads to frequent tantrums. He enters a team tournament in Varna, Bulgaria, where he realizes Soviet grandmasters are deliberately drawing games with the collusion of the World Chess Federation. Erupting in a rant that this system makes it impossible for a non-Soviet player to win the championship, Bobby quits the tournament and gives up chess.
When Bobby returns to the U.S., lawyer Paul Marshall offers to help him modify the tournament rules, working pro bono to give Fischer a fair chance to win future tournaments. Fischer re-enters professional chess and selects Father William Lombardy, a former World Junior Chess Champion and Roman Catholic priest, as his second. Lombardy struggles to calm Bobby's rock-star behavior and impossible demands.
As his demands are accepted, Bobby overcomes most grandmasters across the world and nears the world championship, becoming a hero to the American public. At the height of the Cold War, Soviet domination of the World Chess Championship is being exploited for propaganda as proof that the communist system is superior to American democracy. U.S. president Richard Nixon and Secretary of State Henry Kissinger closely monitor and encourage Bobby's progress.
During a tournament in Santa Monica, California, Bobby loses to Soviet grandmaster Boris Spassky, the world champion. The next morning, an enraged Bobby approaches and berates Spassky on the beach. Privately, Lombardy tells Marshall that excessive focus on chess strategy has destroyed the sanity of the game's greatest players.
As he pursues the world championship, the pressure drives Bobby into paranoia and delusional psychosis. Meeting with Marshall, Bobby's sister Joan quotes from her brother's letters about how the Communists collude with International Jewry to destroy him. Joan explains that Bobby believes this despite being Jewish himself and pleads with Marshall to arrange for Bobby to receive psychiatric help. Marshall is dismissive, but as Bobby's breakdown escalates, he suggests to Lombardy that Bobby needs therapy and medication, which Lombardy rebuffs.

title: Yves Saint Laurent
tagline: Fashions fade. Style is forever.
overview: A look at the life of French designer Yves Saint Laurent from the beginning of his career in 1958 when he met his lover and business partner, Pierre Berge.

Yves Saint Laurent is a 2014 biographical drama film that explores the life of French fashion designer Yves Saint Laurent and his relationship with his partner, Pierre Berge. The movie delves into the complexities of their partnership, which was marked by both deep love and intense rivalry.

At its core, the film grapples with the theme of identity, particularly in the context of Saint Laurent's own identity as a designer and an individual. His struggles to reconcile his artistic vision with the commercial demands of the fashion industry serve as a backdrop for exploring the tensions between creativity and conformity.

The movie also touches on the theme of love and loss, as Saint Laurent navigates the challenges of maintaining his relationship with Berge while dealing with the pressures of fame and the onset of AIDS. The film's portrayal of their relationship is nuanced and multifaceted, capturing the intensity and passion that defined their partnership.

Furthermore, Yves Saint Laurent examines the theme of legacy and the weight of expectation that comes with being a cultural icon. As Saint Laurent struggles to come to terms with his own mortality, he must also confront the expectations placed upon him by those around him, including his fans, his colleagues, and even himself.

Ultimately, the film presents a complex and multifaceted portrait of Yves Saint Laurent, one that is both deeply personal and universally relatable. Through its exploration of identity, love, loss, legacy, and creativity, Yves Saint Laurent offers a powerful and thought-provoking meditation on the human experience.

title: Christmas Belle
overview: With her California hometown in the rearview mirror, Belle heads north on business to catalog the sale of a large mansion. While the job is a dream, the client, Hunter Lowell, is not. But, as the two spend more time together, his icy demeanor begins to melt. Although their relationship is budding, Belle’s long-time suitor, Tony, arrives, sending mixed signals to Hunter while adding chaos to the holiday season.
plot:
Christmas Belle is a 2013 American romantic drama television film directed by Alex Wright from a screenplay by Joany Kane. Produced by Marquis Productions, it stars Haylie Duff and Nicholas Gonzalez, with Mark Famiglietti, C. Thomas Howell and Sheree J. Wilson in supporting roles. Running about 85 minutes, it premiered on 8 December 2013 and was later broadcast in France as Le Noël de Belle. Its holiday romance loosely echoes the outline of Beauty and the Beast, beginning with its heroine's nickname.

Duff plays Isabella "Belle" Everhart, who leaves her California hometown and heads north on an assignment from her father, Rex (Howell). She is to catalogue the contents of the grand Lowell estate, a mansion set amid vineyards, which its owner, Hunter Lowell (Gonzalez), wants sold before Christmas. Hunter is gruff, preoccupied and openly cold toward her, and only accepts her presence because he is in a hurry to get the job done.

Belle loves the work, especially the mansion's library of rare books, and befriends the housekeeper, Angie (Wilson). Her eagerness to prepare the house for the sale gets her into trouble when she rearranges a room she was told to leave alone, but the incident breaks the ice, and Hunter tries to make amends for his behaviour. As they spend more time together, his icy manner begins to melt and the two grow close. Their budding romance is thrown into confusion when Belle's long-time suitor, Tony (Famiglietti), arrives in town with her father, determined to win her with grand gestures and a few lies that send mixed signals to Hunter and add chaos to the holiday season.

The film drew modest notices typical of the made-for-television Christmas romance. The blog Tranquil Dreams found the story predictable and somewhat disjointed, lacking depth, but praised the chemistry and charm of Duff and Gonzalez and admired the picturesque estate, with its barn and covered bridge, and the homey small-town setting. The same review criticised the heavy-handed direction, including repeated, overly dramatic scenes of a shirtless Hunter's morning runs and an orchestral score that at one point drowned out the dialogue, concluding that the film was average but fairly enjoyable. HallmarkDB described it as largely standard for the genre, lifted slightly by its enemies-to-lovers arc.

title: John Wick
tagline: Don't set him off.
overview: Ex-hitman John Wick comes out of retirement to track down the gangsters that took everything from him.
plot:
John Wick is a 2014 action-thriller film directed by Chad Stahelski and written by Derek Kolstad. The movie follows the story of John Wick, a retired hitman who seeks vengeance against a group of criminals who kill his dog, a gift from his late wife.

The film begins with John Wick (Keanu Reeves), a former hitman who has retired to a quiet life in New York City. He is living with his wife, Helen (Bridget Moynahan), and their dog, Daisy, a Beagle that was a gift from her mother. After Helen's death, John Wick is left alone and struggling to cope with the loss.

However, his peaceful life is disrupted when Iosef Tarasov (Alfie Allen), the son of a powerful crime lord, Vladimir Tarasov (Michael Nyqvist), breaks into John Wick's home and steals his 1969 Mustang. The car holds sentimental value for John Wick, as it was a gift from his late wife.

Iosef, who is arrogant and reckless, kills Daisy in front of John Wick, which sets off a chain reaction of events that puts John Wick on the path to revenge. He seeks out Viggo Tarasov's men, including Marcus (Willem Dafoe) and Tessa (Adrianne Palicki), who are responsible for his dog's death.

As John Wick navigates the underworld of high-stakes assassins, he faces off against a series of deadly opponents, each with their own unique skills and abilities. He also encounters Santino D'Antonio (Riccardo Scamarcio), a ruthless Italian gangster who is working for Viggo Tarasov.

Throughout the film, John Wick's skills as a hitman are put to the test as he takes on his enemies in intense hand-to-hand combat sequences. The action scenes are fast-paced and well-choreographed, showcasing Keanu Reeves' physical abilities.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Viggo Tarasov is using Iosef's actions as a way to provoke John Wick into coming out of retirement. However, John Wick's motivations for revenge are complex, driven by a mix of anger, sadness, and a desire for justice.

The film culminates in an epic showdown between John Wick and Santino D'Antonio at the Continental Hotel, where John Wick seeks refuge from Viggo Tarasov's men. The final confrontation is intense and bloody, with John Wick emerging victorious but scarred by his experiences.

plot:
Pelé: Birth of a Legend is a 2016 biographical sports drama film directed by Mauro Fiore, written by David Seidler, and produced by Imagine Entertainment. The movie tells the story of Pelé, a Brazilian soccer player widely regarded as one of the greatest players of all time.

The film begins with Pelé's childhood in Três Corações, Minas Gerais, Brazil, where he grows up playing soccer with his friends and family. His talent is quickly recognized by local coach José Leite de Oliveira, who encourages him to pursue a career in soccer. Pelé's mother, Dora, supports her son's dreams, while his father, João, struggles to provide for the family.

As Pelé grows older, he joins the Santos FC youth team and begins to make a name for himself on the field. He eventually catches the attention of coach Vicente Feola, who becomes his mentor and helps him develop his skills. Pelé's hard work and dedication pay off when he is selected to play for the Brazilian national team.

The film follows Pelé's rise to fame as he leads Brazil to victory in the 1958 World Cup, becoming a hero to the nation. However, the movie also explores the challenges he faces, including racism and sexism, which threaten to derail his career. Despite these obstacles, Pelé perseveres and continues to excel on the field.

One of the most significant plot points in the film is Pelé's relationship with his wife, Assíria. The two meet while Pelé is playing for Santos FC, and their romance blossoms. However, their love is put to the test when Pelé is offered a chance to play for the New York Cosmos in the United States.

The movie ends with Pelé's retirement from professional soccer and his transition into coaching. He becomes a successful coach, leading Brazil to victory in the 1970 World Cup. The film concludes with Pelé reflecting on his life and legacy, proud of what he has accomplished but also aware of the challenges he faced along the way.

Throughout the film, the cinematography is stunning, capturing the beauty of Brazil's landscapes and the intensity of soccer matches. The performances by the cast, including Vincent Cassel as Pelé, are also noteworthy, bringing depth and nuance to their characters.

Overall, Pelé: Birth of a Legend is an inspiring and uplifting film that celebrates the life and achievements of one of the greatest soccer players of all time.

title: Kill the Messenger
tagline: Can you keep a national secret?
overview: A reporter becomes the target of a vicious smear campaign that drives him to the point of suicide after he exposes the CIA's role in arming Contra rebels in Nicaragua and importing cocaine into California. Based on the true story of journalist Gary Webb.
plot:
Kill the Messenger is a 2014 American biographical crime thriller directed by Michael Cuesta and written by Peter Landesman, based on Nick Schou's book of the same name and on Gary Webb's book Dark Alliance. Jeremy Renner, who also produced the film, stars as the investigative journalist Gary Webb, with a supporting cast that includes Rosemarie DeWitt, Mary Elizabeth Winstead, Oliver Platt, Michael Sheen, Ray Liotta and Andy García. The film depicts Webb's reporting on CIA involvement in cocaine trafficking to fund the Nicaraguan Contras and the campaign that destroyed his career.

In 1996, Webb, a reporter for the San Jose Mercury News, writes an article about abuses of civil asset forfeiture and is contacted by a woman whose boyfriend is facing drug charges. She gives him a secret grand jury transcript revealing that the government's key witness, the Nicaraguan trafficker Danilo Blandón, is a paid informant. Webb follows the trail to the case of the Los Angeles dealer "Freeway" Rick Ross and to a prison in Managua, where Blandón's partner confirms a scheme in which cocaine profits were used to arm the Contras with the knowledge of figures in the United States government.

Despite warnings from officials and sources that the story could put him in danger, Webb publishes his findings as a three-part series titled "Dark Alliance", which causes a national sensation. Embarrassed at having been scooped by a regional paper, major newspapers including the Los Angeles Times, The Washington Post and The New York Times begin investigating his reporting, and their coverage increasingly targets Webb himself, including an affair from his past. His editors lose confidence in him, transfer him to a minor bureau and distance the paper from the series, and Webb, isolated and under pressure, eventually resigns.

The film closes by noting that Webb was found dead in 2004 from two gunshot wounds to the head, a death that was ruled a suicide.

Kill the Messenger was released on October 10, 2014. It grossed about 6.7 million dollars worldwide against a budget of 5 million dollars. Reviews were generally positive, with 77 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes, whose consensus said that its fury over the real story outweighs its factual inaccuracies, and a Metacritic score of 60.

plot:
Tusk is a 2014 Canadian black comedy horror film directed by Kevin Smith and written by Smith and Joseph Keery. The film stars Michael Parks, Justin Long, Haley Joel Osment, and Genesis Rodriguez.

The story begins with Wallace Bryton (Justin Long), a podcaster who hosts a popular show called "The Tusk That Took My Tush" where he interviews guests about their unusual experiences. On his latest episode, Wallace meets Howard Howe (Michael Parks), an eccentric old man who claims to have undergone a transformation into a walrus-like creature after being attacked by a whale.

Wallace is skeptical of the story but agrees to meet with Howard in person. However, when Wallace arrives at Howard's remote cabin, he finds himself in a desperate situation. Howard has indeed transformed into a walrus, and Wallace soon discovers that he too has undergone a similar transformation, turning him into a human-walrus hybrid.

As the days pass, Wallace struggles to cope with his new form, which is both physically and emotionally challenging. He tries to find a way to reverse the transformation but realizes that Howard's cabin is surrounded by a group of ruthless poachers who are hunting walruses for their tusks.

The plot thickens as Wallace forms an unlikely alliance with Howard, who has become increasingly unstable and violent in his human-walrus form. As they navigate the treacherous wilderness together, Wallace begins to question his own identity and humanity.

Throughout the film, Kevin Smith explores themes of identity, masculinity, and the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control. The film's tone is darkly comedic, with a touch of absurdity that adds to its offbeat charm.

As the story unfolds, Wallace and Howard face numerous challenges, including the poachers, treacherous terrain, and their own internal struggles. In the end, Wallace manages to escape from the cabin and find his way back to civilization, but not before confronting the darker aspects of himself and the true nature of his transformation.

The film's climax features a tense showdown between Wallace and Howard, who has become increasingly unhinged in his human-walrus form. The outcome is both shocking and unsettling, leaving the audience with a lasting sense of unease.

Overall, Tusk is a unique and unsettling film that explores themes of identity and humanity through a darkly comedic lens. With its blend of horror, comedy, and drama, it has become a cult classic among fans of offbeat cinema.

Apocalypse's plan involves using four powerful mutants - Mystique (Jennifer Lawrence), Angel (Ben Hardy), Beast (Tye Sheridan), and Warpath (Liev Schreiber) - to gather the ancient technology needed to bring about a new era. The X-Men must stop Apocalypse before it's too late, but they soon realize that their greatest enemy is not just Apocalypse himself, but also his own past.

Throughout the movie, we see flashbacks of Apocalypse's life in ancient Egypt and his rise to power. We also learn more about the relationships between our main characters, particularly Erik Lehnsherr and Professor X, who have a complex and troubled history.

The final battle takes place in Cairo, where the X-Men face off against Apocalypse and his minions. The movie culminates in an epic showdown between the two teams, with the fate of humanity hanging in the balance.

In the end, the X-Men are able to defeat Apocalypse by using their combined powers and working together as a team. However, not before Apocalypse unleashes a devastating attack on the city, leaving many innocent lives lost.

The movie concludes with a sense of hope and renewal for the X-Men, as they vow to continue fighting for peace and understanding between humans and mutants. The ending also sets up the stage for future movies in the franchise, particularly the next installment, X-Men: Dark Phoenix.

Overall, X-Men: Apocalypse is an action-packed and emotionally resonant film that explores themes of power, identity, and the struggle for survival. With its impressive visuals, engaging characters, and epic battles, it's a must-see for fans of the X-Men franchise.

title: Odnoklassniki.ru: The Magic Laptop
overview: An advertising creative in a rut finds his life turned upside down when he discovers his ability to write his wishes into reality.
plot:
Odnoklassniki.ru: The Magic Laptop (Russian: Odnoklassniki.ru: NaCLICKay udachu) is a 2013 Russian fantasy romantic comedy directed by Pavel Khudyakov, a cinematographer and music video director. The title sponsor, the Russian social network Odnoklassniki, appears in the film's name. Pyotr Fyodorov plays the hero, Lyosha, with Kornelia Polyak, the director's wife and a producer of the film, as his love interest and Fyodor Bondarchuk in a caricatured supporting role, alongside Sergey Druzyak and Zhanna Friske, in her last film role; the American rapper Snoop Dogg appears as himself. The screenplay was written by a team of former Comedy Club humorists, including Tair Mamedov and the film received backing from the Russian Cinema Fund.

Lyosha is a talented young advertising creative who has come to conquer Moscow, but nothing is going his way. He has no work, no money for rent and no personal life, his parents nag him, and a project he spent a year on has found no takers. At a casting session at an advertising agency, he makes a poor impression, arriving badly dressed, unsure of himself and carrying a broken laptop. Then things get worse: he is fined for parking, evicted from his flat and left to haul his sofa to a park with a friend, where he dreams of being able to solve every problem with the press of a single button. Luck comes from an unexpected direction when he meets a mysterious figure, Snoop Dogg himself, who gives him a magic laptop. Whatever Lyosha writes as a status on his social network page immediately comes true. He gains money, an expensive car, new clothes, a house and travel, and even becomes the boss of the agency that refused to hire him. The one thing the computer cannot give him is real love, which he must find without search queries, and he learns that everything in life has its price.

The film was released in Russia on 12 December 2013. Russian critics treated it as a light diversion. Yevgeny Ukhov of Film.ru called it a frivolous, disposable comedy with a very obvious, rather adolescent moral that could amuse undemanding viewers, finding the scenes in which Lyosha discovers the laptop's powers the funniest but the selfish hero hard to sympathize with, and singling out Bondarchuk's caricatured character as the liveliest presence. Kinoafisha's editor compared the story to Pushkin's fairy tale of the fisherman and the fish for today's youth, while Kino Mail.ru noted parallels with Bruce Almighty.

title: Annabelle
tagline: Before the Conjuring, there was Annabelle.
overview: A couple begins to experience terrifying supernatural occurrences involving a vintage doll shortly after their home is invaded by satanic cultists.
plot:
Annabelle is a 2014 American supernatural horror film directed by John R. Leonetti and written by Gary Dauberman. The movie is based on the popular Annabelle doll, which originated from The Conjuring universe.

The story begins with a young couple, John and Mia Form (played by Brian Tyler and Alice Eve), who are expecting their first child. They move into a new home in Rhode Island, where they discover an antique shop called "Manny's" run by the eccentric Mr. Mann (played by Joe Bonsall). While browsing through the shop, Mia finds an antique porcelain doll with a distinctive face, which she names Annabelle.

Unbeknownst to Mia, Annabelle has a dark history. The doll was once owned by a young girl named Dolores, who died under mysterious circumstances. The doll's presence is said to be cursed, and many people who have owned it have met with tragic ends.

As soon as Mia brings the doll home, strange things begin to happen. She starts experiencing terrifying nightmares and begins to feel an intense sense of dread whenever she looks at Annabelle. John dismisses her concerns, but soon, he too starts to experience strange occurrences, including finding himself in a trance-like state while watching TV.

As the events escalate, Mia becomes convinced that Annabelle is possessed by a malevolent spirit. She researches the doll's history and discovers that it was once owned by Dolores, who died under mysterious circumstances. The more she learns about Annabelle's past, the more she realizes that the doll is not just a simple antique but a vessel for an evil entity.

As the possession intensifies, Mia becomes increasingly unhinged, and John starts to suspect that something is seriously wrong with his wife. In a desperate attempt to save her, John turns to a local paranormal investigator, Ed Warren (played by Patrick Wilson), who has experience with supernatural entities.

Ed and his wife Lorraine (played by Vera Farmiga) help Mia to understand the true nature of Annabelle's curse. They perform an exorcism ritual to try and rid the doll of its evil presence. However, the ritual goes awry, and Annabelle becomes even more malevolent.

In a thrilling climax, John and Ed engage in a fierce battle with Annabelle, who has become a vessel for a powerful demon. In the end, they manage to trap the entity inside the doll, but not before it unleashes a devastating attack on Mia.

The movie ends with John, still traumatized by the events, deciding to get rid of Annabelle once and for all. He dismembers the doll and buries it in the backyard, hoping that this will finally bring an end to the curse.

Overall, Annabelle is a chilling horror film that explores the theme of demonic possession through the lens of a creepy antique doll. The movie's tense atmosphere and well-developed characters make it a must-watch for fans of the genre.

Overall, The Scribbler is a thought-provoking film that sheds light on the complexities of human psychology and the lasting impact of trauma on individuals.

title: While We're Young
tagline: Life Never Gets Old.
overview: An uptight documentary filmmaker and his wife find their lives loosened up a bit after befriending a free-spirited younger couple.
plot:
Middle-aged couple Josh and Cornelia Srebnick are filmmakers living in a shaky marriage in New York City. Josh has spent the last 10 years struggling on the post-production of his documentary film about leftist intellectual Ira Mandelstam while not letting his producer wife help him with the project.
After finishing a lecture at the college where he teaches, Josh is approached by Jamie and Darby Massey, a young millennial couple who invite him and Cornelia out to dinner. Jamie claims to be a fan of Josh's work and the works of his accomplished documentary filmmaker father-in-law, Leslie Breitbart. Josh is immediately awestruck by Jamie and Darby's non-conservative outlook on life as he and Cornelia begin spending more and more time with them, joining in on their bohemian lifestyle.
An aspiring filmmaker himself, Jamie talks with Josh about their projects, including Josh's own documentary. This inspires Jamie to make a film about connecting with an old high school friend that he found on Facebook. Jamie and Darby invite Josh and Cornelia to an ayahuasca ceremony where a hallucinating Cornelia kisses Jamie while Jamie receives Josh's approval in helping with the production of his film. Cornelia agrees to produce the film. Jamie and Josh find the old friend, Kent Arlington, who is in the hospital after a suicide attempt. Josh and Jamie discover that Kent was involved in a civilian massacre during an Army tour in Afghanistan, creating an even bigger story for Jamie's film.
While pitching his own film, Josh is dismayed when he cannot engage a potential hedge fund investor with the concept of his intellectual documentary. He goes to Leslie for a second opinion. When Leslie's criticisms and suggestions are brought down by Josh, they get into an argument over Josh and Cornelia's inability to have children, as well as Josh calling himself a disappointment to himself.
Josh attends a party for a screening of Jamie's film, which is met far more positively by Leslie and the hedge fund investor. A jealous Josh argues with Cornelia over Jamie's success, and they separate. Josh meets up with Darby, who is sick of Jamie's increasingly self-centered attitude and tells him about Cornelia kissing Jamie. Josh confronts Cornelia the next morning and denounces Jamie.
While teaming up with his editor on cutting his film, Josh comes across footage for Jamie's film, finding evidence that suggests the meeting with Kent was actually staged. Finding him, Kent reveals that he was really friends with Darby, not Jamie, and that he was contacted by Jamie weeks before their shoot. Capturing his confession on camera, Josh goes to Jamie and Darby to confront him, only to discover that a fed-up Darby is moving out and that Jamie is at the tribute celebrating Leslie at Lincoln Center.
Josh confronts Jamie in private at the event, admonishing him for compromising the truth and genuineness of his story for dramatic purposes.

title: The Wedding Ringer
tagline: He's the best man... money can buy.
overview: Doug Harris is a loveable but socially awkward groom-to-be with a problem: he has no best man.  With less than two weeks to go until he marries the girl of his dreams, Doug is referred to Jimmy Callahan, owner and CEO of Best Man, Inc., a company that provides flattering best men for socially challenged guys in need.  What ensues is a hilarious wedding charade as they try to pull off the big con, and an unexpected budding bromance between Doug and his fake best man Jimmy.
plot:
The Wedding Ringer is a 2015 American buddy comedy film directed by Jeremy Garelick in his directorial debut and co-written by Garelick and Jay Lavender. Kevin Hart stars as Jimmy Callahan, who runs a business supplying best men, with Josh Gad as Doug Harris, Kaley Cuoco as his fiancée, Gretchen, Affion Crockett, Olivia Thirlby, Jorge Garcia and Ken Howard. Produced by Adam Fields, Will Packer Productions and Miramax and distributed by Screen Gems, it was released on 16 January 2015.

Doug, a socially awkward but successful tax attorney, is engaged to the beautiful Gretchen Palmer, but with the wedding approaching, he realizes that he has no friends to serve as his best man or groomsmen. He turns to Jimmy, whose company, The Best Man, Inc., provides fake best men for grooms who lack friends of their own, complete with invented histories. Doug needs not only a best man but seven groomsmen to match Gretchen's bridesmaids, a package known as the "Golden Tux" that Jimmy has never attempted. Jimmy agrees to take on the job for $50,000.

Jimmy assumes the identity of "Bic," supposedly a military priest stationed in El Salvador, and assembles a misfit group of groomsmen, among them an escaped convict, a man who can dislocate his shoulder and another who can speak sentences backwards, all given fake identities. At a family brunch, Doug nearly blows his cover, until Jimmy accidentally sets Gretchen's grandmother on fire. To win over Gretchen's skeptical father, Ed, Jimmy and Doug's groomsmen are drawn into a muddy football game against Ed's old college teammates, and Doug's bachelor party turns into a wild night. As the wedding approaches, Doug and Jimmy develop a genuine friendship, while Doug begins to wonder whether Gretchen truly loves him, and Jimmy must decide whether the relationship has become more than just a job.

The Wedding Ringer received generally negative reviews, with critics finding its humor crude and its story predictable, though Hart and Gad's chemistry drew some praise. It was a box-office success, grossing more than $79 million worldwide against a budget of $23 million.

title: Everest
tagline: The Storm Awaits.
overview: Inspired by the incredible events surrounding a treacherous attempt to reach the summit of the world's highest mountain, "Everest" documents the awe-inspiring journey of two different expeditions challenged beyond their limits by one of the fiercest snowstorms ever encountered by mankind. Their mettle tested by the harshest of elements found on the planet, the climbers will face nearly impossible obstacles as a lifelong obsession becomes a breathtaking struggle for survival.
plot:
Everest is a 2015 biographical survival film directed and produced by Baltasar Kormákur from a screenplay by William Nicholson and Simon Beaufoy. It dramatizes the 1996 Mount Everest disaster, in which eight climbers died, following two commercial expeditions: Adventure Consultants, led by Rob Hall, and its rival Mountain Madness, guided by Scott Fischer.

In May 1996 the teams gather at base camp. Hall's clients include the experienced climber Beck Weathers, former mailman Doug Hansen, Yasuko Namba, who is chasing the last of her Seven Summits, and Outside journalist Jon Krakauer, while Helen Wilton runs the camp. Hall has promised his pregnant wife Jan in New Zealand that he will be home for the birth. He persuades Fischer to cooperate to limit crowding. On summit day the climbers lose more than an hour when they find fixed ropes missing on the upper slopes, and Beck, whose vision is failing, is told to wait and turn back if it does not improve. Hall reaches the top on schedule, but on the way down he meets Doug still struggling upward and, against his own 2 p.m. turnaround rule, lets him go on; they summit two hours late. A blizzard then hits. Doug, out of oxygen and hypoxic, wanders off the fixed line and falls to his death, and the ailing Fischer lies down and dies. Lost in the storm, other climbers leave Beck and Yasuko behind to seek help. Guide Andy Harris brings Hall oxygen, but the valve is frozen, and Harris later dies in a hallucinatory state. Stranded and frozen, Hall is put through to Jan, asks her to name their daughter Sarah, and dies. Beck revives, finds Yasuko dead and staggers into camp; his wife Peach arranges a helicopter rescue flown by Nepal Army pilot Madan Khatri Chhetri. Jan later gives birth to Sarah, and closing titles note that Beck lost his hands and nose to frostbite.

Jason Clarke plays Hall and Jake Gyllenhaal plays Fischer, with Josh Brolin as Weathers, John Hawkes as Hansen, Michael Kelly as Krakauer, Robin Wright as Peach, Sam Worthington as guide Guy Cotter and Emily Watson as Helen, alongside Keira Knightley and Martin Henderson. It was shot in Italy, Nepal and Iceland. The film opened the 72nd Venice International Film Festival on 2 September 2015 and was released by Universal, first in IMAX 3D. Critics praised its cinematography more than its storytelling, giving it 73% on Rotten Tomatoes, and Krakauer criticized it as partly fabricated. It grossed $221.3 million on a $55 million budget.

As the earthquake hits, Chief Gaines is in the air, flying over the city to rescue those trapped by the disaster. He manages to save his family, but not before they are separated from each other. Emma and their children are taken to a hospital for treatment, while Chief Gaines sets out on a perilous journey to find them.

The movie's plot development focuses on Chief Gaines' quest to reunite with his family amidst the devastating aftermath of the earthquake. Along the way, he teams up with Dr. Lawrence Hayes (Ioan Gruffudd), a doctor who is also searching for his wife and daughter, and Darryl Kenny (Paul Braunson), a rescue pilot who becomes an ally.

As Chief Gaines navigates through the treacherous terrain, he faces numerous challenges, including treacherous landscapes, collapsing buildings, and treacherous sea conditions. He also encounters various obstacles, such as a group of looters and a corrupt government official who is more concerned with his own interests than helping those in need.

Throughout the movie, Chief Gaines' character undergoes significant development as he confronts his personal demons and learns to put the needs of others before his own. His relationship with his family is also explored, particularly his bond with his daughter, Henry, who becomes a source of motivation for him throughout the ordeal.

The ending of San Andreas is an emotional and intense conclusion to Chief Gaines' journey. After facing numerous challenges and setbacks, he finally reunites with his family, but not before they have both suffered significant physical and emotional trauma. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Chief Gaines reflecting on the importance of family and the need for resilience in the face of adversity.

Overall, San Andreas is an action-packed disaster film that explores themes of family, love, and resilience in the face of catastrophic events. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie was a commercial success and helped establish Dwayne Johnson as a leading action hero.

title: The Swan Princess: A Royal Family Tale

overview: Shortly after the Royal Family adopts a young girl named Alise, she is taken away into the forest. Princess Odette, Derek and their woodland friends, must work together to find a way to bring her home to the castle.
plot:
The Swan Princess: A Royal Family Tale is a 2014 American computer-animated musical fantasy film directed by Richard Rich and produced by Crest Animation Productions and Nest Family Entertainment. The fifth film in The Swan Princess series, it features the voices of Laura Bailey as Princess Odette and Yuri Lowenthal as Prince Derek. It was released directly to DVD and Blu-ray on February 25, 2014, marking the twentieth anniversary of the original film.

Centuries earlier, a malevolent force called the Forbidden Arts came from the underworld seeking to destroy every rival to its magical power. It deceived the scullions, a community of talking flying squirrels, into believing that the Swan Princess must be destroyed. When Odette was born, the Forbidden Arts tried to use the sorcerer Rothbart against her, but he was defeated by Derek. In the present, Odette and Derek are pressed by Derek's mother, Queen Uberta, to start a family, unaware that they are being watched by the scullions under their leader, Mangler. The Forbidden Arts attempts to burn Odette but is repelled by her power, and the fire instead destroys a nearby house, killing the father of a little girl named Alise. Odette, who also lost her father, bonds with the silent, grieving child. They decide to adopt her.

The scullions raid Uberta's castle and kidnap Alise to lure the couple into a trap. Derek is struck by a poisoned dart, but a kindly scullion, whom Odette names Scully, cures him and explains the false legend and the true nature of the Forbidden Arts, which is seeking a magical stone that Scully has protected. Odette convinces the scullions that she means them no harm, and when Mangler fires a dart at her, a young scullion named Jojo is hit instead and saved by Odette. The scullions then discover the true prophecy, proving Odette's goodness. They free Uberta and the others. However, the Forbidden Arts seizes the stone.

Odette and Scully enter the cave of the Forbidden Arts to rescue Alise. Scully defeats Mangler, but Odette cannot break Alise's prison. Speaking for the first time, Alise tells her to destroy the crystal that houses the Forbidden Arts. When Odette is unable to do so, Scully throws himself on the crystal, sacrificing himself to destroy the evil force. Alise is freed and calls Odette "Mommy," and the kingdom celebrates as Princess Alise is presented to her people.

The film was followed in 2016 by The Swan Princess: Princess Tomorrow, Pirate Today.

The film's protagonist, Dr. Robert Laing (played by Tom Hiddleston), is a young doctor who moves into the high-rise building with his wife, Daphne (played by Elisabeth Moss). As he becomes increasingly disillusioned with the class divisions and the decadent lifestyle of the wealthy residents, he begins to question the morality of their actions.

The film also explores themes of power, control, and the corrupting influence of privilege. The high-rise building becomes a symbol of the elite's desire for exclusivity and superiority, while the lower classes are forced to live in squalor and desperation. As tensions rise and violence escalates, the boundaries between the haves and have-nots become increasingly blurred.

Through its exploration of these themes, High-Rise raises important questions about the nature of humanity and the consequences of our actions. The film is a cautionary tale about the dangers of unchecked ambition and the importance of empathy and understanding in breaking down social barriers.

Overall, High-Rise (2015) is a gripping and thought-provoking film that challenges viewers to confront the darker aspects of human nature and the consequences of our choices.

plot:
The Lobster is a 2015 black comedy film written and directed by Yorgos Lanthimos, produced by Haut et Court, and released by A24. The movie stars Colin Farrell, Rachel Weisz, John C. Reilly, and Olivia Colman.

In the not-too-distant future, single people are forced to find a mate within 45 days, or else they will be transformed into an animal of their choice.
