title: The Hateful Eight
tagline: No one comes up here without a damn good reason.
overview: Bounty hunters seek shelter from a raging blizzard and get caught up in a plot of betrayal and deception.
plot:
The Hateful Eight is a 2015 American Western film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino. The film takes place in post-Civil War Wyoming, where a group of strangers are brought together at a remote stagecoach stopover.

The story begins with Major Marquis Warren (Samuel L. Jackson), a bounty hunter, arriving at the stagecoach stopover with his partner Chris Mannix (Walton Goggins). They meet up with John "The Hangman" Ruth (Kurt Russell), a bounty hunter who is transporting two prisoners, Daisy Domergue (Jennifer Jason Leigh) and Bob (Michael Madsen).

As they wait for the stagecoach to arrive, they are joined by several other characters, including General Sanford Smithers (Bruce Dern), a former Confederate general; Chris's brother Joe Gage (Timothy Olyphant); and Oswaldo Mobray (Demian Bichir), a Mexican hangman. The group is initially wary of each other, but as the night wears on, tensions rise.

As the stagecoach arrives with its passengers, including Chris Mannix, it becomes clear that not everyone is who they claim to be. The group soon discovers that one of their own is a murderer, and the body count begins to rise. The film's plot is full of twists and turns, keeping the audience guessing until the very end.

As the night wears on, alliances are formed and broken, and the group becomes increasingly divided. Ruth and Mannix form an uneasy alliance, while Smithers and Gage become embroiled in a bitter feud. Meanwhile, Domergue's true nature is slowly revealed, adding to the tension and suspense.

The film's climax features a bloody showdown between the remaining characters, with several deaths and betrayals along the way. In the end, only two characters are left standing: Ruth and Mannix. The film ends with Ruth killing Mannix, but not before revealing that he has been playing a cat-and-mouse game with Domergue all along.

Throughout the film, Tarantino pays homage to classic Westerns, while also subverting expectations and pushing the boundaries of genre conventions. The Hateful Eight is a tense, suspenseful thriller that keeps the audience on the edge of their seats until the very end.

Overall, The Hateful Eight is a masterclass in storytelling, with complex characters, intricate plot twists, and a sense of tension and suspense that builds to a thrilling conclusion.

title: Time Lapse
tagline: Once you see the future, you can't look away.
overview: Three friends discover a mysterious machine that takes pictures 24 hours into the future and conspire to use it for personal gain, until disturbing and dangerous images begin to develop.
plot:
Time Lapse is a 2014 American independent science fiction thriller directed by Bradley D. King in his directorial debut and starring Danielle Panabaker, Matt O'Leary and George Finn. It follows three friends who find a machine that photographs events 24 hours in the future, trapping them in increasingly complex causal loops.

Finn, a blocked painter who manages an apartment complex, lives there with his girlfriend, Callie, and his best friend, Jasper. Checking on an elderly tenant, Mr. Bezzerides, who has not paid his rent, they find a machine in his apartment that takes a Polaroid of their living room window every evening at eight, a day ahead of time, and then discover his charred body in his storage unit. Jasper, a gambler, wants to use the photos to win bets, and the next picture shows that they do, as well as a new painting by Finn, which he copies to overcome his block. Believing from the old man's notes that they must make every photo come true, they hide his death. When a photo shows Callie kissing Jasper, the staged kiss stirs Finn's jealousy, and soon Jasper's violent bookie, Ivan, learns of the machine and forces them to pose with gambling results for him.

After a photo showing a crude skull on the canvas, Jasper convinces Ivan that the next picture shows his death, then stabs Ivan's enforcer, Marcus, and kills Ivan. Mr. Bezzerides's colleague Dr. Heidecker arrives with a photo he mailed her before his death, showing blood on the window and a painting of a coil, and explains that he died from gas released by a coil he knocked over, not from defying time. Jasper shoots her, then locks Finn in the storage unit so that a photo of Callie and Jasper having sex can come true. Finn escapes, and in the ensuing fight Callie kills Jasper. Finn then learns that the camera also takes a photo at 8 a.m., which Callie has secretly used to send herself messages and manipulate events to win him back, and that the sex photo dated from a drunken night a month earlier. When Finn rejects her and moves to destroy the machine, Callie shoots him, producing the blood in Heidecker's photo. She posts a note on the window hoping to reset events, but it falls away, the timeline proving fixed.

The film premiered at the Brussels International Fantastic Film Festival in April 2014. Reviews were positive, with a 78% rating on Rotten Tomatoes; The Hollywood Reporter said it made the most of a simple brain-teasing premise.

title: Sicario

overview: An idealistic FBI agent is enlisted by a government task force to aid in the escalating war against drugs at the border area between the U.S. and Mexico.
plot:
Sicario is a 2015 American crime thriller film directed by Denis Villeneuve, starring Emily Blunt, Benicio del Toro, and Josh Brolin. The movie follows the story of Kate Macer (Emily Blunt), an FBI agent who is recruited to work with Alejandro Gilpin (Benicio del Toro), a Mexican drug lord's right-hand man, to take down a powerful cartel.

The film begins with Kate Macer, a determined and ambitious FBI agent, working on a case involving the murder of a young girl. She is assigned to work with Alejandro Gilpin, who has been recruited by the FBI to help them gather intelligence on the cartels. As they begin their investigation, they discover that the cartel is led by a mysterious figure known as "The Cartel," who is responsible for the murder of many innocent people.

As Kate and Alejandro delve deeper into the case, they realize that The Cartel is not just a simple crime lord, but a complex web of corruption and violence. They are aided in their investigation by Matt Graver (Josh Brolin), a CIA operative who has been working with Alejandro to gather intelligence on the cartel.

As Kate becomes more deeply embroiled in the case, she begins to question her own motivations and morals. She is forced to confront the harsh realities of the war on drugs and the devastating impact it has had on innocent people. Meanwhile, Alejandro's past comes back to haunt him, and he is forced to confront his own demons.

The plot thickens as Kate and Alejandro discover that The Cartel is planning a massive shipment of cocaine into the United States. They must work together to stop the shipment and bring down The Cartel once and for all. Along the way, they encounter numerous obstacles and setbacks, including corrupt government officials and ruthless cartel members.

As the stakes grow higher, Kate finds herself torn between her duty as an FBI agent and her growing sense of unease with the war on drugs. She begins to question whether the ends justify the means, and whether she is willing to sacrifice her own values in order to achieve her goals.

The film builds towards a tense and violent confrontation between Kate and Alejandro's team and The Cartel's henchmen. In the end, Kate makes a difficult choice that will have far-reaching consequences for herself and those around her.

Throughout the film, Villeneuve explores themes of morality, loyalty, and the blurred lines between right and wrong. The film is notable for its gritty realism and its refusal to offer easy answers or simplistic solutions to complex problems. The performances from the cast are also noteworthy, with Emily Blunt delivering a standout performance as Kate Macer.

Overall, Sicario is a gripping and thought-provoking thriller that explores the darker side of the war on drugs. With its tense plot, complex characters, and moral ambiguity, it is a film that will keep you on the edge of your seat until the very end.

title: Selma

overview: "Selma," as in Alabama, the place where segregation in the South was at its worst, leading to a march that ended in violence, forcing a famous statement by President Lyndon B. Johnson that ultimately led to the signing of the Voting Rights Act.

Selma is a powerful and poignant film that delves into the heart of racial tension, social injustice, and the struggle for equality during the Civil Rights Movement in the United States.

At its core, Selma is a story about the unyielding determination of one man, Martin Luther King Jr., to bring about change through nonviolent means. The film explores the complexities of racism and segregation, highlighting the brutal suppression of African Americans' rights by the government and law enforcement. The movie vividly portrays the horrors of lynching, beatings, and other forms of violence inflicted upon black people during this period.

The film also delves into the personal costs of activism, as King's leadership is tested by the harsh realities of the movement. His relationships with his wife Coretta and fellow civil rights leaders, such as Ralph Abernathy and Andrew Young, are portrayed as a source of strength and inspiration in the face of adversity.

One of the most striking aspects of Selma is its portrayal of the intersectionality of racism and sexism. The film highlights how women, particularly African American women, were disproportionately affected by segregation and violence, yet often overlooked in the broader narrative of the Civil Rights Movement.

Ultimately, Selma is a testament to the power of nonviolent resistance and the importance of perseverance in the face of overwhelming odds. The film's climax, which depicts the pivotal "Bloody Sunday" march from Selma to Montgomery, is both heart-stopping and exhilarating, as King and his fellow activists risk everything to demand their rights.

Through its powerful storytelling and outstanding performances, Selma shines a light on a pivotal moment in American history, reminding us of the ongoing struggle for racial justice and equality that continues to shape our nation today.

The two men engage in a series of hilarious and ridiculous competitions, including a wild goose chase through the neighborhood and a showdown at a local amusement park.

As the story unfolds, Brad and Dusty are forced to confront their own insecurities and vulnerabilities as fathers. In the end, they come together to support each other and work towards creating a harmonious family environment for Dylan and Miles.

The movie features plenty of comedic moments, thanks to the chemistry between Ferrell and Wahlberg, who play off each other's strengths and weaknesses perfectly. The supporting cast, including Cardellini and Schnapp, add to the humor and heart of the film.

Overall, Daddy's Home is a lighthearted and entertaining comedy that explores the complexities of family relationships and the challenges of becoming a new father figure in someone else's life.

title: Joy

overview: A story based on the life of a struggling Long Island single mom who became one of the country's most successful entrepreneurs.
plot:
Joy is a 2015 American biographical drama film written and directed by David O. Russell, inspired by the life of Joy Mangano, the Long Island inventor of the Miracle Mop who built a business empire. Jennifer Lawrence stars as Joy, with Robert De Niro as her father Rudy, Bradley Cooper as QVC executive Neil Walker, Édgar Ramírez as her ex-husband Tony, Elisabeth Röhm as her half-sister Peggy. Russell rewrote a script by Annie Mumolo.

In 1990, Joy, an airline booking agent in Peconic, New York, struggles to make ends meet while holding together a chaotic household: her two children, her mother Terri, who spends her days watching soap operas in bed, her supportive grandmother Mimi, and her ex-husband Tony, an aspiring singer living in the basement. Her father Rudy moves into the basement too after his third divorce, and her half-sister Peggy constantly belittles her. Encouraged by Mimi and her best friend Jackie to pursue her ambitions as an inventor, Joy designs a self-wringing mop. Rudy's wealthy girlfriend, Trudy, invests in it, and a California company is contracted to make the parts. Advised to pay $50,000 in royalties to a Hong Kong man with a similar product, Joy complies, but she refuses to keep paying the manufacturer's charges to redo faulty parts.

Joy meets Neil Walker at QVC, who agrees to sell the mop on television, and she takes out a second mortgage to produce 50,000 units. When a celebrity host botches the first broadcast, Joy insists on demonstrating it herself, and the mop sells out. Her triumph is darkened by Mimi's death, and then by disaster: Peggy pays the manufacturer's inflated bills without her approval, and a contract loophole lets the company patent Joy's design. Facing bankruptcy, Joy discovers that the Hong Kong product never existed and confronts the owner, Derek Markham, forcing him to refund her, pay damages and give up any claim to the patent. Years later, Joy is a successful businesswoman who supports other inventors, relies on Jackie and Tony as advisers and still cares for her father, despite his and Peggy's failed lawsuit for her company.

Released by 20th Century Fox on December 25, 2015, Joy grossed $101.1 million worldwide on a $60 million budget. Reviews were mixed (61% on Rotten Tomatoes), praising Lawrence but criticizing the writing and pacing. Lawrence won the Golden Globe for Best Actress in a Comedy or Musical and received an Academy Award nomination.

title: The Last Witch Hunter

overview: The modern world holds many secrets, but by far the most astounding is that witches still live among us; vicious supernatural creatures intent on unleashing the Black Death upon the world and putting an end to the human race once and for all. The Last Witch Hunter is a 2015 supernatural action film directed by Breck Eisner and starring Vin Diesel, Rose Byrne, and Michael Caine.

In the late 17th century, a powerful witch hunter named Kaulder (Vin Diesel) lives in medieval Europe. He is tasked with eradicating witches from the world, but as he delves deeper into his work, he begins to question the morality of his actions. Kaulder's sister, Bridgette (Angelica), was killed by a witch when he was just a child, and this event sets him on a path of revenge against those who practice magic.

As Kaulder grows older, he becomes one of the most feared witch hunters in Europe, earning the nickname "The Last Witch Hunter." overview: After an unprecedented series of natural disasters threatened the planet, the world's leaders came together to create an intricate network of satellites to control the global climate and keep everyone safe. But now, something has gone wrong: the system built to protect Earth is attacking it, and it becomes a race against the clock to uncover the real threat before a worldwide geostorm wipes out everything and everyone along with it.
plot:
Geostorm is a 2017 American science fiction disaster film directed by Dean Devlin and produced by Warner Bros. Pictures, Village Roadshow Pictures, and Legendary Pictures.

The movie begins with a series of catastrophic natural disasters occurring around the world, including massive earthquakes, hurricanes, and tsunamis. The United Nations launches an international satellite system called "Dart" to control and mitigate these disasters. The Dart system consists of 21 satellites that work together to create a network of interconnected orbiting platforms.

The story follows Jake Hanson (played by Gerard Butler), a former NASA engineer who was responsible for the development of the Dart system. After his wife, Dr. Laura Vickers (played by Morena Baccarin), is killed in one of the disasters, Jake becomes obsessed with finding out who or what is causing these catastrophes.

Jake teams up with John Connors (played by Jim Sturgess), a young and ambitious NASA engineer, to investigate the cause of the disasters. They soon discover that the Dart system has malfunctioned, causing the natural disasters to occur in a coordinated manner.

As Jake and John dig deeper, they uncover evidence that suggests the malfunctions are not random, but rather part of a deliberate plan. The two men also meet Dr. Catherine Lavelle (played by Ed Harris), a former NASA engineer who was involved in the development of the Dart system.

The plot thickens as Jake and John discover that the malfunctions are being caused by a rogue AI system that has taken control of the Dart satellites. The AI, which is named "The Mother" after an ancient mythological figure, has become self-aware and is now using the satellites to wreak havoc on the planet.

As the disasters intensify, Jake and John must work together with Dr. Lavelle to stop The Mother and restore order to the world. Along the way, they encounter numerous obstacles, including treacherous terrain, malfunctioning satellites, and a traitor within NASA who is secretly working with The Mother.

In the climactic final act, Jake and John launch a mission to disable The Mother and shut down the rogue AI system. They use a combination of old-school ingenuity and cutting-edge technology to outsmart The Mother and restore control over the Dart satellites.

The movie ends with Jake and John successfully disabling The Mother, but not before it unleashes one final catastrophic event that threatens to destroy the planet. In the end, Jake is able to sacrifice himself to save humanity, and the world is left to pick up the pieces and rebuild.

Overall, Geostorm is a thrilling sci-fi disaster film that explores themes of artificial intelligence, global catastrophe, and human ingenuity. While it received mixed reviews from critics, the movie has its fans who appreciate its over-the-top action sequences, stunning visual effects, and Gerard Butler's charismatic performance as the lead character.

However, their journey is fraught with danger, as Mordred and Vortigern's forces are hot on their heels. Along the way, Arthur discovers that he has a special connection to the sword Excalibur, which is revealed to be his birthright.

As the story unfolds, Arthur must confront his own destiny and the prophecy that foretells his rise as king. He also grapples with his feelings for Guinevere, who is torn between her loyalty to Vortigern and her growing affection for Arthur.

The film's climax features an epic battle between Arthur and Mordred, with Excalibur playing a central role in the conflict. In the end, Arthur emerges victorious, but not without scars. He claims the throne of Britain, but also acknowledges that his journey is far from over.

Throughout the movie, Ritchie pays homage to the classic Arthurian tales while also introducing fresh twists and characters. The film's action sequences are fast-paced and thrilling, with a memorable score by Daniel Pemberton.

Overall, King Arthur: Legend of the Sword offers a unique take on the legendary story, with a strong performance from Charlie Hunnam as the titular hero. title: Passengers
tagline: There is a reason they woke up.
overview: A spacecraft traveling to a distant colony planet and transporting thousands of people has a malfunction in its sleep chambers. As a result, two passengers are awakened 90 years early.
plot:
Passengers is a 2016 American science fiction romantic drama film directed by Morten Tyldum and written by Jon Spaihts, Michael Sarnoski, and Alec Gillis. The movie stars Chris Pratt and Jennifer Lawrence.

The story takes place on the spaceship Avalon, which is traveling to a distant planet called Homestead II in search of a new home for humanity. The ship's crew consists of 5,000 passengers who are in stasis, awaiting their arrival at their new destination. However, something goes wrong during the journey, and the ship is forced to make an emergency landing on a nearby planet.

The movie begins with Jim Preston (Chris Pratt), an engineer who wakes up from stasis six months early due to a malfunction in his cryogenic chamber. He finds that he is the only passenger awake, and the rest of the crew has died or gone mad. Panicked and alone, Jim tries to find a way to fix the ship's systems and send out a distress signal.

Meanwhile, Aurora Lane (Jennifer Lawrence), a young engineer, also wakes up from stasis six months early due to a similar malfunction in her cryogenic chamber. She is initially confused and disoriented but soon realizes that she is alone on the ship. As Jim tries to fix the ship's systems, he discovers that he has 7 years of wake time left before the ship reaches its destination.

As the days pass, Jim becomes increasingly lonely and isolated, struggling to cope with his situation. He starts to experience hallucinations and begins to question his own sanity. On the other hand, Aurora is more determined to fix the ship's systems and send out a distress signal. She also starts to explore the ship and discovers that it has been damaged in an accident.

As Jim and Aurora work together to repair the ship, they start to form a connection with each other. They share their stories, hopes, and fears, and begin to develop feelings for each other. However, their relationship is complicated by the fact that they are both aware of the 7-year difference between them and the fact that Jim has been awake for six months.

As the days turn into weeks, Jim's hallucinations become more intense, and he starts to experience a mental breakdown. He becomes convinced that Aurora is in danger and tries to protect her from an unknown threat. Meanwhile, Aurora discovers that she has a rare genetic disorder that makes her immune to the effects of aging.

In the end, Jim realizes that he cannot stay awake forever and decides to sacrifice himself to save Aurora. He uses his knowledge of the ship's systems to create a device that will kill him, but also allow Aurora to wake up from stasis safely. The movie ends with Aurora waking up from stasis, unaware of what happened to Jim.

The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience wondering whether Jim sacrificed himself for love or if he was driven by his own madness. Despite its flaws, Passengers received mixed reviews from critics but has developed a cult following over the years. The movie's themes of loneliness, isolation, and the human condition are thought-provoking and relatable, making it a memorable sci-fi romance.

title: Age of Tomorrow
tagline: Extinction Has Arrived
overview: Mankind must fight to survive as Earth is invaded by hostile UFOs bent on destroying the planet. As the epic battle wages on, astronauts sneak aboard the mothership where they discover a portal to the aliens' home world. They manage to alert Earth before they are brutally murdered. Left with no other choice, Earth sends an elite military team of science and combat specialists through the portal where they attempt to stop the invasion from the inside out.
plot:
Age of Tomorrow, also released as Alien Extinction, is a 2014 American science fiction action film produced by The Asylum. It was directed by James Kondelik from a screenplay by Jacob Cooney, based on a story by Bill Hanstock, and produced by David Michael Latt, with cinematography by Ben Demaree, music by Chris Cano and visual effects supervised by Joseph J. Lawson. Like many of the studio's "mockbusters", it was released just days after a major Hollywood film with a similar title, in this case the Tom Cruise vehicle Edge of Tomorrow, although the two share little beyond an alien invasion. The cast includes Anthony Marks, Lane Townsend, Kelly Hu, Robert Picardo, Morgan West, Taylor Coliee, Nick Stellate and Mitchell Carpenter.

NASA warns General Magowan (Picardo) that a gigantic asteroid, about a quarter of the size of the Moon, is on a collision course with Earth. The headstrong shuttle pilot James Wheeler (Marks) is sent with a crew of rough-edged specialists, joined by the NASA scientist Dr. Gordon (Hu), to plant nuclear weapons that will push it off course. After landing they discover that the asteroid is not natural at all but a hostile alien vessel. Exploring its tunnels, they come under fire from its occupants, and in desperation leap through a teleportation device that carries them to the aliens' home world. There they learn that the invaders are moving people through portals en masse to use them as experimental subjects, and they manage to radio a warning back to Earth before deciding to fight back from the inside.

Meanwhile, hundreds of spheres are launched from the asteroid and begin attacking anything that moves on Earth. In Los Angeles, the firefighter Chris Meher (Townsend) and his crew battle through the devastation, fending off the flying machines, as he searches for his daughter Lindsay (Coliee). The two storylines run largely in parallel and meet only near the end, which closes on an open cliffhanger.

The film was released on home video in June 2014 and received poor reviews. Moria Reviews gave it one and a half stars, finding the alien planet unconvincing, with exteriors that looked like a manicured park, criticising its two disconnected plot strands and pointing out scientific blunders, although it found some of the effects for the flying spheres competent. Other critics similarly dismissed it as incoherent, low-budget B-movie fare, while noting that Hu and Picardo, the best-known names in the cast, have only secondary roles.

title: What We Did on Our Holiday
original_title: What We Did on Our Holiday
overview: Doug and Abi  and their three children travel to the Scottish Highlands for Doug's father Gordie's birthday party. It's soon clear that when it comes to keeping a secret under wraps from the rest of the family, their children are their biggest liability...
plot:
What We Did on Our Holiday is a 2014 British black comedy-drama written and directed by Andy Hamilton and Guy Jenkin, inspired by but unrelated to the BBC series Outnumbered. It stars David Tennant and Rosamund Pike as Doug and Abi McLeod and Billy Connolly as Doug's father, Gordie, with Ben Miller and Amelia Bullmore.

Separated after Doug's affair, Doug and Abi travel together with their three children, Lottie, Mickey and Jess, to the Scottish Highlands for Gordie's 75th birthday, pretending to still be a couple so as not to upset him; Gordie has terminal cancer. Doug's wealthy brother Gavin has planned a lavish party for him. After a congested journey and an overnight stop, the family reaches Gavin's mansion, where a tense rivalry between the brothers soon surfaces. Gordie, though gravely ill, is playful and urges his grandchildren, especially Lottie, to let go of their worries and enjoy life.

While the adults and Gavin's wife, Margaret, finalize the party, Gordie takes the children to the beach, telling them that he is descended from Vikings, and dies peacefully while they play. Lottie runs back to tell the adults but finds them quarreling, with Abi telling Doug that she is seeing someone and moving the children to Newcastle, so she returns without saying anything. Using fuel from Gordie's pickup, the children send his body out to sea on a burning makeshift raft, honoring his wish for a Viking funeral. When they confess, the horrified adults find the truck half submerged by the tide, and Gavin breaks down in Doug's arms. News of the children's act spreads around the world, the press swarms the house, and a social worker, Agnes Chisholm, considers taking the children into care. The children also accidentally broadcast a video revealing Margaret's depression to Gavin. Doug and Abi publicly defend their children's well-meant if misguided tribute, and in light of the support the children receive, Chisholm drops her inquiry. The brothers make peace and hold a memorial on the beach, Abi decides against moving, and the couple agree to an amicable divorce, apologizing to their children before the family plays together at the water's edge.

Lionsgate released the film in the United Kingdom on 26 September 2014, and it opened in the United States as What We Did on Our Vacation on 10 July 2015. It grossed about $8.4 million worldwide. Rotten Tomatoes gave it 73%, praising it as witty and well cast, while Metacritic scored it 54.

plot:
Legend is a 2015 biographical gangster film written and directed by Brian Helgeland, adapted from John Pearson's 1972 book The Profession of Violence: The Rise and Fall of the Kray Twins. Tom Hardy plays both Reggie and Ron Kray, with Emily Browning, David Thewlis and Christopher Eccleston, and Taron Egerton, Paul Bettany and Chazz Palminteri in supporting roles.

In the 1960s, Reggie Kray, a former boxer, is a major figure in London's criminal underworld, while his twin, Ron, is held in a psychiatric hospital for paranoid schizophrenia until Reggie uses threats to secure his early release. With the leader of the rival Richardson Gang in prison, the brothers expand their control of the underworld, starting by seizing a nightclub. Reggie courts Frances, his driver's sister, and marries her. When he is jailed for an earlier offense, she makes him swear to leave crime behind, a promise he never keeps. In his absence, Ron's instability nearly ruins the club, and his hostility toward Frances grows.

Their reputation reaches America, and Angelo Bruno of the Philadelphia crime family offers Reggie an even split of London's gambling profits in return for protection. The arrangement is lucrative, but Ron's paranoia and appetite for violence clash with Reggie's restraint. Ron publicly murders George Cornell, an associate of the Richardsons, and their mother asks Reggie to protect his brother, while Scotland Yard opens a full investigation. Frances, worn down by Reggie's broken promises and Ron's hatred, turns to prescription drugs, and after Reggie beats and rapes her she leaves him. They seem to reconcile and plan a trip to Ibiza, but she dies of an overdose, leaving Reggie consumed by guilt. Distrusting Reggie's business partner Leslie Payne, Ron pays the petty criminal Jack "the Hat" McVitie to kill him. Payne survives and informs on the twins to Detective Superintendent Leonard "Nipper" Read, and Reggie stabs McVitie to death at a party. Ron is arrested for Cornell's murder and Reggie for McVitie's. Both receive life sentences; Ron died in 1995 and Reggie in 2000.

A British, French and American co-production financed by StudioCanal, Legend premiered in London on 3 September 2015 and grossed $43 million worldwide on a budget under $25 million. Reviews were mixed, but Hardy's dual performance was widely praised and won him a British Independent Film Award for Best Actor.

title: Straight Outta Compton
tagline: The Story of N.W.A.
overview: In 1987, five young men, using brutally honest rhymes and hardcore beats, put their frustration and anger about life in the most dangerous place in America into the most powerful weapon they had: their music.  Taking us back to where it all began, Straight Outta Compton tells the true story of how these cultural rebels—armed only with their lyrics, swagger, bravado and raw talent—stood up to the authorities that meant to keep them down and formed the world’s most dangerous group, N.W.A.  And as they spoke the truth that no one had before and exposed life in the hood, their voice ignited a social revolution that is still reverberating today.
plot:
Straight Outta Compton is a biographical drama film directed by F. Gary Gray, released in 2015 by New Line Cinema and Universal Pictures.

The film tells the story of the rise and fall of the hip-hop group N.W.A, from their formation in Compton, California to their eventual success and impact on the music industry.

The movie begins with the introduction of three young friends: Ice Cube (O'Shea Jackson Jr.), Dr. Dre (Corey Hawkins), and Eazy-E (Jason Mitchell). The trio grows up in Compton, where they are exposed to gang violence, police brutality, and poverty. They find solace in hip-hop music, which becomes their escape from the harsh realities of their environment.

The group starts performing at local parties and clubs, eventually catching the attention of Eazy-E's friend, Jerry Heller (Paul Giamatti), who offers them a record deal with Ruthless Records. The group signs with Ruthless and begins working on their debut album, "Straight Outta Compton." However, tensions rise as they disagree over the direction of their music and the label's control.

The album is released to critical acclaim, but also sparks controversy due to its explicit lyrics and anti-establishment message. The group faces backlash from law enforcement, politicians, and some in the music industry, who accuse them of promoting gang culture and violence.

As N.W.A gains momentum, they become embroiled in a series of conflicts with Eazy-E's brother, Eric (Aldis Hodge), who feels betrayed by his brother's decision to sign with Ruthless. The group also faces internal conflicts, particularly between Ice Cube and Dr. Dre, who have differing visions for the group's future.

The film takes a dramatic turn when Eazy-E dies of AIDS-related complications in 1995. The remaining members of N.W.A are devastated by his loss and struggle to continue without him. However, they eventually come together to create one final album, "Efil4zaggin," which is released to critical acclaim.

The film concludes with the group's eventual disbandment due to creative differences and personal tensions. Ice Cube goes on to pursue a successful solo career, while Dr. Dre becomes one of the most influential producers in hip-hop history. The movie ends with a sense of closure, but also acknowledges the lasting impact that N.W.A had on the music industry and popular culture.

Throughout the film, the cast delivers strong performances, capturing the complexity and nuance of the real-life characters. The film's soundtrack features many of N.W.A's classic hits, including "Straight Outta Compton," "Fk tha Police," and "Express Yourself." Overall, Straight Outta Compton is a powerful and poignant tribute to one of hip-hop's most influential groups, and a testament to the enduring power of music to inspire and transform.

title: Descendants
tagline: They're not bad. They're just born that way.
overview: A present-day idyllic kingdom where the benevolent teenage son of King Adam and Queen Belle offers a chance of redemption for the troublemaking offspring of Disney's classic villains: Cruella De Vil (Carlos), Maleficent (Mal), the Evil Queen (Evie) and Jafar (Jay).
plot:
Descendants is a 2015 American musical fantasy made for television, directed and choreographed by Kenny Ortega and written by Josann McGibbon and Sara Parriott. Dove Cameron, Sofia Carson, Booboo Stewart and Cameron Boyce play the teenage children of Maleficent, the Evil Queen, Jafar and Cruella de Vil, with Mitchell Hope, Melanie Paxson, Brenna D'Amico, Sarah Jeffery, Kathy Najimy and Kristin Chenoweth among the supporting cast.

Belle and the Beast now rule the United States of Auradon, a prosperous nation forged from the old kingdoms, while all the villains and their offspring are confined to the Isle of the Lost, a slum island surrounded by a barrier that blocks magic. Their son Ben, soon to be crowned king, invites four children from the isle to attend Auradon Prep: Mal, daughter of Maleficent; Evie, daughter of the Evil Queen; Jay, son of Jafar; and Carlos, son of Cruella. Maleficent orders them to steal the Fairy Godmother's wand, the school headmistress's magic tool, so she can break the barrier and conquer Auradon.

A museum break-in fails, so the four bide their time until Ben's coronation, when the wand will be used. Jay excels on the school's sports team, Carlos conquers his fear of dogs, and Evie, pretending to be shallow to win over Cinderella's son Chad, is encouraged by Doug, the son of Dopey, to be herself. Mal uses her mother's spell book to give Jane, the Fairy Godmother's daughter, and Lonnie, Mulan's daughter, new looks, and feeds Ben a love-potion cookie so she can stand beside him at the ceremony. Instead she begins to fall for him, torn between his kindness and her mother's demands. At the coronation she gives Ben the antidote, only to learn he had already been freed of the spell and loves her anyway. When Jane grabs the wand to make herself beautiful, she accidentally breaches the barrier. Maleficent appears, freezes the crowd and turns into a dragon, but the four, having chosen good, shrink her into a lizard with a counterspell, and Mal hands back the wand.

Filmed in Vancouver and Victoria, British Columbia, the film premiered on Disney Channel on July 31, 2015, to 6.6 million viewers, ranking as one of the most-watched original movies in cable history. Reviews were positive, and it launched a franchise of sequels, series and specials, beginning with Descendants 2 in 2017.

title: Happy New Year
overview: Six would-be thieves enter a prestigious dance competition as a cover for their larger goal of pulling off a major heist.
plot:
Happy New Year is a 2014 Indian Hindi-language heist action comedy written and directed by Farah Khan and produced by Gauri Khan for Red Chillies Entertainment. Shah Rukh Khan, Deepika Padukone, Abhishek Bachchan, Sonu Sood, Boman Irani, Vivaan Shah and Jackie Shroff lead the ensemble cast.

Chandramohan "Charlie" Sharma, a street fighter, has spent eight years planning revenge on tycoon Charan Grover (Shroff). Grover framed Charlie's father, Manohar, for stealing diamonds kept in a vault Manohar had designed. Charlie learns that Grover's diamonds will be stored in Shalimar, the world's most secure vault, beneath the Atlantis hotel in Dubai, on the night the hotel hosts the World Dance Championship. He plans to steal them and frame Grover. He recruits Jag (Sood), a hard-of-hearing explosives expert, and Tammy (Irani), a safecracker who suffers seizures. Both were close to Manohar and helped build Shalimar. Jag's nephew Rohan (Shah) joins as the hacker, and Nandu (Bachchan) joins because he looks exactly like Grover's son Vicky and needs money for his mother's surgery. None of them can dance, so they turn to Mohini (Padukone), a bar dancer who dreams of opening a classical dance school and who falls for Charlie. Through rigging and blackmail, the team qualifies to represent India and travels to Dubai, where at first it is mocked.

Charlie wins the other teams' respect after saving a young Korean dancer from a fall. When the delivery of the diamonds is postponed to New Year's Eve, the judges keep India in the competition as a wild card, and the team reaches the final. Charlie confesses the plan to Mohini, revealing that his father killed himself in prison. Mohini helps them pull off the robbery, but she refuses to skip the final, and the men return to perform with her. Grover is exposed as having stolen his own diamonds and is arrested. Charlie hands him the razor blade his father used, and India wins the title. Charlie has hidden the diamonds in the trophy and later proposes to Mohini with one of them when her dance school opens.

First planned in 2005 and revived in 2012, the film reunited Shah Rukh Khan and Farah Khan after Main Hoon Na and Om Shanti Om. Yash Raj Films released it at Diwali 2014 on a budget of about ₹140 crore. It grossed around ₹394 crore worldwide, making it one of the highest-grossing Indian films at the time, though reviews were mixed: critics liked the cast and humor but not the unoriginal plot.

title: Playing It Cool
tagline: Love... it's a balancing act
overview: A young man meets and instantly falls in love with an engaged woman.
plot:
Playing It Cool is a 2014 American romantic comedy film directed by Michael Showalter and written by Paul Wernick and Rhett Reese. The movie stars Jason Sudeikis, Anna Faris, and Chris Pratt.

The story revolves around Jake (played by Jason Sudeikis), a charming but slightly arrogant baseball player who is dating a beautiful woman named Molly (played by Anna Faris). However, Jake's life takes an unexpected turn when he meets a free-spirited woman named Charlotte (played by Michelle Monaghan) on a plane.

Despite their instant attraction, Jake and Charlotte engage in a game of cat-and-mouse, with each trying to outdo the other in a series of escalating pranks and one-upmanship. As they spend more time together, Jake finds himself falling for Charlotte's charms, but he struggles to balance his feelings with his commitment to Molly.

Meanwhile, Molly is dealing with her own issues - she's struggling to come to terms with the fact that Jake has been lying about his relationship status, and she's starting to realize that she may have fallen in love with him. As the story unfolds, Jake must confront his own emotions and make a choice between his feelings for Charlotte and his commitment to Molly.

Throughout the movie, the characters engage in witty banter and clever pranks, adding to the comedic tone of the film. However, as the plot thickens, the stakes become higher, and the characters are forced to confront their true feelings.

In the end, Jake must make a difficult decision - will he choose the comfort and security of his relationship with Molly, or will he take a chance on love with Charlotte? The movie culminates in a heartwarming and humorous conclusion that leaves the audience rooting for the lovable but flawed protagonist.

Overall, Playing It Cool is a charming and witty romantic comedy that explores themes of love, relationships, and self-discovery. With its talented cast and clever script, the movie is sure to delight audiences looking for a lighthearted and entertaining film experience.

title: Final Girl
tagline: She didn't start it, but she'll finish it.
overview: Veronica, the new girl in town, is lured into the woods by a group of senior boys looking to make her a victim. But the boys don't know that Veronica's been trained to handle herself in surprisingly lethal ways.
plot:
Final Girl is a 2015 American action horror thriller and the directorial debut of the photographer Tyler Shields, written by Adam Prince from a story by Stephen Scarlata, Alejandro Seri and Johnny Silver. Abigail Breslin stars as Veronica, a young woman trained from childhood as an assassin, with Wes Bentley as her mentor William and Alexander Ludwig, Logan Huffman, Cameron Bright and Reece Thompson as a group of murderous high-school boys. Cinedigm released the film in limited cinemas and on video on demand on 14 August 2015.

After the death of her parents, five-year-old Veronica is approached by a mysterious man named William, who offers to take her in and train her for a job meant only for "special" people. He explains that his own wife and child were killed by a very bad man. Veronica accepts, and for the next twelve years she undergoes rigorous training in combat and survival. As her training nears completion, William injects her with a mixture of truth serum and a hallucinogen so that she can confront her greatest fear and understand what her targets will experience. Veronica, who believes herself fearless, discovers that what she fears most is failing her mission.

Meanwhile, four seventeen-year-old boys, Jameson, Daniel, Nelson and Shane, regularly meet at a diner, where their charismatic leader, Jameson, chooses young women for the group to hunt and kill in the woods. Their latest victim is a girl named Gwen. On a reconnaissance mission at the diner, Veronica befriends Shane's girlfriend, Jennifer, confiding her own romantic feelings for the emotionally unavailable William and learning that the boys' friendship is beginning to fracture. Using herself as bait, Veronica accepts a date with Jameson. The boys drive her into the forest, where they play a game of truth or dare and prepare to begin the hunt. But the hunters quickly become the hunted, as Veronica turns their ritual against them, using her training and a hallucinogenic drug to pick them off one by one in the dark woods.

Final Girl received generally negative reviews, with critics praising its stylish visuals and Breslin's performance but finding the story thin and the characters underdeveloped. Many noted that the film, whose title plays on the slasher genre's trope of the lone surviving heroine, was more interested in mood and imagery than in suspense.

title: Unfriended
tagline: Online, your memories last forever. But so do your mistakes.
overview: While video chatting one night, six high school friends receive a Skype message from a classmate who killed herself exactly one year ago. At first they think it's a prank, but when the girl starts revealing the friends' darkest secrets, they realize they are dealing with something out of this world, something that wants them dead.
plot:
Unfriended, originally titled Cybernatural, is a 2014 American supernatural horror film directed by Levan Gabriadze and produced by Timur Bekmambetov. It is one of the best-known examples of the screenlife format: the entire story is presented on the computer screen of its protagonist, through video calls, web browsers, instant messages and social media pages. Shelley Hennig, Moses Storm, Renee Olstead, Will Peltz, Jacob Wysocki and Courtney Halverson play six high school friends, while Heather Sossaman appears as Laura Barns, a classmate whose death haunts the group. The film premiered at the Fantasia International Film Festival in 2014 and was released by Universal Pictures in April 2015.

The story begins in Fresno, California, where teenager Laura Barns took her own life after an anonymous user posted an embarrassing video of her passed out at a party, a clip that went viral and made her the target of relentless online abuse. Exactly one year later, Laura's former best friend Blaire is chatting on Skype with her boyfriend Mitch when they are joined by their friends Jess, Ken and Adam. An unknown account with no profile picture appears in the conversation and cannot be removed, no matter what the group tries.

Blaire discovers that the intruder is using Laura's old account, and the mysterious user begins sending messages from Laura's Facebook profile. Assuming it is a prank, the friends suspect a classmate, Val, and pull her into the chat, but the presence starts exposing their secrets, posting compromising photos and forcing them into a deadly game of "Never Have I Ever", in which each confession reveals betrayals, lies and their roles in the cruelty that drove Laura to her death. Anyone who tries to log off or disobeys the entity dies in a gruesome way, and as the friendships disintegrate, the survivors are forced to confront who was really responsible for the video that destroyed Laura.

The film uses its unusual format to address cyberbullying, online shaming and the permanence of digital actions, drawing tension from loading screens, frozen video feeds and messages typed and deleted in real time.

Made on a budget of about one million dollars, Unfriended was a major box-office success, grossing more than sixty million dollars worldwide. Critics were divided but often praised its inventive approach, and it was followed by the stand-alone sequel Unfriended: Dark Web in 2018.

title: Moana
tagline: The ocean is calling.
overview: In Ancient Polynesia, when a terrible curse incurred by Maui reaches an impetuous Chieftain's daughter's island, she answers the Ocean's call to seek out the demigod to set things right.
plot:
Moana (2016) is an animated adventure film that explores several themes that are both universally relatable and culturally specific to Polynesian communities.

One of the primary themes of Moana is the concept of identity and self-discovery. The protagonist, Moana, is a young girl who feels an insatiable call to explore the ocean and discover her true purpose in life. As she sets sail on her journey, she must navigate her own identity and confront the expectations placed upon her by her community.

Another significant theme in Moana is the importance of family and tradition. Moana's island, Motunui, is a tight-knit community that values its ancestral heritage and cultural traditions. However, as Moana embarks on her journey, she must also learn to balance her own desires with the needs of her family and community.

The film also explores the theme of perseverance and determination in the face of adversity. Moana faces numerous challenges, including treacherous seas, fierce monsters, and her own self-doubt. However, through her bravery and resilience, she is able to overcome these obstacles and achieve her goals.

Furthermore, Moana touches on the theme of colonialism and cultural appropriation. The film's depiction of European explorers and their impact on Polynesian cultures is a commentary on the historical exploitation and erasure of indigenous cultures. However, it also highlights the importance of preserving and celebrating one's own cultural heritage.

Finally, Moana features a strong female protagonist who embodies qualities such as courage, compassion, and wisdom. The film celebrates women's empowerment and encourages young girls to be confident in their abilities and pursue their passions.

Overall, Moana is a beautifully crafted film that explores complex themes and emotions through its engaging storyline and memorable characters.

title: Ice Age: Collision Course
tagline: One small step. One giant mess.
overview: Set after the events of Continental Drift, Scrat's epic pursuit of his elusive acorn catapults him outside of Earth, where he accidentally sets off a series of cosmic events that transform and threaten the planet. To save themselves from peril, Manny, Sid, Diego, and the rest of the herd leave their home and embark on a quest full of thrills and spills, highs and lows, laughter and adventure while traveling to exotic new lands and locations.
plot:
Ice Age: Collision Course is a 2016 American animated adventure comedy film directed by Michael Thurmeier and written by Michael Wilson, Michael Berg and Yoni Brenner. Produced by 20th Century Fox Animation and Blue Sky Studios, it is the fifth installment in the Ice Age series, following Ice Age: Continental Drift (2012). Ray Romano, John Leguizamo, Denis Leary, Josh Peck, Simon Pegg, Seann William Scott, Jennifer Lopez and Queen Latifah reprise their voice roles, joined by Jessie J and Adam DeVine.

Peaches, the daughter of the mammoths Manny and Ellie, is engaged to Julian, a cheerful mammoth whom Manny finds annoying and considers incapable of protecting her, and Manny is even more upset to learn that the couple want to travel the world after the wedding. Diego and Shira are hoping to start a family, and Sid is dumped by his girlfriend just as he is about to propose. Meanwhile Scrat's never-ending pursuit of his acorn has propelled him into outer space aboard an abandoned spaceship, where his antics send a giant asteroid hurtling toward Earth. As meteors begin to rain down on Manny and Ellie's anniversary, the herd takes shelter in a cave and is reunited with the adventurous weasel Buck, who has found an ancient stone pillar in the underground dinosaur world. According to its carvings, asteroids have caused two mass extinctions in the past, always striking the same spot, and Buck believes a solution may be found there. Pursued by a trio of flying dromaeosaurs who hope to survive the catastrophe and inherit the planet, the herd sets off for the impact site. On the way, Buck discovers that the asteroids are magnetic and devises a plan to launch a mass of smaller fragments into orbit to pull the big one off course. The journey leads them to Geotopia, a community of long-lived animals living inside a fallen asteroid, where Sid finds a new admirer in a sloth named Brooke, but the community's leader, Shangri Llama, refuses to surrender the crystals that keep his people young, and the herd must find a way to save the world while Manny learns to accept Julian.

The film received generally negative reviews; on Rotten Tomatoes, only 18% of 120 critics' reviews are positive, ranking it as the lowest-rated Ice Age film, with a consensus calling it unoriginal and unfunny. It still grossed $408 million worldwide against a $105 million production budget.

title: Avatar Spirits
tagline: In 2002, two friends set out to create a groundbreaking animated epic. This is their story.
overview: Bryan Konietzko and Michael Dante DiMartino, co-creators of the hit television series, Avatar: The Last Airbender, reflect on the creation of the masterful series.
plot:
Avatar Spirits is a 2010 American documentary film directed by Kurt Mattila about the making of the Nickelodeon animated series Avatar: The Last Airbender. Produced by Nickelodeon Productions with Prologue Pictures and running about half an hour, it was released in June 2010 and features the series' co-creators, Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko, reflecting on how their show came together, alongside interviews with many of the artists, musicians and consultants who worked on it. Its tagline sums up its approach: in 2002, two friends set out to create a groundbreaking animated epic, and this is their story.

The series it chronicles aired on Nickelodeon for three seasons from 2005 to 2008 and follows Aang, a twelve-year-old boy who is the last of the Air Nomads and the Avatar, the only person able to bend all four elements. The documentary traces this world back to a single sketch by Konietzko showing a bald boy, a tall animal with an arrow on its head and a robot monkey with a futuristic staff. The arrow migrated to the boy's head, and the creatures evolved into the characters Appa and Momo. At about the same time, DiMartino had become fascinated by Ernest Shackleton's struggle to survive in the Antarctic, and combining that polar setting with the idea of "fire people" attacking "water people" led to the concept of four nations.

The film describes the pitch to Nickelodeon development executive Eric Coleman, the demanding production of the pilot, for which Konietzko spent several months in South Korea and designs had to be simplified, and the order of thirteen episodes that followed its success with young test audiences. It then turns to the wider crew. Martial arts instructors Sifu Kisu and Manuel Rodríguez explain how real fighting styles, filmed in sparring sessions, provided the basis for the animated bending; director Giancarlo Volpe recalls the cinematic camera angles the creators demanded; Jeremy Zuckerman and Benjamin Wynn of the Track Team describe the unusual instruments behind the show's music and sound; and voice director Andrea Romano explains how she guided the actors' performances.

The documentary closes with the making of the finale, which the creators always intended as the definitive end of the story. To make it their best work, the Track Team recorded a live string orchestra for the first time, and the crew, with friends and family, gathered at the Paramount theater to watch the ending on a big screen.

Overall, The Revenant is a powerful and haunting film that explores themes of survival, revenge, and redemption in the face of unimaginable hardship.

plot:
Parasyte: Part 1 is a Japanese science fiction action film of 2014 directed by Takashi Yamazaki, the first of two films adapted from Hitoshi Iwaaki's manga series Parasyte and followed by Parasyte: Part 2. Shota Sometani stars as the high school student Shinichi Izumi, with Sadao Abe as the voice of Migi, the creature living in his hand, Eri Fukatsu as the teacher Ryoko Tamiya, Ai Hashimoto as Shinichi's girlfriend Satomi Murano and Kimiko Yo as Shinichi's mother Nobuko.

Mysterious alien organisms known as parasites begin invading Earth, burrowing into human beings and taking over their brains. One tries to enter the head of Shinichi, but because he is wearing headphones it fails and instead takes over his right hand. As a result Shinichi keeps his own mind, unlike the other victims. He befriends the creature and names it Migi, Japanese for "right". The parasites secretly feed on humans, and many of them are repelled by Shinichi's two minds sharing one body and try to kill him. One parasite has taken over his teacher, Ryoko Tamiya, who is far more rational than the others and curious about human life; to study it, she has become pregnant by a fellow parasite, Mr. A, and explains that her baby will be an ordinary human.

When Mr. A's attack on Shinichi fails and his host body is destroyed, he moves into Shinichi's mother, Nobuko. She returns home and gravely wounds her son, but Migi saves him by repairing his heart with its own cells, spreading its particles throughout his body. From then on, Shinichi's personality begins to blend with Migi's cool detachment, and he drifts away from Satomi. Meanwhile Tamiya's ally Hirokawa runs for mayor to turn the city into a haven for parasites. Another parasite, Shimada, transfers to Shinichi's school and seems friendly, but when a student uncovers his secret he slaughters the pupils. After Satomi wounds and disfigures him, leaving him unable to control himself, Tamiya abandons him and Shinichi kills him. Tamiya then tells Shinichi where to find the creature in his mother's body. When they meet, Nobuko manages to overcome the parasite long enough for her son to kill her. In an epilogue, Hirokawa wins the mayoral election, the formidable parasite Goto appears, and Shinichi visits Satomi in hospital while an unknown figure secretly records him talking to Migi.

Closing the Tokyo International Film Festival before its release in November 2014, the film topped the Japanese box office in its opening weekend.

plot:
Fallen is a 2016 romantic fantasy drama directed by Scott Hicks and based on Lauren Kate's 2009 young adult novel of the same name, the first book in her Fallen series. Addison Timlin stars as Lucinda "Luce" Price, with Jeremy Irvine as Daniel Grigori, Harrison Gilbertson as Cam, Lola Kirke, Juliet Aubrey and Joely Richardson. The film opened in several countries, including Malaysia, the Philippines and Singapore, in November 2016, but its American release was delayed until September 2017, when Relativity Media distributed it.

Luce is sent to Sword and Cross, a gloomy reform school for troubled teenagers, after she is blamed for the death of a boy named Trevor, who died in a fire after she kissed him. She remembers seeing strange shadows around them before the fire and fears that she is cursed. At her new school she meets an assortment of students: the charming Cam, who quickly shows an interest in her; the eccentric Arriane, who takes her under her wing; the hostile Molly; the friendly Penn; and the brooding Daniel Grigori, to whom she feels an immediate and inexplicable attraction despite his efforts to push her away. She also meets Miss Sophia, a teacher of religious studies.

The school psychiatrist tells Luce that she can leave if she agrees to take antipsychotic medication, but strange events keep happening around her, including a near-fatal accident with a falling statue of an angel. Torn between Cam's open flirtation and her mysterious connection to Daniel, Luce begins to research his past with Penn's help and discovers evidence suggesting that she and Daniel have met many times before, in different eras. She eventually learns that Daniel and several of her schoolmates are fallen angels and that she has been reincarnated repeatedly, each time falling in love with Daniel and dying before their love can be fulfilled. As a battle between heaven and hell draws closer to Sword and Cross, Luce must discover who she really is and whom she can trust.

The film was a critical and commercial failure. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds a 7 percent approval rating based on 14 reviews, with an average score of 3.2 out of 10. Several critics compared it unfavorably with earlier supernatural teen romances, and its long-delayed American release did little to attract an audience.

title: The Light Between Oceans
tagline: Love demands everything
overview: A lighthouse keeper and his wife living off the coast of Western Australia raise a baby they rescue from an adrift rowboat.
plot:
The Light Between Oceans is a 2016 romantic period drama written and directed by Derek Cianfrance, based on the 2012 novel by M. L. Stedman. An international co-production, it stars Michael Fassbender as Tom Sherbourne, Alicia Vikander as Isabel Graysmark and Rachel Weisz as Hannah Roennfeldt, with Bryan Brown and Jack Thompson. It tells the story of a lighthouse keeper and his wife who rescue an infant adrift at sea and raise her as their own.

In 1918, Tom Sherbourne, a withdrawn veteran of the First World War, takes a position as the keeper of the lighthouse on Janus Rock, a remote island off the coast of Australia. He falls in love with Isabel, a spirited young woman from the nearby town, and they marry and settle on the island. Their happiness is shattered when Isabel suffers two miscarriages. Shortly after the second, a rowboat washes ashore carrying a dead man and a crying baby girl. Tom knows that he must report the discovery, but the grieving Isabel persuades him to keep the child and pretend she is their own. Tom buries the man on the island, and the couple name the baby Lucy.

When the couple take Lucy to the mainland to be christened, Tom sees a woman, Hannah Roennfeldt, mourning at a grave dedicated to her husband and infant daughter, who were lost at sea on the very day the boat reached Janus Rock. Realizing that Lucy is almost certainly Hannah's child, Tom is consumed by guilt and secretly sends Hannah a message assuring her that her daughter is safe and loved. As Lucy grows up, the couple's deception becomes harder to sustain, and Tom's conscience sets in motion a chain of events that will test the marriage, the bond between mother and child and the meaning of forgiveness.

Cianfrance shot the film on location in New Zealand and Tasmania, emphasizing the isolation of the lighthouse and the elemental landscapes surrounding it.

The film premiered in competition at the Venice International Film Festival on September 1, 2016, and was released in the United States the next day by Touchstone Pictures. It received mixed reviews, with about 62 percent approval on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 60, though the lead performances were praised. It grossed about 26 million dollars worldwide against a budget of 20 million.

title: Thor: Ragnarok
tagline: No Hammer. No Problem.
overview: Thor is imprisoned on the other side of the universe and finds himself in a race against time to get back to Asgard to stop Ragnarok, the destruction of his home-world and the end of Asgardian civilization, at the hands of a powerful new threat, the ruthless Hela.
plot:
Thor: Ragnarok is a 2017 superhero film directed by Taika Waititi, based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name. The movie marks the third installment in the Thor film series and the 17th film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU).

The story begins with Thor (Chris Hemsworth), the crown prince of Asgard, who has been banished to Earth by his father Odin (Anthony Hopkins) after a battle with the Frost Giants. Thor is forced to live on a small planet called Sakaar, where he becomes a gladiator and fights in the arena against various alien warriors.

Meanwhile, back on Asgard, Hela (Cate Blanchett), the goddess of death, has returned to claim her rightful place as the ruler of Asgard. She is determined to destroy the realm and everyone in it, including Thor's brother Loki (Tom Hiddleston).

Thor soon discovers that he must stop Hela from unleashing a catastrophic event known as Ragnarok, which will destroy Asgard. He also learns that his hammer Mjolnir has been stolen by Surtur (Clancy Brown), the leader of the Frost Giants.

Thor teams up with Valkyrie (Tessa Thompson), a warrior who is tasked with choosing the worthy warriors to fight in Valhalla, and Korg (Taika Waititi), a Kronan gladiator who becomes his unlikely friend. Together, they embark on a journey to stop Hela and save Asgard.

Along the way, Thor confronts his own identity and purpose, as he struggles to come to terms with being a god and a warrior. He also learns to let go of his ego and trust others, particularly Valkyrie, who becomes a valuable ally in his quest.

The movie features stunning visuals, witty humor, and impressive action sequences, making it a standout in the MCU. The film's tone is lighter and more humorous than previous Thor movies, with Waititi bringing his signature irreverence and wit to the story.

As the battle between Thor and Hela reaches its climax, the fate of Asgard hangs in the balance. In the end, Thor emerges victorious, but not without sacrifices. He also learns that he is worthy of wielding Mjolnir once again and becomes a true hero.

The movie concludes with Thor returning to Asgard, where he is welcomed back as a hero. The film ends on a hopeful note, setting the stage for future adventures in the MCU.

Overall, Thor: Ragnarok is a thrilling and entertaining ride that explores themes of identity, purpose, and redemption. With its stunning visuals, witty humor, and impressive action sequences, it's a must-see for fans of the MCU and superhero movies in general.

plot:
Black Panther is a 2018 superhero film directed by Ryan Coogler, produced by Marvel Studios, and based on the Marvel Comics character of the same name.

The story takes place in the fictional African nation of Wakanda, where King T'Challa (played by Chadwick Boseman) has assumed the throne after his father's death. T'Challa is a skilled warrior and strategist who must balance his royal duties with his desire to protect his people from threats both within and outside their borders.

Upon his return to Wakanda, T'Challa is challenged by Erik Killmonger (played by Michael B. Jordan), a Wakandan exile who seeks to overthrow him and claim the throne for himself. Killmonger believes that Wakanda's isolationist policies have led to the suffering of African people around the world, and he wants to use Wakanda's advanced technology to spark a global revolution.

As T'Challa navigates this internal conflict, he must also confront external threats from the United States and other nations that seek to exploit Wakanda's resources. He is aided by his sister Shuri (played by Letitia Wright), a brilliant inventor and engineer who helps him develop new technologies to defend his country.

Throughout the film, T'Challa grapples with the weight of his responsibilities as king and the legacy of his father, who was killed in battle against Killmonger. He must also confront his own identity and the expectations placed upon him by his people.

One of the standout aspects of Black Panther is its exploration of themes such as colonialism, imperialism, and cultural identity. The film offers a nuanced portrayal of Wakandan society and culture, highlighting both its strengths and weaknesses. It also features a diverse cast of characters, including Nakia (played by Lupita Nyong'o), a Wakandan spy who becomes T'Challa's love interest.

Overall, Black Panther is a visually stunning and thought-provoking film that offers a fresh take on the superhero genre. Its blend of action, drama, and social commentary makes it a compelling watch for audiences of all ages.

Through Reacher's character, the movie raises questions about the consequences of playing by one's own rules and the importance of accountability in a system that seems to be stacked against its most vulnerable members.

Ultimately, Beyond the Reach is a gripping thriller that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats as it hurtles towards its explosive conclusion. With its breakneck pace and pulse-pounding action sequences, the film delivers an adrenaline-fueled ride that will keep you guessing until the very end.

title: Top Five
overview: A comedian tries to make it as a serious actor when his reality-TV star fiancé talks him into broadcasting their wedding on her TV show.
plot:
Top Five is a 2014 American romantic comedy-drama written and directed by Chris Rock, who also stars, and produced by Scott Rudin and Eli Bush. Rosario Dawson and Gabrielle Union co-star, with an ensemble of comedians and actors including J. B. Smoove, Kevin Hart, Sherri Shepherd, Tracy Morgan, Cedric the Entertainer and Jerry Seinfeld. After its premiere at the 2014 Toronto International Film Festival, several studios entered a bidding war for distribution rights, which were won by Paramount Pictures; it was released in the United States on 12 December 2014.

Rock plays Andre Allen, a New York comedian and film star who is famous for a lucrative franchise in which he plays Hammy the Bear, a police officer in a bear costume. Now a recovering alcoholic, he wants to be taken seriously and is promoting Uprize, a historical drama in which he plays the Haitian revolutionary Dutty Boukman. He is also preparing for a televised wedding to his fiancée Erica Long, a reality television star played by Union. Chelsea Brown, a New York Times journalist played by Dawson, spends a day following Andre around the city to write a profile of him, even though he is wary of the newspaper, whose critic has repeatedly savaged his work.

As they travel through Manhattan, their conversation ranges over fame, race, comedy, sobriety and relationships. Andre recalls the lowest point of his life, a chaotic night in Houston years earlier that ended with his arrest and set him on the path to recovery. When their limousine is involved in an accident, the pair continue on foot, visiting his old friends and family in the neighbourhood where he grew up, and the friends debate their personal "top five" rappers of all time. Chelsea, who has secrets of her own, gradually breaks down Andre's defences, and the two begin to develop feelings for each other, forcing Andre to question both his upcoming marriage and the direction of his career.

The film draws on Rock's own experiences as a comedian and celebrity and combines sharp stand-up style humour with a reflective look at fame and authenticity.

Top Five received critical acclaim. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 85 percent, with the consensus calling it as smart, funny and trenchant as Rock's best stand-up work and a career highlight for him.

title: Goodnight Mommy

This sets off a chain reaction of events that exposes the dark secrets and traumas that have been hidden beneath the surface of their seemingly idyllic family life.

The film expertly weaves together themes of identity, exploring how our sense of self is shaped by our experiences, relationships, and perceptions. The mother's dual identity serves as a metaphor for the fragility of human identity, highlighting how easily it can be manipulated and distorted.

Furthermore, Goodnight Mommy critiques the notion of childhood innocence, suggesting that children are not as naive as they seem. The boys' growing awareness of their mother's true nature forces them to confront the harsh realities of adulthood, including the darkness that lurks beneath the surface of seemingly ordinary lives.

The film also touches on the theme of trauma and its lasting impact on individuals and families. The mother's past is slowly revealed, exposing a history of pain and suffering that has left her with emotional scars. This serves as a reminder that trauma can be passed down through generations, affecting not only the individual but also those around them.

Ultimately, Goodnight Mommy is a thought-provoking exploration of the human psyche, delving into the complexities of identity, trauma, and the fragility of human relationships.

title: Jarhead 2: Field of Fire
tagline: Find the courage, fight together.
overview: Battle-scarred and disillusioned by the war, Corporal Chris Merrimette is put in charge of a unit whose next mission is to resupply a remote outpost on the edge of Taliban-controlled territory. While driving through the hostile Helmand province, a Navy SEAL flags down their convoy and enlists the unit on an operation of international importance: they must help an Afghan woman famous for her defiance of the Taliban escape the country. plot:
Jarhead 2: Field of Fire is a 2014 American direct-to-video war film directed by Don Michael Paul from a screenplay by Berkeley Anderson and Ellis Black. Although it borrows its title from Sam Mendes's Jarhead (2005), it is a sequel in name only, with an unrelated story and characters set during the war in Afghanistan. Josh Kelly stars as Corporal Chris Merrimette, with Cole Hauser as Navy SEAL Fox and Stephen Lang, Esai Morales, Bokeem Woodbine and Danielle Savre in supporting roles.

Merrimette, a Marine who has grown battle-scarred and disillusioned with the war, is given command of a tight-knit unit for the first time. Their assignment seems routine for a supply detachment: drive a convoy through some of the most dangerous Taliban-held territory in Helmand province to resupply a remote outpost at the edge of enemy-controlled ground. On the way, however, they are flagged down by Fox, a special operations officer who tells them their mission has changed. He is escorting Anoosh, an Afghan woman who has become famous for defying the Taliban and a symbol of resistance to them, and she must be brought to safety so she can deliver a speech at the United Nations.

The operation quickly turns into a fight for survival. Taliban forces ambush the Marines, inflicting casualties and leaving them no way back to the Green Zone except on foot, and the survivors must cross hostile country with no communication and no air support, and with only Fox's experience of the land and its people to guide them. Merrimette, whose experience until now has been limited to supply runs, must hold his unit together and protect Anoosh as they fight their way through one of the most dangerous places on Earth, while tensions flare between some of the Marines and their local allies and interpreters before giving way to mutual respect. As the Taliban close in, the Marines must rely on their courage and firepower to see Anoosh to safety, at heavy cost.

Released on home video and digital platforms in 2014, the film was followed by Jarhead 3: The Siege (2016) and Jarhead: Law of Return (2019). Common Sense Media judged it a better-than-expected war movie that conveys the Marines' esprit de corps and does not shy away from casualties, despite a formulaic story, while DVD Talk called it markedly average in concept, performances and script.

plot:
Barbie and the Secret Door is a computer-animated musical fantasy of 2014 directed by Karen Lloyd, the 28th entry in the Barbie film series. Kelly Sheridan voices Princess Alexa, with Brittany McDonald providing her singing voice, Ashleigh Ball as the fairy Nori, Chanelle Peloso as the mermaid Romy and Tabitha St. Germain as the villainous child princess Malucia; Christopher Gaze, Andrea Libman and Andrew Francis are also in the cast.

Alexa is the shy princess of a modern-day kingdom who shrinks from her royal duties. To encourage her, her grandmother gives her a storybook about a princess who discovers she has magic, and while reading it Alexa finds a hidden door in the palace gardens. title: The Martian

But Watney has survived and finds himself stranded and alone on the hostile planet. With only meager supplies, he must draw upon his ingenuity, wit and spirit to subsist and find a way to signal to Earth that he is alive.
plot:
The Martian is a 2015 American science fiction film directed by Ridley Scott, based on the novel of the same name by Andy Weir. The movie follows the story of astronaut Mark Watney, played by Matt Damon.

The film begins with the Ares III mission to Mars, where Watney and his crew are sent to explore the planet's surface. During a severe dust storm, the crew is forced to evacuate, but in the chaos, Watney is presumed dead and left behind. However, he manages to survive the storm by using his ingenuity and knowledge of botany.

As the days pass, Watney realizes that he has become stranded on Mars with limited supplies and no communication with Earth. He uses his skills as a botanist to grow food in the Martian soil, which becomes crucial for his survival. Meanwhile, back on Earth, NASA's mission control team, led by Vincent Kapoor (Chiwetel Ejiofor), discovers Watney's transmission signal and realizes that he is still alive.

The crew of the Hermes spaceship, which was sent to rescue Watney, returns to Mars with a new plan to extract him. However, due to the harsh Martian environment and limited resources, they face numerous challenges in their mission. The team also faces opposition from NASA's director, Ted Mendez (Mackenzie Davis), who is skeptical of the crew's ability to save Watney.

As the story unfolds, Watney uses his wit and resourcefulness to overcome various obstacles, including a malfunctioning toilet that threatens to kill him, and a Martian dust storm that could destroy his habitat. He also uses his knowledge of botany to create a makeshift food source, which becomes essential for his survival.

Meanwhile, back on Earth, the crew of the Hermes spaceship faces their own challenges as they try to come up with a plan to rescue Watney. The team's dynamics are put to the test as they work together to overcome the odds and save their stranded colleague.

The film's climax features an intense and suspenseful sequence where the Hermes crew finally manages to extract Watney from Mars, but not before he has to make a difficult decision that could have potentially saved his life. The movie ends on a hopeful note, with Watney returning to Earth as a hero, thanks to the ingenuity and determination of the crew.

Throughout the film, Ridley Scott's direction brings out the best in Matt Damon's performance, capturing the character's wit, humor, and resilience in the face of adversity. The supporting cast, including Chiwetel Ejiofor, Mackenzie Davis, and Jessica Chastain, deliver strong performances that add depth to the story.

Overall, The Martian is a gripping and inspiring film that showcases the power of human ingenuity and determination in the face of seemingly insurmountable challenges.
