plot:
Avengers: Endgame is a 2019 superhero film directed by Anthony and Joe Russo, and produced by Marvel Studios. The movie serves as the culmination of a decade-long story arc in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU).

The film takes place after the events of Avengers: Infinity War, where Thanos (Josh Brolin) has collected all six Infinity Stones and wiped out half of all life in the universe with a mere snap of his fingers. The remaining Avengers, led by Tony Stark/Iron Man (Robert Downey Jr.), Steve Rogers/Captain America (Chris Evans), Bruce Banner/Hulk (Mark Ruffalo), Thor (Chris Hemsworth), and Natasha Romanoff/Black Widow (Scarlett Johansson), are left to mourn the loss of their friends and allies.

The Avengers come up with a plan to use the Quantum Realm, a subatomic dimension that was introduced in Ant-Man, to travel through time and gather the Infinity Stones. They aim to use the stones to restore balance to the universe by undoing Thanos' snap.

The team embarks on a perilous journey through time, visiting key moments in their pasts to collect the stones. Along the way, they encounter alternate versions of themselves from different timelines, including an older Tony Stark who has become a mad scientist, and a younger Steve Rogers who is struggling with his own identity.

As the Avengers gather the stones, they also face numerous challenges and obstacles, including Thanos' army and their own personal demons. The film's climax features an epic battle between the Avengers and Thanos, which ultimately leads to the restoration of balance in the universe.

Throughout the film, the characters grapple with the consequences of their actions and the weight of their responsibilities as heroes. Tony Stark, in particular, comes to terms with his own mortality and the legacy he leaves behind for his daughter, Morgan.

Avengers: Endgame is a emotionally charged and visually stunning conclusion to the Infinity Saga, which has become one of the most beloved and successful franchises in cinematic history. The film's themes of sacrifice, friendship, and redemption make it a must-see for fans of the MCU.

overview: As the Avengers and their allies have continued to protect the world from threats too large for any one hero to handle, a new danger has emerged from the cosmic shadows: Thanos. A despot of intergalactic infamy, his goal is to collect all six Infinity Stones, artifacts of unimaginable power, and use them to inflict his twisted will on all of reality. Everything the Avengers have fought for has led up to this moment - the fate of Earth and existence itself has never been more uncertain.
plot:
Avengers: Infinity War is a 2018 superhero film directed by Anthony and Joe Russo, produced by Marvel Studios, and based on the Marvel Comics series of the same name. The movie brings together a vast ensemble cast of characters from the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) to fight against an intergalactic threat.

The story begins with Thanos (Josh Brolin), a powerful Titan who seeks to collect all six Infinity Stones, which would grant him unimaginable power and allow him to wipe out half of all life in the universe. The Avengers, led by Iron Man (Robert Downey Jr.), Captain America (Chris Evans), Thor (Chris Hemsworth), Hulk (Mark Ruffalo), Black Widow (Scarlett Johansson), and Hawkeye (Jeremy Renner), are alerted to Thanos' plan and band together to stop him.

Meanwhile, the Guardians of the Galaxy, consisting of Peter Quill (Chris Pratt), Gamora (Zoe Saldana), Drax (Dave Bautista), Rocket Raccoon (Bradley Cooper), and Groot (Vin Diesel), also become entangled in Thanos' quest. The two groups eventually join forces to take down Thanos.

As the battle against Thanos intensifies, the Avengers and their allies face numerous challenges, including Thanos' army of Black Order warriors, the Chitauri, and other formidable foes. Along the way, characters like Doctor Strange (Benedict Cumberbatch), Spider-Man (Tom Holland), and Black Panther (Chadwick Boseman) also make appearances.

Throughout the film, Thanos' motivations are explored, revealing a tragic backstory that drives his desire to collect the Infinity Stones. The movie's climax features an epic showdown between the Avengers and Thanos, resulting in a devastating conclusion that sets the stage for the events of Avengers: Endgame.

One of the standout aspects of Avengers: Infinity War is its ability to balance individual character arcs with the larger narrative. The film expertly weaves together multiple storylines, creating a sense of urgency and stakes that propels the audience towards the movie's shocking conclusion.

Overall, Avengers: Infinity War is a masterclass in ensemble storytelling, featuring an impressive cast of characters and a narrative that is both action-packed and emotionally resonant.

title: Captain Marvel
tagline: Higher. Further. Faster.
overview: The story follows Carol Danvers as she becomes one of the universe’s most powerful heroes when Earth is caught in the middle of a galactic war between two alien races. Set in the 1990s, Captain Marvel is an all-new adventure from a previously unseen period in the history of the Marvel Cinematic Universe.
plot:
Captain Marvel is a 2019 superhero film produced by Marvel Studios and directed by Anna Boden and Ryan Fleck. The movie follows the story of Carol Danvers, an Air Force pilot who becomes one of the most powerful heroes in the Marvel Cinematic Universe.

The film begins with Carol Danvers (played by Brie Larson) as a young Air Force pilot during the 1990s. She is part of a secret government program called S.H.I.E.L.D., which is experimenting with the power of Kree technology, an alien energy source that enhances human abilities. During a mission to rescue a group of hostages from an alien ship, Carol's plane is attacked by the Kree, and she is exposed to the energy.

The attack leaves Carol severely injured, but also imbues her with incredible powers, including superhuman strength, speed, agility, and durability. She becomes one of the most powerful beings in the universe, capable of flying and wielding energy blasts.

As Carol awakens from her coma, she discovers that she has become a superhero known as Captain Marvel. She is recruited by Nick Fury (played by Samuel L. Jackson), who reveals to her that she is not human but rather an alien hybrid, the result of a Kree-human experiment.

Carol soon learns that the Kree have been at war with the Skrulls, another alien species, for centuries. The Skrulls, led by Talos (played by Ben Mendelsohn), are seeking to invade Earth and assimilate its inhabitants into their own species. Nick Fury reveals that Carol's powers make her a key player in the battle against the Skrulls.

As Captain Marvel, Carol teams up with Nick Fury and his team to stop the Skrulls' invasion. Along the way, she meets Goose (played by a Flerken), a small, shapeshifting alien creature that becomes her loyal companion.

The film's plot thickens as Carol discovers that Talos is actually a Skrull who has been working with S.H.I.E.L.D. to gather intelligence on the Kree and Skrulls. He reveals that he has been searching for Carol, who is the key to unlocking the secrets of the Kree-human experiment.

As the battle between the Skrulls and the Kree reaches its climax, Captain Marvel must confront her own identity and the true nature of her powers. In a thrilling showdown, she faces off against Talos and his minions, using her powers to save the world from destruction.

In the end, Carol Danvers emerges as one of the most powerful heroes in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, ready to take on new challenges and defend the Earth against any threat that may arise. The film concludes with a post-credits scene setting up the events of Avengers: Endgame, where Captain Marvel plays a crucial role in the battle against Thanos.

Overall, Captain Marvel is an action-packed, visually stunning film that explores themes of identity, power, and belonging. Brie Larson shines as Carol Danvers, bringing depth and nuance to the character's journey from humble Air Force pilot to superhero icon.

title: The Atticus Institute
tagline: The only case of possession confirmed by the U.S. Government.
overview: In the early 1970s, Dr. Henry West creates an institute to find people with supernatural abilities. When Judith Winstead comes to the facility, she exhibits amazing abilities that the military wants to turn into a weapon.
plot:
The Atticus Institute is a 2015 American independent horror film written and directed by Chris Sparling. Presented as a pseudo-documentary, it concerns a paranormal research institute that becomes home to what is described as the only case of demonic possession ever confirmed by the United States government. It stars William Mapother as the institute's founder, Dr. Henry West, and Rya Kihlstedt as his subject, Judith Winstead.

The story unfolds through footage intercut with interviews. In the early 1970s, West founds the Atticus Institute in rural Pennsylvania in the hope of proving that psychic abilities such as extrasensory perception are real, but every subject who appears to possess such powers proves to be a fraud. The demoralized team's fortunes change when Judith is brought in by her sister Margaret, who is troubled by her disturbing behavior. Judith easily masters every test, and increasingly demanding experiments reveal abilities far greater than anyone expected. As her powers grow, her behavior becomes more unstable; strange events afflict the staff and their families, and many aides resign.

Seeking help, the team turns to the U.S. military, whose advisers devise tests that draw out new abilities, including telekinesis and pyrokinesis. When a spectral photography experiment triggers a violent reaction, the images show a cloud-like entity briefly leaving Judith's body, and the researchers realize that she is possessed by a demon. Citing national security, the military takes over the institute, hoping to turn the demon into a weapon against the Soviet Union during the Cold War, and subjects Judith to increasingly inhumane experiments, including electroshock, over West's objections. When attempts to make the entity locate enemy bases fail, the military stages an exorcism with a soldier wired to Judith. The procedure goes wrong: Judith gravely injures the priest, and a blast of force knocks out everyone present. When the cameras come back on, Judith is herself again, but the demon has taken over West's body. He kills her by telekinetically bursting her heart and walks out. Closing notes state that Judith was buried in an undisclosed location and that West, who vanished on October 23, 1976, was declared legally dead in 1982.

The film was released on January 23, 2015, and was poorly received; critics praised its found-footage documentary format but faulted its pacing and lack of originality, and it holds 50% on Rotten Tomatoes from six reviews.

title: The 5th Wave

overview: 16-year-old Cassie Sullivan tries to survive in a world devastated by the waves of an alien invasion that has already decimated the population and knocked mankind back to the Stone Age.
plot:
The 5th Wave is a science fiction film directed by Neill Blomkamp, released in 2016. The movie is based on the novel of the same name by Rick Yancey.

In the near future, an alien invasion has devastated Earth, and the extraterrestrial beings, known as "The Others," have begun to abduct humans, leaving behind a trail of destruction and chaos. The story follows Cassie Sullivan (Chloe Moretz), a 16-year-old girl who is trying to survive in this new world.

Cassie's life takes a dramatic turn when she witnesses the abduction of her brother, Sam (Harris Dickinson). She soon discovers that the Others are not just random abductors but are actually targeting specific individuals with unique skills and abilities. Cassie learns that she has been chosen as one of the "Five," a group of children who possess special talents that will help humanity fight back against The Others.

The movie begins with Cassie's life in a post-apocalyptic world, where she is forced to live on her own after her mother's death. She meets Evan Walker (Alex Roe), a mysterious and handsome young man who claims to be one of the "Five." title: Capture the Flag
overview: When the brave and determined 12-year-old Mike Goldwing discovers that an eccentric billionaire plans to fly to the moon, steal its vast, valuable natural resources, and destroy the American flag planted by the Apollo XI astronauts during man's historic moon landing, the countdown to a spectacular adventure begins! plot:
Capture the Flag (Spanish: Atrapa la bandera) is a 2015 Spanish computer-animated science fiction adventure comedy directed by Enrique Gato and written by Patxi Amezcua. Produced by 4 Cats Pictures and animated by Lightbox Entertainment, it was distributed worldwide by Paramount Pictures, a milestone for Spanish animation following the studio's earlier deal for Gato's Tad the Lost Explorer. The Spanish voice cast includes Carme Calvell, Michelle Jenner, Javier Balas and Dani Rovira. It was released in Spain on 28 August 2015.

Twelve-year-old Mike Goldwing comes from a family of NASA astronauts. His grandfather Frank has been estranged from the family for years, embittered at having lost his chance to travel to the Moon on the Apollo 11 mission. Richard Carson III, a megalomaniac Texan billionaire, wants to claim ownership of the Moon in order to mine its rich reserves of Helium-3. To support his claim, he spreads the conspiracy theory that the 1969 Moon landing was faked in a studio, and plans to travel to the Moon himself to destroy the only physical proof: the American flag planted by the Apollo 11 astronauts.

The President of the United States orders NASA to mount a new lunar mission to stop him, with Frank recalled as commander, while Carson hires a saboteur to derail the launch. Mike decides to stow away on the mission to win his grandfather's respect. With his friends Marty and Amy and Marty's pet iguana, Igor, he sneaks into the Kennedy Space Center, where Marty is caught after an encounter with alligators in the surrounding marshes. When Carson's agent triggers the rocket's launch ahead of schedule, Mike, Amy, Igor and Frank blast off for the Moon with Carson in pursuit. On the lunar surface, they race to secure the flag and expose the billionaire's scheme to the world, while Mike and Frank rebuild their relationship and Frank finally realizes his dream of walking on the Moon.

Capture the Flag was well received in Spain, where it won the Goya Award for Best Animated Film, but reviews elsewhere were mixed, with a 46 percent rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Variety called it solid family entertainment, while noting that it did not match the standards of the leading Hollywood animation studios.

Annihilation is a 2018 American science fiction film directed by Alex Garland, based on the novel of the same name by Jeff VanderMeer. The movie stars Natalie Portman, Jennifer Jason Leigh, Tessa Thompson, and Oscar Isaac.

The story begins with a prologue that shows a catastrophic event known as "the Shimmer," which has been occurring for decades in an area of the United States where the laws of nature do not apply. The Shimmer is a mysterious, alien-infused zone that seems to be alive and constantly changing.

The main character, Lena (Natalie Portman), is a biologist who has lost her husband, Kane, to the Shimmer during one of his expeditions into the area. Lena joins an all-female team, led by Dr. Ventress (Jennifer Jason Leigh), to explore the Shimmer and uncover its secrets.

As they venture deeper into the Shimmer, the team encounters strange and terrifying creatures that defy explanation. They also discover that the Shimmer is not just a physical environment but also a psychological one, where the laws of reality are constantly shifting.

The team's journey takes them through different biomes within the Shimmer, each with its own unique characteristics and dangers. Along the way, they encounter other survivors who have been affected by the Shimmer in different ways, including a mysterious figure known as "the Biologist" (Tessa Thompson).

As Lena delves deeper into the Shimmer, she begins to experience strange visions and hallucinations that blur the lines between reality and fantasy. She also discovers that her husband's body has undergone a transformation, becoming one with the Shimmer.

The team eventually reaches the heart of the Shimmer, where they discover a mysterious structure known as "the Lighthouse." Inside the Lighthouse, Lena encounters a figure who claims to be the Biologist, but it becomes clear that this is not the same person she encountered earlier.

In the end, Lena emerges from the Shimmer with no memory of her past or her identity. She has become one with the alien entity that inhabits the Shimmer, and her body has undergone a transformation that blurs the lines between human and non-human.

The film ends with Lena walking away from the camera, into an unknown future, as the Shimmer continues to expand and change around her. The ending is intentionally ambiguous, leaving the audience to wonder what happened to Lena and whether she will ever be able to return to her old life.

Overall, Annihilation is a thought-provoking and visually stunning film that explores themes of identity, self-destruction, and the unknown. It challenges the viewer to consider the consequences of playing with forces beyond human control and the dangers of delving too deep into the mysteries of the universe.

Initially, the trio manages to evade Mr. Gray's defenses and steal some cash from his safe. However, things take a turn for the worse when Rocky discovers that Mr. Gray has been waiting for them all along. Despite being blind, Mr. Gray uses his other senses to track down the intruders and set up an elaborate trap.

As the night progresses, the group finds themselves in a desperate fight for survival. Bo is killed by Mr. Gray's booby traps, while Manco is severely injured. Rocky manages to escape with his life but not without realizing that he has underestimated Mr. Gray's abilities.

Throughout the movie, Alvarez uses tension and suspense to create a sense of unease in the audience. The film's score, composed by Tom Spezialy, adds to the tension, creating an atmosphere of dread and fear.

In the end, Rocky manages to outsmart Mr. Gray and escape from his house. However, he is left with a newfound respect for the old man and a realization that some people are capable of more than we think. The movie ends on a somber note, leaving the audience to ponder the true nature of Mr. Gray's abilities and the consequences of underestimating others.

Overall, Don't Breathe is a tense and suspenseful horror-thriller that explores themes of vulnerability, trust, and the power of the human mind. The film features strong performances from its cast, particularly Daniel Radcliffe, who brings depth and nuance to his character.

Ultimately, Replicas is a thought-provoking exploration of grief, identity, and what it means to be human. plot:
Dragonheart 3: The Sorcerer's Curse is a 2015 fantasy adventure film directed by Colin Teague and released direct-to-video by Universal. The third installment of the Dragonheart franchise and a prequel to the 1996 original, it stars Julian Morris as a young squire, Tamzin Merchant, Jassa Ahluwalia and Jonjo O'Neill, with Ben Kingsley voicing the dragon Drago.

In 9th-century northern Britain, a circle of druids foresees a falling star from the constellation Draco. One of them, Brude, summons a Pict clan known as the Painted tribe to slaughter the others and lead the northern clans to war against the southern kingdoms beyond Hadrian's Wall. Only a druid apprentice, Lorne, escapes. On the southern side of the wall, the squire Gareth completes his final tests to be knighted. He is the best fighter among the candidates but fails to collect enough taxes from the peasants, and his superior, Sir Horsa, refuses to knight him unless he pays a hundred crowns.

When a meteor falls north of the wall, Gareth goes in search of the riches it is said to contain, and instead finds a dragon emerging from it with a clutch of eggs. Gareth saves one of the eggs during a fight with the Painted tribe but is gravely wounded, and the dragon, moved by his mercy, shares its heart with him, binding them together. Brude places a curse on the dragon and seizes the eggs. Gareth names the dragon Drago and joins Lorne and Rhonu, a rebel leader of the clans opposing Brude, in an effort to rescue the eggs. Brude's Sorcerer's Curse threatens to place him under the sorcerer's control by the full moon.

The companions recover the eggs and head for the wall, where Gareth confesses to Drago that he is not truly a knight. They are arrested, and the eggs are seized by Horsa to be sold, as the Painted tribe and the enslaved Drago attack. Gareth's courage frees the dragon, who helps the defenders and the northern clans repel the attack. Gareth kills Horsa and Rhonu kills Brude, though she is fatally wounded until an unhatched dragon shares its heart with her. Gareth is knighted and becomes the settlement's leader, and the wall is renamed the Dragon's Gate as peace is established between north and south.

The film received mixed but generally positive reviews, with critics noting its impressive effects for a direct-to-video production and considering it an improvement over Dragonheart: A New Beginning. It earned over $2 million in domestic home video sales.

title: The Neon Demon
tagline: Beauty is vicious.
overview: When aspiring model Jesse moves to Los Angeles, her youth and vitality are devoured by a group of beauty-obsessed women who will take any means necessary to get what she has.
plot:
The Neon Demon is an arthouse horror film of 2016 directed by Nicolas Winding Refn, who wrote it with Mary Laws and Polly Stenham, following a teenage model whose beauty provokes obsession and envy in the Los Angeles fashion world. Elle Fanning stars as Jesse, with Karl Glusman as the photographer Dean, Jena Malone as the make-up artist Ruby, Bella Heathcote and Abbey Lee as the models Gigi and Sarah, Christina Hendricks as agency owner Roberta Hoffman, Alessandro Nivola as designer Robert Sarno and Keanu Reeves as the motel manager Hank.

Jesse, a sixteen-year-old orphan, has just arrived in Los Angeles from a small town in Georgia to become a model. Through a first shoot with Dean she meets Ruby, who introduces her to the older models Gigi and Sarah. Roberta signs her, tells her to say she is nineteen, and sends her to the celebrated photographer Jack McCarther. That night Jesse returns from a date with Dean, who is interested in her as a person, to find that a cougar has wrecked her motel room; the leering owner, Hank, demands payment, which Dean covers. Jack photographs her naked and painted in gold, and the shoot's success deepens the older models' envy. At a casting for Sarno, the designer ignores Sarah and is captivated by Jesse. When Sarah asks how it feels to be the one everyone wants and Jesse replies that it is everything, Sarah lunges at her; Jesse cuts her hand on broken glass, and Sarah sucks the blood.

Jesse closes Sarno's show amid hallucinations of triangles and mirrored reflections of herself, and afterwards, as Sarno tells Dean that beauty is the only thing that matters, she rejects Dean, having embraced a new narcissism. After a nightmare about Hank and the sound of someone trying her door, she hears an intruder attack the young girl in the next room and flees to Ruby's house. There she rejects Ruby's advances and reveals that she is a virgin. Later, at the house, Ruby, Gigi and Sarah pursue Jesse, push her into an empty swimming pool, kill her and devour parts of her body, bathing in her blood. At a shoot the next day, Jack is suddenly fascinated by Sarah, but Gigi, overcome with sickness, vomits up one of Jesse's eyes and, crying that she must get Jesse out of her, stabs herself fatally with scissors. Sarah swallows the eye and returns to work.

A French, Danish and American co-production, the film was in competition for the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 2016. Critics were divided, giving it 59% on Rotten Tomatoes.

title: Blonde
tagline: Watched by all, seen by none.
overview: From her volatile childhood as Norma Jeane, through her rise to stardom and romantic entanglements, this reimagined fictional portrait of Hollywood legend Marilyn Monroe blurs the lines of fact and fiction to explore the widening split between her public and private selves.
plot:
Blonde is a 2022 American psychological drama film written and directed by Andrew Dominik, based on Joyce Carol Oates's 2000 novel. A fictionalized account of the life and career of Marilyn Monroe, it stars Ana de Armas as Monroe, with Adrien Brody, Bobby Cannavale, Xavier Samuel and Julianne Nicholson. After a development period that began in 2010, it was shot in Los Angeles, with production wrapping in July 2021. The film shifts between aspect ratios and alternates between color and black and white.

In 1933, young Norma Jeane Mortenson lives with her mentally unstable mother Gladys, who on her seventh birthday shows her a framed photograph of a man she claims is Norma Jeane's father. After a night of terrifying violence in which Gladys tries to drown her in the bath, Norma Jeane is sent to an orphanage and her mother to a psychiatric hospital. In the 1940s she becomes a pin-up model under the name Marilyn Monroe and, while trying to break into films, is sexually assaulted by a studio head. Her career takes off with Don't Bother to Knock and Niagara, and she begins a relationship with Charles "Cass" Chaplin Jr. and Edward G. "Eddy" Robinson Jr., but she increasingly feels that the glamorous persona of Marilyn is not her real self. A pregnancy ends in an abortion she begs to stop. She marries Joe DiMaggio, whose jealousy turns violent after nude publicity photos surface, and they divorce after she finishes The Seven Year Itch. She then marries the playwright Arthur Miller, who is won over by her insight into his work, but suffers a miscarriage. Throughout, she longs for the father she has never met and receives letters from a man claiming to be him. During the making of Some Like It Hot she grows unstable, clashing with director Billy Wilder and relying on pills, and by 1962, dependent on drugs and alcohol and exploited by powerful men including the President, she struggles to reconcile Norma Jeane with the image the world has made of her.

Blonde premiered at the 79th Venice International Film Festival on September 8, 2022, and was released on Netflix on September 28 after a limited theatrical run, the first NC-17-rated film released exclusively to a streaming service. It proved highly divisive: de Armas's performance was praised and earned her an Academy Award nomination for Best Actress, while many critics found its fictionalization exploitative, and it holds a 42% rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

The film also touches on the idea of the American Dream, highlighting the ways in which the pursuit of wealth and status can lead individuals down a path of moral compromise and destruction. Through Cody and Brian's story, The Trust critiques the excesses of capitalism and the ways in which it can consume and destroy those who are caught up in its cycle.

Ultimately, The Trust is a gripping and intense thriller that explores the complexities of human relationships and the devastating consequences of unchecked ambition.

title: Before I Wake
tagline: Fear your dreams.
overview: An orphaned child's dreams—and nightmares—manifest physically as he sleeps.
plot:
Before I Wake, released in some international territories as Somnia, is a 2016 American supernatural horror fantasy directed and edited by Mike Flanagan, who co-wrote the screenplay with Jeff Howard. Kate Bosworth and Thomas Jane star as a grieving couple, with Jacob Tremblay as their foster son, and Annabeth Gish, Topher Bousquet and Dash Mihok in supporting roles. Its release was delayed for years after its original distributor, Relativity Media, filed for bankruptcy; it eventually premiered at the Fantasia International Film Festival in July 2016 and was released in the United States by Netflix.

Jessie and Mark Hobson are still mourning their young son Sean, who died in an accidental drowning, when they decide to foster eight-year-old Cody Morgan. Their social worker explains that Cody's mother died of cancer when he was three and that two previous foster placements did not work out. On his first night in the house, Cody nervously tells Jessie about a terrifying creature he calls the Canker Man and does everything he can to stay awake.

That night, Jessie and Mark are astonished when a cloud of glowing, multicoloured butterflies, Cody's favourite creatures, fills their living room, only to vanish the moment the boy wakes. They soon realise that Cody's dreams physically manifest while he sleeps. After he sees a photograph of Sean, the couple are able to see and touch their dead son again, and Jessie begins showing Cody home videos of Sean so that his dreams will bring the boy back, a choice Mark considers a dangerous exploitation of the child. But Cody's nightmares also come to life, and the Canker Man, a gaunt and menacing figure, begins to appear and consume people. As those around Cody disappear, Jessie investigates the boy's past to understand the origin of the creature and what it is connected to.

Flanagan uses the supernatural premise to explore grief, parenthood and the way loss can make people selfish, and the film moves from dreamlike wonder toward horror before ending on a melancholy note about memory and acceptance.

Before I Wake received generally positive reviews. On Rotten Tomatoes it holds an approval rating of about 67 percent; the consensus notes that it is not always lucid enough to overcome its wobbly story but crafts an effective horror landscape, with Tremblay's performance singled out for praise.

overview: CIA Agent Bill Pope is on a mission to track down a shadowy hacker named 'The Dutchman'. When he gets mysteriously killed, an experimental procedure transfers his memories into a dangerous ex-convict. plot:
Criminal is a 2016 American action thriller film directed by Nima Nourizadeh and written by Chris Morgan. The movie stars Gerard Butler, Michael Pitt, Alice Eve, and John Malkovich.

The story follows Bradley "Brad" Jones (Gerard Butler), an FBI agent who specializes in tracking down and capturing serial killers. Brad is a skilled profiler with a unique ability to understand the minds of his subjects. He has a reputation for being one of the best in the business, but also struggles with his own dark past.

One day, Brad receives a package containing a severed finger from a serial killer known as "The Vermin" (John Malkovich). The finger is sent to the FBI lab, where it's analyzed and matched to a series of gruesome murders across Europe. As the investigation unfolds, Brad becomes obsessed with tracking down The Vermin.

Meanwhile, in Berlin, German detective Lena Clark (Alice Eve) is working on her own case involving a serial killer known as "The Vermin." She's initially dismissive of Brad's involvement but eventually teams up with him to catch the killer. As they work together, Lena and Brad develop a romantic connection.

However, things take a dark turn when Brad discovers that The Vermin has been using his own skills against him. The serial killer has been manipulating Brad's past, making him question his own sanity and identity. It becomes clear that The Vermin is not just any ordinary serial killer but someone who knows Brad's deepest secrets.

As the story unfolds, it's revealed that The Vermin was once a patient of Brad's at an asylum where he was being treated for his own dark past. The serial killer has been using this knowledge to manipulate and control Brad, making him doubt his own identity and purpose.

In the climactic final act, Brad and Lena finally track down The Vermin, who is revealed to be a former patient of Brad's at the asylum. In a tense showdown, Brad confronts his past and The Vermin, ultimately emerging victorious but not without scars.

Throughout the movie, Gerard Butler delivers a strong performance as the complex and troubled Brad Jones. His character's inner turmoil and struggle with his own demons make him a compelling protagonist. The supporting cast, including Alice Eve and John Malkovich, add depth to the story, making it a gripping thriller that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats.

Overall, Criminal is a tense and thought-provoking thriller that explores themes of identity, trauma, and the blurred lines between good and evil. With its strong performances and intricate plot, it's a must-see for fans of action-thrillers.

title: Snowden
tagline: The only safe place is on the run.
overview: CIA employee Edward Snowden leaks thousands of classified documents to the press.
plot:
Snowden is a 2016 biographical thriller directed by Oliver Stone, who wrote it with Kieran Fitzgerald, based on Luke Harding's book The Snowden Files and Anatoly Kucherena's Time of the Octopus. Joseph Gordon-Levitt plays Edward Snowden, the intelligence contractor who leaked classified National Security Agency documents in 2013, with Shailene Woodley as his girlfriend Lindsay Mills, Melissa Leo as Laura Poitras, Zachary Quinto as Glenn Greenwald, Tom Wilkinson as Ewen MacAskill, Rhys Ifans as his CIA mentor Corbin O'Brian and Nicolas Cage as Hank Forrester. A German, French and American co-production, it began filming in Munich in February 2015.

The story is framed by Snowden's secret 2013 meeting in Hong Kong with the documentary filmmaker Poitras and the journalist Greenwald, where he reveals evidence of illegal mass surveillance. In flashback, a broken leg ends his Army training in 2004, and he joins the CIA, where a deputy director takes a chance on him and he excels at cyberwarfare. He begins a relationship with Mills, whom he meets online, though their political views are sharply opposed. Posted to Geneva under diplomatic cover, he grows uneasy when his superiors entrap a target to extract information, and he resigns.

Working next for the NSA in Japan, he designs a backup system called Epic Shelter and learns how the agency monitors even allied nations, planting malware in their infrastructure. The strain ends his relationship with Mills, but they reunite in Maryland. Diagnosed with epilepsy, he accepts a post in Hawaii, where he discovers that his program is feeding real-time data to drone strikes in Pakistan. Disillusioned, he smuggles a microSD card into his office inside a Rubik's Cube, copies the evidence, and leaves for Hong Kong. With MacAskill's help the first stories are published on 5 June 2013. Snowden is smuggled out of Hong Kong on a flight to Latin America via Russia, but when the United States revokes his passport he is stranded in Moscow, where he is granted asylum and is later joined by Mills.

After a screening at San Diego Comic-Con and a premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival, Open Road Films released it in the United States on 16 September 2016. Reviews were mixed: critics praised Gordon-Levitt's performance but faulted Stone's direction, and it holds a 61% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. It grossed $37.3 million worldwide against a $40 million budget.

title: Remember
tagline: Dark truths will come to light.
overview: With the aid of a fellow Auschwitz survivor and a hand-written letter, an elderly man with dementia goes in search of the person responsible for the death of his family.
plot:
Remember is a 2015 Canadian-German drama thriller directed by Atom Egoyan and written by Benjamin August, a first-time screenwriter who wanted to create a lead role for an older actor. Producer Robert Lantos saw Egoyan as the ideal director, and Egoyan considered the project timely because the last Holocaust survivors and perpetrators were still alive and trials were under way in Germany. Shooting began in July 2014 in Sault Ste. Marie and northern Ontario.

In a New York nursing home, Zev Guttman, an 89-year-old Auschwitz survivor with dementia, keeps waking up looking for his wife, Ruth, who died two weeks earlier. His friend Max Rosenbaum, another survivor who is physically incapacitated, reminds him of his promise: to find and kill Otto Wallisch, the camp Blockführer who murdered both their families and is believed to have entered the United States under the name Rudy Kurlander. Four men by that name have been identified, and Zev and Max are the last people able to recognize him. Guided by Max's detailed letter and travel arrangements, Zev slips away, buys a pistol in Cleveland and sets off to visit each candidate in turn.

The first Kurlander turns out to have fought in North Africa, and the second, in Ontario, was himself imprisoned at Auschwitz as a gay man. In Idaho, Zev learns that the third has died; the man's son, a neo-Nazi state trooper, turns violent on discovering that Zev is Jewish, and Zev kills his dog and then him. After a fall in Reno, Zev reaches the fourth Kurlander's home near Lake Tahoe and recognizes his voice. Threatening the man's granddaughter, he demands the truth, and the old man reveals that he is Kunibert Sturm and that Zev himself is Otto Wallisch: both had been Blockführers and afterward tattooed each other with numbers to pass as Jewish survivors. Zev shoots Sturm, declares "I remember" and kills himself, and back in New York Max reveals that he recognized Zev as Wallisch on his arrival and that the two men had killed his family.

Christopher Plummer plays Zev and Martin Landau plays Max, with Bruno Ganz, Heinz Lieven and Jürgen Prochnow as Kurlanders, Dean Norris as the trooper and Henry Czerny as Zev's son. The film screened in competition at the Venice Film Festival and was released by A24 in the United States in March 2016. Critics were mostly positive, especially about Plummer's performance, with 69% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, and August won the Canadian Screen Award for Best Original Screenplay.

title: 10.0 Earthquake
tagline: The end is near.
overview: Los Angeles is about to be hit by a devastating earthquake, and time is running out to save the city from imminent danger.
plot:
10.0 Earthquake is a 2014 American low-budget disaster film directed by David Gidali. Henry Ian Cusick stars as Jack, an engineer, with Cameron Richardson as Emily Schiffman, a young scientist with the United States Geological Survey, Jeffrey Jones as Marcus Gladstone, and Kristen Dalton, Chasty Ballesteros, Heather Sossaman, Olivia Jordan, David Chokachi and Malcolm Barrett in supporting roles.

Emily, newly working for the USGS, notices a series of small, highly localized earthquakes striking the Los Angeles area and develops a theory that they are building toward a catastrophic super quake. If she is right, the entire city could collapse into a chasm of molten rock. The cause, it emerges, is a deep-drilling fracking operation run by a company that has pushed its drilling far below the surface. Jack, an engineer at the company who is going through a divorce and is estranged from his teenage daughter, realizes that his employer is responsible for the disaster and feels obliged to help stop it.

As the tremors grow stronger and more frequent, the film moves between Jack and Emily and a series of other characters scattered across the region, among them a group of young people on an outing in the wilderness, whose lives are suddenly threatened when the ground opens beneath them. Jack and Emily race across the increasingly devastated city, dodging collapsing roads and vanishing bridges, as they attempt to carry out a plan to divert the epicenter of the coming quake toward Long Beach, a move that could save millions of lives, including that of Jack's daughter, but which requires them to act before the final, massive quake strikes.

The film received little mainstream critical attention. A review on the site Cinematic Diversions found that, although it resembled the cheap disaster films produced by The Asylum and its computer-generated effects were often crude, it benefited from a better-than-expected script and solid acting, and its structure of small, deadly localized tremors gave it a tension reminiscent of the Final Destination films. The reviewer also noted the scientific implausibility of its fracking premise. Gidali later remarked that the screenplay had been completely rewritten shortly before shooting began.

plot:
Central Intelligence is a 2016 American action comedy film directed by Rawson Marshall Thurber and produced by New Line Cinema.

The movie begins with Bob Stone (played by Kevin Hart), an overweight and awkward high school student who dreams of becoming a spy. However, his life takes a drastic turn when he meets Calvin Joyner (played by Dwayne Johnson), the star athlete of their high school. Despite their vastly different personalities, they become close friends.

Years later, Bob receives a message from Calvin, informing him that he has been recruited by the CIA and is now working undercover as a spy. However, his cover is blown, and he is forced to go into hiding after being targeted by a group of assassins hired by a rogue agent named James King (played by Karl Urban).

Calvin returns Bob's call, and they reunite to take down James King, who has stolen a deadly virus that can kill millions. As they embark on their mission, they must navigate through various obstacles, including treacherous terrain, high-tech gadgets, and James King's henchmen.

Throughout the movie, Calvin tries to help Bob regain his confidence and learn how to be a spy, while also dealing with his own personal demons. Meanwhile, Bob struggles to keep up with Calvin's high-octane lifestyle, leading to some hilarious moments of culture shock.

As they delve deeper into their mission, Bob and Calvin discover that James King is working for a shadowy organization known as "The Syndicate." They must use all their skills and resources to infiltrate The Syndicate's headquarters and stop the virus from being released.

In the climactic final act, Bob and Calvin face off against James King in an intense showdown. With Calvin's spy training and Bob's... um, unique set of skills, they manage to defeat James King and save the world from the deadly virus.

The movie ends with Bob finally finding his place as a spy, thanks to Calvin's mentorship. The two friends share a heartwarming moment, and the film concludes on a high note, leaving the audience laughing and entertained.

Overall, Central Intelligence is a fun and action-packed comedy that showcases the chemistry between Kevin Hart and Dwayne Johnson. With its witty dialogue, impressive stunts, and hilarious moments, it's no wonder this movie became a box office hit.

title: The Accountant
tagline: Calculate your choices.
overview: As a math savant uncooks the books for a new client, the Treasury Department closes in on his activities and the body count starts to rise.
plot:
The Accountant is a 2016 American action thriller film directed by Gavin O'Connor and written by Bill Dubuque. The movie stars Ben Affleck as Christian Wolff, a socially awkward and numerically gifted accountant with high-functioning autism.

The story begins with Christian Wolff (Ben Affleck), a brilliant and resourceful accountant who works for a large corporation. However, Christian's exceptional skills are not recognized or valued by his employers, leading him to feel isolated and unappreciated. He is forced to work as an accountant in a small firm, where he struggles to connect with others due to his autism.

One day, Christian receives a call from a mysterious woman named Mary Elizabeth Monroe (Anna Kendrick), who hires him for a high-stakes job. plot:
Dragon Ball Z: Resurrection 'F' is a Japanese animated science fantasy martial arts film of 2015 directed by Tadayoshi Yamamuro, the sequel to Dragon Ball Z: Battle of Gods (2013) and the nineteenth animated feature based on Akira Toriyama's Dragon Ball manga. Toriyama wrote the screenplay and supervised it. The voice cast is led by Masako Nozawa as Goku and his son Gohan, Ryō Horikawa as Vegeta and Ryūsei Nakao as Frieza, with Kōichi Yamadera as the god of destruction Beerus and Masakazu Morita as his attendant Whis.

Sorbet, commander of what remains of Frieza's army, comes to Earth and forces the Pilaf Gang to gather the Dragon Balls and summon the dragon Shenron to bring Frieza back to life. Because Frieza was cut to pieces by Future Trunks, he is revived in fragments, which Sorbet's soldiers reassemble with advanced technology. Plotting revenge on the Super Saiyans but learning that Goku has grown far stronger, he delays his invasion to train for the first time in his life. Jaco the Galactic Patrolman warns Bulma. With Goku and Vegeta away training with Whis on Beerus's planet, Gohan, Piccolo, Krillin, Master Roshi, Tien Shinhan and Jaco band together and defeat thousands of Frieza's soldiers, but the newly powerful tyrant overwhelms them. Bulma reaches Whis, and the two Saiyans return to save their friends.

Goku takes on Frieza first and quickly gains the upper hand, until Frieza realizes he is holding back and the two agree to fight at full strength. Goku transforms into a blue-haired godly Super Saiyan form, later named Super Saiyan Blue, while Frieza becomes Golden Frieza. Frieza has the advantage at first, but Goku notices that his inexperience with the form drains his energy quickly and defeats him, offering him the chance to leave Earth. Instead Sorbet shoots Goku in the chest with a ray gun, and Frieza invites Vegeta to finish off his rival and become his second-in-command. Vegeta refuses, transforms into Super Saiyan Blue himself and dominates Frieza, deflecting a blast that kills Sorbet. Humiliated, Frieza destroys the Earth, killing Vegeta, while Whis shields Goku, Beerus and the others on a fragment of rock. Whis then turns back time by three minutes, and Goku kills Frieza with a Kamehameha before he can strike; a post-credits scene shows Frieza back in Hell.

Released in Japan on 18 April 2015, it opened at number one at the box office and grossed $61.7 million worldwide on a $5 million budget. Reviews were generally positive.

The Power Rangers face off against Lord Zedd's army of monsters and robots, including the Putty Patrollers, the Megazord, and the Tyrannosaurus Rex. Along the way, they also meet Alpha 5 (Bill Hader), a talking computer who helps them on their quest.

As the final battle approaches, the Power Rangers discover that Lord Zedd's plan is to destroy Angel Grove and rule over the world. The group uses all of their powers and work together to defeat Lord Zedd and his minions in an epic showdown.

Its ensemble cast is led by Eden Sher and Victoria Justice as two misfit best friends, with Ashley Rickards, Claudia Lee, Katie Chang, Peyton List, Avan Jogia, Jazmyn C. Richardson, Frank Whaley and Ted McGinley. The story follows a group of unpopular teenagers who band together to topple the ruling clique at their high school.

Mindy Lipschitz, a science nerd, and Jodi Schellenberger, a music nerd and aspiring songwriter, have endured years of torment from the school's mean girls, the ruthless queen bee Whitney Bennett and her younger sidekick Mackenzie Smith. The friends intend to get through their senior year unnoticed, but after an attempt to reason with Whitney ends in a humiliating prank, they decide to beat their persecutors at their own game. Mindy, the brains of the operation, and Jodi set out to unite the school's outcasts and start a social revolution.

They recruit leaders of the various misfit factions, including a fantasy nerd, a sci-fi nerd and a tech nerd, along with Virginia Vanderkamp, a wealthy, depressed loner and overachiever with dirt on everyone; Claire Stewart, a Girl Scout with a secret who eventually comes out as a lesbian; Sugar Jones, who wants to stand up for civil rights and women's rights; and Dave Quinn, an affable slacker and former member of Whitney's circle who becomes Jodi's boyfriend. Their alliance of cliques briefly creates a nerd utopia, highlighted by a weekend party with cosplay, and even Mackenzie abandons Whitney to spend time with Mindy, while it emerges that Whitney's claims of wealth are false and her parents are servants in the mansion where she lives. But the push for liberation turns into a thirst for revenge, new dictatorial impulses emerge, and the friends' crusade begins to strain their own friendship.

Originally titled The Outskirts, the film was shot in July and August 2014 in New York City and at a high school in Great Neck. Swen Group acquired it in March 2017 and released it in limited theaters and on video on demand on April 14, 2017; it reached Netflix that August. Reviews were mixed, with a Metacritic score of 47. The Hollywood Reporter found it amiable but underwhelming, praising Sher and Justice as sympathetic leads in a story indebted to countless earlier high school comedies.

tagline: There are two sides to every story.
overview: A young woman comes to in a roadside diner with no idea where she is or how she got there. Split between two timelines, she gets taken on a violent journey as she seeks out the person responsible for her lover's death.
plot:
88 is a 2015 Canadian thriller directed by April Mullen and written by Tim Doiron, starring Katharine Isabelle as Gwen, a woman whose revenge plot unravels when she slips into fugue states and must piece her memories back together. Christopher Lloyd, Kyle Schmid, Jesse McCartney and Michael Ironside also appear.

Gwen snaps out of a daze in a diner, unsure where she is, and finds a pistol in her bag; when police confront her, she accidentally shoots a waitress and flees. A key leads her to a hotel room she does not remember, where she finds the body of her best friend, Winks. A man who arrives to kill her is himself killed by Ty, who insists that the two of them had planned to murder an underworld boss named Cyrus at the diner. Gwen swears she could never kill anyone, but she leaves with him. Flashbacks reveal that she blames Cyrus for the death of her boyfriend, Aster: after she saw Cyrus with a dead woman, later revealed to be Ty's sister, he ordered both Gwen and Aster killed.

Seeking weapons from the illegal arms dealer Lemmy, Gwen and Ty are tracked down by Sheriff Knowles; Lemmy dies in the ensuing shootout, Ty escapes wounded, and the terrified Gwen is arrested. She claims Cyrus framed her, and Knowles, more interested in the gangster, offers her a deal if she can deliver him. Ty storms the station, killing several officers, but dies in a crossfire as he and Gwen escape. More flashbacks show that Gwen herself caused several deaths while in a fugue state, including the killing of Winks, who had given them Cyrus's location but whose concern for Gwen made her suspicious. Still unsure of her own motives, Gwen resumes her hunt, shooting a police officer who pulls her over for speeding. Confronting Cyrus, she blames him for every death, but he denies it, and under his prodding she remembers that she accidentally shot Aster herself while trying to warn him. Telling her to blame him so she might escape prosecution, Cyrus shoots himself in front of her. A final flashback returns to the diner, where Aster's favorite song on the jukebox sends the distraught Gwen into a daze.

The film premiered at the Glasgow Film Festival, and Millennium Entertainment released it on home video in the United States on January 6, 2015. Canadian critics were unenthusiastic: the National Post gave it zero stars, while The Globe and Mail and the Toronto Star rated it 2.5 and 2 out of 4.

title: The Stanford Prison Experiment

overview: This film is based on the actual events that took place in 1971 when Stanford professor Dr. Philip Zimbardo created what became one of the most shocking and famous social experiments of all time.

The Stanford Prison Experiment (2015) is a thought-provoking drama that delves into the darker aspects of human nature and the effects of power dynamics on individuals. At its core, the film explores the theme of how quickly normal, well-adjusted people can descend into madness when given absolute authority over others.

The movie masterfully portrays the psychological manipulation that occurs when individuals are stripped of their autonomy and forced to adopt roles that are antithetical to their own identities. As the experiment progresses, the participants' behavior becomes increasingly erratic and sinister, revealing a disturbing underbelly of human psychology.

One of the primary themes of The Stanford Prison Experiment is the dangers of unchecked power and the corrupting influence it can have on individuals. The film highlights how even well-intentioned people can become perpetrators when given the authority to dictate the actions of others. This theme is expertly woven throughout the narrative, as the characters' behavior becomes more and more disturbing as they are given greater control over their "prisoners."

Another significant theme in the movie is the concept of dehumanization. As the participants begin to adopt their roles, they start to view themselves and others as less than human, stripping away any semblance of empathy or compassion. This dehumanization serves as a catalyst for the descent into madness, as individuals become more willing to engage in cruel and sadistic behavior.

The Stanford Prison Experiment also touches on the theme of social conditioning, highlighting how societal norms and expectations can shape our behavior and influence our actions. The film suggests that even the most well-adjusted individuals can be molded into conforming to certain roles or expectations, leading to a loss of individuality and autonomy.

Overall, The Stanford Prison Experiment is a thought-provoking drama that sheds light on the darker aspects of human nature and the dangers of unchecked power and dehumanization.

title: War Dogs

overview: Based on the true story of two young men, David Packouz and Efraim Diveroli, who won a $300 million contract from the Pentagon to arm America's allies in Afghanistan.
plot:
War Dogs is a biographical crime comedy-drama film directed by Todd Phillips, released in 2016 by Warner Bros. Pictures.

The movie is based on the true story of Efraim Diveroli and David Packouz, two young men from Los Angeles who become arms dealers during the Iraq War. The film follows their journey from their early days as small-time hustlers to becoming successful arms dealers, and eventually, to their downfall.

The story begins with Efraim (played by Jonah Hill), a struggling young man working at his father's car wash in Los Angeles. He is joined by David Packouz (played by Miles Teller), a charismatic but aimless young man who has just dropped out of college. The two become fast friends and start selling marijuana to make ends meet.

Their fortunes change when they are approached by Efraim's uncle, Alonzo (played by Jeremy Renner), who is working for the U.S. government as an arms dealer. He offers them a lucrative deal to supply the Afghan military with machine guns, which they initially reject due to their inexperience and lack of knowledge about the business.

However, after some persuasion from Efraim's uncle, they decide to take on the job. They start by purchasing 1,000 AK-47 machine guns from an Israeli arms dealer, but things quickly go awry when they realize that they have no idea how to deliver the guns or handle the complex logistics of selling them.

Despite their inexperience, Efraim and David manage to convince some of their friends to join their operation, including a young man named Kristofer (played by Bradley Cooper), who becomes their partner. The group starts to build a network of suppliers and buyers, but their success is short-lived.

As the story unfolds, it becomes clear that Efraim and David's partnership is built on lies, deceit, and a lack of trust. They start to turn on each other, and their relationships with their friends and family begin to fray.

The film takes a dark turn when Efraim and David are approached by a Russian arms dealer, Viktor (played by Anatol Yusef), who offers them an even bigger deal. However, things take a deadly turn when they realize that the guns they have been selling are being used against American soldiers in Afghanistan.

In the end, Efraim and David's empire comes crashing down around them. They are arrested and charged with conspiracy to defraud the U.S. government, and their lives are forever changed.

Throughout the film, Jonah Hill and Miles Teller deliver strong performances as the two main characters. Jeremy Renner brings his signature charm and wit to the role of Efraim's uncle, while Bradley Cooper shines in a supporting role as Kristofer.

Overall, War Dogs is a gripping and intense drama that explores the darker side of human nature. It is a cautionary tale about the dangers of greed, ambition, and the consequences of playing with fire.

title: Homesick
overview: When Charlotte, 27, meets her brother Henrik, 35, for the first time as an adult, it becomes an encounter without boundaries, between two people who don't know what a normal family is. How does sibling love manifest itself if you have never experienced it before? Homesick is an unusual family drama about seeking a family, and breaking every rule to be one.
plot:
Homesick (Norwegian: De nærmeste, literally "The Nearest") is a 2015 Norwegian drama directed by Anne Sewitsky, her third feature after Happy, Happy, which won the World Cinema Grand Jury Prize for drama at Sundance in 2011. Produced by Maipo Film, it stars Ine Marie Wilmann as Charlotte and Simon J. Berger as Henrik, with Anneke von der Lippe as their mother Anna, Silje Storstein as Charlotte's best friend Marte and Oddgeir Thune as her boyfriend Dag. Daniel Voldheim was the cinematographer and Christoffer Heie the editor.

Charlotte is a 27-year-old dance teacher in Oslo who seems to lead a happy life, teaching young children, with a musician boyfriend and a best friend in whom she confides. Behind her smile, however, she is deeply needy. Her alcoholic father is dying of cirrhosis, and her self-centered mother Anna, about to leave on a trip to fulfil her dreams, shows her little affection. When Henrik, Anna's son from her first marriage, whom Charlotte has never known, moves with his wife and son from Sweden to Oslo, she grows curious and spies on him, even turning up unannounced at his home. Henrik's wife encourages the half-siblings to spend an evening together to clear the air, and after a night of drinking and fooling around they develop an attraction that turns into an incestuous affair. Two people who have never known what a normal family is try to work out what sibling love can be, breaking every rule in the process. Dag ends their relationship after finding explicit messages on her phone, while Marte furiously accuses Charlotte of draining the life out of everyone she meets.

Homesick premiered at the 2015 Sundance Film Festival, was nominated for the Dragon Award for Best Nordic Film at the Göteborg Film Festival, screened in the Contemporary World Cinema section in Toronto, and was shortlisted as Norway's Oscar submission before The Wave was chosen. Reviews were mixed. Ben Umstead of ScreenAnarchy called it a complex, humane drama that treats the taboo relationship as a romance rather than judging it, and praised Wilmann's nuanced, surprising performance. For FIPRESCI, Ulrich Wimmeroth admired Wilmann's outstanding debut but found the film cold and distant, since the affair seems to carry no real consequences.

plot:
The Flintstones & WWE: Stone Age SmackDown! is a 2015 American direct-to-video animated film directed by Spike Brandt and Tony Cervone. The second co-production between Warner Bros. Animation and WWE Studios, it places Fred Flintstone, Barney Rubble and the rest of Bedrock alongside Stone Age versions of WWE wrestlers. Jeff Bergman voices Fred, Kevin Michael Richardson Barney, Tress MacNeille Wilma and Grey Griffin Betty, while John Cena, CM Punk, Rey Mysterio, Mark Henry, Brie and Nikki Bella, Vince McMahon and The Undertaker voice their animated counterparts.

Fred has promised his wife, Wilma, a vacation, but his boss, Mr. Slate, refuses him time off and money, having just hired a relative, John Cenastone. At a fair run by the Lodge of Water Buffaloes, Fred tries to raise cash by having Hoppy, the pet hopparoo of his friend Barney, box challengers. Hoppy wins repeatedly until the thug CM Punkrock humiliates him, and an outraged Barney defeats Punkrock, who storms off with his partner, Marble Henry. Seeing a chance to make money from wrestling, Fred teams up with a seafood seller, Mr. McMagma, to stage a show at an abandoned circus. Cenastone recruits the masked clerk Rey Mysteriopal and The Undertaker, a gloomy gravedigger, and Fred pushes a reluctant Barney into the ring against The Undertaker. Barney is about to win when Wilma and Betty arrive to scold their husbands, but the trouble passes because Fred has made enough money.

Inspired by McMagma, Fred wants more and rents Bedrock Stadium for a rematch between Barney and Punkrock, also booking Henry and the Boulder Twins. Barney refuses to take part, and Fred goes ahead without him. When Fred admits Barney will not appear, the other wrestlers walk out, disappointed that he has neglected his friend, and Fred is left to face Punkrock and his allies alone, taking a beating. Moved by Fred's sacrifice, Barney joins the fight with the other wrestlers, Wilma and Betty intimidate the Boulder Twins and young Bamm-Bamm easily defeats Henry. After the victory, Fred quits wrestling, sells the idea to McMagma and takes everyone on vacation.

Warner Home Video released the film on March 10, 2015. It was the first new Flintstones production in more than thirteen years, and Russi Taylor's last film. IndieWire wrote that it recaptured the heyday of Hanna-Barbera so meticulously that it left viewers yearning for more Flintstones cartoons.

Leonardo (Jellystone) is struggling with leadership, feeling overwhelmed by the responsibility of being the leader of the group. Donatello (Beezle) is trying to find a way to defeat Krang and Baxter, who are using advanced technology to wreak havoc on New York City.

Meanwhile, Michelangelo (Raph's brother) is dealing with his own demons, feeling like he doesn't fit in with the rest of the group. Raphael (Michelangelo's brother) is struggling with anger issues, which puts him at odds with Leonardo and Donatello.

The Turtles also have to navigate their relationships with April and Casey Jones (Stephen Amell), a hockey-masked vigilante who becomes an ally in their fight against Shredder and Krang. Overall, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows is an entertaining and action-packed sequel that expands on the characters and world introduced in the first film. While it may not be as strong as its predecessor, it still delivers plenty of laughs, excitement, and heart.

title: Zipper
tagline: Why take the risk
overview: Sam Ellis is a man on the rise — a hot-shot federal prosecutor on the cusp of a bright political future. But what was meant to be a one-time experience with an escort turns into a growing addiction — a new demon threatening to destroy his life, family, and career.
plot:
Zipper, also released as Reckless, is a 2015 American political drama thriller written and directed by Mora Stephens with co-writer Joel Viertel. Patrick Wilson stars as Sam Ellis, a federal prosecutor whose compulsive pursuit of high-priced escorts threatens a promising political career, with Lena Headey as his wife, Jeannie, Dianna Agron as an intern, Richard Dreyfuss as a campaign consultant and Ray Winstone as a magazine writer, alongside Penelope Mitchell and John Cho.

Sam is a rising star in South Carolina, a smug, family-values prosecutor with a strong record of taking on errant officials, a young son and a polished home run by Jeannie, a former lawyer who is beautiful, stylish and politically connected. After a work celebration he shares a drunken kiss with an aggressively seductive intern, Dalia, but rejects her advances. When he interviews an alluring escort as a witness in a case, however, his desires take over. Already given to online pornography, he begins browsing high-end escort websites and, while Jeannie is away for a weekend, nervously uses a prepaid phone to book a $1,000-an-hour date at a luxury hotel. The awkward first encounter leaves him hooked, and a montage of cash withdrawals and hotel trysts follows.

At the same time, Sam is being groomed for an open seat in Congress, with the help of his shrewd wife, a ruthless consultant and a writer whose flattering profile is meant to launch his campaign. His secret life grows more reckless just as his image faces intense scrutiny: his card is declined when he tries to buy Jeannie a guilt gift, and at his most desperate he is struck by a car while running for more cash. In one twist, he effectively takes charge of the investigation into his favorite escort agency to protect himself, and he forms an unexpectedly personal bond with a college dropout turned escort. When the reporter threatens to expose the scandal, the focus shifts to Jeannie, who must weigh her husband's betrayal against her own ambitions, including her dream of becoming First Lady.

Zipper premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 27, 2015, and Alchemy released it in limited theaters and on demand on August 28, 2015. Reviews were largely negative, with 20% on Rotten Tomatoes, though critics praised Wilson's committed performance and Headey's complex portrayal of the wife; The New York Times found it engrossing.

title: The Little Prince
tagline: Growing up isn't the problem... forgetting is.
overview: Based on the best-seller book 'The Little Prince', the movie tells the story of a little girl that lives with resignation in a world where efficiency and work are the only dogmas. Everything will change when accidentally she discovers her neighbor that will tell her about the story of the Little Prince that he once met.
plot:
The Little Prince (French: Le Petit Prince) is a 2015 English-language French-Italian animated fantasy film directed by Mark Osborne and based on the 1943 novella by Antoine de Saint-Exupéry. The voice cast includes Jeff Bridges, Rachel McAdams, Paul Rudd, Marion Cotillard, James Franco, Benicio del Toro, Ricky Gervais, Paul Giamatti, Bud Cort and Albert Brooks, with Mackenzie Foy as the Little Girl. The film combines computer animation for its framing story with stop-motion animation made to resemble paper and the original watercolour illustrations for the sections adapted directly from the book.

Rather than adapting the novella directly, the film wraps it in a new story. A single mother and her young daughter move into a new neighbourhood, where the mother has organised a rigid life plan meant to secure the girl a place at the prestigious Werth Academy, leaving no time for play or friendship. Next door lives an eccentric elderly Aviator, voiced by Bridges, who sends the girl a page of a story he has written and drawn. Gradually she visits him in secret and hears about the Little Prince, a boy he says he met after crash-landing in the Sahara many years before.

Through the Aviator's tale the girl learns of the prince's tiny home, Asteroid B-612, his struggle against invasive baobab sprouts, and his love for a vain but beautiful Rose. Too young to understand each other, the prince and the rose part, and he travels to other asteroids, meeting lonely adults such as a King, a Conceited Man and a Businessman obsessed with counting stars, before arriving on Earth and befriending a Fox who teaches him that what is essential is invisible to the eye. When the Aviator falls ill, the girl sets off on her own fantastical journey to find the grown-up Prince in a grey world controlled by the Businessman, where imagination has been replaced by productivity.

The film reflects on childhood, memory, friendship and the danger of growing up without wonder, while the girl must reconcile her mother's expectations with the lessons of the story.

The Little Prince premiered out of competition at the 2015 Cannes Film Festival and received positive reviews, with praise for its animation and its respectful handling of the source. It won the César Award for Best Animated Film, and it was released on Netflix in several countries.

Turbo Kid is a 2015 Canadian science fiction action film directed by François Simard, Anouk Whissell, and Yoann-Karl Whissell.

The movie's main theme revolves around the struggle for identity and self-discovery in a post-apocalyptic world. The protagonist, Turbo (played by Munro Chambers), is a young man who lives on a farm with his abusive father. After being bullied and belittled by his father, Turbo finds solace in an underground fighting tournament where he discovers his unique fighting style.

As the story unfolds, Turbo's journey becomes one of self-discovery and empowerment. He must confront his troubled past and learn to accept himself for who he is, flaws and all. The film explores themes of toxic masculinity, abuse, and the importance of finding one's own path in life.

The movie also touches on the idea of community and found family, as Turbo forms bonds with a group of misfits who become his allies in the fight against their common enemies. Through its blend of action, humor, and heart, Turbo Kid presents a powerful exploration of identity, self-acceptance, and the human need for connection and belonging.

Overall, Turbo Kid is a visually stunning and energetic film that balances action and drama with a strong narrative focus on character development and emotional depth.

title: The Great Wall
tagline: 1700 years to build. 5500 miles long. What were they trying to keep out?
overview: European mercenaries searching for black powder become embroiled in the defense of the Great Wall of China against a horde of monstrous creatures.
plot:
The Great Wall is a 2016 monster film directed by Zhang Yimou, his first English-language feature, from a screenplay by Carlo Bernard, Doug Miro and Tony Gilroy and a story by Max Brooks, Edward Zwick and Marshall Herskovitz. An American and Chinese co-production, it stars Matt Damon, Jing Tian, Pedro Pascal, Willem Dafoe and Andy Lau. Filming began in Qingdao in March 2015, and the film premiered in Beijing on December 6, 2016, before release in China on December 16 and in the United States through Universal Pictures in February 2017.

During the reign of Emperor Renzong, European mercenaries searching for gunpowder are attacked by a monster north of the Great Wall. Only the Irishman William Garin and the Spaniard Pero Tovar survive, cutting off its arm, and they are captured by the Nameless Order, the army that guards the Wall against the Tao Tei, alien creatures that arrived with a meteorite and attack every sixty years. When a horde storms the Wall a week early, the two mercenaries, freed by Ballard, an Englishman who came east twenty-five years before, fight brilliantly and win the Order's respect. After General Shao is killed, Commander Lin takes command, and Strategist Wang notices that the magnet Garin carries seems to subdue the beasts.

Garin helps capture a Tao Tei alive to prove the theory, but an imperial envoy takes it to the capital. The attacks prove to be a diversion while the creatures dig a tunnel through the Wall's base. Tovar and Ballard steal black powder and knock Garin out when he tries to stop them, and Garin is jailed until Lin frees him. When the captive creature awakens in the capital and summons the horde, Lin, Garin, Wang and the young soldier Peng race there in hot-air balloons. Peng and Wang die buying time, and Garin throws the magnet into the horde, opening a gap for Lin's explosive spear to kill the queen, after which the rest of the horde dies. Rather than accept gunpowder as a reward, Garin asks to take the captured Tovar home with him.

Damon and Pascal play the mercenaries. Reviews were mixed to poor, with 35% approval on Rotten Tomatoes, although some critics admired its inventive action and visual style. It grossed $334.9 million worldwide against a $150 million budget, including $170.9 million in China, but was expected to lose about $75 million and was considered a box-office bomb.

title: Creed
tagline: Your legacy is more than a name
overview: The former World Heavyweight Champion Rocky Balboa serves as a trainer and mentor to Adonis Johnson, the son of his late friend and former rival Apollo Creed.
plot:
Creed is an American sports drama of 2015 directed by Ryan Coogler, who wrote it with Aaron Covington. The seventh film in the Rocky franchise and a spin-off sequel to Rocky Balboa (2006), it stars Michael B. Jordan as Adonis Creed, son of the late champion Apollo Creed, and Sylvester Stallone as Rocky Balboa, with Tessa Thompson as Bianca, Phylicia Rashad as Apollo's widow Mary Anne, the real boxer Tony Bellew as "Pretty" Ricky Conlan and Graham McTavish as Conlan's trainer.

In 1998, Adonis Johnson, Apollo's son from an extramarital affair, is in a Los Angeles youth detention centre when Mary Anne offers to take him in. Years later, despite a comfortable finance job, he fights in amateur bouts in Tijuana, and he quits to box professionally. Rejected by a Los Angeles gym run by the son of his father's trainer, and against Mary Anne's fears, since Apollo died in the ring, he moves to Philadelphia and asks Rocky, his father's rival and friend, to train him. Rocky reluctantly agrees, revealing that Apollo won their secret third fight. At the Front Street Gym Adonis trains with Rocky's old friends and falls for Bianca, a singer facing progressive hearing loss.

Fighting as Adonis "Hollywood" Johnson, he beats a local boxer, but the news that he is Apollo's son leaks. The camp of light-heavyweight champion Ricky Conlan, who faces prison and wants a final bout, offers Adonis a title shot on condition he fight under the Creed name, and with Bianca's encouragement he accepts. Rocky collapses and is diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma; having lost Adrian, Paulie and his friends, he refuses chemotherapy. After a quarrel, a jail stint and a reconciliation, Adonis makes Rocky's treatment a condition of fighting. At Goodison Park in Conlan's home city of Liverpool, wearing American flag trunks sent by Mary Anne, Adonis knocks the champion down for the first time in his career and goes the distance, losing a split decision but winning the crowd's respect. The film ends with Adonis helping the weakened Rocky climb the steps of the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

Released by Warner Bros. on 25 November 2015, Creed grossed $173.6 million worldwide on a $35 million budget and drew rave reviews, with 95% on Rotten Tomatoes. Stallone won the Golden Globe for Best Supporting Actor and an Oscar nomination, and two sequels followed.

title: Alien Outpost
tagline: Mankind's Last Stand
overview: A documentary crew follows an elite unit of soldiers in the wake of an alien invasion.
plot:
Alien Outpost, originally titled Outpost 37, is a 2014 science fiction war film directed by Jabbar Raisani, who co-wrote it with Blake Clifton. Adrian Paul, Reiley McClendon, Rick Ravanello, Joe Reegan, Matthew Holmes and Douglas Tait star. Presented as a found-footage documentary, it follows a camera crew recording the daily lives of soldiers at a remote outpost twelve years after an alien invasion, and its format deliberately echoes real war documentaries such as Restrepo and Korengal.

In 2021, aliens known as "Heavies" invade Earth and overwhelm the uncoordinated responses of the world's nations. After the United Nations is replaced by a unified military force, the United Space Defense Force (USDF), the invaders are driven off the planet, although thousands of their soldiers remain stranded on Earth. A network of defensive satellites is believed to protect the planet from a second invasion.

In 2033, two embedded journalists accompany reinforcements to Outpost 37, one of the last USDF bases in a mountainous demilitarized zone on the border between Pakistan and Afghanistan. After a period of hazing, the new arrivals settle into the routine of the base. Hostile local villagers attack the outpost, and the soldiers' requests for supplies and reinforcements are repeatedly denied by a command that seems to have forgotten them. A German volunteer named Hans joins the mostly American unit, and Saleem, a local man loyal to the soldiers who once saved him, brings reports of strange animal mutilations in nearby villages. Patrols sent to investigate discover that the remaining Heavies are not simply hiding but preparing something far larger, and that the outpost may be the last line of defense against a renewed threat.

The film received generally unfavorable reviews, with a Metacritic score of 26 out of 100. Frank Scheck of The Hollywood Reporter called the plot an excuse for video game-style military mayhem, Jeannette Catsoulis of The New York Times praised the cast but felt the acting could not overcome the script, and Michael Rechtshaffen of the Los Angeles Times was likewise unenthusiastic in his review.

title: GirlHouse

overview: In an attempt to make some extra cash while away at College, Kylie moves into a house that streams content to an X-rated website. After a deranged fan hacks in to determine the house's location, she finds herself in a terrifying fight for her life.
plot:
GirlHouse is a 2014 American comedy film that explores the theme of female empowerment and the objectification of women in society. The movie follows the story of a group of young women who are forced to participate in a mysterious experiment, where they are subjected to various forms of psychological manipulation and humiliation.

title: The Walking Deceased
